Umbilical artery abnormalities

↓

Middle cerebral artery (brain-sparing effect)

↓

Ductus venosus abnormalities

↓

Umbilical vein pulsations

↓

Fetal acidemia and decompensation

The ductus venosus (DV) reflects fetal cardiac function and central venous pressure. Abnormal findings include:

• Increased pulsatility index
• Absent or reversed “a” wave

These changes indicate:

• Myocardial dysfunction
• Worsening fetal hypoxia
• Impending fetal acidemia

Why Other Options Are Incorrect

• Umbilical artery increased resistance: Earliest sign of placental insufficiency but less predictive of acidemia.
• MCA decreased PI: Represents the brain-sparing effect and compensatory adaptation.
• Pulsatile umbilical vein: Very late sign of severe fetal compromise, but DV abnormalities are the most reliable predictor of acidemia before this stage.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A G2P1 woman is suspected to have absent Nitabuch membrane. Which ultrasound finding most supports this diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Placental vascular lacunae

Absence or deficiency of the Nitabuch membrane leads to abnormal placental adherence disorders collectively called the placenta accreta spectrum (PAS):

• Placenta accreta
• Placenta increta
• Placenta percreta

Defective decidua basalis allows chorionic villi to invade abnormally into the myometrium. Characteristic ultrasound finding:

• Placental vascular lacunae (“Swiss cheese” appearance)
• Other findings:

• Loss of retroplacental clear zone
• Thinning of myometrium
• Increased Doppler vascularity

Risk factors:

• Previous cesarean section
• Placenta previa
• Prior uterine surgery/curettage

Why other options are incorrect:

• Snowstorm appearance → hydatidiform mole
• Ring of fire appearance → ectopic pregnancy/corpus luteum on Doppler
• Retroplacental clots → placental abruption

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A gynecologist is performing a hysterectomy. She accidentally nicks the ureter in the ureteric canal as it pierces the Mackenrodt's ligament. Which vessels are likely to be damaged here?
options: Uterine artery above and uterine plexus of veins below
Uterine plexus of veins above and uterine artery below
Ovarian artery above and uterine artery below
Uterine artery above and ovarian artery below
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Uterine artery above and uterine plexus of veins below

Anatomical Basis

The ureter runs through the ureteric canal (tunnel in the base of Mackenrodt's/cardinal ligament) in a precise relationship:

Uterine ARTERY → crosses ABOVE the ureter ("water under the bridge")
─────────────────────────────────────────
URETER → passes through ureteric canal
─────────────────────────────────────────
Uterine venous → lies BELOW the ureter
PLEXUS

The Classic Mnemonic

"Water (ureter) under the bridge (uterine artery)"

The artery crosses superior to the ureter \~1.5 cm lateral to the cervix at the base of the broad ligament.

The uterine venous plexus drains inferiorly and lies below the ureter in the same canal.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A gynecology professor asks students to identify agents used in emergency contraception. Which of the following is incorrectly listed as an emergency contraceptive?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Mirena (Levonorgestrel IUS)

Emergency contraception (EC) is used to prevent pregnancy after unprotected intercourse or contraceptive failure. It works primarily by delaying or inhibiting ovulation and must be used within a specified time window.

Approved Methods of Emergency Contraception

• Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg single dose

• Effective up to 72 hours (can be used up to 120 hours with reduced efficacy)

• Ulipristal acetate 30 mg

• Effective up to 120 hours (5 days) after unprotected intercourse

• Copper-T IUCD

• Most effective form of emergency contraception
• Can be inserted within 5 days of unprotected intercourse
• Also provides long-term contraception

Mirena (Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system, LNG-IUS) is not an approved emergency contraceptive.

• It is designed for long-term contraception, treatment of heavy menstrual bleeding, and endometrial protection.
• Unlike the Copper-T IUCD, it is not used for postcoital emergency contraception.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A health worker uses the GATHER technique during a family planning counseling session. After greeting the client, she immediately starts telling her about contraceptive options. A supervisor notes an error. The step being skipped is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Ask

• GATHER = Greet → Ask → Tell → Help → Educate → Review.
• After Greet = must Ask (understand client's needs/concerns) before Telling.
• Worker skipped Ask and went straight to Tell → missing the assessment step.
• Cafeteria approach = contraceptive choice based on client needs — also violated if Ask is skipped.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A lady was discharged after a normal vaginal delivery. On the third day she came back with fever, tachycardia and seizures. Fundus showed papilledema with no focal deficits. Diagnosis is?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Cortical vein thrombosis

• The given clinical situation likely suggests Cortical Vein Thrombosis.
• Cortical Vein thrombosis

o Risk factors:

• Pregnancy and puerperium
• Oral contraceptives
• Pro thrombotic conditions

o Clinical presentation

• Highly variable
• Headache is the most common symptom.
• With or without
• Vomiting
• Papilledema
• Focal deficits

o Investigation

• Brain MRI with MR venography - most sensitive
• CT - normal in 30 % of cases.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A multiparous woman is in labor at 38 weeks of gestation. On examination, the uterus appears asymmetrical. In fundal grip, the fetal pole is not palpable, and on pelvic grip, the lower pole of the uterus is empty. All of the following are true about the given presentation except:
options: Placenta previa should be ruled out
Uterine diadelphys is likely in the patient
There are high chances of cord prolapse in the patient
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Uterine diadelphys is likely in the patient

The findings of asymmetrical uterus, empty lower pole on pelvic grip, and inability to palpate the fetal pole on fundal grip suggest an oblique/transverse lie.

Key points about transverse/oblique lie:

•

Lower uterine segment is empty because no fetal presenting part occupies the pelvis.

•

Cord prolapse risk is high since the presenting part does not occlude the cervix.

•

Placenta previa should be ruled out because it can cause abnormal lie.

•

Delivery is usually by cesarean section if the lie persists in labor.

Incorrect statement: Uterus didelphys is likely — uterine malformations are not the typical cause of this presentation.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A newborn is born with ambiguous genitalia. Gonads are not palpable. What is the most common cause?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH)

A newborn with ambiguous genitalia and non-palpable gonads is most likely to have 46,XX Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH), most commonly due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency. In these infants, the ovaries are intra-abdominal and therefore not palpable, while excess adrenal androgens cause virilization of the external genitalia. In contrast, palpable gonads strongly suggest a 46,XY disorder of sex development (DSD) because ovaries do not descend into the labioscrotal folds. Among these, partial androgen insensitivity syndrome (PAIS) is the commonest cause of ambiguous genitalia with palpable testes. Early diagnosis of CAH is crucial because the salt-wasting form can present with life-threatening adrenal crisis during the first 1–2 weeks of life.

| Ambiguous genitalia | Most likely diagnosis

| ------------------- | ---------------------

| Non-palpable gonads | 46,XX CAH (21-hydroxylase deficiency)

| Palpable gonads | 46,XY DSD (most commonly Partial Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A patient has a suspected submucosal fibroid. Which investigation is the IOC for submucosal fibroid specifically?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Saline Infusion Sonography (SIS)

Transvaginal ultrasonography (TVS) is the initial investigation of choice for uterine fibroids. However, when a submucosal fibroid is suspected, Saline Infusion Sonography (SIS) is the investigation of choice, as instillation of sterile saline distends the endometrial cavity and clearly delineates intracavitary lesions. SIS has excellent sensitivity for detecting and characterizing submucosal fibroids and endometrial polyps, and helps plan hysteroscopic surgery. Hysteroscopy remains the gold standard diagnostic and therapeutic procedure, allowing direct visualization and simultaneous resection, whereas MRI is reserved for large, multiple, atypical fibroids or preoperative mapping, not routine diagnosis.

• IOC for uterine fibroid: TVS
• IOC for submucosal fibroid: Saline Infusion Sonography (SIS)
• Gold standard for diagnosis and treatment: Hysteroscopy
• MRI pelvis: Reserved for complex cases, large fibroids, adenomyosis differentiation, or preoperative planning.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A patient undergoing IVF develops OHSS. Which drug prevents OHSS by decreasing VEGF?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Cabergoline

Ovarian Hyperstimulation Syndrome (OHSS) is a potentially life-threatening complication of controlled ovarian stimulation during IVF. It results from human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)-induced overproduction of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) by granulosa cells, leading to increased vascular permeability, third-space fluid loss, ascites, pleural effusion, and hemoconcentration. Cabergoline, a dopamine D2 receptor agonist, is the drug of choice for OHSS prevention because it inhibits VEGF receptor-2 (VEGFR-2) phosphorylation, thereby reducing vascular permeability without significantly affecting implantation or pregnancy rates. Metformin reduces OHSS risk mainly in women with PCOS, but cabergoline is the specific anti-VEGF therapy.

High-Yield

• Mediator of OHSS: VEGF
• Drug preventing OHSS: Cabergoline (D2 agonist)
• Mechanism: ↓ VEGFR-2 activation → ↓ Vascular permeability
• Risk factors: PCOS, high AMH, multiple follicles, high estradiol levels, hCG trigger
• Severe OHSS: Ascites, pleural effusion, hemoconcentration, thromboembolism

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A patient with 6 weeks amenorrhea and a positive pregnancy test presents with lower abdominal pain and moderate per vaginam bleeding. She is hemodynamically stable. Transvaginal ultrasound shows no gestational sac in the uterus. The ovaries are normal, and there is no free fluid in the pouch of Douglas. What is the next best step in management?
options: Declare as complete abortion and follow up after 15 days
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Follow-up with serial B-hCG levels

When a patient has a positive pregnancy test but no intrauterine gestational sac on transvaginal ultrasound, the condition is termed pregnancy of unknown location (PUL).

• If the patient is hemodynamically stable and there are no signs of ectopic rupture, the best approach is serial quantitative β-hCG monitoring.

Rationale:

• In a normal early intrauterine pregnancy, β-hCG levels approximately double every 48 hours.
• Failure of appropriate rise or plateauing levels may suggest ectopic pregnancy or early pregnancy loss.
• Once β-hCG reaches the discriminatory level (\~1500–2000 mIU/mL), an intrauterine gestational sac should be visible on transvaginal ultrasound.

Why other options are incorrect:

• Methotrexate: used only after ectopic pregnancy is confirmed or strongly suspected.
• Diagnostic laparoscopy: reserved for hemodynamically unstable patients or confirmed ectopic pregnancy.
• Declaring complete abortion: premature without confirming the pregnancy location.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A patient with uterine inversion is taken for laparotomy after failed manual methods. On traction on the round ligaments, the inverted fundus begins to rise through the cervical ring and the uterus is restored without incising the ring. What is the indicated operative method called as?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Huntington method

In uterine inversion refractory to manual replacement, operative correction can be performed at laparotomy. If the surgeon applies upward traction on the round ligaments or the inverted uterine fundus using clamps, gradually “walking” the uterus back through the cervical ring without incising the constriction ring, this is the Huntington procedure. The stem explicitly states that the uterus is restored without incising the ring, which distinguishes Huntington from Haultain.

● Huntington method: laparotomy, identify the cup-shaped inversion, apply traction on round ligaments or fundus, progressively elevating the uterus through the ring without cutting the ring.

●  Haultain method: used when the cervical ring is tight and replacement fails. It involves posterior incision of the constriction ring to allow reposition.

Other options:

B. Haultain method

Incorrect here because Haultain requires incision of the constriction ring (usually posterior). The stem states no incision was needed.

C. B-Lynch suture

Used for uterine atony causing postpartum hemorrhage as a uterine compression suture, not for inversion reduction.

D. Hayman suture

Another uterine compression suture for atonic postpartum hemorrhage, not a method for inversion correction.

Huntington procedure:

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman at 35 weeks with BP 170/110 mmHg and 3+ proteinuria develops seizures. What is the most appropriate immediate step?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Secure airway

This patient has eclampsia (new-onset generalized seizures in a woman with severe preeclampsia).

In any actively seizing patient, the immediate priority is:

1. Airway
2. Breathing
3. Circulation (ABC approach)

Therefore, the first step is to:

• Secure the airway
• Place the patient in left lateral position
• Prevent aspiration and maintain oxygenation

After stabilization:

• Administer magnesium sulfate (drug of choice for seizure control/prevention)
• Control severe hypertension (eg, IV labetalol, hydralazine)
• Plan definitive delivery after maternal stabilization

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman at 8 weeks gestation whose previous child had 21-hydroxylase deficiency CAH is given dexamethasone. The rationale for this intervention and its timing is:
options: Given at 24–34 weeks to mature fetal lungs
Given as early as 6–8 weeks to suppress fetal ACTH and reduce virilisation of female fetus Given only after CVS confirms CAH in fetus
Given only after CVS confirms CAH in fetus
Given to mother for 3 days at delivery to prevent adrenal crisis in the newborn
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Given as early as 6–8 weeks to suppress fetal ACTH and reduce virilisation of female fetus Given only after CVS confirms CAH in fetus

In pregnancies at risk for classical 21-hydroxylase deficiency congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH), maternal dexamethasone is started as early as 6–8 weeks of gestation, before external genital differentiation begins (≈9 weeks). Dexamethasone crosses the placenta and suppresses fetal ACTH secretion, thereby reducing adrenal androgen production and preventing virilization of an affected female fetus. Because fetal sex and genotype are not yet known at this stage, treatment is started empirically and continued only if prenatal testing confirms an affected female fetus; it is discontinued if the fetus is male or unaffected.

High-Yield

• Drug: Dexamethasone (crosses placenta; unlike prednisolone)
• Start: 6–8 weeks gestation (before genital differentiation)
• Mechanism: ↓ Fetal ACTH → ↓ Adrenal androgen production
• Continue only if: Affected female fetus confirmed by prenatal diagnosis
• Stop if: Male fetus or unaffected female fetus

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman in her 7th week of gestation was diagnosed with trichomoniasis. Which of the following can be used to treat her condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Oral metronidazole

Trichomoniasis is a sexually transmitted infection caused by Trichomonas vaginalis, a motile protozoan.

• Frothy yellow-green vaginal discharge
• Vaginal irritation/pruritus
• Strawberry cervix (punctate cervical hemorrhages)
• Elevated vaginal pH

Oral metronidazole is the treatment of choice, including during pregnancy

• Symptomatic pregnant women should be treated
• Metronidazole is considered safe in pregnancy
• Sexual partners must also be treated to prevent reinfection

Why other options are incorrect:

• Azithromycin → Chlamydia
• Clotrimazole → Candida infection
• Cotrimoxazole → not used for trichomoniasis

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman undergoes evaluation for possible fetal chromosomal abnormalities due to abnormal screening results. The clinician discusses various available diagnostic and screening modalities. Some of these methods provide fetal cells for direct chromosomal analysis, while others only estimate the risk of aneuploidy without providing definitive diagnosis. In this context, which of the following methods cannot be used for fetal karyotyping?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Fetal skin biopsy

Fetal karyotyping requires the collection of fetal cells capable of chromosomal analysis. Definitive prenatal diagnosis of chromosomal abnormalities is therefore possible only with procedures that obtain fetal or placental cells.

1. Chorionic Villus Sampling (CVS)

• Performed at 10–13 weeks
• Uses trophoblastic cells for chromosomal analysis

2. Amniocentesis

• Performed after 15 weeks
• Uses cultured fetal cells from amniotic fluid

3. Cordocentesis (PUBS)

• Performed after 18 weeks
• Uses fetal blood lymphocytes for rapid karyotyping

Fetal skin biopsy is not used for routine fetal karyotyping. Its primary indications are:

• Diagnosis of certain genetic skin disorders
• Epidermolysis bullosa
• Ichthyosis and other rare dermatological conditions

It is an invasive procedure and has largely been replaced by molecular genetic techniques.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman with a subserosal fibroid uterus develops severe acute abdominal pain at 28 weeks’ gestation. There is no history of fever, and the white blood cell count is 8,000 cells/µL. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Torsion of fibroid

Torsion of a pedunculated fibroid is a complication of uterine fibroids during pregnancy in which the fibroid twists around its vascular stalk, causing acute ischemia and severe abdominal pain. It should be suspected in a pregnant woman with:

• Known fibroid uterus / Sudden severe abdominal pain
• No fever / Normal or mildly elevated WBC count / Signs of acute abdomen

A subserosal pedunculated fibroid may twist around its vascular pedicle, leading to:

• Venous obstruction
• Ischemia
• Severe abdominal pain

Why Other Options Are Incorrect:

• A. Red degeneration of fibroid: Usually presents with pain, low-grade fever, and leukocytosis due to hemorrhagic infarction.
• B. Preterm labor: Characterised by uterine contractions with cervical changes, not isolated severe abdominal pain.
• D. PID: Rare in pregnancy and typically presents with fever, leukocytosis, and pelvic infection signs.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A primigravida at 38 completed weeks of gestation develops primary postpartum hemorrhage ( PPH ) due to uterine atony. The second messenger system through which the first pharmacological agent of choice act is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Phospholipase C

The first-line pharmacological agent for primary postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) due to uterine atony is oxytocin.

Mechanism of action of oxytocin:

• Oxytocin binds to Gq protein–coupled oxytocin receptors on uterine smooth muscle.
• This activates phospholipase C (PLC).
• PLC increases IP₃ and DAG, leading to increased intracellular Ca²⁺.
• Increased calcium causes strong uterine contractions, helping control bleeding.

Second messenger pathway:

Oxytocin → Gq receptor → Phospholipase C → IP₃/DAG → ↑ Ca²⁺ → uterine contraction

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A primigravida came to the labor room at 40 weeks +5 days gestation for induction of labor. On per vaginal examination, the cervix is 1 cm dilated and 30% effaced. The vertex is at -1 station and the cervix is soft and posterior. What will be the modified Bishop score for this lady?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 5

The Modified Bishop score is used to assess cervical favorability before induction of labor and predicts the likelihood of successful vaginal delivery.

| Cervical Feature | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3

| ---------------- | --- | --- | --- | ---

| Cervical dilatation | ˂ 1cm | 1-2 cm | 3-4 cm | 5+cm

| Cervical length | 4 cm | 2-4 cm | 1-2 cm | ˂ 1 cm

| Effacement* | 30 | 40-50 | 60-70 | >80

| Station of presenting part | -3 cm | -2 cm | -1/0 cm | +1/+2 cm

| Consistency of the cervix | Firm | Average | Soft |

| Position of cervix | Posterior | Mid position | Anterior |

Scoring in this patient:

• Dilation: 1 cm → 1 point
• Effacement: 30% → 1 point
• Station: –1 → 2 points
• Consistency: Soft → 1 point
• Position: Posterior → 0 points

Total = 5

Interpretation:

• Score ≥6–8: Favorable cervix (successful induction likely)
• Score <6: Unfavorable cervix → cervical ripening needed (e.g., prostaglandins or Foley catheter)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A virgin female is investigated for genital TB. What specimen is used instead of endometrial biopsy?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Day 1 of menstrual blood

Female genital tuberculosis (FGTB) most commonly involves the fallopian tubes and endometrium and is an important cause of infertility. The investigation of choice is an endometrial biopsy obtained in the late secretory (premenstrual) phase, when granulomatous lesions are most likely to be detected. However, in virgin females, endometrial biopsy is generally avoided to preserve hymenal integrity. In such cases, Day 1 menstrual blood is collected for CBNAAT/GeneXpert, PCR, mycobacterial culture, or microscopy, as it contains shed endometrial tissue and provides a non-invasive alternative for diagnosis.

• IOC for genital TB: Premenstrual endometrial biopsy
• Virgin female: Day 1 menstrual blood for CBNAAT/PCR/culture
• Most commonly affected organ: Fallopian tube (\~95–100%)
• Most common presentation: Infertility (followed by menstrual disturbances and chronic pelvic pain)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A woman at 30 weeks gestation presents with calf pain and redness. DVT is diagnosed. Which drug should be used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. LMWH

Low Molecular Weight Heparin = drug of choice for DVT in pregnancy

• Does not cross placenta (too large)
• Safe for fetus at all gestational ages
• Predictable pharmacokinetics, no INR monitoring needed
• Used throughout pregnancy and for 6 weeks postpartum (minimum 3 months total)

Distractor Analysis

| Option | Crosses Placenta | Safe in Pregnancy | Why Wrong

| ------ | ---------------- | ----------------- | ---------

| A. LMWH | ❌ No | ✅ YES — DOC | Correct

| B. Warfarin | ✅ Yes | ❌ NO | Teratogenic (6–12 weeks) → warfarin embryopathy; fetal hemorrhage later
Not used without LMWH bridging anyways

| C. Fondaparinux | ❌ Minimal | Limited data | Not first-line; used only if LMWH contraindicated (HIT)

| D. Rivaroxaban | ✅ Yes | ❌ NO | DOACs contraindicated in pregnancy — teratogenic, fetal bleeding risk

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A woman presents to the emergency department with abdominal pain and fever. On examination, cervical motion tenderness and mucopurulent vaginal discharge are noted. Which of the following investigations will you undertake to establish the diagnosis of pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), according to CDC criteria? 1. Laparoscopy 2. MRI 3. Biopsy and histopathological examination 4. Blood tests for ESR and CRP
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 1, 2, 3, 4

Pelvic inflammatory disease is usually diagnosed clinically, but laparoscopy provides definitive confirmation.

• Other investigations just help in supportive diagnosis, but are not confirmatory.
• Early diagnosis is important to prevent infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

Laparoscopy: Considered the gold standard

• Allows direct visualization of inflamed fallopian tubes, purulent exudate or pelvic adhesions)
• Confirms PID beyond doubt. Hence, definitive

MRI:

• Helpful for complications (e.g., tubo-ovarian abscess) not diagnostic for PID itself.

Biopsy and histopathological examination:

• Endometrial biopsy can show endometritis
• Supports diagnosis but not definitive for PID

Blood tests (ESR, CRP):

• Indicate inflammation, Nonspecific, cannot confirm PID

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A woman, G3P2L0, presents with 9 weeks of amenorrhea. She has a history of cervical conization performed one year ago and is currently on follow-up, with no recurrence on Pap smear. What is the most appropriate management in this pregnancy?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Ultrasound to assess cervical length

Women with a history of cervical surgery (e.g., cervical conization /LEEP) are at increased risk of cervical insufficiency and preterm birth; but prophylactic cerclage is not routinely recommended unless there is a history of second-trimester loss or documented cervical shortening.

Recommended management:

• Perform transvaginal ultrasound surveillance of cervical length during pregnancy (usually from 16–24 weeks).
• Cerclage is considered only if cervical length <25 mm or if there is a history of recurrent mid-trimester losses.

Why other options are incorrect:

• Cervical cerclage: not done prophylactically without evidence of cervical shortening or prior losses.
• Bed rest: not proven to prevent preterm birth.
• Abdominal cerclage: reserved for severe cervical insufficiency or failed prior vaginal cerclage.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: According to ACOG recommendations, low-dose aspirin prophylaxis is advised in high-risk pregnant women for prevention of preeclampsia. All of the following are indications for low-dose aspirin prophylaxis except:
options: Gestational diabetes mellitus diagnosed at 30 weeks
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Gestational diabetes mellitus diagnosed at 30 weeks

Low-dose aspirin (75–150 mg/day) is recommended in:

• APLA syndrome
• Chronic hypertension
• Multifetal pregnancy
• Kidney disease
• Pregestational diabetes mellitus

Timing

• Start early, ideally between 12–16 weeks
• Should be initiated at or before 16 weeks
• Continued till 36 weeks

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: According to Hellin’s rule, if the incidence of twins in a population is 1 in 80 pregnancies, the approximate incidence of quadruplets will be:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1 in 80³ pregnancies

Hellin’s Rule

If Twin incidence = 1 in 80

Then,

| Pregnancy | Incidence

| --------- | ---------

| Twins | 1 in 80

| Triplets | 1 in 80²

| Quadruplets | 1 in 80³

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: After a traumatic delivery, a Kleihauer–Betke test is performed to calculate the Anti-D dose. Which statement is most accurate regarding standard Anti-D coverage?
options: 300 mcg Anti-D neutralizes 30 mL fetomaternal hemorrhage
300 mcg Anti-D neutralizes 3 mL fetomaternal hemorrhage
150 mcg Anti-D neutralizes 30 mL fetomaternal hemorrhage
Anti-D dose does not depend on FMH volume
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 300 mcg Anti-D neutralizes 30 mL fetomaternal hemorrhage

After potential fetomaternal hemorrhage, Anti-D dose is based on the volume of fetal red cells entering maternal circulation.

• Anti-D dosing depends on FMH volume when hemorrhage is large.
• 300 micrograms (1500 IU) cover 30 mL fetal whole blood or 15 mL fetal RBCs.
• 50 micrograms (where used) cover smaller early gestation FMH volumes, while 300 micrograms is the standard postpartum dose in many protocols.
• Kleihauer–Betke identifies fetal HbF-containing cells. Adult HbF elevation can cause false positives, and flow cytometry is more accurate when available.
• Anti-D is ideally given within 72 hours but can still be beneficial later in some scenarios.

Other options

B. 300 mcg neutralizes 3 mL

Incorrect. This underestimates the protective capacity by 10-fold.

C. 150 mcg neutralizes 30 mL

Incorrect. 150 micrograms covers about 15 mL fetal whole blood (or roughly 7.5 mL fetal RBCs), not 30 mL.

D. Anti-D dose does not depend on FMH volume

Incorrect. Standard postpartum dosing is fixed for routine cases, but additional Anti-D is required when FMH exceeds standard coverage.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All are true about dysgerminoma except:
options: LDH is the most important tumor marker
hCG may be elevated in some cases
AFP is typically elevated in dysgerminoma
Dysgerminoma is associated with dysgenetic gonads
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. AFP is typically elevated in dysgerminoma

The most common malignant germ cell tumor of the ovary, accounting for \~50% of all malignant GCTs. It is the ovarian counterpart of testicular seminoma.

Analyzing Each Option

| Statement | True/False | Explanation

| --------- | ---------- | -----------

| A. LDH is most important tumor marker | ✅ TRUE | LDH (especially LDH-1 isoform) is the primary marker for dysgerminoma — used for diagnosis AND monitoring

| B. hCG may be elevated | ✅ TRUE | Syncytiotrophoblastic giant cells within the tumor can secrete hCG in \~5% of cases

| C. AFP is typically elevated | ❌ FALSE ✔ | AFP is NOT elevated in dysgerminoma — this is the exception answer

| D. Associated with dysgenetic gonads | ✅ TRUE | Strong association with 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis (Swyer syndrome) and Turner mosaics

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All are true about Sayana Press except:
options: It contains 104 mg DMPA given subcutaneously via a Uniject self-injectable, auto-disable device
It is injected intramuscularly into the gluteus or deltoid, like the conventional Antara injection
It provides 3 months of contraceptive protection and can be self-administered after brief training
For a missed dose with unprotected intercourse in the past 5 days, levonorgestrel is preferred and ulipristal acetate is avoided
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. It is injected intramuscularly into the gluteus or deltoid, like the conventional Antara injection

None

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All are true except:
options: Emergency contraception can be used in the postpartum period
Postpartum IUCD insertion can be done up to 48 hours after delivery
Laparoscopic tubal ligation is contraindicated in the immediate postpartum period
Interval sterilization is performed after 2 weeks postpartum
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Interval sterilization is performed after 2 weeks postpartum

Postpartum contraception should be individualized based on breastfeeding status, timing after delivery, and future fertility desires.

• Emergency contraception can be used in the postpartum period if unprotected intercourse occurs.
• Postpartum IUCD (PPIUCD) can be inserted:

• Within 10 minutes of placental delivery
• During cesarean section
• Up to 48 hours postpartum

• Laparoscopic sterilization is generally avoided in the immediate postpartum period because the enlarged uterus makes the procedure technically difficult; minilaparotomy is preferred.

Interval sterilization is not performed after 2 weeks postpartum.

• Interval sterilization is usually performed ≥6 weeks after delivery, when the uterus has involuted and pelvic anatomy has returned to normal.
• The period between 48 hours and 6 weeks postpartum is generally avoided for elective sterilization procedures.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All are true regarding congenital malformations in infants of diabetic mothers except:
options: Most commonly involved system is cardiovascular system
Most common congenital anomaly is ventricular septal defect
Most specific anomaly is caudal regression syndrome
Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy is irreversible after delivery
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy is irreversible after delivery

Maternal pregestational diabetes, especially when poorly controlled during organogenesis, significantly increases the risk of major congenital malformations in the fetus.

Congenital Malformations in Infants of Diabetic Mothers

• Cardiovascular system is the most commonly affected system.
• Common cardiac defects include:

• Ventricular septal defect (VSD) (most common)
• Transposition of great arteries
• Tetralogy of Fallot

Caudal regression syndrome (sacral agenesis) is the anomaly most strongly associated with maternal diabetes and is considered virtually pathognomonic.

Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) is not irreversible.

• It results from fetal hyperinsulinemia causing myocardial hypertrophy, particularly of the interventricular septum.
• Most cases improve spontaneously after birth as insulin levels normalize.
• Cardiac hypertrophy usually regresses within the first few months of life.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All of the following are diagnostic criteria for pregestational diabetes in pregnancy except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 2-hour postprandial glucose ≥140 mg/dL

Pregestational (overt) diabetes in pregnancy refers to diabetes that is present before pregnancy or first recognized during pregnancy using standard diagnostic criteria for diabetes in nonpregnant adults.

Any one of the following is diagnostic:

• Fasting plasma glucose ≥126 mg/dL
• Random plasma glucose ≥200 mg/dL (with classic symptoms)
• HbA1c ≥6.5%
• 2-hour plasma glucose ≥200 mg/dL during a 75-g OGTT

2-hour postprandial glucose ≥140 mg/dL is not a diagnostic criterion for overt (pregestational) diabetes.

• A value of 140 mg/dL is used in the screening/diagnosis of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) in certain protocols.
• Overt diabetes requires significantly higher glucose thresholds.

Identifying overt diabetes is important because it is associated with:

• Congenital malformations
• Miscarriage
• Preeclampsia
• Macrosomia
• Stillbirth

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All of the following are features of fetal alcohol syndrome, except:
options: Smooth philtrum with thin vermilion border
Neural tube defect due to folate antagonism
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Neural tube defect due to folate antagonism

Fetal Alcohol Syndrome (FAS) is the most severe manifestation of prenatal alcohol exposure and is a leading preventable cause of neurodevelopmental disability.

1. Growth Abnormalities

• Prenatal and postnatal growth restriction
• Low birth weight
• Failure to thrive

2. Craniofacial Features

• Microcephaly
• Smooth/flattened philtrum
• Thin upper vermilion border
• Short palpebral fissures
• Midface hypoplasia

3. CNS Abnormalities

• Intellectual disability
• Learning difficulties
• Behavioral problems
• Developmental delay

Neural tube defects due to folate antagonism are not a feature of fetal alcohol syndrome. Neural tube defects are classically associated with:

• Folate deficiency
• Antiepileptic drugs (especially valproate)
• Folate antagonist medications

Alcohol causes neurodevelopmental injury through direct teratogenic effects rather than folate antagonism.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All of the following are included in high-risk pregnancy under Government of India guidelines except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Maternal age >30 years

A high-risk pregnancy is one in which the mother, fetus, or newborn has an increased risk of morbidity or mortality and therefore requires special monitoring and management under Government of India antenatal care guidelines.

Conditions considered high-risk:

Examples include:

• Previous cesarean section (LSCS) → increased risk of uterine rupture, placenta previa, placenta accreta

• Low-lying placenta / placenta previa → risk of antepartum hemorrhage

• Maternal infections such as syphilis → risk of congenital infection, stillbirth, neonatal complications

These conditions require closer antenatal surveillance and institutional delivery.

Not considered high-risk in GOI criteria:

• Maternal age >30 years alone is not categorized as high-risk under Government of India guidelines.

• However, extreme maternal ages (e.g., <18 years or >35 years) are generally considered higher risk in obstetrics literature.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All of the following are physiological cardiovascular changes seen in normal pregnancy except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Increased pulmonary capillary wedge pressure

Physiological cardiovascular changes in pregnancy

| Increased | Decreased | Remain same

| --------- | --------- | -----------

| Cardiac output | Peripheral vascular resistance | JVP

| Stroke volume | Systolic BP | Left ventricular ejection fraction

| Heart rate | Diastolic BP | Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure

| Femoral venous pressure | MAP | —

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All of the following are true regarding vaccination in pregnancy, except:
options: Vaccines that contain toxoids may be administered during pregnancy
The hepatitis B vaccine series may be administered during pregnancy
Receiving the varicella vaccine is an indication for pregnancy termination
Conception should be delayed by 1 month after receiving the rubella vaccine
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Receiving the varicella vaccine is an indication for pregnancy termination

Vaccination during pregnancy depends on whether the vaccine is live attenuated or inactivated. Vaccines Safe in Pregnancy:

•

Inactivated vaccines and toxoids are safe during pregnancy.

•

Examples:

- Tetanus toxoid (Td/Tdap)

- Hepatitis B vaccine

- Influenza (inactivated)

Therefore:

•

Vaccines containing toxoids can be given in pregnancy.

•

Hepatitis B vaccination can be safely administered during pregnancy.

Live vaccines are generally contraindicated during pregnancy due to a theoretical risk of fetal infection. Examples:

•

Rubella vaccine

•

Varicella vaccine

•

MMR vaccine

Women are advised to avoid conception for 1 month after receiving rubella or varicella vaccines.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All of the following can be used to evaluate the cervical factor in infertility EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. HSG

Cervical factor infertility occurs when abnormalities in cervical mucus or cervical anatomy --> interfere with sperm transport through the cervix.

Tests used to evaluate cervical factor:

• Huhner test (Postcoital test) → evaluates interaction between sperm and cervical mucus after intercourse during ovulation
• Postcoital test → assesses sperm motility and survival in cervical mucus
• Sims test → evaluates sperm penetration through cervical mucus

These tests help determine whether cervical mucus is hostile to sperm.

Test not used for cervical factor:

•

Hysterosalpingography (HSG) ; it evaluates:-

•

Uterine cavity abnormalities

• Tubal patency

It does not assess cervical mucus or sperm–cervical interaction--> so it is not used to evaluate cervical factor infertility.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All of the following findings indicate uterine scar rupture, except:
options: Loss of station of presenting part
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Maternal bradycardia

Uterine rupture is a life-threatening obstetric emergency, most commonly occurring in women with a previous uterine scar undergoing labor.

• Fetal bradycardia (earliest and most common sign)
• Sudden abdominal pain
• Vaginal bleeding
• Loss of uterine contractions
• Loss of station of the presenting part
• Maternal tachycardia and hypotension due to hemorrhage
• Easily palpable fetal parts abdominally

Maternal bradycardia is not a feature of uterine rupture.

• Maternal hemorrhage causes tachycardia, followed by hypotension and shock.
• Bradycardia is not an expected clinical finding.

Why Other Options Are Correct?

• Fetal bradycardia: Most sensitive early sign of scar rupture.
• Past history of classical cesarean section: Major risk factor for uterine rupture.
• Loss of station of presenting part: Occurs when the fetus escapes partially or completely through the uterine defect.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All of the following management plans are correct except:
options: Pregnant woman with history of three second-trimester abortions → Cervical cerclage + progesterone
Pregnant woman with history of two second-trimester abortions and cervical length ≤2.5 cm on TVS → Cervical cerclage + progesterone
Pregnant woman with history of one PTL/second-trimester abortion and cervical length ≤2.5 cm → Only progesterone
Pregnant woman with no history of abortion but cervical length <2.5 cm → Only progesterone
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Pregnant woman with history of one PTL/second-trimester abortion and cervical length ≤2.5 cm → Only progesterone

Prevention of recurrent preterm birth (PTL) and cervical insufficiency is based on a combination of obstetric history and transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) cervical length.

| Clinical Scenario | Management

| ----------------- | ----------

| ≥3 previous second-trimester losses/preterm births | History-indicated cerclage + progesterone

| ≥2 second-trimester losses with cervical length ≤2.5 cm | Cerclage + progesterone

| Previous PTL/second-trimester loss with cervical length ≤2.5 cm | Cerclage + progesterone

| No prior PTL/loss but cervical length <2.5 cm | Progesterone alone

A woman with:

• Previous preterm labor or second-trimester loss, and
• Short cervix (≤2.5 cm)

is at high risk for recurrent preterm birth and generally requires both cervical cerclage and progesterone, not progesterone alone.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All of the following statements are true except:
options: The shortest anteroposterior ( AP ) diameter of the pelvic inlet is the obstetric conjugate
The diagonal conjugate is measured from tip of the sacral promontory to the lower margin of the pubic symphysis
The obstetric conjugate is calculated by subtracting 1.5 cm from the diagonal conjugate
A contracted pelvis is defined as s transverse diameter <10cm and an AP diameter <12cm
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. A contracted pelvis is defined as s transverse diameter <10cm and an AP diameter <12cm

Pelvic adequacy is assessed using multiple pelvic diameters and overall obstetric assessment. Although the obstetric conjugate is important, a contracted pelvis cannot be defined by a single measurement alone. Clinical pelvimetry and labor outcome are also essential considerations.

A) True — The obstetric conjugate is the shortest AP diameter of the pelvic inlet.

B) True — Diagonal conjugate is measured from the sacral promontory to the lower margin of the pubic symphysis on per vaginum exam.

C) True — Obstetric conjugate ≈ diagonal conjugate − 1.5 cm.

D)  False — A contracted pelvis is defined when any pelvic diameter is reduced below normal size

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: An 18-year-old woman comes to the OPD with primary amenorrhea. Ambignuous external genitalia were noted at birth, and a laparotomy performed at 17 months of age revealed a normal uterus and fallopian tubes. An ovarian biopsy at that time shows normal-appearing primordial follicles. Her blood pressure is 120/78 mm Hg, and height is 160 cm (5 ft 3 in). She has nodulocystic acne over the chest and back. There is no breast development, normal pubic and axillary hair, and marked clitoromegaly. Laboratory investigations reveal a normal female karyotype ( 46,XX ), normal glucose, and normal serum electrolytes. Serum FSH, LH, testosterone, and androstenedione levels are elevated. Pelvic imaging shows multiple ovarian cysts. Which of the following is the most likely?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Aromatase deficiency

Aromatase deficiency is a rare disorder in which the enzyme aromatase (which converts androgens to estrogens) is deficient.

Clinical features:

• Primary amenorrhea
• Ambiguous genitalia or clitoromegaly
• No breast development due to lack of estrogen
• Normal uterus and ovaries
• Normal pubic/axillary hair because androgens are present
• Elevated FSH and LH due to lack of estrogen feedback
• Ovarian cysts due to gonadotropin stimulation
• Severe acne from androgen excess

Differentiation from other conditions:

• CAH: electrolyte abnormalities and adrenal androgen excess
• Kallmann syndrome: low FSH/LH with anosmia
• Swyer syndrome: 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis with streak gonads

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Anti-D immunoglobulin is not given in which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Intrauterine transfusion at 28 weeks

Anti-D immunoglobulin is administered to Rh-negative, unsensitized pregnant women to prevent Rh isoimmunization by neutralizing Rh-positive fetal red blood cells that enter maternal circulation.

Indications for Anti-D prophylaxis include any event causing fetomaternal hemorrhage, such as:

• Amniocentesis or chorionic villus sampling

• Abortion/MTP (including early pregnancy termination)

• Manual removal of placenta

• Antepartum hemorrhage, abdominal trauma, external cephalic version

• Routine antenatal prophylaxis at 28 weeks and post-delivery if baby is Rh-positive

However, Anti-D is NOT given after intrauterine transfusion (IUT) because:

• The fetus is already Rh-sensitized and being treated for hemolytic disease of the fetus/newborn (HDFN).

• Anti-D prophylaxis is preventive, not therapeutic.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Arrange the following antenatal investigations in chronological order: 1. MSAFP, E3, HCG, Inhibin-A 2. TIFA scan 3. Growth-Liquor scan 4. NT-NB
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 4-1-2-3

Antenatal screening investigations are performed at specific gestational ages to assess chromosomal abnormalities, fetal anatomy, and fetal growth.

Chronological order:

1. NT–NB scan (Nuchal translucency & nasal bone)

·         11–13+6 weeks

·         Screening for chromosomal anomalies (e.g., Down syndrome)

2. Quadruple marker test (MSAFP\, β-hCG\, estriol\, inhibin-A)

·         15–20 weeks

·         Screening for chromosomal abnormalities and neural tube defects

3. TIFA scan (Targeted Imaging for Fetal Anomalies)

·         18–22 weeks

·         Detailed anomaly scan

4. Growth–Liquor scan

·         Third trimester (\~28–34 weeks)

·         Assess fetal growth and amniotic fluid volume

Correct order: NT–NB → Quadruple test → TIFA → Growth-Liquor scan (4-1-2-3)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Arrange the following sites of endometriosis in decreasing order of frequency of involvement: 1. Pouch of Douglas 2. Uterosacral ligament 3. Broad ligament 4. Ovary 5. Fallopian tube
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 4 > 1 > 3 > 2 > 5

Endometriosis most commonly involves pelvic organs and peritoneal surfaces, particularly areas where retrograde menstruation implants endometrial tissue.

Decreasing Order of Frequency:

1. Ovary (most common)
2. Pouch of Douglas
3. Broad ligament
4. Uterosacral ligament
5. Fallopian tube

The ovary is the most frequent site due to formation of endometriomas (“chocolate cysts”).

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: As a senior resident in the OBG department, you would consider uterine artery embolization (UAE) as a treatment option in all of the following cases except:
options: Prior to the removal of Placenta accreta in Multiparous woman
Patient diagnosed with calcified and pedunculated submucous fibroids
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Patient diagnosed with calcified and pedunculated submucous fibroids

Uterine artery embolization (UAE) is a minimally invasive procedure in which embolic agents are injected into the uterine arteries to block blood supply, causing ischemia and shrinkage of uterine pathology.

UAE is used in the management of:

• Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) when bleeding is not controlled by medical or surgical methods
• Placenta accreta spectrum (as a preoperative measure to reduce blood loss)
• Symptomatic uterine fibroids causing menorrhagia or bulk symptoms, especially in women who have completed childbearing

Pedunculated submucous fibroids, particularly if calcified, are not suitable for UAE because:

• These fibroids have a narrow stalk
• Embolization can cause ischemic necrosis and detachment
• This may lead to fibroid expulsion, infection, or sepsis

Such fibroids are better treated with hysteroscopic removal (myomectomy).

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Choose the correct order of the following steps performed during a total abdominal hysterectomy: A) Clamp, cut, and ligate the infundibulopelvic ligament B) Clamp, cut, and ligate uterine vessels C) Clamp, cut, and ligate the round ligament D) Open the uterovesical fold of the peritoneum
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. c-a-d-b

In a total abdominal hysterectomy (TAH), pedicles are sequentially clamped, cut, and ligated to safely mobilize the uterus while protecting nearby structures (especially the ureter and bladder).

Correct sequence:

1. Round ligament → opened first to access the broad ligament
2. Infundibulopelvic ligament (ovarian vessels) → ligated if ovaries are removed
3. Uterovesical peritoneal fold opened → bladder reflected downward
4. Uterine vessels ligated → done near the cervix after bladder mobilization

Order:

Round ligament → Infundibulopelvic ligament → Uterovesical fold → Uterine vessels

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Comparing CuT-380A and Cu-375, all are correctly matched except:
options: CuT-380A thread = polyethylene; Cu-375 = monofilament nylon
CuT-380A insertion = difficult with higher expulsion; Cu-375 = easy with better attachment
Cu-375 requires plunger rod for insertion; CuT-380A does not
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Cu-375 requires plunger rod for insertion; CuT-380A does not

• Exactly reversed.
• CuT-380A needs plunger rod; Cu-375 does NOT need plunger rod (user-friendly design).
• Cu-375 shape = inverted U; CuT-380A = T-shaped.
• Copper in CuT-380A = on arms too; Cu-375 = only on stem.

| Feature | CuT-380A | Cu-375

| ------- | -------- | ------

| Shape | T-shaped | Inverted U

| Lifespan | 10 years | 3–5 years

| Copper location | Arms + stem | Stem only

| Insertion | Difficult, ↑ bleeding, ↑ expulsion | Easy, better attachment

| Thread | Polyethylene | Monofilament nylon

| Plunger rod | Needed | Not needed

| Govt. use | CuT-380 + Cu-375 both used | used

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: During early embryonic development, an important milestone is reached when cardiac activity begins and fetoplacental circulation is established. On which day does the fetal heart start beating?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Day 21

The fetal cardiovascular system is the first functional organ system to develop during embryogenesis, ensuring early delivery of oxygen and nutrients to the rapidly growing embryo.

Cardiac Development Timeline

• Day 18: Formation of the cardiogenic area and primitive heart tube
• Day 21–22: Primitive heart begins to beat and blood circulation starts
• Day 28: Heart tube undergoes looping and further chamber development

Clinical Importance

• Cardiac activity begins at approximately 3 weeks after fertilization
• Fetal cardiac motion can usually be detected by:

• Transvaginal ultrasound: 5.5–6 weeks gestation
• Transabdominal ultrasound: 6–7 weeks gestation

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: During pregnancy, which of the following parameters increases?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Total oxygen-carrying capacity of blood

During pregnancy, total oxygen-carrying capacity of blood increases due to a rise in maternal red blood cell (RBC) mass stimulated by increased erythropoietin production.

• Plasma volume: ↑ \~40–50%
• RBC mass: ↑ \~20–30%
• Because plasma volume increases more than RBC mass → physiological (dilutional) anemia of pregnancy occurs.
• Despite dilutional anemia, the overall oxygen-carrying capacity increases because the absolute RBC mass is higher.

Why other options are incorrect:

• Serum iron concentration: ↓ (due to increased fetal demand and expanded erythropoiesis)
• Serum ferritin: ↓ (reflects depleted maternal iron stores)
• Serum potassium: Usually unchanged or slightly decreased due to hemodilution.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: During suction evacuation, uterine perforation occurs with a Karman cannula. What is the next best step?
options: Stop procedure and do not remove cannula
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Stop procedure and do not remove cannula

Uterine perforation is a recognized complication of dilatation and curettage (D&C) or suction evacuation, especially in pregnant, postpartum, or scarred uteri.

• Sudden loss of resistance during instrumentation
• Instrument passing farther than expected
• Excessive bleeding
• Suspected injury to adjacent organs

If perforation occurs with a Karman cannula:

• Stop the procedure immediately
• Do not remove the cannula
• Leave the cannula in place to mark the perforation site
• Assess the extent of injury, often by laparoscopy/laparotomy if indicated

The cannula:

• Helps identify the site and direction of perforation
• Assists the surgeon during evaluation and repair
• Prevents loss of localization of the injury

Why Other Options Are Incorrect?

• Remove cannula immediately and observe: May obscure the perforation site and delay recognition of injury.
• Continue evacuation carefully: Risks worsening uterine and visceral injury.
• Start oxytocin infusion only: Does not address the perforation or possible visceral damage.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Fixative for PAP smear:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 95% ethyl alcohol

The most commonly used fixative for a Pap smear is 95% ethyl alcohol. This fixative preserves the cellular detail necessary for accurate cytological evaluation by preventing cellular autolysis and degradation. The use of 95% ethyl alcohol ensures that the cells maintain their morphology, which is critical for detecting abnormalities such as dysplasia or carcinoma.

• 95% Ethyl Alcohol: This is the standard fixative for Pap smears, ensuring optimal preservation of cellular details.
• Ethanol Spray: In modern practice, an ethanol spray fixative is available, which can be conveniently used in an office setting to fix the smear immediately after it is taken.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: For a given drug, animal reproduction studies have shown an adverse effect on the fetus, but there are no adequate and well-controlled studies on humans. However, potential benefits may warrant the use of the drug in pregnant women despite potential risks. Such a drug would be classified as
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Category C

The FDA pregnancy drug risk categories describe the potential risk of medications to the fetus when used during pregnancy.

Category C drugs:

• Animal studies show adverse fetal effects, but
• No adequate, well-controlled human studies are available.
• The drug may still be used if the potential maternal benefit justifies the potential fetal risk.

Comparison with other categories:

• Category A: Controlled human studies show no fetal risk.
• Category B: Animal studies show no risk or animal risk not confirmed in humans.
• Category C: Animal risk present; human data lacking → use if benefit outweighs risk.
• Category D: Positive evidence of human fetal risk, but may be used in life-threatening conditions.
• Category X: Contraindicated in pregnancy (risk clearly outweighs benefit).

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: From which spinal segment is the sympathetic nerve supply to the ovary derived?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. T10-T11

The ovary receives sympathetic innervation from spinal segments T10–T11, which travel via the ovarian plexus accompanying the ovarian vessels.

• Sympathetic supply: T10–T11
• Fibers arise from the thoracic sympathetic chain → pass through aortic/ovarian plexus → reach the ovary along the ovarian artery.
• These fibers mainly mediate vasomotor control and pain sensation from the ovary.

Ovarian pain (e.g., ovarian torsion, follicular rupture) is typically referred to the T10–T11 dermatomes, producing pain in the periumbilical or lower abdominal region.

Important contrast:

• Ovary: Sympathetic T10–T11
• Uterus: Sympathetic T12–L2
• Pelvic parasympathetic supply (pelvic organs): S2–S4 via pelvic splanchnic nerves

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Hormone replacement therapy ( HRT ) should be prescribed to which of the following patients?
options: A 35-year-old woman who has undergone Total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy ( TAH + BSO )
A 9-year-old girl who has Turner syndrome
A 47-year-old woman with hot flushes and history of breast cancer
A 60-year-old woman with a history of ischemic heart disease
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. A 35-year-old woman who has undergone Total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy ( TAH + BSO )

Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT) is indicated in women with premature or surgical menopause, --> especially younger than 40–45 years, to prevent complications of estrogen deficiency such as osteoporosis, cardiovascular disease, and vasomotor symptoms.

Correct indication:

• Women undergoing TAH + BSO at a young age → sudden loss of ovarian estrogen → HRT recommended until the natural age of menopause (\~50 years).

Why other options are incorrect:

• Turner syndrome (9-year-old): requires puberty induction with estrogen, not menopausal HRT.
• History of breast cancer: HRT contraindicated because estrogen may stimulate tumor recurrence.
• Ischemic heart disease: HRT generally avoided due to thrombotic and cardiovascular risk.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Identify the correct statements 1. The secondary oocyte arrested in meiosis II is released during ovulation 2. Tubectomy is done at ampulla due to uniform muscle thickness 3. External cephalic version ( ECV ) is contraindicated in a primigravida with twin pregnancy 4. In the treatment of vault prolapse, the mesh is fixed to the sacral promontory
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 3, 4

Correct statements:

1. Secondary oocyte arrested in meiosis II is released during ovulation – TRUE

At ovulation, the ovary releases a secondary oocyte that is arrested in metaphase of meiosis II. Completion of meiosis II occurs only after fertilization.

3. External cephalic version (ECV) is contraindicated in twin pregnancy – TRUE

External cephalic version is performed to convert breech to vertex presentation in singleton pregnancies. It is contraindicated in multiple pregnancies (e.g., twins) due to the risk of cord entanglement, placental complications, and fetal distress.

4. Mesh fixation to sacral promontory in vault prolapse – TRUE

In vaginal vault prolapse, the standard surgical repair is Sacrocolpopexy, where a mesh is attached between the vaginal vault and the sacral promontory to restore pelvic support.

Incorrect statement:

2. Tubectomy done at ampulla due to uniform muscle thickness – FALSE

In female sterilization, tubectomy is usually performed at the isthmic portion of the fallopian tube, not the ampulla. The isthmus is narrow with thick muscular walls, making it easier and more effective for ligation and excision.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Identify the correct statements about the most common fetal head positions associated with different pelvic types: 1. Persistent occiput posterior (OP) → Anthropoid pelvis 2. Face presentation to pubis → Android pelvis 3. Right occiput posterior (ROP) → Platypelloid pelvis 4. Left occiput transverse (LOT) → Gynecoid pelvis
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1, 4

| Pelvic type | Characteristic fetal head position | Explanation

| ----------- | ---------------------------------- | -----------

| Gynecoid pelvis | Occiput transverse (LOT/ROT) | Round inlet allows normal rotation; transverse positions are common during engagement before rotating to occipitoanterior.

| Anthropoid pelvis | Persistent occiput posterior (OP) | Oval inlet with larger anteroposterior diameter favors posterior positions.

| Android pelvis | Deep transverse arrest / persistent transverse position | Funnel-shaped pelvis restricts rotation.

| Platypelloid pelvis | Transverse engagement | Wide transverse diameter with short AP diameter; OP or ROP is not typical.

1. Persistent OP → Anthropoid pelvis: Correct
2. Face presentation to pubis → Android pelvis: Incorrect (face-to-pubis occurs due to persistent OP, not specifically android pelvis)
3. ROP → Platypelloid pelvis: Incorrect (platypelloid pelvis favors transverse engagement)
4. LOT → Gynecoid pelvis: Correct

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Identify the true statements: 1. Flexion point in ventouse delivery is 3 cm posterior to the anterior fontanelle 2. Carcinoma cervix causing hydronephrosis is Stage IIIb 3. When the first twin has a non-vertex presentation, the preferred method of delivery is a cesarean section. 4. Post-partum IUCD can be inserted after 24 hours, for one week after delivery
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 2, 3

Correct statements:

2. Hydronephrosis in carcinoma cervix → Stage IIIB

In the Cervical cancer, FIGO staging, Stage IIIB includes:

• Tumor extending to pelvic wall, or

• Hydronephrosis / non-functioning kidney due to ureteric obstruction by the tumor.

3. First twin non-vertex → Cesarean delivery preferred

In twin pregnancy, the presentation of the first twin determines the route of delivery.

• First twin vertex → vaginal delivery can be attempted

• First twin non-vertex (breech/transverse) → cesarean section is recommended to reduce fetal complications.

Incorrect statements:

1. Flexion point in ventouse delivery

The correct flexion point is 3 cm anterior to the posterior fontanelle (or 6 cm posterior to the anterior fontanelle), not 3 cm posterior to the anterior fontanelle.

4. Postpartum IUCD timing

Intrauterine device insertion postpartum can be done:

• Within 10 minutes of placental delivery (post-placental)

• Within 48 hours after delivery

• After 6 weeks postpartum

It is not recommended between 48 hours and 6 weeks, so insertion after 24 hours for one week is incorrect.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: If bilateral tubal block is seen on hysterosalpingography (HSG), which of the following is the next best step?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Laparoscopic chromopertubation

Hysterosalpingography (HSG) is a screening test used to assess uterine cavity and tubal patency in infertility evaluation.

However, it may produce false-positive tubal blockage, commonly due to tubal spasm, mucus plugs, or technical factors.

Therefore, when bilateral tubal block is detected on HSG, the next best step is confirmation with laparoscopic chromopertubation, which is the gold standard test for tubal patency.

• A dye (usually methylene blue) is injected through the cervix.
• During laparoscopy, direct visualization of dye spilling from the fimbrial ends confirms tubal patency.
• Also allows detection of associated pelvic pathologies such as:

• Endometriosis
• Pelvic adhesions
• Tubal disease

Why other options are incorrect:

• IVF: Considered only after confirming true tubal blockage.
• Hysteroscopy: Evaluates uterine cavity, not tubal patency.
• Hysteroscopy with D&C: Not useful for assessing fallopian tubes.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: In a clinical trial, 120 accidental pregnancies occur in 1000 women followed for 12 months. Pearl's index is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 12

• Pearl's Index = (Accidental pregnancies / Total women months of exposure) × 1200.
• Women months = 1000 × 12 = 12,000. PI = (120/12,000) × 1200 = 12.
• Alternatively: (120/1000 women years) × 100 = 12.
• Expressed per hundred women years (HWY).
• Lower PI = more effective contraceptive.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: In the Zuspan regimen, what is the maintenance dose of MgSO₄ after the loading dose?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1g/hour IV infusion

Magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄) is the drug of choice for prevention and treatment of eclamptic seizures. The Zuspan regimen is a commonly used intravenous protocol.

Zuspan Regimen

• Loading dose: 4 g IV over 5–10 minutes
• Maintenance dose: 1 g/hour continuous IV infusion

Before each dose/while infusion is running, ensure:

• Respiratory rate >12/min
• Urine output >25–30 mL/hour
• Presence of deep tendon (patellar) reflexes

Signs of Magnesium Toxicity

• Loss of deep tendon reflexes
• Respiratory depression
• Cardiac conduction abnormalities/cardiac arrest

Antidote: 10 mL of 10% calcium gluconate IV administered slowly

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: In which of the following patients is a karyotype most likely required?
options: 18-year-old with amenorrhea and an elevated prolactin level
16-year-old with amenorrhea with normal secondary sexual characters and no mullerian structures on sonography
16-year-old with amenorrhea with normal secondary sexual characters and uterus seen on imaging
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 16-year-old with amenorrhea with normal secondary sexual characters and no mullerian structures on sonography

Karyotyping is indicated in cases of primary amenorrhea when a disorder of sex development (DSD) is suspected, particularly when Müllerian structures (uterus, cervix) are absent.

A 16-year-old with primary amenorrhea, normal secondary sexual characteristics, and absent Müllerian structures on imaging suggests either:

• Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome (AIS) → 46,XY karyotype, testes present, female phenotype, absent uterus

• Müllerian agenesis (Mayer–Rokitansky–Küster–Hauser syndrome, MRKH) → 46,XX karyotype, normal ovaries, absent uterus

Because these two conditions have different karyotypes and management, karyotype testing is essential for diagnosis and differentiation.

Why other options do not require immediate karyotyping:

• Amenorrhea with hirsutism → more suggestive of PCOS or hyperandrogenism

• Amenorrhea with hyperprolactinemia → likely prolactinoma or endocrine cause

• Amenorrhea with normal secondary sexual characters and uterus present → often due to outflow tract obstruction (e.g., imperforate hymen) or endocrine causes

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: In which stage of puberty does estrogen not have a major role?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Pubarche

Puberty involves several milestones regulated by different hormones.

Hormonal Control:

• Thelarche (breast development): Estrogen-mediated
• Menarche (onset of menstruation): Estrogen-driven endometrial proliferation
• Growth spurt: Estrogen stimulates GH–IGF axis and epiphyseal maturation
• Pubarche (pubic/axillary hair): Caused by adrenal androgens (DHEA, DHEA-S), not estrogen

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Injury to the deepest part of the perineal body, leading to cystocele, enterocele, and urethral descent, involves which of the following muscles?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Pubococcygeus

The perineal body is a central fibromuscular structure in the perineum that provides attachment to several pelvic floor muscles and plays a crucial role in pelvic organ support.

Deepest and most important muscle related to pelvic support:

• Pubococcygeus muscle, part of the levator ani, which forms the main support for pelvic organs.

Function of pubococcygeus:

• Supports the bladder, uterus, and rectum
• Maintains pelvic floor integrity
• Prevents pelvic organ prolapse

Damage to the deep perineal body and pubococcygeus muscle (e.g., during childbirth) can lead to:

• Cystocele (bladder prolapse)
• Enterocele (herniation of small bowel)
• Urethral descent

Other muscles:

• Bulbospongiosus, ischiocavernosus, and superficial transverse perineal are superficial perineal muscles and contribute less to pelvic organ support.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: IUD insertion timing — all correctly matched except:
options: Post placental = within 10 min of delivery
Post partum = after 10 min, within 48 hours
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Post surgical abortion = after 7 days

• Post surgical abortion = 12–15 days, not 7.
• Non-pregnant female = within first 10 days of menses.
• Key note: ectopic pregnancy is NOT a contraindication for copper IUD insertion.

| Timing | Window

| ------ | ------

| Intra caesarean | During C/S

| Post placental | Within 10 min of delivery

| Post partum | After 10 min → within 48 hrs

| Interval | After 6 weeks

| Post surgical abortion | 12–15 days

| Non-pregnant female | Within first 10 days of menses

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: MgSO₄ prevents eclamptic seizures primarily by which mechanism?
options: NMDA receptor antagonism and cerebral vasodilation
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. NMDA receptor antagonism and cerebral vasodilation

Magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄) is the drug of choice for the prevention and treatment of eclamptic seizures in women with severe preeclampsia and eclampsia.

Mechanism of Action:

• Blocks NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartate) receptors in the central nervous system
• Reduces neuronal excitability and seizure propagation
• Causes cerebral vasodilation, reducing cerebral ischemia and vasospasm
• Stabilizes the blood-brain barrier and decreases cerebral edema

Why Other Options Are Incorrect:

• GABA-A receptor potentiation: Mechanism of benzodiazepines and barbiturates.
• Sodium channel blockade: Mechanism of drugs such as phenytoin.
• Inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis: Mechanism of NSAIDs.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: MgSO₄ should be used with extreme caution or avoided in which condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Myasthenia gravis

Magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄) is the drug of choice for prevention and treatment of eclamptic seizures, but it should be used with extreme caution or avoided in certain neuromuscular disorders.

Myasthenia gravis is a disorder of neuromuscular transmission caused by antibodies against acetylcholine receptors.

MgSO₄:

• Inhibits acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction
• Reduces muscle fiber excitability
• Can markedly worsen neuromuscular weakness

Potential consequences:

• Respiratory muscle paralysis
• Respiratory failure
• Need for mechanical ventilation

Other Contraindications/Cautions

• Myasthenia gravis (major contraindication)
• Significant renal failure (risk of magnesium toxicity)
• Heart block or myocardial conduction defects

Why Other Options Are Incorrect

• Chronic hypertension: Not a contraindication; MgSO₄ is commonly used in severe preeclampsia/eclampsia.
• Gestational diabetes: Not a contraindication.
• Twin pregnancy: Not a contraindication.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Modified Robson's classification - Group 2 includes which of the following?
options: Nulliparous, singleton, cephalic pregnancy, induced labour
Nulliparous, singleton, cephalic pregnancy, spontaneous labour
Multiparous without previous cesarean section, spontaneous labour
Multiparous without previous cesarean section, induced labour or cesarean section before labour
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Nulliparous, singleton, cephalic pregnancy, induced labour

Robson Group 2 includes nulliparous women with a singleton cephalic pregnancy who undergo induction of labor or prelabor cesarean section. This group is analyzed separately to assess cesarean rates related to induction.

The 10 Robson Groups

1. Nulliparous, single, cephalic, ≥37 weeks, spontaneous labor
2. Nulliparous, single, cephalic, ≥37 weeks, induced or CS before labor
3. Multiparous (no previous CS), single, cephalic, ≥37 weeks, spontaneous labor
4. Multiparous (no previous CS), single, cephalic, ≥37 weeks, induced or CS before labor
5. Previous CS, single, cephalic, ≥37 weeks
6. Nulliparous breech
7. Multiparous breech (including previous CS)
8. Multiple pregnancy
9. Transverse/oblique lie (including previous CS)
10. Single cephalic, <37 weeks (including previous CS)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: On doing a per-vaginal examination of a woman in labor, you were able to palpate the mouth with hard alveolar margins, nose, malar eminence, and supraorbital ridges of the fetus. Which of the following would have been the engaging diameter for this presentation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Submentovertical

Palpation of mouth, nose, malar eminence, and supraorbital ridges on vaginal examination indicates a face presentation of the fetus.

Engaging Diameter:

• In face presentation, the fetal head is fully extended.
• The engaging diameter is submentovertical (\~11.5 cm).

| Diameter | Attitude of the Head | Presentation

| -------- | -------------------- | ------------

| Suboccipitobregmatic (9.5 cm) | Complete Flexion | Vertex

| Suboccipitofrontal (10 cm) | Incomplete Flexion | Vertex

| Occipitofrontal (11.5 cm) | Marked Deflexion | Vertex

| Mentovertical (14 cm) | Partial Extension | Brow

| Submentobregmatic (9.5 cm) | Complete Extension | Face (MC in Anencephaly)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Regarding antiepileptic drugs (AEDs) in pregnancy, all of the following are true except:
options: Valproic acid is the most teratogenic antiepileptic drug
Levetiracetam and lamotrigine are among the safest antiepileptics in pregnancy
If a woman conceives while on antiepileptics, the same drug should usually be continued except valproate
Antiepileptic drug clearance decreases during pregnancy, hence drug levels need not be monitored
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Antiepileptic drug clearance decreases during pregnancy, hence drug levels need not be monitored

Women with epilepsy should ideally receive preconception counseling, use the lowest effective dose of a single antiepileptic drug (monotherapy), and take high-dose folic acid supplementation before conception and during early pregnancy.

1. Valproic acid is the most teratogenic AED and is associated with:

• Neural tube defects
• Cardiac defects
• Craniofacial abnormalities
• Neurodevelopmental delay and autism spectrum disorders

2. Levetiracetam and lamotrigine have the best safety profiles in pregnancy and are preferred when clinically appropriate.

3. If pregnancy occurs while on AED therapy\, treatment is usually continued because uncontrolled maternal seizures pose significant risks to both mother and fetus. However\, valproate should be avoided whenever possible and switched preconceptionally if feasible.

AED clearance does not decrease during pregnancy; it increases.

• Pregnancy increases renal clearance and hepatic metabolism of several AEDs, especially lamotrigine and levetiracetam.
• Serum drug concentrations may fall significantly during pregnancy.
• Therefore, therapeutic drug monitoring is often required to maintain seizure control and guide dose adjustments.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Regarding delivery in twin pregnancy, all of the following statements are correct except:
options: Vaginal delivery is possible in DCDA twins at 38 weeks
Internal podalic version is indicated when the second twin is in transverse lie
Internal podalic version is contraindicated in previous cesarean section
Vaginal delivery is preferred in monochorionic monoamniotic twins
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Vaginal delivery is preferred in monochorionic monoamniotic twins

The mode of delivery in twin pregnancy depends on chorionicity, amnionicity, gestational age, fetal presentations, and obstetric factors.

• DCDA twins can be delivered vaginally if the first twin is cephalic and there are no contraindications.
• Elective delivery of uncomplicated DCDA twins is usually planned around 38 weeks.
• Internal podalic version (IPV) may be performed for the second twin in transverse lie to facilitate breech extraction by an experienced obstetrician.
• Previous cesarean section is a contraindication to IPV due to the increased risk of uterine rupture.

Monochorionic monoamniotic (MCMA) twins have a high risk of:

• Cord entanglement
• Cord compression
• Intrauterine fetal demise

Therefore, planned cesarean section is the preferred mode of delivery, usually at 32–34 weeks after corticosteroid administration.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Regarding external cephalic version (ECV), all of the following statements are correct except:
options: ECV is usually performed at around 37 weeks of gestation
Adequate liquor and intact membranes are prerequisites for ECV
Routine induction of labour is recommended immediately after successful ECV
Oligohydramnios is an absolute contraindication for ECV
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Routine induction of labour is recommended immediately after successful ECV

External Cephalic Version (ECV) is a procedure used to convert a breech or transverse lie fetus to cephalic presentation by external abdominal manipulation, thereby reducing the need for cesarean delivery.

• Usually performed at 36–37 weeks gestation.
• Requires:

• Adequate amniotic fluid
• Intact membranes
• Reassuring fetal status

• Success rates are higher in multiparous women and with adequate liquor.

Contraindications

• Oligohydramnios
• Placenta previa
• Multiple pregnancy (except selected second twin)
• Ruptured membranes
• Significant uterine anomalies
• Any contraindication to vaginal delivery

A successful ECV is not an indication for routine induction of labor.

• Pregnancy is usually allowed to continue spontaneously.
• Induction is performed only for standard obstetric indications.
