The Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification (POP-Q) system is the standardized and internationally accepted method for assessing and staging pelvic organ prolapse (POP). It uses nine specific anatomical measurements relative to the hymenal ring.

Among these measurements, Total Vaginal Length (TVL) is the only parameter measured without the patient straining (Valsalva maneuver). It is measured with the prolapse completely reduced.

Why not the other options?

• B. Pb (Perineal Body): Measured during maximum Valsalva/straining.
• C. GH (Genital Hiatus): Measured during maximum strain, from the external urethral meatus to the posterior hymen.
• D. Point D: Represents the posterior fornix (only present if the uterus is present) and is measured during maximal Valsalva.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is the first step after fitting the pessary to check if the pessary is adequately retained? (NEET PG 2018)
options: Asking the patient to void and see if the pessary is in place
Seeing if the patient feels any discomfort, which means that the pessary is retained
Asking the patient to perform the Valsalva manuever and see if the pessary is in place
Being able to admit two fingers between the ring and the pessary.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Asking the patient to perform the Valsalva manuever and see if the pessary is in place

A pessary is a vaginal support device used for pelvic organ prolapse and stress urinary incontinence. After pessary insertion, the first step to check adequate retention is Asking the patient to perform the Valsalva maneuver

This increases intra-abdominal pressure and helps determine whether:

• The pessary remains properly positioned
• It slips, rotates, or is expelled

Additional assessment after proper retention:

• Patient comfort
• Ability to void normally
• Ability to walk and perform routine activities

A properly fitted pessary should stay in place during straining but should not cause pain or excessive pressure.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which one of the following is a common pathology associated with ureteric injury while performing surgical procedure of abdominal hysterectomy?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Pelvic endometriosis

Ureteric injury is a recognized complication of abdominal hysterectomy, particularly in the presence of distorted pelvic anatomy. Pelvic endometriosis is one of the most common pathological conditions predisposing to ureteric injury because it causes dense fibrosis, adhesions, and distortion of normal tissue planes, making ureteric identification difficult.

Why are the other options incorrect?

• B. Adenomyosis: Adenomyosis enlarges the uterus but does not usually distort the ureteric course to the same extent as pelvic endometriosis.
• C. Hydrosalpinx: Although it may cause adnexal enlargement, it is less commonly associated with ureteric injury.
• D. Ovarian teratoma: A benign ovarian teratoma rarely causes extensive pelvic fibrosis or ureteric distortion.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which one of the following is not a differential diagnosis of chronic inversion of uterus?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Gartner’s cyst

Chronic uterine inversion is a rare condition in which the uterine fundus remains inverted for more than 4 weeks, usually following mismanaged third stage of labor or due to a fundal uterine tumor (e.g., submucous fibroid). It presents as a mass protruding through the cervix or vagina, often associated with irregular bleeding, foul discharge, pelvic pain, and anemia.

Because it presents as a vaginal mass, it must be differentiated from other causes of protruding genital tract masses.

• Gartner’s cyst is a remnant of the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct, located in the anterolateral wall of the upper vagina.
• It presents as a vaginal cystic swelling and does not resemble an inverted uterus, making it not a differential diagnosis of chronic uterine inversion.

Why not the other options?

• A. Fibroid polyp: A prolapsed submucous fibroid may present as a vaginal mass and closely mimics chronic uterine inversion.
• B. Fungating cervical malignancy: An advanced cervical cancer may present as an irregular bleeding vaginal mass and should be differentiated from uterine inversion.
• C. Cervical prolapse: Cervical or uterovaginal prolapse presents as a protruding vaginal mass and is an important differential diagnosis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which one of the following statements is true regarding neurovascular anatomy of the uterus?
options: The uterine artery arises from the anterior division of the external iliac artery.
The uterine artery crosses the ureter 3.5 cm lateral to the internal os.
The venous channels of the uterus drain into the internal iliac veins.
The somatic distribution of the uterine pain is the area of the abdomen supplied by T5 and T6.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. The venous channels of the uterus drain into the internal iliac veins.

• A. The uterine artery arises from the anterior division of the external iliac artery: Incorrect. The uterine artery arises from the anterior division of the internal iliac artery, not the external iliac artery.
• B. The uterine artery crosses the ureter 3.5 cm lateral to the internal os: Incorrect. The uterine artery crosses over the ureter approximately 1.5–2 cm lateral to the internal os, not 3.5 cm.
• C. The venous channels of the uterus drain into the internal iliac veins: Correct. The uterine venous plexus drains predominantly into the uterine veins → internal iliac veins.
• D. The somatic distribution of the uterine pain is the area of the abdomen supplied by T5 and T6: Incorrect. Uterine pain is primarily referred through T10–L1 segments. Fundal pain may be referred around T10, while cervical pain is transmitted via pelvic visceral afferents.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 25-year-old girl is presented to Gynaecology OPD with complaints of abdominal pain, heavy menstrual bleeding with a mass arising from the hypogastrium corresponding to 16 weeks gravid uterus. Her urine pregnancy test is negative. The most likely diagnosis would be:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Uterine fibroid

Uterine fibroids (leiomyomas) are the most common benign tumors of the uterus in women of reproductive age. They commonly present with:

• Heavy menstrual bleeding (menorrhagia)
• Pelvic pain or pressure
• Enlarged irregular uterus, which may be palpable as an abdominal mass
• Negative pregnancy test despite uterine enlargement

Why not the other options?

• A. Pelvic inflammatory disease: Usually presents with fever, lower abdominal pain, vaginal discharge, and cervical motion tenderness, not a large uterine mass.
• C. Ovarian tumour: May present as an adnexal mass, but heavy menstrual bleeding is less characteristic, and the uterus is usually normal in size.
• D. Endometriosis: Causes dysmenorrhea, chronic pelvic pain, dyspareunia, and infertility, but not a 16-week-sized uterine enlargement.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 30-year-old married woman came for an infertility evaluation. On performing further investigations, intramural fibroids of sizes 7x5cm and 5x3cm were seen at the right and left cornual ends of the uterus. Her husband's semen analysis was found to be normal. What is the appropriate management of this case? (NEET PG 2021)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Laparoscopic Myomectomy

Intramural fibroids located near the cornual region can impair fertility by:

• Distorting the uterine cavity
• Interfering with implantation
• Obstructing tubal ostia
• Altering uterine contractility and blood flow

In an infertile woman with:

• Large symptomatic intramural fibroids
• Normal semen analysis
• Fibroids affecting the cornual region

The appropriate management is Laparoscopic myomectomy.

• Removes fibroids while preserving fertility
• Improves chances of conception
• Minimally invasive with faster recovery

Why other options are incorrect:

• A. Uterine artery embolization is generally avoided in women desiring future fertility
• C. ART does not correct the mechanical distortion caused by fibroids
• D. GnRH analogues temporarily shrink fibroids but are not definitive treatment

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 35-year-old non-pregnant woman presents with persistent intermenstrual spotting for the past several months. Her serum β-hCG is negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Endometrial polyp

Endometrial polyps are the most common cause of persistent intermenstrual (between-period) bleeding in reproductive-aged women after pregnancy has been excluded (β-hCG negative). They are localized overgrowths of endometrial glands and stroma that bleed irregularly.

• Best initial imaging: Transvaginal ultrasonography (TVS).
• Most sensitive test: Saline infusion sonography (SIS).
• Gold standard for diagnosis and treatment: Hysteroscopy with polypectomy.

Why the Other Options Are Incorrect

• A. PCOS: Typically causes oligomenorrhea/amenorrhea with irregular heavy bleeding due to anovulation, not persistent intermenstrual spotting.
• C. Endometrial hyperplasia: Usually presents with abnormal heavy or prolonged uterine bleeding, especially in women with chronic unopposed estrogen exposure.
• D. Submucosal fibroid: Commonly causes heavy menstrual bleeding (menorrhagia) and may cause intermenstrual bleeding, but persistent spotting is more characteristic of an endometrial polyp.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 35-year-old woman is diagnosed with a uterine leiomyoma on ultrasound during evaluation for abnormal uterine bleeding. She is planned for surgical management with myomectomy. Which of the following is the most appropriate next investigation prior to the procedure?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. MRI pelvis

MRI pelvis is the best imaging modality for preoperative mapping of uterine fibroids, especially before myomectomy, as it accurately defines the number, size, location, and type of leiomyomas, helping plan the surgical approach and differentiate fibroids from adenomyosis.

Why not the other options?

• A. CT pelvis: Poor soft tissue characterization; not routinely used for fibroid evaluation.
• C. Hysterosalpingography (HSG): Used to assess the uterine cavity and tubal patency in infertility, not for preoperative fibroid mapping.
• D. Plain X-ray pelvis: Limited role; may show calcified fibroids but is not useful for surgical planning.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 45-year-old postmenopausal woman presents with vaginal bleeding. A transvaginal ultrasound reveals an endometrial thickness of 8.0 mm. What should be the next step in management? (NEET PG 2015)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Histopathological examination of curettage

Postmenopausal bleeding must always be evaluated for endometrial carcinoma until proven otherwise. Transvaginal ultrasound is used to measure endometrial thickness:

• Endometrial thickness ≤4 mm → low risk of malignancy
• Endometrial thickness >4 mm → requires endometrial sampling

This patient has:

• Postmenopausal bleeding
• Endometrial thickness of 8 mm

Therefore, the next step is histopathological evaluation of the endometrium by endometrial biopsy or curettage.

Why other options are incorrect:

• Hysterectomy is not performed before tissue diagnosis
• Progesterone therapy should not be started without excluding malignancy
• Follow-up sonography alone is inappropriate in symptomatic women with thickened endometrium

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 45-year-old woman with irregular bleeding is found to have an endometrial thickness of 15 mm. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Endometrial biopsy

In a 45-year-old with abnormal uterine bleeding and ET = 15 mm, the priority is to rule out endometrial hyperplasia or carcinoma.

Even without ultrasound findings, guidelines recommend biopsy in all women ≥45 with AUB.

Normal endometrial thickness varies with menstrual cycle, but in AUB evaluation:

| Patient group | Suspicious ET

| ------------- | -------------

| Premenopausal with AUB
Perimenopausal | >12 mm

| Postmenopausal bleeding | >4 mm

This patient has 15 mm, which is abnormally thick.

Procedure : A catheter is inserted into the uterus to obtain endometrial tissue.

Advantages

• Outpatient procedure
• Quick and minimally invasive
• High sensitivity for endometrial carcinoma

Detects

• Endometrial hyperplasia
• Endometrial carcinoma
• Hormonal endometrial changes

B. Hysterectomy  is not the first step.

It is done only after:

• Confirmed malignancy
• Failed medical treatment

C. MRI Pelvis  is used for:

• Staging endometrial cancer
• Assessing myometrial invasion

D. Hysteroscopy and Fractional Curettage

This procedure is more invasive and usually performed when:

• Biopsy is inconclusive
• Focal lesion suspected
• Persistent bleeding despite normal biopsy

PALM-COEIN

| Structural causes (PALM) | Non-structural causes (COEIN)

| ------------------------ | -----------------------------

| Polyp | Coagulopathy

| Adenomyosis | Ovulatory dysfunction

| Leiomyoma | Endometrial

| Malignancy / hyperplasia | Iatrogenic / Not classified

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 46-year-old nulliparous woman is found to have an endometrial thickness of 16 mm on TVS. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Endometrial biopsy

A thickened endometrium in a perimenopausal woman raises suspicion for:

• Endometrial Hyperplasia
• Endometrial Carcinoma

Risk factors present in this patient:

| Risk Factor | Significance

| ----------- | ------------

| Age >45 years | Higher malignancy risk

| Nulliparity | More lifetime estrogen exposure

| Thick endometrium (16 mm) | Abnormal finding

Therefore histological confirmation is required.

Typical findings:

| Group | Endometrial Thickness

| ----- | ---------------------

| Premenopausal proliferative phase | 5–7 mm

| Secretory phase | up to 12–14 mm

| Postmenopausal | <4 mm

In a 46-year-old woman, 16 mm is abnormally thick, so tissue diagnosis is required.

Endometrial Biopsy is the first-line diagnostic test.

Common method: Pipelle biopsy

Purpose:

• Detect hyperplasia
• Diagnose endometrial cancer

B) Hysterectomy

Too aggressive without histological diagnosis.

Risk Factors for Endometrial Cancer

| Risk Factor | Mechanism

| ----------- | ---------

| Nulliparity | Continuous estrogen exposure

| Obesity | Peripheral estrogen production

| PCOS | Chronic anovulation

| Diabetes | Metabolic risk

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 49-year-old well-off businesswoman presents with irregular, heavy bleeding. Her mother tells her this is normal at her age, but she seeks medical advice. What is the next best step?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. TVS

Abnormal Uterine Bleeding is common in perimenopausal women due to hormonal imbalance but must always be evaluated to rule out pathology.

Common causes are classified using the PALM-COEIN system.

| Structural causes | Non-structural causes

| ----------------- | ---------------------

| P – Polyp | C – Coagulopathy

| A – Adenomyosis | O – Ovulatory dysfunction

| L – Leiomyoma | E – Endometrial

| M – Malignancy | I – Iatrogenic

| | N – Not classified

In perimenopausal women (40+ years) with heavy bleeding: irregular cycles may be normal but heavy bleeding always requires evaluation with endometrial sampling to exclude malignancy, hyperplasia, and structural lesions before considering any treatment options. TVS is needed to see any structural cause and endometrial thickness.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 52-year-old postmenopausal woman presents with bleeding. Evaluation reveals a 3 cm fibroid in the uterine wall and an endometrial thickness of 8 mm. What is the next best step in management?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Endometrial biopsy

Postmenopausal bleeding (PMB) is considered endometrial carcinoma until proven otherwise. The first-line investigation is transvaginal ultrasonography (TVS) to measure endometrial thickness (ET).

In women with PMB:

• ET ≤4 mm → Very low risk of endometrial carcinoma; biopsy is usually not required unless bleeding persists.
• ET >4 mm → Endometrial biopsy is mandatory to exclude endometrial hyperplasia or carcinoma, regardless of the presence of other uterine pathologies such as fibroids.

In this patient, although a 3 cm intramural fibroid is present, it does not explain the increased endometrial thickness (8 mm). Therefore, the priority is to obtain an endometrial tissue diagnosis.

Why not the other options?

• A. CECT: Has no role in the initial evaluation of PMB; used only if malignancy is diagnosed and extrauterine disease is suspected.
• C. Pap smear: Screens for cervical neoplasia, not endometrial pathology.
• D. MRI: Used for local staging of confirmed endometrial carcinoma, not for establishing the diagnosis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman with a fibroid uterus develops severe acute pain abdomen and fever at 28 weeks of gestation. WBC count is 8000cells/µl. The most likely diagnosis is? (NEET PG 2019)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Red degeneration of fibroid

Red degeneration (carneous degeneration) is the most common complication of uterine fibroids during pregnancy. It typically occurs:

• In the second trimester
• Most commonly around 28–34 weeks gestation

Clinical features:

• Sudden severe abdominal pain
• Localized uterine tenderness
• Mild fever
• Nausea and vomiting
• Normal or mildly elevated WBC count

Pathogenesis:

• Rapid fibroid growth during pregnancy outgrows its blood supply
• Leads to hemorrhagic infarction and necrosis within the fibroid

Fever with a relatively normal WBC count favors red degeneration rather than infection.

Management:

• Conservative treatment
• Analgesics, hydration, and rest

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A woman with a history of hysterectomy presents with vaginal bleeding. Speculum and vaginal examination reveal no obvious abnormality. What is the most likely cause of her bleeding?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Vaginal cuff (vault) granulation tissue

Vaginal cuff (vault) granulation tissue is the most common cause of vaginal bleeding after hysterectomy, particularly within months after surgery, although it can present later. It results from excessive granulation tissue at the vaginal vault closure.

• Presentation: Spotting or postcoital bleeding after hysterectomy.
• Examination: Small, friable, red granulation tissue at the vaginal cuff (may require careful speculum examination).
• Treatment: Chemical cauterization with silver nitrate or excision if persistent.

Why the Other Options Are Incorrect?

• A. Cervical ectropion: Impossible after total hysterectomy because the cervix has been removed.
• B. Cervical polyp: Cannot occur after total hysterectomy.
• C. Endometrial carcinoma: Cannot arise if the uterus has been removed (except in supracervical hysterectomy, where only the cervix remains).

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Causes of AUB are subdivided by the acronym PALM-COEIN. What are the characteristics of PALM causes? I. Structural lesions II. Diagnosed by ultrasound III. Confirmed by histopathology Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. I, II and III

The FIGO PALM-COEIN classification is the standard system used to classify the causes of Abnormal Uterine Bleeding (AUB) in reproductive-aged women.

The PALM group includes structural causes that can usually be identified by imaging and confirmed by histopathological examination, whereas the COEIN group comprises non-structural causes. All the statements regarding PALM causes are correct:

• I. Structural lesions: PALM includes structural abnormalities of the uterus.
• II. Diagnosed by ultrasound: Most PALM lesions can be detected by transvaginal ultrasonography, saline infusion sonography, hysteroscopy, or MRI.
• III. Confirmed by histopathology: Tissue diagnosis confirms conditions such as endometrial hyperplasia, malignancy, adenomyosis (after hysterectomy), and polyps.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Endometrial sampling for diagnosis of ovulation is done on which day of menstrual cycle?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 21st–23rd day

Endometrial biopsy to assess ovulation is performed during the late secretory (premenstrual) phase, typically on days 21–23 of a 28-day menstrual cycle. The presence of secretory endometrium confirms that ovulation has occurred.

Why not the other options?

• A. 8th–10th day: Early proliferative phase.
• B. 12th day: Late proliferative phase, before ovulation.
• C. 14th day: Around the time of ovulation; secretory changes have not yet developed.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: For which of the following conditions, surgery is indicated in a case of Fibroid Uterus? I. Symptomatic and failed medical management II. Size >12 weeks III. Pedunculated fibroid Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. I, II and III

Uterine fibroids (leiomyomas) are the most common benign tumors of the uterus, arising from the smooth muscle cells of the myometrium. Surgery is indicated when fibroids cause significant symptoms, complications, or suspicion of malignancy, or when conservative treatment has failed.

All the listed conditions are indications for surgery:

• I. Symptomatic and failed medical management: Surgery is indicated in women with persistent heavy menstrual bleeding, pain, pressure symptoms, infertility, or recurrent pregnancy loss despite adequate medical therapy.
• II. Size >12 weeks: A uterus enlarged to more than 12 weeks’ gestational size is generally considered an indication for surgery, particularly if associated with rapid growth, pressure symptoms, or diagnostic uncertainty.
• III. Pedunculated fibroid: Pedunculated submucosal or subserosal fibroids are prone to torsion, degeneration, or prolapse, making surgical removal appropriate.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Primary dysmenorrhoea can be treated by which of the following? 1. Antiprostaglandin 2. Cyclic combined estrogen and progesterone preparations 3. Presacral neurectomy 4. Uterine curettage Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 1, 2 and 3

Primary dysmenorrhea is painful menstruation without any pelvic pathology. It is caused by excessive endometrial prostaglandin (PGF₂α) production, leading to uterine hypercontractility and ischemia.

Why are the statements correct/incorrect?

• 1. Antiprostaglandins (NSAIDs): Correct. First-line treatment (e.g., mefenamic acid, ibuprofen, naproxen).
• 2. Cyclic combined estrogen and progesterone preparations (Combined oral contraceptive pills): Correct. Suppress ovulation, reduce endometrial proliferation, and decrease prostaglandin production.
• 3. Presacral neurectomy: Correct. Reserved for severe, refractory cases when medical therapy fails.
• 4. Uterine curettage: Incorrect. Has no role in the treatment of primary dysmenorrhea.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following statements is true regarding endometrial hyperplasia?
options: Diagnosed by a hysteroscopic guided biopsy or a D & C
After biopsy, no other follow-up is required
Hysterectomy should be done in all cases
Majority will regress without any treatment
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Diagnosed by a hysteroscopic guided biopsy or a D & C

• Endometrial Hyperplasia is a precancerous condition of the uterine endometrium commonly presenting with abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB).
• It occurs due to prolonged estrogen stimulation without progesterone opposition.
• It is a histopathological diagnosis that requires tissue sampling for confirmation (cannot be made based on clinical symptoms or imaging alone)

The definitive diagnosis requires histopathological examination of endometrial tissue. Methods include:

• Endometrial Biopsy
• Dilation and Curettage
• Hysteroscopy

| Risk factor | Mechanism

| ----------- | ---------

| PCOS | Chronic anovulation

| Obesity | Peripheral estrogen production

| Nulliparity | Longer estrogen exposure

| Estrogen therapy | No progesterone opposition

| Type | Risk of cancer | | Treatment

| ---- | -------------- | --- | ---------

| Without atypia | Low risk (\~1–3%) | | Progestin therapy

| Atypical hyperplasia (EIN) | High risk (≈30%) | | Hysterectomy (definitive treatment)

B) No follow-up required ❌

Patients need regular follow-up and repeat biopsy.

C) Hysterectomy in all cases ❌

Reserved for atypical hyperplasia or completed family.

D) Majority regress without treatment ❌

Regression occurs mainly with progesterone therapy, not spontaneously.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which one of the following is the most important haematological condition to be ruled out while investigating a case of puberty menorrhagia?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Coagulation disorder

Puberty menorrhagia (adolescent heavy menstrual bleeding) is most commonly due to anovulatory cycles caused by an immature hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis. However, the most important hematological condition that must be ruled out is an underlying coagulation disorder, especially von Willebrand disease (vWD), the commonest inherited bleeding disorder.

Why not the other options?

• A. Anaemia: A consequence of heavy bleeding, not the underlying hematological disorder to be ruled out.
• C. G-6PD deficiency: Causes hemolytic anemia, not menorrhagia.
• D. Leukemia: Can cause bleeding due to thrombocytopenia but is much less common than coagulation disorders.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 16 weeks pregnant woman is evaluated using Quadruple test. Which of the following is not part of it?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Inhibin B

The quadruple test is a maternal serum screening test performed between 15–20 weeks of gestation to detect the risk of chromosomal abnormalities and neural tube defects.

Components of the Quadruple Test

| Marker | Source | Significance

| ------ | ------ | ------------

| AFP (Alpha-fetoprotein) | Fetal liver | Neural tube defects

| β-hCG | Placenta | Chromosomal abnormalities

| Unconjugated estriol (uE3) | Placenta + fetal adrenal | Fetal wellbeing

| Inhibin A | Placenta | Increased in Down syndrome

Role of Each Marker

| Marker | Down Syndrome Pattern

| ------ | ---------------------

| AFP | ↓

| β-hCG | ↑

| Estriol | ↓

| Inhibin A | ↑

• Inhibin B is mainly used in reproductive endocrinology and ovarian reserve assessment.
• It is not included in the quadruple test.

Only Inhibin A is used in the quadruple screening test.

Other Prenatal Screening Tests-

| Test | Markers | Trimester

| ---- | ------- | ---------

| Double test | β-hCG + PAPP-A | 1st trimester

| Triple test | AFP + β-hCG + Estriol | 2nd trimester

| Quadruple test | AFP + β-hCG + Estriol + Inhibin A | 2nd trimester

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 22-year-old pregnant woman at 13 weeks of gestation informs you about accidental exposure to radiation from a chest X-ray at 7 weeks of gestation. What should be the next step advised to her? (NEET PG 2020)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Continue pregnancy

Current evidence establishes that fetal risks — including malformations, growth restriction, and spontaneous abortion — are not significantly increased at radiation doses below 0.05 Gy (5 rads).

Importantly, diagnostic X-rays rarely deliver doses exceeding 0.1 Gy (10 rads). To put this into perspective, a dose of 0.1 Gy is equivalent to more than 1,000 chest X-rays — illustrating just how negligible the exposure from a single diagnostic study truly is.

Therefore, continuing the pregnancy is the most appropriate and reassuring advice for a woman who has undergone routine diagnostic imaging.

Why Other Options Are Incorrect:

• Option B — Terminate Pregnancy: Termination is unwarranted. The radiation dose from a single chest X-ray falls far below the threshold associated with increased fetal risk, making termination both unnecessary and unjustified.
• Option C — Pre-invasive Diagnostic Testing: Invasive diagnostic procedures carry their own procedural risks and are not indicated when the radiation exposure is this minimal.
• Option D — Chromosome Screening: The radiation dose from a standard chest X-ray does not meaningfully elevate the risk of chromosomal abnormalities, rendering routine chromosome screening unnecessary in this context.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 24-year-old woman at 16 weeks of gestation is found to have anemia on routine antenatal screening. She is otherwise asymptomatic, and laboratory evaluation is consistent with iron deficiency anemia. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for this patient?
options: 100 mg iron + 500 mcg folic acid once daily
60 mg iron + 500 mcg folic acid once daily
100 mg iron + 500 mcg folic acid twice daily
60 mg iron + 500 mcg folic acid twice daily
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 60 mg iron + 500 mcg folic acid twice daily

Iron deficiency anemia diagnosed during pregnancy should be treated with therapeutic oral iron, not the prophylactic dose. In a hemodynamically stable pregnant woman with mild-to-moderate iron deficiency anemia, the recommended treatment is 60 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid twice daily, along with dietary counseling and assessment of response.

Why not the other options?

• A. 100 mg iron + 500 mcg folic acid once daily: Not the standard recommended therapeutic regimen in national antenatal programs.
• B. 60 mg iron + 500 mcg folic acid once daily: This is the prophylactic dose used to prevent anemia during pregnancy.
• C. 100 mg iron + 500 mcg folic acid twice daily: Higher than the recommended routine therapeutic dose for uncomplicated iron deficiency anemia.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 24-year-old woman with a history of generalized tonic-clonic epilepsy has been on long-term antiepileptic therapy for the past 2 years. She reports progressive weight gain, irregular menstrual periods, excessive facial hair, and acne. Examination reveals central obesity, and pelvic ultrasonography shows bilaterally enlarged ovaries with multiple small peripheral follicles, consistent with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). Which of the following drugs is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Divalproex sodium

Valproate (divalproex sodium) is strongly associated with the development of PCOS, particularly in adolescent girls and women of reproductive age receiving long-term therapy.

Clinical features include:

• Weight gain
• Menstrual irregularities (oligomenorrhea/amenorrhea)
• Hyperandrogenism (acne, hirsutism)
• Polycystic ovaries on ultrasonography
• Reduced fertility

The mechanism is thought to involve weight gain, insulin resistance, and altered ovarian steroidogenesis, leading to increased androgen production.

Because of these endocrine and reproductive adverse effects, along with its high teratogenic risk (e.g., neural tube defects and impaired neurodevelopment), valproate should generally be avoided in women of childbearing potential whenever suitable alternatives are available.

Why not the other options?

• B. Lithium: Primarily used as a mood stabilizer in bipolar disorder. It commonly causes hypothyroidism, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, tremor, and weight gain, but PCOS is not a typical adverse effect.
• C. Lamotrigine: A preferred antiepileptic in women of reproductive age because it has minimal endocrine effects, causes little weight gain, and has a lower teratogenic risk than valproate.
• D. Carbamazepine: May cause diplopia, ataxia, hyponatremia (SIADH), leukopenia, and hepatic enzyme induction, but PCOS is not classically associated with its use.

| Drug | Important adverse effects

| ---- | -------------------------

| Valproate (Divalproex sodium) | Weight gain, PCOS, hyperandrogenism, teratogenicity, hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis

| Lamotrigine | Rash, Stevens–Johnson syndrome, relatively safe in pregnancy

| Carbamazepine | Diplopia, ataxia, SIADH, agranulocytosis, enzyme induction

| Lithium | Hypothyroidism, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, tremor, Ebstein anomaly (in pregnancy)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 28-year-old G5L4 with all 4-girl children presents at 18 weeks and asks for the sex of the child on ultrasound. This is her first antenatal visit. What should be done?
options: Do ultrasound for gestational age, check for abnormalities, check sex, and tell the mother
Do ultrasound for gestational age, check for abnormalities, check sex but don’t tell the mother
Do ultrasound for gestational age, check for abnormalities, don’t check the sex or reveal to the mother
Don’t do ultrasound, do ANC only
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Do ultrasound for gestational age, check for abnormalities, don’t check the sex or reveal to the mother

Sex determination during pregnancy is regulated by the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act. This law was introduced to prevent female feticide and sex-selective abortions.

PCPNDT Act Allows

Doctors can perform ultrasound for legitimate medical reasons:

| Allowed Indications | Purpose

| ------------------- | -------

| Gestational age assessment | Dating pregnancy

| Detection of fetal anomalies | Screening abnormalities

| Placental localization | Obstetric evaluation

However: Sex determination or disclosure is strictly prohibited.

At 18 weeks, ultrasound is important for:

• Dating pregnancy
• Fetal anomaly scan
• Placental position
• Fetal growth assessment

| Action | Legal Status

| ------ | ------------

| Determining fetal sex | ❌ Illegal

| Disclosing fetal sex | ❌ Illegal

| Advertising sex determination | ❌ Illegal

Penalty includes:

• Imprisonment up to 3 years
• Fine up to ₹50,000
• Cancellation of medical registration

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A lady who is 38 weeks pregnant comes to the OPD for a routine checkup. She has a history of normal twin delivery at term 4 years ago. What is her gravida and para score? (NEET PG 2020)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. G2P1

• The obstetric score is used to summarize the past obstetric history as follows:

o   G - Gravidity, denoting the total number of pregnancies, including the present one

o   P - Parity, denoting the total number of pregnancies crossing the period of viability

o   This includes both live births and stillbirths

o   The current pregnancy is not included

o   A - Abortus or the number of pregnancies that were lost for any reason, including induced abortions or miscarriages

o   L - Living children.
• The GTPAL system includes the following:

o   Gravida

o   Term (>37 weeks)

o   Preterm (20w - 36w 6d)

o   Abortions (<20 weeks)

o   Number of living children

Obstetric Score

• Gravidity: G2 (Second pregnancy)
• Parity: P1 (One previous pregnancy reaching viability, twins count as one para)

So, the correct obstetric score for this lady is G2P1.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A patient presents at 18 weeks with raised AFP, low Estrol, low HCG, low Inhibin-A. What is the next best step?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Anomaly scan

The next step is a detailed anomaly scan (targeted ultrasound) to look for structural fetal anomalies, especially neural tube defects. A targeted anomaly scan at 18–20 weeks can detect:

• Neural tube defects (spina bifida, anencephaly)
• Abdominal wall defects
• Cardiac anomalies
• Limb abnormalities

Because AFP elevation suggests structural defects, ultrasound is the first investigation.

The quadruple test is done between 15–20 weeks of pregnancy.

Markers included:

| Marker | Source

| ------ | ------

| AFP (Alpha-fetoprotein) | Fetal liver

| β-hCG | Placenta

| Unconjugated estriol (uE3) | Placenta + fetal adrenal

| Inhibin-A | Placenta

Different chromosomal or structural abnormalities produce characteristic patterns.

| Condition | AFP | hCG | Estriol | Inhibin A

| --------- | --- | --- | ------- | ---------

| Down syndrome | ↓ | ↑ | ↓ | ↑

| Trisomy 18 | ↓ | ↓ | ↓ | Normal/↓

| Neural tube defects | ↑ AFP | Normal | Normal | Normal

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman at 36 weeks of gestation presents to you with complaints of feeling light-headedness and dizziness when she lies on her back and feels relieved if she lies on her side or when walks. What is the most likely reason behind this?
options: Excessive venous pooling at the feet
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. IVC compression

This condition is known as Supine Hypotensive Syndrome. In late pregnancy, the enlarged uterus compresses the inferior vena cava when the woman lies on her back.

Gravid uterus compresses IVC

↓

Reduced venous return to heart

↓

Decreased cardiac output

↓

Maternal hypotension

↓

Dizziness and light-headedness

Common features include:

| Symptom | Reason

| ------- | ------

| Dizziness | Reduced cerebral perfusion

| Nausea | Hypotension

| Pallor | Decreased cardiac output

| Tachycardia | Compensatory response

It may also reduce uteroplacental blood flow.

Best management:

• Left lateral position

This shifts the uterus away from the vena cava.

Supine position → IVC compression

Left lateral position → venous return restored

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman attending an antenatal clinic expresses concern about dietary restrictions during pregnancy. She mentions avoiding a commonly consumed fruit due to a widespread cultural belief that it may harm the fetus or induce miscarriage. Which of the following fruits is most commonly avoided in India due to this misconception?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Papaya

Papaya is the fruit most commonly avoided during pregnancy in India due to the widespread misconception that it causes miscarriage. However, the evidence differs according to the ripeness of the fruit.

• Ripe papaya is safe to consume during pregnancy and is a good source of vitamins A, C, folate, and dietary fiber.
• Unripe (green) papaya contains latex, which is rich in papain and chymopapain. In large amounts, latex may stimulate uterine contractions, so unripe papaya should be avoided, especially in early pregnancy.

Why not the other options?

• A. Banana: Safe and nutritious during pregnancy.
• B. Mango: Safe in moderation; provides vitamin A and C.
• C. Orange: Safe and an excellent source of vitamin C and folate.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman doesn’t recall LMP. What is the best method to calculate period of gestation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Crown–rump length (CRL)

Crown–Rump Length is the most accurate ultrasound parameter for determining gestational age in early pregnancy.

| Feature | Explanation

| ------- | -----------

| Used in | First trimester (7–13 weeks)

| Accuracy | ± 3–5 days

| Purpose | Dating pregnancy

These measurements are used later in pregnancy.

| Parameter | Best Use

| --------- | --------

| BPD (Biparietal diameter) | Second trimester dating

| AC (Abdominal circumference) | Fetal growth assessment

| FL (Femur length) | Growth evaluation in third trimester

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman in her first trimester presents with lymphadenopathy and past history of toxoplasmosis. Current serology shows IgG Toxoplasma positive. What is the most appropriate advice?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Safe to continue pregnancy

Toxoplasmosis is a parasitic infection that can cause congenital infection if acquired during pregnancy. Transmission usually occurs via:

• Undercooked meat
• Cat feces
• Contaminated food or soil

| Serology Result | Meaning

| --------------- | -------

| IgG positive, IgM negative | Past infection

| IgM positive | Recent infection

| IgG negative | No immunity

In this case: IgG positive = past infection

This means the mother already developed protective immunity.

Therefore fetal infection risk is extremely low.

Classic triad:

| Feature | Explanation

| ------- | -----------

| Hydrocephalus | CSF obstruction

| Intracranial calcifications | Brain damage

| Chorioretinitis | Eye involvement

However, this occurs only if infection is acquired during pregnancy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman in her third trimester experiences dizziness while climbing stairs and is found to have low blood pressure. Which physiological change in pregnancy most likely explains this finding?
options: Increased plasma volume and increased peripheral vascular resistance
Decreased plasma volume and peripheral vascular resistance
Increased plasma volume and decreased peripheral vascular resistance
Decreased plasma volume and increased peripheral vascular resistance
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Increased plasma volume and decreased peripheral vascular resistance

Pregnancy is associated with an increase in plasma volume and a decrease in peripheral vascular resistance (PVR). Progesterone and other vasodilators (e.g., nitric oxide, relaxin) cause systemic vasodilation, leading to a fall in blood pressure despite an increase in cardiac output. This explains symptoms such as dizziness or lightheadedness, especially on exertion or with postural changes.

Why not the other options?

• A. Increased plasma volume and increased peripheral vascular resistance: PVR normally decreases, not increases, during pregnancy.
• B. Decreased plasma volume and peripheral vascular resistance: Plasma volume increases by 40–50% during pregnancy.
• D. Decreased plasma volume and increased peripheral vascular resistance: Opposite of the normal physiological adaptation of pregnancy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A primigravida comes to antenatal clinic at 6 weeks of pregnancy and mentions that she is a known case of epilepsy and is taking antiepileptic drug tablet Valproate since two years. What will be your next step regarding her medication?
options: Continue Valproate, increase the dose and explain her risk of teratogenicity
Stop Valproate and start her on Levetiracetam
Stop Valproate and start her on Phenytoin
Put her on polytherapy as one drug might not be effective
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Stop Valproate and start her on Levetiracetam

Sodium valproate is a potent teratogen and is associated with increased risks of:

• Neural tube defects
• Craniofacial abnormalities
• Cardiac defects
• Neurodevelopmental impairment

Therefore, in a woman who is pregnant, valproate should be avoided whenever an effective alternative is available. Levetiracetam is considered a safer alternative during pregnancy.

Why not the other options?

• A. Continue and increase Valproate dose, and explain risk of teratogenicity: Incorrect. Increasing the dose would increase fetal exposure and teratogenic risk.
• B. Stop Valproate and start Levetiracetam: Correct. Levetiracetam has a substantially more favorable pregnancy safety profile.
• C. Stop Valproate and start on Phenytoin: It also carries fetal risks, including fetal hydantoin syndrome, so it is not preferred over levetiracetam.
• D. Put on polytherapy: Generally avoided because monotherapy at the lowest effective dose is preferred during pregnancy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A primigravida comes to antenatal clinic for a routine antenatal visit. When should she be screened for diabetes in pregnancy?
options: At 24 to 28 weeks of pregnancy and/or repeat at 30 to 32 weeks of pregnancy
Early in pregnancy and/or repeat at 24 to 28 weeks of pregnancy
Early in pregnancy and/or repeat at 30 to 32 weeks of pregnancy
At 9 to 11 weeks of pregnancy and/or repeat at 30 to 32 weeks of pregnancy
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Early in pregnancy and/or repeat at 24 to 28 weeks of pregnancy

Diabetes in pregnancy should be screened early in pregnancy, particularly at the first antenatal contact, to detect pre-existing diabetes or early gestational diabetes.

If the initial test is normal, repeat screening at 24–28 weeks because insulin resistance increases substantially during this period.

Therefore:

Early pregnancy → repeat at 24–28 weeks → B.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A primigravida woman at 12 weeks comes for nutritional advice. Which is recommended?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Additional 300 kcal in 2nd trimester

Pregnancy requires additional calories to support:

• Fetal growth
• Placental development
• Maternal metabolic changes

According to nutritional guidelines, extra calories are mainly required from the second trimester onwards. No extra calories are needed in 1st trimester. Second trimester requires \~300–340 kcal extra; third trimester \~450 kcal. Hence option A matches recommendations. Some sources say Additional 300 kcal throughout pregnancy but the above information is more accurate.

| Nutrient | Requirement

| -------- | -----------

| Protein | \~60 g/day

| Iron | 27 mg/day

| Folic acid | 400–600 µg/day

| Calcium | 1000–1200 mg/day

| BMI Category | Weight gain

| ------------ | -----------

| Normal BMI | 11–16 kg

| Underweight | 12–18 kg

| Overweight | 7–11 kg

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Blood volume increases during pregnancy above non-pregnant level at 30–34 weeks:
options: Blood volume does not increase at all
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. By 40–50%

During normal pregnancy, maternal blood volume increases by approximately 40–50%, reaching its maximum at around 30–34 weeks of gestation. This physiological hypervolemia helps meet the increased metabolic demands of pregnancy and protects against blood loss during delivery.

Why not the other options?

• A. By 10–20%: Too low.
• B. By 25–30%: Less than the normal physiological increase.
• D. Blood volume does not increase at all: Incorrect.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Chadwick’s sign describes:
options: The dusky hue of the vestibule and anterior vaginal wall visible at about 8th week of pregnancy
Softening of cervix at 6th week of pregnancy
The abdominal and vaginal fingers apposed below the body of the uterus during bimanual examination
Regular and rhythmic uterine contraction which can be elicited during bimanual examination at 4–8 weeks of pregnancy
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. The dusky hue of the vestibule and anterior vaginal wall visible at about 8th week of pregnancy

Chadwick’s sign is one of the probable signs of pregnancy and refers to the bluish or violaceous discoloration (dusky hue) of the vulva, vestibule, vagina, and cervix due to increased pelvic vascularity and venous congestion. It becomes apparent at approximately 6–8 weeks of gestation.

Why not the other options?

• B. Softening of cervix at 6th week of pregnancy: This is Goodell’s sign.
• C. The abdominal and vaginal fingers apposed below the body of the uterus during bimanual examination: This is Hegar’s sign, caused by softening of the uterine isthmus.
• D. Regular and rhythmic uterine contraction elicited during bimanual examination at 4–8 weeks: This is Palmer’s sign.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Consider the following statements regarding chorionic villus sampling (CVS) used for prenatal diagnosis: 1. It is done between 15 to 20 weeks of gestation. 2. Amniotic fluid studies give earlier diagnosis of prenatal genetic conditions than chorionic villus sampling. 3. Limb reduction deformity is low when CVS is performed after 9 completed weeks of gestation. 4. Inj. Anti-D 50 microgram should be administered following this procedure in an Rh-negative mother. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 3 and 4 only

1. CVS is done between 15–20 weeks — Incorrect

• Chorionic villus sampling is usually performed at 10–13 weeks of gestation.
• Therefore, it provides earlier genetic diagnosis than amniocentesis.

2. Amniotic fluid studies give earlier diagnosis than CVS — Incorrect

• CVS provides earlier diagnosis, because it can be performed in the first trimester.
• Amniocentesis is generally performed from 15 weeks onward.

3. Limb reduction deformity is low when CVS is performed after 9 completed weeks — Correct

• CVS performed very early, particularly before 10 weeks, has been associated with an increased risk of limb-reduction defects.
• Hence, CVS should be performed after 9 completed weeks.

4. Anti-D 50 microgram after CVS in an Rh-negative mother — Correct

• CVS is an invasive procedure with potential fetomaternal hemorrhage.
• Anti-D immunoglobulin should be given to an unsensitized Rh-negative woman following the procedure; the dose used for early pregnancy procedures is typically 50 µg (250 IU).

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Consider the following statements regarding non-invasive prenatal screening (NIPS) for screening high-risk pregnancies for aneuploidies: 1. It is carried out on maternal blood. 2. It is done before 10 weeks gestation. 3. It has a negative predictive value of about 98%. 4. Invasive testing is needed for confirmation of a positive test. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 3 and 4

Non-Invasive Prenatal Screening (NIPS), also known as cell-free fetal DNA (cfDNA) testing, is a screening test for common fetal aneuploidies such as Trisomy 21 (Down syndrome), Trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), and Trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome). It analyzes cell-free fetal DNA in maternal blood, has very high sensitivity and negative predictive value, but a positive result must always be confirmed by invasive diagnostic testing.

Why is C correct?

• 1. It is carried out on maternal blood. ✅

• NIPS analyzes cell-free fetal DNA present in maternal plasma.

• 2. It is done before 10 weeks gestation. ❌

• NIPS is performed from 10 weeks of gestation onwards, when sufficient fetal DNA is present.

• 3. It has a negative predictive value of about 98%. ✅

• NIPS has an excellent negative predictive value (≈98–99% or higher), making it highly reliable for ruling out common aneuploidies.

• 4. Invasive testing is needed for confirmation of a positive test. ✅

• Since NIPS is a screening test, positive results require confirmation by chorionic villus sampling (CVS) or amniocentesis with fetal karyotyping or chromosomal microarray.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: During examination of a normal umbilical cord, which structures are expected?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 2 umbilical arteries and 1 umbilical vein

The Umbilical Cord normally contains three vessels embedded in Wharton’s jelly. Normal cord = 3 vessels: two arteries carrying deoxygenated blood from fetus to placenta, one vein carrying oxygenated blood back.

| Structure | Function

| --------- | --------

| 1 Umbilical vein | Carries oxygenated blood from placenta to fetus

| 2 Umbilical arteries | Carry deoxygenated blood from fetus to placenta

| Wharton’s jelly | Protects vessels

Sometimes one artery is absent, called Single Umbilical Artery.

Associated anomalies:

| System | Examples

| ------ | --------

| Renal | Renal agenesis

| Cardiac | Congenital heart disease

| Gastrointestinal | Atresia

SUA is commonly associated with congenital anomalies and IUGR.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: During pregnancy, iron supplementation is needed for:
options: All pregnant mothers from 16 weeks onwards
Only those pregnant mothers who have Hb <10 g%
Only those pregnant mothers who are not eating green vegetables
All pregnant mothers since 6 weeks of pregnancy
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. All pregnant mothers from 16 weeks onwards

Under the Government of India (Anemia Mukt Bharat/National Iron Plus Initiative), all pregnant women should receive routine iron and folic acid (IFA) supplementation starting in the second trimester (after 14–16 weeks), irrespective of their hemoglobin level, to prevent iron deficiency anemia.

Why not the other options?

• B. Only those pregnant mothers who have Hb <10 g%: Incorrect. IFA is prophylactic for all pregnant women, not only for anemic women.
• C. Only those pregnant mothers who are not eating green vegetables: Incorrect. Dietary intake alone is not sufficient.
• D. All pregnant mothers since 6 weeks of pregnancy: Incorrect. Routine supplementation is started after the first trimester.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: How does the Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) change in pre-eclampsia? (NEET PG 2016)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Decreases

In normal pregnancy, renal plasma flow and glomerular filtration rate (GFR) increase due to systemic vasodilation. However, in preeclampsia, GFR decreases because of widespread endothelial dysfunction and renal vasospasm.

Renal changes in preeclampsia:

• Vasoconstriction of renal vessels
• Reduced renal perfusion
• Glomerular endotheliosis (swelling of glomerular endothelial cells)
• Decreased GFR

Consequences:

• Reduced urine output
• Increased serum creatinine and uric acid
• Sodium and water retention
• Proteinuria due to glomerular injury

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Ideal weight gain during pregnancy for a woman with normal BMI should be:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 11–16 kg

For a woman with a normal pre-pregnancy BMI (18.5–24.9 kg/m²), the Institute of Medicine (IOM) recommends a total gestational weight gain of 11.5–16 kg. In MCQs, this is commonly rounded to 11–16 kg.

Why not the other options?

• A. 7 kg: Too low; appropriate only in selected obese women.
• C. 18 kg: Excessive for a woman with normal BMI.
• D. More than 18 kg: Not recommended due to increased maternal and fetal complications.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Patient experiences softening of the cervix in early pregnancy. This sign is called as?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Goodell

Goodell's sign refers to the softening of the cervix, which is observed during early pregnancy. This sign occurs due to increased vascularization and changes in the connective tissue of the cervix, making it feel softer compared to the non-pregnant state, where the cervix feels firm like the tip of the nose.

| Probable Signs | Description

| -------------- | -----------

| Goodell’s sign | Soft cervix

| Jacquemier’s
Chadwick’s sign | Bluish hue of ant vaginal wall

| Osiander’s sign | Increased pulsation felt through the lateral fornices

| Piscacek’s sign | Asymmetrical uterine enlargement in lateral implantation

| Hegar’s sign | On bimanual exam, the abdominal and vaginal finger appose below the body of the uterus

| Palmer’s sign | Rhythmic uterine contractions elicited on bimanual exam

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Primary cause of physiological dyspnea during pregnancy:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Progesterone stimulation of respiratory center

Progesterone:

• Stimulates respiratory center
• Increases tidal volume
• Causes mild hyperventilation

Pregnancy produces: chronic compensated respiratory alkalosis

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Testosterone helps in development of fetal organs. Which stimulates its production?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. HCG from placenta

Testosterone is produced by fetal Leydig cells in the testes and is essential for male genital differentiation. Human Chorionic Gonadotropin is secreted by the placenta during early pregnancy.

Mechanism:

Placenta releases hCG

↓

hCG acts like LH

↓

Stimulates fetal Leydig cells

↓

Testosterone production

Thus hCG acts as a substitute for LH in early fetal life.

Testosterone helps form:

| Structure | Development

| --------- | -----------

| Internal genitalia | Epididymis, vas deferens

| External genitalia | Penis, scrotum

| Secondary sexual differentiation | Later in puberty

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The clinical feature of physiological edema in pregnancy:
options: Is present on both lower limbs and abdomen
Is associated with cardiac or renal pathology
Is usually of moderate or severe grade
Disappears or markedly reduces on rest
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Disappears or markedly reduces on rest

Physiological edema is common in late pregnancy due to venous stasis from uterine compression of the inferior vena cava and pelvic veins, along with increased plasma volume. It is typically bilateral, mild, confined to the lower limbs, and improves with rest or leg elevation.

Why not the other options?

• A. Is present on both lower limbs and abdomen: Physiological edema is usually limited to the feet and ankles; generalized edema involving the abdomen is abnormal.
• B. Is associated with cardiac or renal pathology: Physiological edema occurs without underlying cardiac or renal disease.
• C. Is usually of moderate or severe grade: It is generally mild.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The softening of the lower uterine segment on bimanual examination is referred to as: (NEET PG 2016)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Hegar's Sign

Hegar sign refers to softening and compressibility of the lower uterine segment detected on bimanual examination during early pregnancy.

It usually appears Around 6–8 weeks of gestation

Mechanism: Increased vascularity and hormonal changes soften the uterine isthmus, making the cervix and uterine body feel separate on examination.

Other classic pregnancy signs:

• Chadwick sign → bluish discoloration of cervix/vagina
• Goodell sign → softening of the cervix
• Osiander sign → increased pulsation felt in lateral vaginal fornices

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: To prevent recurrence, expectant mothers with a previous fetus with neural tube defect should receive folic acid daily at the dose of:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 4 mg

Women with a previous pregnancy affected by a neural tube defect (NTD) are at high risk of recurrence. To reduce this risk, they should receive high-dose folic acid (4 mg/day), starting at least 1 month before conception and continuing through the first 12 weeks of pregnancy, when neural tube closure occurs.

Why are the other options incorrect?

• A. 4 μg: Far below the recommended daily requirement.
• B. 400 μg: Recommended for low-risk women planning pregnancy, not for women with a previous NTD-affected pregnancy. ⭐
• D. 400 mg: Excessively high and not recommended.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: To reduce the risk of neural tube defects in the baby, which of the following are recommended?
options: Folate supplements, from one month before conception to three months after
Folate supplements, from confirmation of pregnancy to the end of first trimester
Zinc supplements, from one month before conception to three months after
Zinc supplements, from confirmation of pregnancy to the end of first trimester
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Folate supplements, from one month before conception to three months after

Folic acid supplementation before conception and during early pregnancy significantly reduces the risk of neural tube defects (NTDs) such as spina bifida and anencephaly. Since neural tube closure occurs by the 28th day after conception, folic acid should be started before pregnancy.

Why not the other options?

• B. Folate supplements, from confirmation of pregnancy to the end of first trimester: Too late, as neural tube closure has usually already occurred.
• C. Zinc supplements, from one month before conception to three months after: Zinc is important for fetal growth but does not prevent neural tube defects.
• D. Zinc supplements, from confirmation of pregnancy to the end of first trimester: Zinc is not the recommended preventive supplement for NTDs.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is altered in thyroid profile throughout pregnancy? (NEET PG 2018)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Total T3 level

During pregnancy, estrogen increases hepatic production of thyroid-binding globulin (TBG), which increases the amount of protein-bound thyroid hormones in circulation. As a result:

• Total T3 and Total T4 levels increase
• Free T3 and Free T4 usually remain near normal
• TSH may be slightly reduced in early pregnancy due to hCG stimulation of TSH receptors

Key physiologic changes:

• ↑ Estrogen → ↑ TBG
• ↑ Bound thyroid hormone
• ↑ Total thyroid hormone levels

Despite elevated total thyroid hormone levels, pregnant women are usually euthyroid because free hormone levels remain relatively normal.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the first line of treatment of mastitis in a lactating mother? (NEET PG 2019)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Dicloxacillin

Lactational mastitis is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus infection entering through nipple cracks during breastfeeding.

First-line treatment: Dicloxacillin (anti-staphylococcal penicillin)

Clinical features:

• Breast pain and erythema
• Fever
• Local warmth and tenderness
• Flu-like symptoms

Important management principles:

• Continue breastfeeding or milk expression to prevent milk stasis
• Adequate analgesia and hydration
• Antibiotic therapy targeting gram-positive organisms

Why dicloxacillin is preferred:

• Effective against penicillinase-producing Staphylococcus aureus
• Common first-line oral therapy for uncomplicated mastitis

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the mean pH of the vagina during pregnancy? (NEET PG 2017)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 4

During pregnancy, the vaginal pH becomes more acidic, with a mean pH of approximately 4.

• Increased estrogen causes accumulation of glycogen in vaginal epithelial cells
• Lactobacilli metabolize glycogen to lactic acid
• This lowers vaginal pH

Functions of acidic vaginal pH:

• Inhibits growth of pathogenic organisms
• Maintains normal vaginal flora
• Protects against ascending infections

Normal vaginal pH in reproductive-age women: Approximately 3.8–4.5

Despite acidic pH, pregnancy increases susceptibility to candidal infection due to high glycogen content.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which infection contracted in pregnancy won't be teratogenic?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. HSV 2

Herpes simplex virus type 2 usually causes neonatal infection during delivery, not congenital malformations. Herpes Simplex Virus Type 2 mainly causes neonatal herpes infection during delivery through contact with infected genital lesions. Certain infections during pregnancy can cross the placenta and cause congenital anomalies in the fetus. These are classically remembered under TORCH Infections. Common teratogenic infections

| Infection | Fetal effects

| --------- | -------------

| Rubella | Cataracts, PDA, deafness
Classic triad:

• Cataracts
• Patent ductus arteriosus
• Sensorineural deafness

| CMV | Microcephaly, periventricular calcification, Hearing loss

| Varicella (Chickenpox) | Limb hypoplasia, skin scarring, Neurological defects

| Toxoplasmosis | Hydrocephalus, chorioretinitis

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following are advantages of state of haemodilution during pregnancy? 1. Optimum gaseous exchange between maternal and foetal circulation due to decreased blood viscosity. 2. Protection against adverse effect of supine and erect posture. 3. Protection against adverse effect of blood loss during delivery. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 2 and 3

Hemodilution is a normal physiological adaptation during pregnancy resulting from a greater increase in plasma volume (40–50%) than in red cell mass (20–30%), leading to physiological anemia of pregnancy. This adaptation is beneficial for both the mother and the fetus.

• 1. Optimum gaseous exchange between maternal and foetal circulation due to decreased blood viscosity. ✓

• Reduced blood viscosity improves uteroplacental blood flow, facilitating efficient oxygen and nutrient transfer to the fetus.

• 2. Protection against adverse effect of supine and erect posture. ✓

• The expanded plasma volume helps maintain venous return and cardiac output, reducing the hemodynamic effects of postural changes during pregnancy.

• 3. Protection against adverse effect of blood loss during delivery. ✓

• Increased circulating blood volume provides a physiological reserve, allowing pregnant women to better tolerate the 500–1000 mL blood loss that normally occurs during childbirth.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following are correct about endocrine changes in normal pregnancy? 1. Increase in levels of maternal serum iodine. 2. Increase in serum levels of Corticotropin-Releasing Hormone (CRH). 3. Increase in serum levels of aldosterone. 4. Increase in serum levels of ACTH. Select the answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 2, 3 and 4

• 1. Increase in levels of maternal serum iodine. ✗

• Maternal serum iodine levels do not increase. In fact, iodine requirement increases during pregnancy due to increased renal clearance and fetal thyroid hormone production, making pregnant women more prone to iodine deficiency if intake is inadequate.

• 2. Increase in serum levels of Corticotropin-Releasing Hormone (CRH). ✓

• The placenta secretes CRH, and maternal CRH levels rise progressively throughout pregnancy, especially in the third trimester.

• 3. Increase in serum levels of aldosterone. ✓

• Activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) leads to increased aldosterone, promoting sodium and water retention and expansion of plasma volume.

• 4. Increase in serum levels of ACTH. ✓

• Placental CRH stimulates increased maternal ACTH secretion, leading to elevated cortisol levels during pregnancy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following are probable signs of pregnancy? 1. Goodell sign 2. Hegar sign 3. Braxton Hicks sign 4. Sehrt sign
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 2 and 3

| Presumptive signs (Signs felt by patient herself) | Probable signs (Signs seen by doctor) | Positive signs (Definitive)

| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------

| Amenorrhoea | Goodell’s sign: Softening of cervix | Fetus seen on ultrasound

| Nausea/vomiting | Hegar’s sign: On bimanual palpation, vaginal and abdominal fingers touch each other. | Hearing fetal heart sounds

| Fatigue | Chadwick’s sign: Blue/violet discoloration of vagina and vulva (Jacquemier’s sign). | Palpation of fetal parts

| Increased urinary frequency (T1 & T3) | Osiander’s sign: Pulsations felt in lateral fornix of vagina. | Fetal skeleton seen on X-ray

| Breast changes | Palmer’s sign:

• Rhythmic painless uterine contractions.
• Not felt by patient.

|

| Quickening | Piskacek’s sign: Unequal growth of uterus |

| | Positive pregnancy test |

| | Increased pigmentation |

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following investigative modalities is generally considered unsafe for use during pregnancy?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. CT scan

CT scan (Computed Tomography) uses ionizing radiation.

Risks during pregnancy

Ionizing radiation can cause:

• Teratogenic effects
• Fetal growth restriction
• Microcephaly
• Childhood malignancy risk

Risk is greatest during:

• 2–15 weeks gestation

CT scan is avoided in pregnancy unless absolutely necessary (life-saving indication).

Ultrasound uses high-frequency sound waves, not radiation.

Therefore, it is safe in pregnancy.

Uses include:

• Fetal growth assessment
• Dating pregnancy
• Congenital anomaly screening

Most commonly used imaging modality in obstetrics.

Doppler ultrasound evaluates blood flow in fetal and placental vessels.

Common uses:

• Umbilical artery Doppler
• Middle cerebral artery Doppler
• Detect fetal growth restriction (FGR)

It also uses sound waves, so it is considered safe.

MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) uses magnetic fields and radio waves, not ionizing radiation.

It is generally considered safe during pregnancy, especially after the first trimester.

Uses in obstetrics:

• Evaluation of placenta accreta spectrum
• Fetal anomalies
• Maternal pelvic pathology

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is least likely to occur during a normal pregnancy? (NEET PG 2016)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Elevated systolic blood pressure

Normal pregnancy is associated with major cardiovascular adaptations to meet increased maternal and fetal metabolic demands. Physiologic cardiovascular changes in pregnancy:

• Increased heart rate
• Increased cardiac output
• Increased blood volume
• Decreased systemic vascular resistance

Because systemic vascular resistance falls due to progesterone-mediated vasodilation and placental circulation, blood pressure usually:

• Decreases slightly during mid-pregnancy
• Returns toward baseline near term

Therefore, elevated systolic blood pressure is not a normal finding in pregnancy and may suggest hypertensive disorders such as gestational hypertension or preeclampsia.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is not considered as a factor for a high-risk pregnancy? (NEET PG 2018)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Previous manual removal of placenta

Previous manual removal of the placenta does not automatically categorize a subsequent pregnancy as high-risk. High-risk pregnancies are characterized by various factors that may complicate the pregnancy or pose risks to the mother and fetus. These factors include existing health conditions, certain lifestyle factors, age-related risks, and specific pregnancy conditions.

High-risk pregnancy factors according to the NIH include:

1. Existing health conditions:

• Hypertension
• Diabetes
• Autoimmune diseases
• PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome)
• Thyroid disorders
• Obesity
• HIV
• Anemia
• Uterine fibroids

2. Age:

• Adolescence
• First-time pregnancy at age >35 years

3. Lifestyle factors:

• Alcohol consumption
• Smoking
• Drug use

4. Pregnancy conditions:

• Multiple pregnancy
• Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM)
• Pre-eclampsia
• Previous preterm birth
• Congenital or chromosomal anomalies
• Polyhydramnios or oligohydramnios
• Rh iso-immunization
• Antepartum hemorrhage
• Fetal growth restriction

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is true about vaginal changes in a normal pregnancy? (NEET PG 2019)
options: Increased glycogen metabolism in the epithelium
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Increased glycogen metabolism in the epithelium

During pregnancy, elevated estrogen levels increase glycogen content in the vaginal epithelium. Lactobacilli metabolize this glycogen to lactic acid, leading to:

• Increased glycogen metabolism
• Increased Lactobacilli
• Acidic vaginal pH (around 4–4.5)

These changes help:

• Maintain normal vaginal flora
• Protect against pathogenic infections

Why other options are incorrect:

• Lactobacilli increase, not decrease
• Vaginal pH becomes acidic, not >6.8
• Vaginal epithelium becomes thickened and congested, not thinned

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding audit in Obstetrics and Gynaecology? I. It can replace the out of date clinical practices with better ones. II. It is an efficient educational tool. III. It should be based on scientific evidences with facts and figures. IV. It is not labour-intensive. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. I, II and III

A clinical audit is a systematic process of reviewing clinical practice against established standards to improve the quality of patient care. It identifies deficiencies in current practice, implements changes based on evidence-based guidelines, and reassesses outcomes to ensure continuous quality improvement. The following statements are correct:

• I. It can replace the out-of-date clinical practices with better ones: Clinical audit identifies gaps between current practice and accepted standards, facilitating the implementation of evidence-based improvements.
• II. It is an efficient educational tool: Audit promotes continuous learning by providing feedback to healthcare professionals and encouraging adherence to best practices.
• III. It should be based on scientific evidence with facts and figures: Clinical audit compares practice against predefined evidence-based standards using measurable outcomes and objective data.

Why is IV incorrect?

• IV. It is not labour-intensive: Clinical audit is labour-intensive and time-consuming, requiring:

• Data collection
• Data analysis
• Implementation of changes
• Re-audit to complete the audit cycle

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct with respect to antenatal USG examination? 1. It helps in detecting gross fetal anomalies. 2. It helps in identifying multiple pregnancies. 3. It helps in identifying viable pregnancy. 4. Best dating is possible with third trimester ultrasound scan. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 2 and 3 only

Antenatal ultrasonography (USG) is an essential investigation in pregnancy. It is used to confirm viability, determine the number of fetuses, detect fetal anomalies, assess gestational age, placental location, and amniotic fluid volume.

Why are the statements correct/incorrect?

• 1. It helps in detecting gross fetal anomalies. Correct.
• 2. It helps in identifying multiple pregnancies. Correct.
• 3. It helps in identifying viable pregnancy. Correct (demonstration of fetal cardiac activity).
• 4. Best dating is possible with third trimester ultrasound scan. Incorrect. First-trimester ultrasound (CRL measurement) provides the most accurate dating of pregnancy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding physiological changes in pregnancy is incorrect?
options: Increase SBP and DBP at 6 weeks
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Increase SBP and DBP at 6 weeks

Cardiovascular Changes in Pregnancy-

During pregnancy:

• Systemic vascular resistance decreases
• Cardiac output increases
• Blood pressure falls in early pregnancy

| Trimester | Blood Pressure

| --------- | --------------

| Early pregnancy | ↓ BP

| Mid pregnancy | Lowest BP

| Late pregnancy | Returns toward baseline

Glucose Metabolism in Pregnancy- Pregnancy is considered a diabetogenic state.

Hormones responsible include:

• Human placental lactogen (hPL)
• Progesterone
• Cortisol
• Estrogen

These hormones cause peripheral insulin resistance.

Hematological changes during pregnancy:

• RBC mass increases by \~20–30%
• Plasma volume increases by \~40–50%

This leads to physiological anemia of pregnancy.

| Parameter | Change

| --------- | ------

| RBC mass | ↑

| Plasma volume | ↑↑

| Hemoglobin concentration | ↓

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 24-year-old lactating female with an 18-month-old child comes with a history of irregular, heavy bleeding seeking contraceptive advice. Which is the contraceptive of choice?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Mala N

Mala N is a combined oral contraceptive (COC) commonly used in national family planning programs.

| Factor | Explanation

| ------ | -----------

| Child age 18 months | Lactation no longer contraindicates COCs

| Heavy bleeding | COCs reduce menstrual bleeding

| Irregular cycles | COCs regulate menstruation

Mechanism:

Estrogen + Progesterone

↓

Suppress FSH and LH

↓

Inhibit ovulation

↓

Endometrial stabilization

↓

Reduced menstrual bleeding

Progestasert (progesterone IUD) / Copper T/ progesterone implant are not ideal in someone already having bleeding problems. Mala N (combined oral contraceptive) is not recommended in a lactating female as estrogen affects the milk output.  Some sources say an 18-month period of lactation justifies COCPs since the child would be on complementary feeds. The best answer hence remains controversial.

A) Progestasert

• Rarely used now
• Less effective than modern options.

B) Copper-T 380A

• Highly effective contraception
• May increase menstrual bleeding, which would worsen symptoms.

D) Norethisterone enanthate depot

• Can cause irregular bleeding
• Not ideal when patient already has heavy irregular bleeding.

Contraception in Lactating Women

| Time after delivery | Recommended contraception

| ------------------- | -------------------------

| <6 weeks | Progestin-only methods

| 6 weeks–6 months | POPs, IUCD

| >6 months | Combined OCPs allowed

Since the child is 18 months old, COCs are safe.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 25-year-old newly married female on liver enzyme inducers is requesting contraceptive advice in a family planning clinic. Which of the following would be the most reliable method of contraception for her?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Depo-Provera injection

Women taking liver enzyme-inducing drugs (e.g., phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, primidone, rifampicin, rifabutin) have reduced efficacy of many hormonal contraceptives because these drugs induce CYP450 enzymes, increasing the metabolism of estrogen and progestins. Depot Medroxyprogesterone Acetate (DMPA; Depo-Provera) is not significantly affected by enzyme induction and remains a highly effective contraceptive.

DMPA 150 mg IM every 3 months provides reliable contraception and maintains efficacy despite concomitant use of liver enzyme-inducing medications.

Why are the other options incorrect?

• A.  Combined oral contraceptive pill: Hepatic enzyme inducers reduce plasma concentrations of estrogen and progestin, increasing the risk of contraceptive failure.
• B. Male condom: Although useful for STI prevention, condoms have a higher typical-use failure rate than DMPA.
• C. Diaphragm: User-dependent method with lower contraceptive efficacy than DMPA.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
