questions.text: A 26-year-old conceives on the IUCD. She wants to continue pregnancy. The IUCD threads are visible. What would be the next best step?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Remove the IUCD gently

If pregnancy occurs with an IUCD and threads are visible, removal is recommended because the device increases risk of:

| Complication | Reason

| ------------ | ------

| Miscarriage | Intrauterine irritation

| Infection | Foreign body

| Preterm labor | Inflammation

If pregnancy continues with an IUCD in situ, the safest approach is gentle removal if strings are visible. Leaving it increases risks of preterm labor, infection, and miscarriage. Removal slightly increases miscarriage risk but is still preferred.

Removal with Shirodkar hook indicated for CuT when threads are not visible.

| Situation | Management

| --------- | ----------

| Threads visible | Remove IUCD

| Threads not visible | Leave IUCD in situ

Attempting blind removal may cause abortion.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 28 year old female is started on Oral Contraceptive Pills. She presents after 2 weeks with a history of missing 4 tablets on different days in the first 2 weeks of the cycle. What will you advise her? (NEET PG 2021)
options: Discontinue the packet and start an alternate method of contraception
Take 4 tablets the next day, continue the remaining packet, use additional contraception (condom) and give Emergency Pill if h/o intercourse in the last 72 h
Take the next pill as soon as possible, continue the remaining packet, use additional contraception (condom) and give Emergency Pill if h/o intercourse in the last 72 h
Take the next pill as soon as possible and continue the remaining tablets
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Take the next pill as soon as possible, continue the remaining packet, use additional contraception (condom) and give Emergency Pill if h/o intercourse in the last 72 h

When ≥2 active oral contraceptive pills are missed during the first 2 weeks of the cycle, contraceptive protection decreases significantly.

Recommended management:

• Take the next active pill as soon as possible
• Continue the remaining pills as scheduled
• Use backup contraception (eg, condoms) for the next 7 days
• Give emergency contraception if unprotected intercourse occurred within the previous 72 hours

Multiple missed pills early in the cycle increase the risk of ovulation and unintended pregnancy

Patients should not:

• Stop the entire packet unnecessarily
• Take multiple missed pills together after several missed doses

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 30-year-old woman presents to the gynecology outpatient department because she is unable to feel the thread of her IUCD. She had the IUCD inserted 6 months ago. On per speculum examination, the IUCD strings are not visible at the external cervical os. She is asymptomatic. What is the immediate next best step in management?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Perform transvaginal ultrasonography

Missing IUCD threads are a common reason for gynecological consultation. In an asymptomatic woman, the first step is to confirm the location of the IUCD using transvaginal ultrasonography (TVS).

Possible causes of missing threads include:

• Retraction of the threads into the cervical canal or uterine cavity (most common)
• Expulsion of the IUCD
• Uterine perforation with migration into the peritoneal cavity
• Broken threads

Management Based on TVS

• IUCD in correct position → Reassure; remove later with retrieval hook/forceps if required.
• IUCD not seen in uterus → Perform X-ray abdomen/pelvis to look for perforation or confirm expulsion.
• Embedded IUCD → Hysteroscopic removal.

Why not the other options?

• A. Reinsert a new IUCD: Incorrect before confirming whether the previous IUCD is still present.
• B. Perform hysteroscopy: Reserved if TVS confirms an intrauterine retained/embedded IUCD that cannot be retrieved.
• D. Press the cervix/uterus to remove: Not an accepted management step.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 32-year-old woman, P2L2, presents for family planning counseling. She reports that she does not desire any future pregnancies and is seeking a permanent method of contraception. Which of the following is the most appropriate sterilization method for this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Modified Pomeroy's method

Modified Pomeroy’s method is the most commonly performed female sterilization procedure, especially in the postpartum period, because it is simple, effective, and associated with a low failure rate.

Principle of Modified Pomeroy’s Method

• A loop of the mid-isthmic fallopian tube is elevated.
• The base of the loop is ligated with an absorbable suture.
• The loop is excised, leaving separated tubal ends after the suture is absorbed, minimizing the chance of recanalization.

Why not the other options?

• B. Partial salpingectomy: A broader term describing removal of part of the tube; Modified Pomeroy is the standard technique used for sterilization.
• C. Salpingostomy: Creates an opening in the tube; used for fertility-preserving management of ectopic pregnancy, not contraception.
• D. Salpingectomy: Complete removal of the fallopian tube. Although bilateral salpingectomy is increasingly performed for ovarian cancer risk reduction, the classical FMGE/NEET PG answer for female sterilization remains Modified Pomeroy’s method.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 33-year-old female patient comes with complaints of menorrhagia for the past 3 months. The duration and regularity of her menstrual cycles are normal. Non-hormonal management has been tried without success. What is the most appropriate next step? (NEET PG 2020)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Hormonal therapy

When non-hormonal treatments have failed, the next appropriate step in managing menorrhagia is hormonal therapy. This includes:

• Combined Oral Contraceptive Pills (COCPs) — regulate the menstrual cycle and reduce blood loss
• Progesterone-only devices — such as the Levonorgestrel-releasing Intrauterine System (LNG-IUS), which is highly effective in reducing menstrual blood flow

It is important to note that first-line management of menorrhagia begins with non-hormonal options, specifically:

• NSAIDs — reduce prostaglandin-mediated blood loss
• Tranexamic acid — an antifibrinolytic agent that limits excessive bleeding

Why Other Options Are Incorrect

•

Option A — Uterine Artery Embolization (UAE): This is an interventional/surgical option reserved for cases where both non-hormonal and hormonal treatments have proven ineffective.

•

Option B — Endometrial Ablation: A surgical modality that should only be considered after hormonal therapy has been attempted and failed.

•

Option D — Hysterectomy: Represents the last resort in menorrhagia management, considered only when all other treatment options have been exhausted or are contraindicated.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 35-year-old woman with a history of chronic hypertension presents for contraceptive counseling. She is otherwise healthy and wishes to start a reliable method of contraception. Which of the following contraceptive methods is contraindicated in this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. OCP

Combined oral contraceptive pills (COCs) are contraindicated in women with chronic hypertension, particularly if blood pressure is ≥160/100 mmHg or there is associated vascular disease, because estrogen increases the risk of hypertension, stroke, myocardial infarction, and venous thromboembolism.

Why not the other options?

• A. Barrier methods: Safe in women with hypertension; no cardiovascular risk.
• B. Copper-T (CuT): Safe and highly effective; hypertension is not a contraindication.
• C. LNG-IUS: Progestin-only intrauterine system is safe in women with hypertension as systemic hormone levels are minimal.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 35-year-old woman with a history of LNG-IUS insertion for contraception presents with irregular bleeding and requests removal of the device. What is the next best step in management?
options: Reassure her and continue the method
Give high-dose estrogen to stop the bleeding
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Reassure her and continue the method

Irregular or unscheduled bleeding is a common side effect during the first 3–6 months after insertion of a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS). Patients should be counseled and reassured that the bleeding pattern usually improves over time, with many women eventually developing light periods or amenorrhea.

Why not the other options?

• A. Remove the IUS: Not indicated unless bleeding is persistent, unacceptable after adequate counseling, or another pathology is identified.
• C. Switch to OCPs: Unnecessary as first-line management; reassurance is usually sufficient.
• D. High-dose estrogen to stop bleeding: Not routinely recommended for LNG-IUS–related irregular bleeding.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A female patient taking DMPA came 14 days late. What should be advised to her?
options: Do UPT and then give DMPA
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Give DMPA, no backup required

Depot Medroxyprogesterone Acetate is a progestin-only injectable contraceptive.

It is commonly given as:

• 150 mg intramuscular injection
• Every 3 months (12 weeks)

The WHO and CDC guidelines allow a grace period of up to 4 weeks after the scheduled injection (can be given upto 2 weeks earlier than scheduled date)

| Timing | Recommendation

| ------ | --------------

| On time (12 weeks) | Give injection

| ≤4 weeks late | Give injection immediately, no backup needed

| >4 weeks late | Pregnancy test + backup contraception

Since this patient is 14 days late, she is within the grace period.

Advantages of DMPA

| Benefit | Explanation

| ------- | -----------

| Highly effective | <1% failure

| Long acting | 3 months protection

| Safe in breastfeeding | Progestin-only

| Decreases menstrual bleeding | Amenorrhea common

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: According to the WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC-1), in which of the following conditions can combined oral contraceptives (OCPs) be safely used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. HIV

Combined Oral Contraceptive Pills contain:

• Estrogen (Ethinyl estradiol)
• Progestin (e.g., Levonorgestrel)

They are widely used for birth control and menstrual regulation.

Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) categorizes the safety of contraceptive methods based on underlying medical conditions. The MEC classification system has four categories:

●        MEC 1: Method is absolutely safe for use

●        MEC 2: Safe for use but has certain limitations (benefits outweigh risks)

●        MEC 3: Relatively contraindicated (risks outweigh benefits)

●        MEC 4: Absolutely contraindicated (method should not be given)

HIV infection without complications is classified as MEC 1 for combined oral contraceptive pills.

For HIV-positive women:

COCs are MEC-1 (safe to use).

Reasons:

• Do not worsen HIV disease progression
• Do not significantly increase viral replication

Diabetes Mellitus - Often MEC-2 or MEC-3, especially with vascular complications.

Hyperlipidemia - COCs may increase lipid levels, so usually MEC-2 or MEC-3.

Hypertension - Estrogen-containing pills may increase thrombotic risk, so classified as MEC-3 or MEC-4 depending on severity.

Benefits of COCs

| Benefit | Effect

| ------- | ------

| Regulates menstrual cycles | Reduces irregular bleeding

| Decreases dysmenorrhea | Less painful periods

| Reduces risk of ovarian cancer | Long-term protection

| Reduces risk of endometrial cancer | Endometrial suppression

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: After male sterilization, additional contraceptive protection is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Needed for 2 to 3 months

Male sterilization (vasectomy) is a highly effective permanent method of contraception. However, it is not immediately effective, as viable sperm remain in the vas deferens and seminal vesicles for several weeks after the procedure.

Therefore, additional contraception is required for 2–3 months (or until semen analysis confirms azoospermia).

• A. Needed for 1 month ✗: Too short; viable sperm may still be present.
• B. Needed for 1–2 months ✗: Not routinely recommended.
• C. Needed for 2–3 months ✓: Correct. Continue another contraceptive method until azoospermia is documented.
• D. Not needed ✗: Incorrect, as vasectomy is not immediately effective.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: After undergoing vasectomy, how many ejaculations and months are required for a man to become sterile?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 20 ejaculations and 3 months

After vasectomy, sperm already present in the reproductive tract must be cleared before sterility is achieved.

Traditionally, men are advised to use another contraceptive method until:

• At least 20 ejaculations, and
• Approximately 3 months have passed.

Semen analysis should be performed to confirm azoospermia (or acceptable rare non-motile sperm) before discontinuing contraception.

Therefore, the correct answer is C. 20 ejaculations and 3 months.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All of the following are contraceptive methods used post-coitus except: (NEET PG 2020)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Danazol

Emergency contraception (postcoital contraception) is used to prevent pregnancy after unprotected intercourse.

Methods used for emergency contraception include:

• High-dose combined estrogen-progestin pills (Yuzpe method)
• Levonorgestrel pills
• Mifepristone (RU-486)
• Copper IUCD (CuT 200/CuT 380A)

Copper IUCD is one of the most effective methods when inserted within 5 days of unprotected intercourse. Danazol is not used for emergency contraception. It is a synthetic androgen primarily used for:

• Endometriosis
• Fibrocystic breast disease
• Hereditary angioedema

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Among the following intra-uterine contraceptive devices, which of the following are included in second generation IUDs? 1. Lippes Loop 2. Copper T-200 3. LNG-20 (Mirena) 4. Copper-T 380 A Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 2 and 4 only

Second-generation IUDs are copper-bearing intrauterine devices, which are more effective than inert IUDs because copper impairs sperm motility and fertilization.

Why are the statements correct/incorrect?

• 1. Lippes Loop❌: First-generation (inert/non-medicated) IUD.
• 2. Copper T-200✔️: Second-generation (copper-bearing) IUD.
• 3. LNG-20 (Mirena)❌: Third-generation (hormone-releasing) IUD.
• 4. Copper T-380A✔️: Second-generation (copper-bearing) IUD.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Combined oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) provide protection against several cancers. Which of the following cancers is not protected against by their use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Cervical cancer

Combined Oral Contraceptive Pills are widely used for contraception and also provide non-contraceptive health benefits. They work by:

• Suppressing ovulation
• Thickening cervical mucus
• Altering endometrium

Long-term use of OCPs reduces the risk of several cancers.

| Cancer | Effect

| ------ | ------

| Endometrial Cancer | ↓ Risk

| Ovarian Cancer | ↓ Risk

| Colorectal Cancer | ↓ Risk

Mechanisms include suppression of ovulation and reduced endometrial proliferation.

Cervical Cancer is not protected against by OCP use.

In fact:

• Long-term OCP use may slightly increase cervical cancer risk in women with persistent HPV infection.

Reason:

HPV infection

↓

Persistent viral replication

↓

Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia

↓

Cervical cancer

Hormonal exposure may enhance HPV persistence.

OCP protects → Ovarian + Endometrial + Colon

OCP does NOT protect → Cervical cancer

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Consider the following conditions in a woman of reproductive age group: 1. Diabetes with retinopathy 2. Age 36 years, non-smoker 3. Liver adenoma 4. History of stroke Which of the above are absolute contraindications for using combined oral contraceptive pills?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 3 and 4

The following are contraindications to combined oral contraceptive pills (COCs):

1. Diabetes with retinopathy — Correct

• Complicated diabetes with retinopathy, nephropathy or neuropathy is a contraindication/major restriction to combined hormonal contraception.

2. Age 36 years, non-smoker — Incorrect

• Age ≥35 years alone, in a nonsmoker, is not an absolute contraindication.
• The major concern is age ≥35 years with smoking, particularly heavy smoking.

3. Liver adenoma — Correct

• Estrogen-containing contraceptives are contraindicated because of the risk of growth/complications of hepatocellular adenoma.

4. History of stroke — Correct

• Previous stroke/cerebrovascular disease is an absolute contraindication to combined hormonal contraception.

Therefore:

1 + 3 + 4 → C.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Consider the following in respect of Ormeloxifene: 1. It is a research product of Central Drug Research Institute, Lucknow. 2. It is a steroidal compound. 3. It is a potent antiestrogen with weak estrogenic properties. 4. It does not inhibit ovulation. Which of the above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1, 3 and 4

Ormeloxifene (Centchroman/Chhaya) is a Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulator (SERM) and a non-steroidal oral contraceptive developed in India. It is included in the National Family Planning Programme under the brand name Chhaya.

• 1. It is a research product of Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI)\, Lucknow. ✅

• Ormeloxifene was developed by the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow.

• 3. It is a potent antiestrogen with weak estrogenic properties. ✅

• It acts as an antiestrogen on the uterus and has weak estrogenic effects on bone and other tissues.

• 4. It does not inhibit ovulation. ✅

• Its primary contraceptive action is preventing implantation by altering endometrial receptivity and accelerating ovum transport.
• Ovulation is usually not inhibited.

Incorrect statement:

• 2. It is a steroidal compound. ❌

• Ormeloxifene is a non-steroidal SERM.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Consider the following statements regarding LNG-20 (Mirena): 1. It is a T-shaped IUD filled with natural hormone progesterone. 2. It is associated with a low pregnancy rate (2 per 1000 women). 3. It is associated with a large number of ectopic pregnancies. 4. It is associated with lower menstrual blood loss as compared to copper IUDs. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 2 and 4 only

LNG-20 (Mirena) is a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) that releases 20 µg of levonorgestrel per day. It provides highly effective long-term reversible contraception and has several non-contraceptive therapeutic benefits, particularly in women with heavy menstrual bleeding.

• 1. It is a T-shaped IUD filled with natural hormone progesterone. ✗

• Mirena contains levonorgestrel, a synthetic progestin, not natural progesterone.

• 2. It is associated with a low pregnancy rate (≈2 per 1000 women). ✓

• Mirena has a failure rate of about 0.2% per year (2 per 1000 women), making it one of the most effective reversible contraceptives.

• 3. It is associated with a large number of ectopic pregnancies. ✗

• Mirena reduces the overall risk of ectopic pregnancy because it is highly effective at preventing pregnancy.
• However, if pregnancy occurs with Mirena in situ, the likelihood that it is ectopic is relatively higher, but the absolute risk remains very low.

• 4. It is associated with lower menstrual blood loss as compared to copper IUDs. ✓

• Levonorgestrel causes endometrial atrophy, significantly reducing menstrual blood loss and dysmenorrhea.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: If 100 couples have used a method for a period of 2 years and have resulted in 10 pregnancies, what will be the effectiveness of the method used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. High

100 couples used the contraceptive method for 2 years:

• Total exposure = 100 × 2 = 200 couple-years
• Pregnancies = 10

Pregnancy rate:

= (10 / 200) × 100

= 5 pregnancies per 100 couple-years

Therefore, the method has an effectiveness of approximately: 100 − 5 = 95%

So, the method is considered highly effective.

Screenshot from Dutta for reference:

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: In non-lactating mothers, after delivery, ovulation:
options: May occur as early as 2 weeks
May occur as early as 4 weeks
May occur as early as 6 weeks
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. May occur as early as 2 weeks

In non-lactating women, ovarian function returns rapidly after childbirth. Ovulation may occur as early as 25–27 days postpartum (about 3–4 weeks), and rarely as early as 2 weeks, making early contraception important.

Why not the other options?

• B. May occur as early as 4 weeks: Ovulation can occur even earlier.
• C. May occur as early as 6 weeks: Too late as the earliest possible time.
• D. Is unusual before 6 weeks: Incorrect. Ovulation may precede the first postpartum menstruation

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: In postpartum period, the intrauterine device may be inserted in the woman:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Up to 48 hours of delivery

A postpartum intrauterine contraceptive device (PPIUCD) can be inserted:

• Post-placental: within 10 minutes of placental delivery.
• Immediate postpartum: after 10 minutes but within 48 hours of delivery.
• Intracesarean: after placental removal and before closure of the uterine incision.
• If >48 hours postpartum, interval insertion is generally deferred until ≥6 weeks postpartum.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Injectable medroxyprogesterone IP 150 mg/mL contraceptive injection is available in Family Health Programme of the Government of India under the name:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Antara

Antara is the Government of India’s injectable contraceptive program under the National Family Health Programme. It contains Depot Medroxyprogesterone Acetate (DMPA) 150 mg/mL, administered as an intramuscular injection every 3 months (13 weeks). It is a highly effective, reversible, long-acting progestin-only contraceptive.

Why are the other options incorrect?

• A.  Saheli: Saheli (Centchroman/Ormeloxifene) is a non-hormonal oral contraceptive developed by CDRI, Lucknow.
• B. Sayana Press: Sayana Press contains DMPA 104 mg for subcutaneous injection, not the 150 mg IM formulation used in the Government of India’s Antara program.
• D. Sahiba: Not a Government of India contraceptive program.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: IUCD can be inserted after delivery till?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 48 hrs

Postpartum IUCD insertion is safe within 10 minutes up to 48 hours after delivery. The period between 48 hours–6 weeks should be avoided due to highest expulsion risk. Insertion after 6 weeks is classified as interval IUCD placement.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Laparoscopic tubal sterilization can be done after:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 6 weeks of delivery

Laparoscopic tubal sterilization is generally performed as an interval sterilization, i.e., after the uterus and reproductive organs have returned closer to their normal non-pregnant state.

• Immediate postpartum sterilization → usually performed by mini-laparotomy, not laparoscopy.
• Laparoscopic interval sterilization → typically performed after 6 weeks postpartum.

Therefore, the correct answer is D. 6 weeks of delivery.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Steroidal contraceptives available in the basket of contraceptive choice from Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India are:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Monophasic

The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (MoHFW), Government of India provides monophasic combined oral contraceptive pills (COCs) in the national family planning programme.

The commonly supplied pill is Mala-N/Mala-D, which contains a fixed dose of estrogen and progestin in all 21 active tablets, making it a monophasic preparation.

• A. Monophasic ✓: Correct. The estrogen and progestin dose remains constant throughout the cycle.
• B. Biphasic ✗: Hormone doses vary in two phases; not supplied under the national programme.
• C. Triphasic ✗: Hormone doses vary in three phases; not part of the Government of India’s contraceptive basket.
• D. Estrogen-only pills ✗: Estrogen-only contraceptive pills are not used because of the high risk of endometrial hyperplasia and other adverse effects.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The most common site of tubal ligation and the reason for ligation at this site is?
options: Isthmus because of more uniform muscle thickness
Ampulla because of more circular muscles than longitudinal muscles
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Isthmus because of more uniform muscle thickness

●        The most common site of tubal ligation is the isthmus.

●        The key reason is that the isthmus has a thick, uniform muscular wall, which:

o    Allows secure ligation

o    Reduces failure and recanalization

o    Makes crushing, cutting, and tying more effective

Although the isthmus is also narrowest part of FT, the classically accepted reason in exams is uniform muscle thickness, not narrowness.

Common Techniques of Tubal Ligation

| Technique | Method

| --------- | ------

| Pomeroy Technique | Most commonly used

| Parkland technique | Segment excision

| Filshie clip | Clip application

| Falope ring | Laparoscopic band

B) Isthmus because of narrowest area

• The isthmus is narrow, but uniform muscular thickness is the main reason for choosing it.

C) Ampulla because of more circular muscles

• The ampulla is wide and thin-walled, making ligation less secure.

D) Ampulla because of narrowest area

• The ampulla is actually the widest part of the tube.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Ulipristal acetate (progesterone receptor modulator) should not be prescribed as emergency contraceptive in women with:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Liver dysfunction

Ulipristal acetate (UPA) is a Selective Progesterone Receptor Modulator (SPRM) used as an emergency contraceptive. It works primarily by delaying or inhibiting ovulation, even when the LH surge has begun. Because ulipristal is extensively metabolized in the liver (via CYP3A4), it is contraindicated in women with severe liver dysfunction.

Why are the other options incorrect?

• A.  Glaucoma: Glaucoma is not a contraindication to ulipristal use.
• C. Kidney failure: Renal impairment is not a major contraindication, and dose adjustment is generally not required for emergency contraception.
• D. Coagulopathy: Coagulopathy is not a contraindication to ulipristal.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Up to what duration of pregnancy is the anti-progesterone compound RU-486 (Mifepristone) effective for inducing abortion? (NEET PG 2015)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 63 days

Mifepristone (RU-486) is an antiprogestin used for medical termination of early pregnancy.

Mechanism of action:

• Blocks progesterone receptors
• Causes decidual breakdown
• Softens cervix
• Increases uterine sensitivity to prostaglandins

It is most effective when used up to 63 days (9 weeks) of gestation

It is commonly combined with misoprostol, a prostaglandin E1 analog, to induce uterine contractions and complete abortion.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the most common reason for women discontinuing the use of an intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD)? (NEET PG 2017)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Abnormal uterine bleeding

The most common reason for discontinuation of intrauterine contraceptive devices (IUCDs), especially copper-containing IUCDs, is abnormal uterine bleeding. Common bleeding-related complaints:

• Menorrhagia
• Intermenstrual bleeding
• Increased menstrual duration
• Dysmenorrhea

Copper IUCDs increase local endometrial inflammatory response, which can increase menstrual blood loss and cramping. Other complications of IUCDs:

• Expulsion
• Pelvic inflammatory disease (rare)
• Ectopic pregnancy (rare overall, but relatively more likely if pregnancy occurs with IUCD in situ)

Important distinction:

• IUCDs do not commonly cause infertility
• Uterine rupture is not a typical complication

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following are absolute contraindications of Combined Oral Contraceptive (COCs)? 1. Arterial or venous thrombosis history 2. Severe hypertension 3. Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia 4. Diabetes with vascular complications Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1, 2 and 4

Combined Oral Contraceptives (COCs) contain estrogen and progestin. Because estrogen increases the risk of thromboembolism and cardiovascular events, COCs are contraindicated in women with conditions that predispose to vascular complications.

• 1. Arterial or venous thrombosis history ✅

• Absolute contraindication.
• Estrogen increases the risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE), stroke, and myocardial infarction.

• 2. Severe hypertension ✅

• Absolute contraindication (BP ≥160/100 mmHg).
• COCs further increase the risk of stroke and cardiovascular events.

• 3. Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia ❌

• Not an absolute contraindication.
• Hormonal contraception, including COCs, may be used once appropriate management has begun and pregnancy has been excluded.

• 4. Diabetes with vascular complications ✅

• Absolute contraindication.
• Estrogen increases the risk of vascular events in women with diabetic nephropathy, retinopathy, neuropathy, or other vascular disease.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following are correct regarding failure rate of contraceptive methods? 1. Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate 0 to 1 per HWY 2. Norplant 0.1 per HWY 3. LNG-IUS 0.02 per HWY 4. Levonorgestrel 3 per HWY Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 1, 2 and 3

The failure rate of a contraceptive method is expressed as the number of pregnancies per 100 woman-years (HWY) of use. Long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs) such as implants and intrauterine systems have the lowest failure rates.

• 1. Depot Medroxyprogesterone Acetate (DMPA) - 0–1 per 100 woman-years ✅: DMPA is a highly effective injectable contraceptive with a failure rate of 0–1 pregnancies per 100 woman-years.
• 2. Norplant - 0.1 per 100 woman-years ✅: Norplant (levonorgestrel implant) is one of the most effective reversible contraceptive methods.
• 3. LNG-IUS - 0.02 per 100 woman-years ✅: The Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS/Mirena) has one of the lowest failure rates (\~0.02/HWY).

Incorrect statement:

• 4. Levonorgestrel - 3 per 100 woman-years ❌: This value is not the accepted failure rate for levonorgestrel contraceptive methods and is therefore incorrect.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following are factors for poor outcome following tuboplasty? 1. Dense pelvic adhesions 2. Length of reconstructed tube less than 8 cm 3. Bilateral hydrosalpinx 4. Reversal after 5 years of sterilization procedure Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 1, 2 and 3

Tuboplasty is a microsurgical procedure performed to restore fallopian tube patency in women with tubal infertility or after sterilization. The success of tuboplasty depends on the extent of tubal damage, tubal length after reconstruction, pelvic pathology, and the condition of the tubal mucosa.

• 1. Dense pelvic adhesions ✓

• Extensive adhesions distort pelvic anatomy, impair tubo-ovarian relationship, and reduce postoperative fertility.

• 2. Length of reconstructed tube less than 8 cm ✓

• A reconstructed tube <8 cm has poor functional capacity, reducing the likelihood of successful conception.

• 3. Bilateral hydrosalpinx ✓

• Hydrosalpinx indicates severe tubal damage with destruction of the mucosa, resulting in poor surgical outcomes and lower pregnancy rates.

• 4. Reversal after 5 years of sterilization procedure ✗

• The interval since sterilization alone is not a major determinant of success. More important factors are:

• Woman’s age
• Method of sterilization
• Remaining tubal length
• Tubal mucosal integrity

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following are major complications of oral pills? 1. Cholestasis jaundice 2. Chloasma and acne 3. Venous thromboembolism 4. Breast cancer Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 3 and 4

Combined Oral Contraceptive Pills (COCs) are highly effective contraceptives containing estrogen and progestin. Although generally safe, they are associated with certain major complications, particularly those related to estrogen.

• 1. Cholestatic jaundice ✓

• Estrogen-containing pills may cause cholestatic jaundice, especially in women with a history of pregnancy-related cholestasis or underlying liver disease.

• 2. Chloasma and acne ✗

• Chloasma is a minor cosmetic side effect.
• Acne usually improves with most combined oral contraceptive pills because of their anti-androgenic effect (though some progestins may worsen acne).
• Therefore, this is not considered a major complication.

• 3. Venous thromboembolism (VTE) ✓

• One of the most important serious complications of COCs due to the estrogen component.
• Risk is higher in smokers, obese women, women >35 years, and those with thrombophilia.

• 4. Breast cancer ✓

• Current or suspected breast cancer is a contraindication to COC use. Long-term use has been associated with a slight increase in breast cancer risk, although the absolute risk is small.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following conditions are indications of removal of intrauterine device? 1. Persistent irregular uterine bleeding 2. Perforation of uterus 3. Pyelonephritis 4. Pregnancy with device in situ Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1, 2 and 4

An intrauterine device (IUD) is a highly effective, long-acting reversible contraceptive. Although it is generally safe, removal is indicated in certain situations such as:

• 1. Persistent irregular uterine bleeding ✓

• Persistent or troublesome bleeding that does not respond to medical treatment is an indication for IUD removal after excluding other causes.

• 2. Perforation of uterus ✓

• Uterine perforation is a definite indication for removal, usually by laparoscopy or laparotomy, depending on the location of the device.

• 3. Pyelonephritis ✗

• Pyelonephritis is an infection of the upper urinary tract and is not related to IUD use; therefore, it is not an indication for IUD removal.

• 4. Pregnancy with device in situ ✓

• If pregnancy occurs with an IUD in place and the strings are visible, the device should be removed early because it reduces the risk of miscarriage, septic abortion, and preterm birth.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following conditions is a contraindication to the use of combined oral contraceptive pills (OCPs)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Breast cancer

Current breast cancer is an absolute contraindication to combined oral contraceptive pills (COCPs) because the estrogen and progestin components may stimulate the growth of hormone-sensitive breast tumors. In contrast, COCPs reduce the risk of ovarian and endometrial cancers.

Why not the other options?

• A. Ovarian cancer: COCPs are protective and reduce the risk of ovarian cancer.
• B. Endometrial cancer: COCPs reduce the risk of endometrial cancer.
• D. Colorectal cancer: Not a contraindication; COCPs may even confer a modest protective effect.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is a contraindication to the use of a long-acting subcutaneous contraceptive implant?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Undiagnosed genital bleeding

Subdermal Contraceptive Implant is a long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC) inserted under the skin of the upper arm.

Common examples include:

• Implanon
• Jadelle

Mechanism of Action

The implant releases progestin (etonogestrel/levonorgestrel).

Main effects:

| Mechanism | Effect

| --------- | ------

| Inhibits ovulation | Prevents egg release

| Thickens cervical mucus | Blocks sperm entry

| Endometrial thinning | Prevents implantation

| Implant | Duration

| ------- | --------

| Implanon / Nexplanon | 3 years

| Jadelle | 5 years

Major contraindications include:

| Condition | Reason

| --------- | ------

| Undiagnosed genital bleeding | Must rule out malignancy

| Breast cancer | Hormone sensitive tumor

| Severe liver disease | Hormone metabolism issue

Abnormal genital bleeding

↓

Possible malignancy

↓

Hormonal contraception may mask symptoms

↓

Diagnosis delayed

Therefore evaluation must be done before starting hormonal contraception.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is not a mechanism of action of the oral contraceptive pill? (NEET PG 2015)
options: Interference with implantation of fertilized ovum
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Interference with placental functioning

Combined oral contraceptive pills prevent pregnancy through multiple mechanisms:

1. Inhibition of ovulation

• Estrogen and progesterone suppress FSH and LH secretion
• Prevents LH surge and ovulation

2. Prevention of fertilization

• Progesterone thickens cervical mucus
• Makes sperm penetration difficult

3. Interference with implantation

• Endometrium becomes less suitable for implantation

Oral contraceptive pills do NOT act by interfering with placental function because placental development occurs only after implantation and establishment of pregnancy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is not the mechanism of action of progesterone only pills? (NEET PG 2018)
options: Kills the sperms in the cervical canal
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Kills the sperms in the cervical canal

Progesterone-only pills (POPs or mini-pills) prevent pregnancy primarily by altering cervical mucus and impairing fertilization.

Mechanisms of action:

• Thickening cervical mucus → prevents sperm penetration
• Altering endometrium → reduces likelihood of implantation
• Suppressing ovulation
• Partially — and it depends entirely on which POP. This is the key nuance, and it's exactly what gets tested.
•

Ovulation suppression is not the primary mechanism of traditional POPs. It is the primary mechanism of desogestrel POP.

Ovulation inhibition by POP type

| POP | Ovulation suppressed | Primary mechanism | Missed-pill window

| --- | -------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------

| Levonorgestrel 30 µg (traditional) | \~40–60% of cycles | Cervical mucus | 3 hours

| Norethisterone 350 µg (traditional) | \~40–60% | Cervical mucus | 3 hours

| Desogestrel 75 µg | \~97–99% | Ovulation inhibition | 12 hours

| Drospirenone 4 mg (24/4) | \~97%+ | Ovulation inhibition | 24 hours

* Progesterone-only pills do NOT kill sperm in the cervical canal- This is unequivocally the best answer.

Important points:

• Ovulation suppression is less consistent than with combined oral contraceptive pills
• POPs are preferred in women who cannot take estrogen (eg, breastfeeding women, smokers >35 years)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding lactational amenorrhea method are correct? 1. It is equally effective in amenorrhoeic as well as menstruating woman if the woman is exclusively breastfeeding. 2. The risk of pregnancy in amenorrhoeic woman who is exclusively breastfeeding is less than 2% in the first 6 months. 3. It requires exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months. 4. The failure rate for exclusively breastfeeding and menstruating women is 15–20%. Select the answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 2 and 3

1. Equally effective in amenorrhoeic and menstruating women — Incorrect

• LAM is effective only when all three criteria are fulfilled: amenorrhea, exclusive/nearly exclusive breastfeeding, and infant age <6 months.
• Once menstruation returns, the risk of pregnancy increases.

2. Pregnancy risk <2% in the first 6 months — Correct

• When the woman is amenorrhoeic and exclusively breastfeeding, LAM provides approximately 98% protection against pregnancy during the first 6 months.

3. Requires exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months — Correct

• LAM requires exclusive or nearly exclusive breastfeeding, with the infant <6 months old.

4. Failure rate of exclusively breastfeeding and menstruating women is 15–20% — Incorrect

• Once menstruation resumes, the woman no longer meets the criteria for LAM, so this is not an appropriate LAM failure-rate statement.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding progesterone-only pills are correct? 1. They contain high-dose progesterone as there is no estrogen component. 2. They do not have “on and off” regimen. 3. They can be used with hepatic enzyme-inducing drugs. 4. The failure rate is 0.3 to 2 per hundred women-years of use. Select the answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 2 and 4

1. High-dose progesterone: Incorrect.

• Progestin-only pills (POPs) contain a low dose of progestin, not high-dose progesterone.
• They do not contain estrogen.

2. No “on and off” regimen: Correct.

• POPs are taken continuously every day, without the hormone-free interval used with combined oral contraceptives.

3. Can be used with hepatic enzyme-inducing drugs: Incorrect.

• Enzyme-inducing drugs can increase progestin metabolism and reduce contraceptive effectiveness.

4. Failure rate 0.3–2 per 100 woman-years: Correct.

• POPs are highly effective when taken correctly, with a low failure rate in typical exam-based figures.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following timings for intrauterine device (IUD) insertion is recommended? 1. Immediate postpartum 2. Within 48 hr of delivery 3. Within 5-7 days of menses 4. Within 5-7 days of next menstrual cycle
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 1, 2, 3

Postpartum IUD Timing

| Timing | Recommendation

| ------ | --------------

| Within 10 min of placental delivery | ✔ Postplacental insertion

| Within 48 hours of delivery | ✔ Allowed

| 48 hours – 6 weeks postpartum | ❌ Not recommended

| After 6 weeks postpartum | ✔ Safe

Mechanism of Action of Copper IUD

Copper ions released

↓

Local inflammatory reaction

↓

Toxic to sperm

↓

Prevents fertilization

1) IUD can be inserted within 10 minutes after placental delivery.

Advantages:

• Woman already in hospital
• High motivation for contraception
• Immediate protection

2) Insertion during the first 48 hours postpartum is also recommended.

However:

• If >48 hours and <6 weeks postpartum, insertion is not recommended because of increased expulsion risk.

3) Within 5–7 Days of Menses

This timing is preferred because:

• Cervix is slightly dilated
• Pregnancy is ruled out
• Insertion is easier and safer

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: With regard to contraception, Pearl Index refers to:
options: Number of pregnancies in 100 woman-years over pregnancy losses
Number of pregnancies in a year
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Number of pregnancies in 100 woman-years

The Pearl Index is the most commonly used measure of contraceptive effectiveness. It is defined as the number of unintended pregnancies that occur per 100 woman-years of contraceptive use. A lower Pearl Index indicates a more effective contraceptive method.

• Pearl Index = Number of pregnancies per 100 woman-years of exposure to a contraceptive method.

Why not the other options?

• A. Number of pregnancies in 1 woman-year: Incorrect; the standard denominator is 100 woman-years.
• C. Number of pregnancies in 100 woman-years over pregnancy losses: Pregnancy losses are not part of the Pearl Index calculation.
• D. Number of pregnancies in a year: Does not account for the number of women or duration of contraceptive use.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 14-year-old girl, a victim of rape, presents at 22 weeks for abortion. What advice will you give her?
options: MTP cannot be done as she has crossed 20 weeks
MTP can be done till 24 weeks
MTP can be done only if the mother's life is at risk
MTP can only be done if there is a substantial fetal anomaly
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. MTP can be done till 24 weeks

Termination of pregnancy in India is governed by the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act.

The 2021 amendment expanded the upper gestational limit for certain categories.

| Gestational Age | Requirement

| --------------- | -----------

| Up to 20 weeks | Opinion of 1 registered medical practitioner

| 20–24 weeks | Opinion of 2 registered medical practitioners

| >24 weeks | Allowed only for major fetal anomalies (medical board approval)

Special Categories Eligible for 20–24 Week Termination

The law specifically includes rape survivors.

Eligible groups:

| Category

| --------

| Survivors of rape or incest

| Minors

| Differently-abled women

| Change in marital status (widow/divorce)

| Severe fetal anomalies

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 22-year-old woman presents with vaginal bleeding at 12 weeks of gestation, diagnosed with a complete hydatidiform mole. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management for this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Suction and Evacuation

Suction evacuation (vacuum aspiration) is the treatment of choice for a hydatidiform mole, particularly in women who wish to preserve fertility, as it provides rapid and complete evacuation of molar tissue with minimal complications.

Why not the other options?

• B. Dilatation and Curettage (D&C): Less effective for complete molar evacuation and associated with greater blood loss; suction evacuation is preferred.
• C. Inj. Methotrexate: Not used for initial treatment; reserved for persistent gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) or selected high-risk cases.
• D. Hysterectomy: Considered only in women who have completed childbearing or have uncontrolled bleeding/high risk of persistent disease; β-hCG surveillance is still required.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 22y primigravida is overdue by 2 weeks. She visits the OPD with complaints of vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain on the right side. On Examination, her vitals are stable. Abdomen examination is unremarkable. A bimanual examination reveals a bulky, soft uterus with no tenderness and no adnexal mass. Mild bleeding +. Beta hCG is 1400 IU. An ultrasound reveals a trilaminar endometrium, and both the adnexa are normal. The next best step is?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Repeat serum beta HCG after 48h

In very early pregnancy, the gestational sac may not yet be visible on ultrasound.

The discriminatory zone for Beta Human Chorionic Gonadotropin is about: 1500–2000 IU/L

Below this level, ultrasound may not detect intrauterine pregnancy.

In normal early pregnancy:

β-hCG level

↓

Should double every 48 hours

| Pattern | Interpretation

| ------- | --------------

| Rise ≥66% in 48h | Normal intrauterine pregnancy

| Plateau / slow rise | Ectopic pregnancy

| Falling levels | Miscarriage

A trilaminar endometrium suggests:

• Possible very early intrauterine pregnancy
• Or pregnancy not yet visible

Approach to Pregnancy of Unknown Location

Positive pregnancy test

↓

No pregnancy seen on ultrasound

↓

Measure β-hCG

↓

Repeat β-hCG after 48 hours

↓

Assess rise or fall

| Pattern | Interpretation

| ------- | --------------

| Rise ≥66% in 48h | Normal intrauterine pregnancy

| Plateau / slow rise | Ectopic pregnancy

| Falling levels | Miscarriage

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 24-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with fever, lower abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, and foul-smelling vaginal discharge 3 days after undergoing an abortion by an unlicensed practitioner. On examination, she is febrile, tachycardic, and has marked uterine tenderness. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Septic abortion

Septic abortion is an abortion complicated by infection of the uterus and/or surrounding tissues, most commonly following an unsafe abortion performed under unsterile conditions. It is a gynecological emergency that requires prompt recognition and treatment.

• Risk factors: Unsafe abortion, retained products of conception, instrumentation by an untrained person.
• Clinical features:

• Fever
• Lower abdominal pain
• Foul-smelling vaginal discharge
• Vaginal bleeding
• Uterine tenderness
• Tachycardia ± hypotension/septic shock

• Common organisms: Polymicrobial infection (E. coli, anaerobes, Streptococci, Staphylococci, Clostridium).

Management

• Immediate broad-spectrum IV antibiotics

• e.g., Clindamycin + Gentamicin ± Ampicillin (or equivalent broad-spectrum regimen)

• IV fluids and hemodynamic stabilization
• Evacuation of retained products after antibiotics are initiated and the patient is stabilized
• Monitor for complications such as septic shock, DIC, and pelvic abscess.

Why the other options are incorrect?

• A. Incomplete abortion: Vaginal bleeding with retained products but no signs of systemic infection.
• C. Threatened abortion: Bleeding with a closed cervix and a viable pregnancy.
• D. Missed abortion: Retained nonviable fetus with minimal symptoms, typically no fever or foul-smelling discharge.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 26-year woman presents with six weeks amenorrhea. Obstetrician notices right adnexal tenderness on cervical motion during examination. Which of the following is an incorrect statement?
options: Abdominal pain is the commonest presentation
Oral methotrexate is treatment of choice
Chances of ectopic increase in PID
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Oral methotrexate is treatment of choice

Ectopic pregnancy occurs when the fertilized ovum implants outside the uterine cavity.

Most common location

| Site | Percentage

| ---- | ----------

| Fallopian tube (ampulla) | \~70%

| Isthmus | \~12%

| Fimbria | \~11%

| Ovary / abdomen | Rare

Classic triad of ectopic pregnancy:

| Feature | Explanation

| ------- | -----------

| Amenorrhea | Missed period

| Abdominal pain | Tubal distension

| Vaginal bleeding | Decidual shedding

Role of Progesterone

Progesterone levels may help assess pregnancy viability, but:

• Low progesterone suggests nonviable pregnancy
• It cannot confirm ectopic pregnancy

| Risk factor | Mechanism

| ----------- | ---------

| Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) | Tubal scarring

| Previous ectopic pregnancy | Tubal damage

| Tubal surgery | Structural abnormalities

| Assisted reproductive techniques | Altered embryo transport

Treatment of Ectopic Pregnancy

Methotrexate works by inhibiting trophoblastic cell proliferation.

Route of administration

➡ Intramuscular injection

Common regimen:

• Single-dose IM methotrexate

| Situation | Treatment

| --------- | ---------

| Hemodynamically stable, small ectopic | IM methotrexate

| Ruptured ectopic | Emergency surgery

| Failed medical therapy | Laparoscopy

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 28-year-old G2P1L1 woman with a previous pregnancy complicated by pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH) has recently been diagnosed with antiphospholipid antibody syndrome (APS). She is planning her next pregnancy and presents for preconception counseling. Which of the following is the most appropriate preconception management?
options: Low-dose aspirin combined with low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH)
No pharmacological therapy before conception; start treatment only after pregnancy is confirmed
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Low-dose aspirin alone

Women with antiphospholipid antibody syndrome (APS) planning pregnancy should begin low-dose aspirin (75–150 mg/day) before conception. Once pregnancy is confirmed, LMWH is added and both are continued throughout pregnancy to reduce the risk of miscarriage, preeclampsia, fetal growth restriction, and thrombosis.

| Stage | Recommended Treatment

| ----- | ---------------------

| Preconception | Low-dose aspirin

| After confirmation of pregnancy | Low-dose aspirin + prophylactic LMWH

| Postpartum | Continue anticoagulation for at least 6 weeks

Why not the other options?

• B. Low-dose aspirin combined with low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH): Recommended after conception, not routinely before pregnancy.
• C. Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) alone: Less effective than combined therapy during pregnancy and not used alone preconception.
• D. No pharmacological therapy before conception; start treatment only after pregnancy is confirmed: Incorrect, as preconception low-dose aspirin is recommended in women with obstetric APS.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 28-year-old woman presents with an unruptured ectopic pregnancy confirmed on ultrasound. Medical management with methotrexate is being considered. Which of the following is a contraindication to methotrexate therapy in this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Cardiac activity +

Methotrexate is the preferred medical treatment for a hemodynamically stable, unruptured ectopic pregnancy. However, the presence of fetal cardiac activity is a relative contraindication because it is associated with a significantly lower success rate of medical management.

Ideal Candidates for Methotrexate

• Hemodynamically stable
• Unruptured ectopic pregnancy
• No fetal cardiac activity
• Adnexal mass <3.5–4 cm
• β-hCG <5,000 IU/L (best success with lower levels)
• Reliable for follow-up

Why not the other options?

• A. β-hCG 2200 IU/L: Suitable for methotrexate; success rates are high at this level.
• C. Sac size of 3 cm: Within the acceptable size for medical management.
• D. Primigravida: Not a contraindication to methotrexate.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 30-year-old G4A3 woman had a history of miscarriage at 8 weeks, the second miscarriage at 11 weeks with no cardiac activity, and the third pregnancy loss at 24 weeks with preterm delivery due to early-onset preeclampsia. What is the most probable diagnosis? (NEET PG 2021)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome

Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome (APS) is an autoimmune thrombophilic disorder characterized by:

• Recurrent pregnancy loss
• Arterial or venous thrombosis
• Placental insufficiency

Obstetric manifestations include:

• Recurrent early miscarriages
• Unexplained fetal death after 10 weeks
• Early-onset severe preeclampsia
• Preterm delivery due to placental insufficiency
• Intrauterine growth restriction

Pathogenesis: Antiphospholipid antibodies cause placental thrombosis and impaired trophoblastic function

Important antibodies:

• Lupus anticoagulant
• Anticardiolipin antibody
• Anti-β2 glycoprotein I antibody

Clinical Criteria

1. Vascular thrombosis: ≥1 arterial, venous, or small-vessel thrombosis.
2. Pregnancy morbidity:

• a. ≥1 fetal death at or beyond the 10th week of gestation.
• b. ≥1 premature birth before the 34th week of gestation due to eclampsia, severe preeclampsia, or placental insufficiency.
• c. ≥3 consecutive embryonic losses before the 10th week of gestation.

Laboratory Criteria

1. Lupus anticoagulant positivity on ≥2 occasions at least 12 weeks apart.
2. Anticardiolipin antibody (IgG and/or IgM) in medium or high titer (e.g., >40 or above the 99th percentile) on ≥2 occasions at least 12 weeks apart.
3. Anti-β2-glycoprotein-I antibody (IgG and/or IgM) in medium or high titer (above the 99th percentile) on ≥2 occasions at least 12 weeks apart.

Diagnosis of Definite APS (Antiphospholipid Syndrome):

Definite APS is present if at least one clinical criterion and one laboratory criterion are met.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 30-year-old P₃L₃ female presents in Gynaecology emergency with acute abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding of short duration (1 hour). She gives history of tubal ligation after birth of third child. On examination, right adnexal tenderness was found and os was closed. What is the probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Ectopic pregnancy

Ectopic pregnancy is implantation of a fertilized ovum outside the uterine cavity, with the fallopian tube (ampulla) being the most common site. It is a gynecological emergency because rupture can lead to massive intra-abdominal hemorrhage and maternal death.

The classic triad of ectopic pregnancy is:

• Amenorrhea
• Acute lower abdominal pain
• Vaginal bleeding

A history of tubal ligation does not eliminate the risk of pregnancy. If pregnancy occurs after tubal sterilization, the likelihood of it being ectopic is significantly increased.

Why not the other options?

• B. Pelvic inflammatory disease: Presents with fever, bilateral pelvic pain, cervical motion tenderness, and purulent vaginal discharge rather than acute vaginal bleeding with a closed os.
• C. Appendicitis: Causes right iliac fossa pain and vomiting but does not cause vaginal bleeding.
• D. Complete abortion: Usually presents with open cervical os initially, passage of products of conception, and pain/bleeding that subside after complete expulsion.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 31-year-old primigravida presents at 16 weeks of gestation for evaluation of fetal chromosomal abnormalities. She requests a test with high sensitivity for trisomies while avoiding any procedure-related risk of pregnancy loss. Which of the following is the best investigation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT)

NIPT is the best non-invasive screening test for fetal aneuploidy. It analyzes cell-free fetal DNA (cffDNA) in maternal blood and can be performed from 10 weeks of gestation onward, making it ideal at 16 weeks. It has excellent detection rates for common trisomies (especially Trisomy 21) and carries no procedure-related risk of fetal loss.

Why not the other options?

• A. Chorionic villus sampling (CVS) – An invasive diagnostic test performed between 11–13+6 weeks. It is no longer the preferred procedure at 16 weeks.
• B. Amniocentesis – The appropriate invasive diagnostic test after 15 weeks, but it carries a small risk of procedure-related pregnancy loss.
• D. Cordocentesis – Usually performed after 18 weeks and reserved for specific indications such as fetal anemia or rapid fetal karyotyping; it has the highest procedure-related risk.

High-Yield Pearl:

• NIPT is a screening test, not a diagnostic test.
• A positive NIPT result must be confirmed with a diagnostic procedure such as amniocentesis or CVS before making irreversible clinical decisions.

Remember:

• CVS: 11–13+6 weeks (diagnostic)
• NIPT: ≥10 weeks (screening)
• Amniocentesis: ≥15 weeks, ideally 16–18 weeks (diagnostic)
• Cordocentesis: ≥18 weeks (special indications)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 32-year-old G2P1 woman presents at 12 weeks of gestation. She is normotensive but had preeclampsia during her previous pregnancy. Which of the following interventions is recommended to reduce the risk of recurrent preeclampsia?
options: Initiate low-dose aspirin from 12 weeks of gestation
Low-dose aspirin combined with low-molecular-weight heparin from 12 weeks of gestation
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Initiate low-dose aspirin from 12 weeks of gestation

Women at high risk of preeclampsia should receive low-dose aspirin (75–150 mg daily) beginning at 12 weeks of gestation (ideally before 16 weeks) until delivery. Aspirin reduces thromboxane A₂ production, improving placental perfusion and lowering the risk of recurrent preeclampsia.

Other options:

• A. Salt restriction throughout pregnancy: Not recommended for prevention.
• C. Low-dose aspirin + LMWH from 12 weeks of gestation: Reserved for selected patients with thrombophilia or antiphospholipid syndrome.
• D. Calcium restriction during pregnancy: Incorrect; calcium supplementation, not restriction, may benefit women with low dietary calcium intake.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 39y G2P1 presents at 18 weeks 5 days for her routine targeted fetal anomaly ultrasound. The fetal anatomy appears normal, but the cervical length is 15mm. Despite being counselled that there is no clear proven benefit for the same; the patient insisted on a cervical cerclage. Which of the following is a complete contra-indication to cerclage?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Ruptured membranes

Cervical Cerclage is performed in cervical insufficiency to prevent preterm birth or second-trimester loss.

| Cervical length | Interpretation

| --------------- | --------------

| ≥25 mm | Normal

| <25 mm | Short cervix

| <15 mm | High risk of preterm birth

When Premature Rupture of Membranes occurs:

Membranes rupture

↓

Amniotic sac exposed

↓

High risk of infection (chorioamnionitis)

↓

Cerclage may trap infection inside uterus

Thus performing cerclage would increase maternal and fetal infection risk.

Ruptured membranes is an absolute contraindication for cervical cerclage.

| Type | Example

| ---- | -------

| History-indicated | Recurrent mid-trimester loss

| Ultrasound-indicated | Cervical length <25 mm before 24 weeks

| Rescue cerclage | Dilated cervix with intact membranes

| Absolute contraindications | Reason

| -------------------------- | ------

| Ruptured membranes | Infection risk

| Active labor | Cervix already dilating

| Intrauterine infection | Risk of sepsis

| Fetal demise or anomaly incompatible with life | No benefit

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A female presents to OPD with 6 weeks of amenorrhea complaints of bleeding per vagina and mild abdominal pain. The urine pregnancy test is positive and hCG level is 2800 IU/L. On investigation, mass is seen on the left adnexa measuring 3 x 2 cm. She is hemodynamically stable. How will you manage this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Single-dose methotrexate injection

Methotrexate- It stops trophoblastic growth, leading to resolution of the ectopic pregnancy. Medical treatment can be given if:

| Criteria | Requirement

| -------- | -----------

| Hemodynamically stable | No rupture

| Mass size <3.5–4 cm | Small ectopic

| β-hCG <5000 IU/L | Lower success failure risk

| No fetal cardiac activity | Non-viable ectopic

This patient fulfills all criteria. She has a stable, unruptured ectopic with mass <3.5 cm and β-hCG <5000 IU/L, fulfilling criteria for medical management. Single-dose intramuscular methotrexate is preferred. Surgery (e.g., salpingectomy) is reserved for hemodynamic instability, larger mass or fetal cardiac activity.

Day 1 → Methotrexate 50 mg/m² IM

↓

Day 4 & Day 7 → β-hCG monitoring

↓

≥15% fall in hCG → treatment successful

| Situation | Management

| --------- | ----------

| Hemodynamic instability | Emergency surgery

| Ruptured ectopic | Laparotomy

| Large ectopic mass | Salpingectomy

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A patient in early pregnancy presents to the emergency department with vaginal spotting. On ultrasound, which of the following findings is diagnostic of a missed abortion?
options: No cardiac activity at a CRL > 7mm
No cardiac activity at a CRL < 7mm
No cardiac activity at a CRL > 25mm
No cardiac activity at a CRL < 12mm
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. No cardiac activity at a CRL > 7mm

Missed abortion is diagnosed when there is no cardiac activity detected on ultrasound at CRL ≥ 7mm. Typical presentation:

• Vaginal spotting
• Loss of pregnancy symptoms
• Closed cervical os

This threshold distinguishes between normal earlssssy development (cardiac activity not yet detectable) and embryonic demise (cardiac activity absent when it should be present).

| Ultrasound finding | Diagnosis

| ------------------ | ---------

| CRL ≥7 mm with no cardiac activity | Diagnostic of missed abortion

| Gestational sac ≥25 mm with no embryo | Anembryonic pregnancy

| Finding | Interpretation

| ------- | --------------

| Gestational sac ≥25 mm with no embryo | Blighted ovum

| No embryo after 2 weeks of sac seen | Pregnancy failure

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A patient was undergoing a hysteroscopic removal of a submucosal fibroid, in which a fluid deficit of 2000 mL is estimated in a patient. What is the immediate complication of this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Pulmonary edema

Hysteroscopy is commonly used for removal of:

• Submucosal fibroids
• Polyps
• Adhesions (Asherman syndrome)

To visualize the uterine cavity, distension fluids are used. Distension media used include:

• Normal saline
• Glycine
• Sorbitol

During the procedure, these fluids can be absorbed into systemic circulation.

Large amount of fluid absorbed

↓

Increased intravascular volume

↓

Fluid overload

↓

Pulmonary congestion

↓

Pulmonary edema

Fluid deficit >2000 mL during hysteroscopy → risk of pulmonary edema.

A large fluid deficit implies significant intravascular absorption of distension medium → acute volume overload. This can precipitate pulmonary edema with respiratory compromise. ATN, DIC, and thromboembolism are not the immediate expected complication here.

Complications of Excess Fluid Absorption

| Complication | Mechanism

| ------------ | ---------

| Pulmonary edema | Fluid overload

| Hyponatremia | Hypotonic fluid absorption

| Cerebral edema | Severe hyponatremia

| Cardiac failure | Volume overload

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A patient, who is 2 months pregnant, reports to a hospital with complaints of increased vaginal bleeding and pain in lower abdomen. Internal examination reveals dilated internal os of cervix and products of conception are felt through it. What is her likely clinical diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Inevitable abortion

Inevitable abortion is defined as vaginal bleeding with cramp-like abdominal pain, cervical dilatation, and no expulsion of products of conception (POC). Once the internal os is dilated, continuation of pregnancy is no longer possible, and abortion is considered inevitable.

Why are the other options incorrect?

• A.  Threatened abortion: Vaginal bleeding occurs, but the cervical os remains closed, and the pregnancy may continue.
• C. Septic abortion: Characterized by fever, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, uterine tenderness, and signs of infection, which are absent here.
• D. Incomplete abortion: Occurs after partial expulsion of products of conception, with retained tissue in the uterus. In this case, the products are felt through the dilated cervix but have not yet been expelled.

| Type of Abortion | Bleeding | Cervical Os | Products of Conception (POC)

| ---------------- | -------- | ----------- | ----------------------------

| Threatened | Mild | Closed | Retained, fetus viable

| Inevitable | Moderate/Heavy | Open | Not expelled, felt through os

| Incomplete | Heavy | Open | Partially expelled, retained POC

| Complete | Minimal after expulsion | Closed | All POC expelled

| Missed | Minimal/Absent | Closed | Dead fetus retained

| Septic | Variable | Usually open | Infected retained POC

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A woman presents with bleeding for 2 days and abdominal pain. Her LMP was 6 weeks back. An ultrasound shows fluid in the pouch of Douglas. What is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Ruptured ectopic pregnancy

An ectopic pregnancy occurs when the fertilized ovum implants outside the uterine cavity, most commonly in the fallopian tube.

Most common site

| Site | Frequency

| ---- | ---------

| Ampulla of fallopian tube | \~70%

| Isthmus | \~12%

| Fimbrial end | \~11%

| Ovary / abdomen | Rare

Classic triad of ectopic pregnancy:

| Symptom | Reason

| ------- | ------

| Amenorrhea | Early pregnancy

| Abdominal pain | Tubal distension or rupture

| Vaginal bleeding | Decidual shedding

The pouch of Douglas (rectouterine pouch) is the lowest point of the peritoneal cavity in women.

Fluid here suggests intraperitoneal bleeding.

In early pregnancy with pain: Free fluid in pouch of Douglas = ruptured ectopic pregnancy until proven otherwise.

A) Abruptio placentae

Occurs after 20 weeks of pregnancy, not at 6 weeks.

B) Placenta previa

Also a late pregnancy complication, typically presenting in the third trimester with painless bleeding.

C) Missed abortion

Usually presents with:

• Absent fetal cardiac activity
• Closed cervical os
• No free intraperitoneal fluid

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: According to the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021, MTP for pregnancy between 20 to 24 weeks needs opinion of:
options: One registered medical practitioner and court order
Two registered medical practitioners and court order
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Two registered medical practitioners

Under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021, for pregnancies >20 weeks but ≤24 weeks in the specified categories of women, termination requires the opinion of not less than two registered medical practitioners, formed in good faith. A court order is not required.

Therefore, B. is correct.

To understand the MTP Act 2021 gestational-age-based requirements for termination of pregnancy and the number of registered medical practitioners required at different gestational ages.

≤20 weeks → 1 RMP

>20 to ≤24 weeks → 2 RMPs

Court order → Not routinely required

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: According to the MTP Act Amendment of 2021, at what gestational age range is the opinion of two registered medical practitioners required for termination of pregnancy?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 20-24 weeks

Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act 2021

The 2021 amendment expanded access to abortion and modified the doctor approval requirements depending on gestational age.

| Gestational Age  | Doctor Requirement

| ---------------- | -------------------

| ≤20 weeks  | Opinion of 1 Registered Medical Practitioner

| 20–24 weeks  | Opinion of 2 Registered Medical Practitioners

| >24 weeks  | Allowed only for fetal abnormalities with approval of a State Medical Board

Thus, two doctors are specifically required for termination between 20 and 24 weeks.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All are members of the medical board in MTP > 24 weeks, except?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Legal advisor

For MTP >24 weeks (special categories), the medical board includes gynecologist, radiologist, pediatrician, and a relevant specialist. A legal advisor is NOT part of the board, as decisions are medical, not legal.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: During pregnancy, pyogenic granuloma, also called granuloma gravidarum, most commonly arises from which location? (NEET PG 2017)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Gingival papillae

Pyogenic granuloma of pregnancy (granuloma gravidarum) is a benign vascular proliferative lesion that commonly develops during pregnancy due to hormonal influences and local irritation. Most common site: Gingival papillae, especially the interdental gingiva

Characteristics:

• Red, soft, highly vascular lesion
• Bleeds easily on touch
• Rapid growth during pregnancy
• Usually appears in the second or third trimester

Pathogenesis: Increased estrogen and progesterone enhance vascular response to local irritation and plaque

Despite the name, pyogenic granuloma is neither pyogenic nor a true granuloma.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The combi-pack approved by the DGH for medical method of MTP in the first trimester comprises of which one of the following combinations?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 200 mg Mifepristone and 800 µg Misoprostol

The combi-pack approved in India for medical termination of early pregnancy contains:

• Mifepristone 200 mg — 1 tablet
• Misoprostol 200 µg × 4 tablets = 800 µg

Mifepristone is an antiprogestin that causes decidual breakdown and increases uterine sensitivity to prostaglandins.

Misoprostol is a PGE₁ analogue that produces cervical softening and uterine contractions, facilitating expulsion of the products of conception.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What are Spiegelberg’s criteria for diagnosis of ovarian pregnancy? 1. Tube on the affected side must be intact. 2. Gestational sac must be in the position of ovary. 3. Gestational sac is connected to uterus by ovarian ligament. 4. Ovarian tissue must be detected on the wall on histological examination. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 2, 3 and 4

Spiegelberg’s criteria are the four diagnostic criteria for primary ovarian pregnancy. All four criteria must be fulfilled to distinguish it from a tubal pregnancy secondarily involving the ovary.

Spiegelberg’s criteria:

1. Tube on the affected side must be intact.
2. Gestational sac must occupy the position of the ovary.
3. Gestational sac must be connected to the uterus by the ovarian ligament.
4. Ovarian tissue must be demonstrated in the wall of the gestational sac on histological examination.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the most common surgical cause of acute abdomen in pregnancy? (NEET PG 2017)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Acute Appendicitis

Acute appendicitis is the most common nonobstetric surgical emergency and the most common surgical cause of acute abdomen during pregnancy.

• Abdominal pain
• Nausea and vomiting
• Fever and leukocytosis

Important pregnancy-related changes:

• Enlarging uterus may displace the appendix upward and laterally
• Pain location may shift from the right lower quadrant to the right upper abdomen in late pregnancy

Diagnosis may be difficult because:

• Pregnancy itself causes nausea, leukocytosis, and abdominal discomfort
• Delay in diagnosis increases risk of perforation and fetal loss

Imaging:

• Ultrasound is often first-line
• MRI is preferred if ultrasound is inconclusive

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following are the clinical features of septic abortion? 1. Persistent tachycardia ≥ 90 bpm 2. Impaired mental status 3. Hypothermia Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 2 and 3

Septic abortion is an abortion complicated by infection of the uterus and surrounding tissues, which may progress to sepsis and septic shock. It is a medical emergency requiring prompt antibiotics, resuscitation, and uterine evacuation.

• 1. Persistent tachycardia ≥90 bpm: Correct. An early sign of systemic infection and sepsis.
• 2. Impaired mental status: Correct. Suggests severe sepsis or septic shock with organ dysfunction.
• 3. Hypothermia: Correct. Although fever is more common, hypothermia (<36°C) is a recognized feature of severe sepsis and is associated with a poorer prognosis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is not a risk factor for ectopic pregnancy? (NEET PG 2017)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Condom

Ectopic pregnancy occurs when implantation takes place outside the uterine cavity, most commonly in the fallopian tube.

Major risk factors include conditions that damage or impair tubal transport:

• Pelvic inflammatory disease
• Previous ectopic pregnancy
• Tubal surgery or tubal ligation
• Intrauterine device (if pregnancy occurs)
• Infertility treatment
• Smoking

Why the options differ:

• IUCDs reduce overall pregnancy risk, but if pregnancy occurs with an IUCD in place, the relative likelihood of ectopic pregnancy is increased
• Pregnancy after tubal ligation has a higher chance of being ectopic
• Oral contraceptive pills overall reduce pregnancy risk, but progesterone-only pills may slightly increase ectopic risk if contraceptive failure occurs
• Condoms protect against sexually transmitted infections and PID, thereby reducing the risk of ectopic pregnancy

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following maternal complications can be seen in hyperemesis gravidarum? I. Wernicke’s encephalopathy II. Hepatic failure III. Hypoprothrombinemia IV. Convulsions Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. I, II, III and IV

Hyperemesis gravidarum (HG) is severe, persistent nausea and vomiting during pregnancy leading to dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, ketosis, and weight loss (>5% of prepregnancy weight). It usually occurs during the first trimester (6–16 weeks) and may result in serious maternal complications if left untreated. All the listed complications can occur in severe hyperemesis gravidarum:

• I. Wernicke’s encephalopathy: Caused by thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency due to prolonged vomiting. It presents with the classic triad of:

• Confusion
• Ophthalmoplegia/nystagmus
• Ataxia

Thiamine should always be administered before intravenous dextrose.

• II. Hepatic failure: Mild elevation of liver enzymes is common, while severe hepatic dysfunction and hepatic failure are rare but recognized complications of severe hyperemesis gravidarum.
• III. Hypoprothrombinemia: Prolonged vomiting may result in vitamin K deficiency, causing hypoprothrombinemia and an increased risk of bleeding.
• IV. Convulsions: Convulsions may occur secondary to severe electrolyte disturbances (especially hyponatremia), Wernicke’s encephalopathy, or profound metabolic derangements.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following metabolic changes is most commonly associated with hyperemesis gravidarum? (NEET PG 2016)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Hyperthyroidism
