Hyperemesis gravidarum is severe, persistent nausea and vomiting during pregnancy leading to dehydration, weight loss, electrolyte imbalance, and ketosis. It is commonly associated with transient hyperthyroidism due to:

• Markedly elevated β-hCG levels
• β-hCG weakly stimulating TSH receptors because of structural similarity to TSH

Clinical/laboratory findings may include:

• Elevated free T4
• Suppressed TSH
• Tachycardia and tremor in some patients

Typical metabolic abnormalities in hyperemesis gravidarum:

• Hypokalemia
• Hyponatremia
• Hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis
• Ketonuria

Conditions with very high β-hCG levels (eg, molar pregnancy, multiple gestation) increase the risk of hyperemesis gravidarum and gestational thyrotoxicosis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which one of the following drugs is most effective in the treatment of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Methotrexate

Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia (GTN) comprises malignant trophoblastic tumors, including invasive mole, choriocarcinoma, placental site trophoblastic tumor (PSTT), and epithelioid trophoblastic tumor (ETT). GTN is one of the most chemosensitive malignancies, with cure rates exceeding 90–100% when treated appropriately.

Methotrexate is the first-line drug for low-risk GTN (WHO score ≤6) and achieves excellent cure rates. It is administered as a single-agent regimen with folinic acid (leucovorin) rescue in many protocols.

Why are the other options incorrect?

• A.  Cisplatin: Cisplatin is not used as first-line therapy. It is reserved for salvage chemotherapy in resistant or recurrent GTN.
• C. Gemcitabine: Gemcitabine is not a standard drug for GTN treatment.
• D. None of the above: Incorrect because methotrexate is the standard first-line treatment for low-risk GTN.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which one of the following is correct regarding choriocarcinoma?
options: Vaginal bleeding is the commonest presenting symptom
About 20–30% of patients with molar pregnancies develop choriocarcinoma
Primary site of involvement is fallopian tube
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Vaginal bleeding is the commonest presenting symptom

• Choriocarcinoma is a highly malignant gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) composed of cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts without chorionic villi. It is characterized by very high β-hCG levels, rapid hematogenous spread, and an excellent response to chemotherapy.
• Irregular vaginal bleeding following a molar pregnancy, abortion, ectopic pregnancy, or term pregnancy is the most common presenting symptom of choriocarcinoma.

Why are the other options incorrect?

• B. About 20–30% of patients with molar pregnancies develop choriocarcinoma:

• Choriocarcinoma develops in approximately:

• 2–3% of complete hydatidiform moles
• <0.5% of partial moles

• The majority of molar pregnancies do not progress to choriocarcinoma.

• C. Primary site of involvement is fallopian tube:

• The primary site is the uterus, arising from trophoblastic tissue.
• The lungs are the most common site of metastasis.

• D. Highly resistant tumour to chemotherapy: Choriocarcinoma is one of the most chemosensitive human malignancies, with cure rates approaching 90–100%, even in metastatic disease when treated appropriately.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 36-year-old woman (P2L2) who previously underwent tubectomy and surgical management of endometriosis (adhesiolysis and excision of lesions), now presents with recurrence of the symptoms. What is the definitive treatment for this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy

Endometriosis is a chronic estrogen-dependent condition.

Common sites:

• Ovary
• Uterosacral ligaments
• Pelvic peritoneum
• Rectovaginal septum

Definitive Treatment : Total Hysterectomy with Bilateral Salpingo-Oophorectomy (TAH + BSO)

Removes uterus ; Removes ovaries → eliminates estrogen source

A) Hysterectomy alone

Ovaries remain → estrogen production continues → recurrence possible.

C) LNG-IUS

Used for symptom control, not definitive treatment.

D) Resection of nodules

Conservative surgery may lead to recurrence.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 36-year-old woman presents with bleeding per rectum that coincides with her menstrual cycles. On per rectal examination, a nodule is palpated anteriorly. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Endometriosis

Deep infiltrating endometriosis (DIE) should be suspected in women with cyclical bleeding per rectum, dyschezia, or painful defecation during menstruation. A tender nodule on the anterior rectal wall on per rectal examination is characteristic of rectovaginal septum or bowel endometriosis.

Why not the other options?

• A. Colorectal cancer: Causes persistent, non-cyclical rectal bleeding, often associated with weight loss or altered bowel habits.
• C. Hemorrhoids: Cause painless bright red bleeding during defecation and are not related to the menstrual cycle.
• D. Inflammatory bowel disease: Produces chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, and rectal bleeding independent of menstruation.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A diagnosis of polycystic ovary syndrome requires the presence of which of the following clinical features? 1. Menstrual irregularity 2. Clinical or biochemical androgen excess 3. Multiple cysts in the ovaries 4. BMI <18.5 kg/m² Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 1, 2 and 3

Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is diagnosed using the Revised Rotterdam criteria (2003), which require any two of the following three features after excluding other causes of hyperandrogenism and ovulatory dysfunction:

1. Ovulatory dysfunction – Oligo-ovulation or anovulation, presenting as menstrual irregularity (oligomenorrhea or amenorrhea).
2. Clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism – Hirsutism, acne, androgenic alopecia, or elevated serum androgen levels.
3. Polycystic ovarian morphology (PCOM) on ultrasonography.

Explanation of the statements:

• Statement 1. Menstrual irregularity: Correct. Menstrual irregularity reflects chronic anovulation and is one of the diagnostic criteria.
• Statement 2. Clinical or biochemical androgen excess: Correct. Clinical or biochemical androgen excess is a core diagnostic feature.
• Statement 3. Multiple cysts in the ovaries: Correct. Polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound is one of the Rotterdam criteria.
• Statement 4. BMI <18.5 kg/m²: Incorrect. BMI <18.5 kg/m² is not a diagnostic criterion. Although many women with PCOS are overweight or obese, lean PCOS is also well recognized.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A lady presented with a pelvic mass which was hyperintense on T1-weighted image, hyperintense on T1-fat saturated image, and hypointense on T2-weighted image with T2 shading. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Endometrioma

Endometriomas (chocolate cysts) show T1 hyperintensity due to blood, remain bright on fat-sat, and T2 shading from repeated hemorrhage. Teratomas contain fat, carcinoma/dysgerminoma lack these features.

Key Radiological Signs

1. T1 Hyperintensity

• Due to blood products (methemoglobin)

2. No Fat Suppression

• Remains bright on T1 fat-sat → confirms blood, not fat

3. T2 Shading Sign

• Progressive loss of signal on T2
• Due to chronic repeated hemorrhage

| Feature | Endometrioma | Teratoma | Ovarian Carcinoma | Dysgerminoma

| ------- | ------------ | -------- | ----------------- | ------------

| T1 | Hyperintense | Hyperintense | Variable | Iso/hypo

| Fat suppression | ❌ No | ✅ Yes | No | No

| T2 | Shading (hypo) | Variable | Heterogeneous | Solid

| Nature | Blood cyst | Fat tumor | Malignant | Solid tumor

| Key sign | T2 shading ⭐ | Fat suppression | Solid nodules | Lobulated mass

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A patient comes after 6 months of vaginal delivery with an episiotomy repair with pain at the site of episiotomy which increases during her periods. On palpation, a nodular lesion is felt. The probable diagnosis is?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Endometriosis

Endometrial tissue implanted in surgical scar

↓

Hormonal stimulation during menstrual cycle

↓

Bleeding within scar tissue

↓

Painful nodular swelling

Cyclical pain in surgical scar = scar endometriosis

Cyclic pain at scar site with nodular lesion is classic for scar endometriosis.

Ectopic endometrial tissue responds to hormones, causing swelling and pain during menses.

Definitive treatment is: Wide Local Excision--> Hormonal therapy has limited benefit.

B) Retained suture

• Causes localized discomfort, but not cyclical pain.

C) Inclusion cyst

• Usually painless cystic swelling, not menstrual pain.

D) Melanoma

• Presents as pigmented lesion, unrelated to menstrual cycle.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A young girl presents with menstrual irregularity, acne, increased hair growth with a Ferriman Gallway score of 8, and a BMI of 29. Her mother has diabetes. Which is not a management option?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. OCP + Anti androgen

These features strongly suggest Polycystic Ovary Syndrome. Anti-androgens are not first-line therapy initially and are usually added only if hirsutism persists after OCP therapy.

First-line therapy is OCP alone. Anti-androgens are added only if symptoms persist after ≥6 months. Lifestyle modification and metabolic counselling are essential in PCOS.

PCOS is a common endocrine disorder characterized by:

| Feature | Explanation

| ------- | -----------

| Menstrual irregularity | Anovulation

| Hyperandrogenism | Acne, hirsutism

| Obesity | Insulin resistance

Diagnosis is based on Rotterdam criteria (any 2 of 3):

1. Oligo/anovulation
2. Hyperandrogenism
3. Polycystic ovaries on ultrasound

The Ferriman–Gallwey score assesses hirsutism.

| Score | Interpretation

| ----- | --------------

| <8 | Normal

| ≥8 | Hirsutism

This patient has mild hirsutism.

Treatment depends on symptoms and metabolic risk.

First-line management

| Treatment | Purpose

| --------- | -------

| Lifestyle modification | Weight reduction

| Exercise / yoga | Improves insulin resistance

| Combined oral contraceptive pills (OCP) | Regulate cycles and reduce androgen

Thus options A, C, and D are correct management options.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: In what proportion of cases is a complete vesicular mole found to be associated with Theca lutein cysts? (NEET PG 2015)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Between 20% and 30%

Theca lutein cysts are bilateral ovarian cysts caused by excessive ovarian stimulation from markedly elevated β-hCG levels. They are commonly associated with:

• Complete hydatidiform mole
• Multiple gestation
• Choriocarcinoma

In complete vesicular mole: Theca lutein cysts occur in approximately 20–30% of cases

Characteristics:

• Usually bilateral and multiloculated
• Caused by luteinization of theca interna cells
• Often regress spontaneously after evacuation of the mole and normalization of β-hCG levels

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What are the diagnostic criteria for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) as defined by the Modified Rotterdam Criteria? 1. Obesity 2. Delayed menstruation 3. Hirsutism 4. Insulin resistance
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 2 and 3

Modified Rotterdam Criteria (2003)

Diagnosis of PCOS requires any 2 out of the following 3 criteria after excluding other causes.

| Criterion | Description

| --------- | -----------

| Oligo-ovulation / anovulation | Irregular or delayed menstruation

| Clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism | Hirsutism, acne, ↑ testosterone

| Polycystic ovaries on ultrasound | ≥20 follicles or ovarian volume ≥10 mL

Thus in the options:

• Delayed menstruation → represents oligo-ovulation
• Hirsutism → represents hyperandrogenism

Hence 2 and 3 are correct.

Polycystic Ovaries on Ultrasound

Typical ultrasound features:

• ≥20 follicles measuring 2–9 mm
• Peripheral arrangement called “string of pearls”
• Ovarian volume ≥10 mL

Clinical Hyperandrogenism (Hirsutism)

Hyperandrogenism may present as:

• Hirsutism
• Acne
• Alopecia

Assessment commonly done using Ferriman–Gallwey score.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: When is dilatation and curettage contraindicated? (NEET PG 2018)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Pelvic inflammatory disease

Dilatation and curettage (D&C) is a gynecologic procedure used for:

• Endometrial sampling
• Management of abnormal uterine bleeding
• Incomplete abortion
• Removal of retained products of conception

Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) is a contraindication because instrumentation of an infected genital tract may:

• Spread infection
• Worsen pelvic sepsis
• Increase risk of infertility and tubo-ovarian abscess

Why other options are incorrect:

• Ectopic pregnancy may require uterine curettage for diagnostic purposes
• Menstrual irregularities are a common indication for D&C
• Endometriosis is not a contraindication

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following statements about polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) is not true? (NEET PG 2015)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Follicle-Stimulating Hormone (FSH) levels are reduced.

Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) is characterized by hyperandrogenism, chronic anovulation, and polycystic ovaries. Typical hormonal findings in PCOS:

• Increased LH levels
• Normal or mildly decreased FSH levels
• Increased androgen levels
• Increased estrogen (especially estrone) due to peripheral conversion of androgens

The LH:FSH ratio is often elevated because LH secretion increases disproportionately.

Why option B is NOT true: FSH levels are usually normal or only mildly low, not markedly reduced

Pathophysiology:

• Increased LH stimulates theca cells → excess androgen production
• Hyperinsulinemia further increases androgen synthesis

Failure of normal follicular maturation leads to anovulation

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following ultrasound findings is diagnostic of polycystic ovarian morphology?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. ≥20 follicles in one ovary

The international diagnostic guidelines for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)—specifically the updated consensus recommendations—define Polycystic Ovarian Morphology (PCOM) by the presence of 20 or more follicles (measuring 2–9 mm) in at least one ovary when using high-resolution transvaginal ultrasound transducers (>8 MHz). Alternatively, an ovarian volume of >10 mL in at least one ovary satisfies the definition. It does not require both ovaries to meet the threshold simultaneously

High-Yield Points

• Current cutoff: ≥20 follicles in one ovary (using high-frequency transvaginal ultrasound ≥8 MHz).
• Older Rotterdam criterion (2003): ≥12 follicles and/or ovarian volume >10 mL.
• Only one ovary needs to meet the criterion.
• PCOM alone does not diagnose PCOS; diagnosis requires fulfillment of accepted PCOS diagnostic criteria after excluding other causes.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which one of the following is correct regarding obesity and infertility?
options: It is associated with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
It is associated with hypergonadotropic hypogonadism
There is no change in HPO axis
It is always associated with endometrial atrophy
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. It is associated with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism

Obesity is an important cause of subfertility/infertility. It alters the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian (HPO) axis, leading to hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, ovulatory dysfunction, and menstrual irregularities.

Why not the other options?

• B. It is associated with hypergonadotropic hypogonadism: Hypergonadotropic hypogonadism is seen in primary ovarian failure, not obesity.
• C. There is no change in HPO axis: Obesity disrupts the HPO axis and impairs ovulation.
• D. It is always associated with endometrial atrophy: Obesity is associated with unopposed estrogen exposure, leading to endometrial hyperplasia and an increased risk of endometrial carcinoma, not atrophy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 14 yr old girl was brought by her mother with complaints that the child has not even menstruated once. On examination secondary sexual characters are seen and uterus and ovaries were seen to be normal on USG.What is next step of management?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Reassure mother and patient

This girl has secondary sexual characters but has not menstruated even once in her life(primary amenorrhea), hence it is  a case of a delayed puberty and the best option is to reassure the mother and the patient.

Delayed puberty in a female is considered if

* No secondary characters are noted by age of 13 years

OR

* With secondary sexual characters, if menses have not commenced by age of 16 years

Precocious puberty is considered if breast development or onset of puberty in those less than 8 years of age.

Note :

In actual clinical scenario in any girl of the reproductive age group presenting with amenorrhea a urine pregnancy test has to be done.

This is a controversial question. According to Williams Gynaecology 3rd edition and Shaw's Gynaecology 16th edition, puberty is considered delayed if menses have not commenced by age of 16 years with secondary sexual characters or no secondary sexual characters by age of 13 years.

According to the website Uptodate, delayed puberty is considered when there is no menses by 15 years of age or no secondary sexual characteristics by 13 years.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 19-year-old female comes to the OPD with complaints of weakness, amenorrhea, and fatigue. Upon eliciting history, she reveals that she is always worried about gaining weight. Her mother complains that she doesn't eat well. Her BMI is 15.8. Laboratory findings in this patient will show which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Hypersecretion of corticotrophin-releasing hormone

The given clinical vignette is suggestive of anorexia nervosa. Hypersecretion of corticotrophin-releasing hormone is seen in a patient with anorexia nervosa.

Anorexia nervosa is a type of eating disorder that is characterized by self-induced starvation to a significant degree, drive for thinness or a morbid fear of fatness, and the presence of medical signs and symptoms resulting from starvation.

Investigations in anorexia nervosa:

* Complete blood count: Leukopenia with a relative lymphocytosis

* Serum electrolyte: Hypokalemic alkalosis (Purging)

* Fasting serum glucose: Often low (emaciated phase) (Option D)

* Serum salivary amylase: Often elevated (if the patient is vomiting)

* ECG: ST segment and T-wave changes (secondary to electrolyte disturbances)

* Hypotension and bradycardia

* High serum cholesterol level (Option A)

* Endocrine changes (caused by the underweight):

* Amenorrhea

* Hypothyroidism (Option B)

* Hypersecretion of corticotrophin-releasing hormone

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 19-year-old female presents with primary amenorrhea. On examination, she has normal breast and pubic hair development, but her vagina ends in a blind pouch, and her uterus is not palpable. What is the next step in the investigation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Pelvic ultrasound

The given clinical scenario of a girl with primary amenorrhea, normal breasts, and pubic hair, with a blind-ending vagina and non-palpable uterus, is suggestive of Mullerian agenesis. The next step would be to do an ultrasound to look for uterine anomalies.

Absent uterus and vagina in a person with female genotype and phenotype are features of Mullerian agenesis, also known as Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser syndrome. In this condition, the ovaries are normal and secondary sexual characters are well-developed with normal external genitalia. This condition is associated with anomalies of the spine/skeleton and the kidneys along with the urinary tract.

Diagnosis is made with the help of pelvic sonography, MRI or laparoscopy. Patients may have rudimentary Mullerian bulbs without an endometrial cavity. These should be surgically excised if they are symptomatic.

Given below is an algorithm for the diagnosis of primary amenorrhea with secondary sexual characteristics:

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 23-year-old G3P1L1A1 at 37 weeks of gestation presents to the ER with labor pains. She has a previous history of emergency cesarean section and dilatation and curettage. During abdominal examination, fetal parts could be palpated easily. Per vaginal examination revealed a 5 cm dilated cervix and her vitals were: BP - 80/60 mm of Hg, RR - 20/ min, HR - 106/ min, SpO2 - 97% under room air. CTG showed a non-reassuring variable fetal heart rate pattern. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Uterine rupture

In the above clinical scenario of a G3P1L1A1 with previous history of emergency cesarean section and dilatation and curettage, presented with labor pain on abdominal examination, fetal parts could be palpated easily, with patient being hypotensive, tachycardic and CTG showed a non-reassuring variable fetal heart rate pattern points towards the diagnosis of the given clinical scenario is uterine rupture.

The risk factors of uterine rupture include:

* More the number (>2) of prior cesarean delivery

* lnterpregnancy interval <24 months

* Induced labor, especially with misoprostol

* Augmentation of labor with high dose oxytocin

* Women having single layer uterine closure in prior cesarean delivery compared to double layer closure

Hypotension, tachycardia, dizziness, confusion, abdominal pain, scar site tenderness are all the signs of uterine rupture. CTG in uterine rupture will show non-reassuring variable fetal heart rate which might progress to late decelerations and bradycardia.

Differential diagnoses for uterine rupture:

* Pre-eclampsia

* Eclampsia

* Pulmonary embolism - amniotic fluid embolism / venous embolism

* Abruptio placenta

* Anaphylaxis to anaesthesia

* Peripartum cardiomyopathy

Management of uterine rupture:

* Confirm the fetal station and arrest of labour

* Stabilize the patient's vitals

* Immediate laparotomy should be performed as early as possible to avoid neurological or hypoxic sequelae in newborns.

* Depending on the extent of rupture and vitals on the table decision of uterine suturing or hysterectomy or sub-total hysterectomy may be taken.

Other options:

Option A : Amniotic fluid embolism - can present with similar symptoms but oxygen saturation will be deteriorating to less than 95% and the respiratory rate will increase.

Option B: Placental abruption -The patient will present with painful vaginal bleeding. There is no history of hypertension and BP is not elevated

Oprion D: Placenta previa is characterized by abnormal implantation of the placenta over the lower uterine segment and presents with painless vaginal bleeding.

Pearl PF2186: Indications & contraindications for induction of labor

Indications:

* Uncontrolled maternal diabetes mellitus

* Gestational hypertension

* Pre-eclampsia

* Post-term pregnancy

* Abruption placentae

* Premature rupture of membranes

* Rh-isoimmunization

* Intra-uterine growth restriction (IUGR)

* Intra-uterine death (IUD)

* Oligohydramnios

Contraindications:

* Contracted/distorted pelvis and cephalopelvic disproportion

* Placenta previa or vasa previa

* Active genital herpes

* Pelvic tumor & carcinoma cervix

* Transverse lie or footling breech

* Appreciable macrosomia

* Severe hydrocephalus

* Umbilical cord prolapse

* High-risk pregnancy with fetal compromise

* Previous classical cesarean or hysterotomy

* Previous history of uterine rupture

* Pelvic surgeries like vesicovaginal fistula/rectovaginal fistula/pelvic floor repair (third or fourth-degree perineal tears repair)

* Previous 3 or more lower transverse cesarian sections.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 25 year old woman comes for her regular antenatal check up. Which arterial gas abnormality is expected to be seen in this woman?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Chronic respiratory alkalosis

Chronic respiratory alkalosis is a normal physiologic change seen in pregnancy.

Progesterone directly stimulates central respiratory centers to increase tidal volume and minute ventilation. This leads to increased PaO2 and decreased PaCO2. This paradoxically causes physiological dyspnea. It is an increased awareness of a desire to breathe.

This results in chronic respiratory alkalosis. Bicarbonate level is decreased from 26 to 22 mmol/L(approximately) in metabolic compensation of respiratory alkalosis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 25-year-old female, with a previous history of chlamydia infection, now presents with low-grade fever and non-specific lower abdominal pain. Examination reveals mild diffuse lower abdominal tenderness on deep palpation, cervical motion tenderness, and a mucopurulent vaginal discharge. What is the long-term sequelae of this condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Infertility

In the above clinical scenario fo apatient with previous history of chlamydia infection, now with low-grade fever, lower abdominal pain, lower abdominal tenderness on deep palpation, cervical motion tenderness, and a mucopurulent vaginal discharge points towards the diagnosis of pelvic inflammatory disease and the most important complication of it is infertility.

Pelvic Inflammatory disease involves inflammation of the upper genital tract including the fallopian tubes as well as the ovaries. The most common cause of PID in sexually active young females is sexually transmitted infections involving gonococci and chlamydia.

Pelvic inflammatory disease and salpingitis may lead to sterility. Other complications are tubo-ovarian abscesses (hydrosalpinx or pyosalpinx), chronic interstitial salpingitis, tubo ovarian cyst and ectopic pregnancies. Rarely peritonitis may develop with perihepatic inflammation (Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome). The patient presents with right upper quadrant pain and tenderness with abnormal liver function tests.

Risk factors of PID:

* Menstrual teenagers

* Multiple sexual partners

* Absence of contraceptive pills

* Previous history of PID

* IUCD users

Protective factors of PID:

* Barrier methods (condoms, diaphragm)

* Oral contraceptive pills

* Pregnancy

* Menopause

Criteria to diagnose PID:

Any one of the minimum criteria + 1 or more additional criteria are required for the clinical diagnosis of PID.

Minimum criteria

*

* Lower abdominal tenderness

* Adnexal tenderness

* Cervical motion tenderness.

Additional criteria

*

* Oral temperature >38.3 oC

* Mucopurulent cervical or vaginal discharge and cervical friability

* Presence of abundant WBC on saline microscopy of vaginal fluid

* Raised ESR or CRP

* Laboratory documentation of positive cervical infection with Gonorrhea or C.trachomatis.

The definitive diagnosis of PID is through:

* Histopathologic evidence of endometritis on biopsy.

* Imaging (TVS/MRI) evidence of thickened fluid-filled tubes i.e., tubo-ovarian abscess.

* Laparoscopic evidence of PID.

Treatment

* OPD management of PID:

* Inj.Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose + Doxycycline 100 mg BD x 14 days + Metronidazole 500 mg BD x 14 days.

* Parenteral treatment for PID (in hospitalised:

* Inj Cefotetan 2g IV BD + Doxycycline 100 mg BD or

* Inj Cefoxitin 2g IV QID + Doxycycline 100 mg BD.

To minimize disease transmission, women should be instructed to abstain from sexual intercourse until therapy is completed, symptoms have resolved, and partners have been adequately treated.

Pearl PF1533: Organisms Responsible for Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

Sexually transmitted: Gonococcus, Chlamydia, Mycoplasma, Trichomonas
Aerobes: Staphylococci , Streptococci ,E. coli

Anaerobes: Bacteroides fragilis, Peptococcus, Clostridium, Actinomyces (IUD)

Others: Tubercular salpingitis

and

and

Minimal damage but the infection may lead to infertility

Tuboplasty

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 26-year-old unmarried woman complained of missed periods. She always had regular menstrual cycles. The pelvic examination is normal. What is the next step of management for this patient?
options: Reassure her that it’s normal to have delayed period
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Beta HCG estimation

The first step to do if a woman misses her period is to rule out pregnancy. Beta-HCG estimation is the next step.

The most common test used for this purpose is the urine pregnancy test (UPT). Serum beta HCG can detect a pregnancy as early as 5 days before the first missed period.

Amenorrhoea is the absence of menstruation.

* It is a symptom and not a disease entity.

* Amenorrhea can be physiological or pathological.

* Primary amenorrhea is defined as no menstruation by age 15.

* Secondary amenorrhea is defined as the absence of menses for 6 or more months or the length of 3 cycles after the establishment of regular menstrual cycles. The most common cause of secondary amenorrhea is pregnancy.

Pearl PF1534: Beta hCG in pregnancy

The pattern of beta hCG :

First detectable in plasma 7 to 9 days post-LH surge

⇓

Doubles every 2 days

⇓

Peaks at 8 to 10 weeks of gestation(~100 IU/mL)

⇓

Begins to decline at 10 to 12 weeks

⇓

Plateau at 16 weeks till term

* Higher maternal plasma hCG levels- Multifetal pregnancy, erythroblastosis fetalis, gestational trophoblastic disease, Down syndrome.

* Lower hCG plasma levels -early pregnancy wastage and ectopic pregnancy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 29-year-old female complains of foul-smelling vaginal discharge. A giemsa stained smear of the discharge is shown below. Which of the following is not seen in this condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Curdy white discharge

The image shows Trichomonas vaginalis and infection causes a frothy, greenish-yellow discharge. Curdy white discharge is seen in vaginal candidiasis.

Trichomonas is a protozoan that’s slightly larger than a leucocyte with four anterior flagella and a single posterior flagellum. It exhibits jerky or twitching motility.

Infection of the female genital tract causes the following symptoms:

* Foul-smelling, frothy, greenish-yellow discharge per vaginum

* Itching around the vulva

* Dysuria and frequent micturition

The vagina looks red and inflamed. The inflamed cervix looks like a strawberry with punctate hemorrhagic spots.

The condition is treated with a single 2 gm dose of metronidazole or tinidazole. The female’s partner must also be treated simultaneously.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 30-year-old female who was using IUCD for contraception presents in the emergency following two episodes of painless spotting per vagina preceded by amenorrhea for 8 weeks. She complained of lightheadedness and her blood pressure is 80/50 mmHg and the pulse rate is 138 beats/minute, with a positive urine pregnancy test. What should be the management of this patient? IUCD- Intra-uterine contraceptive device
options: IV fluids followed by oral methotrexate
Stabilizing the patient followed by suction evacuation
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Immediate laparotomy

The given clinical scenario implies a case of hemodynamically unstable ruptured ectopic pregnancy, and the management of this patient would be a laparotomy.

The given clinical scenario strongly indicates a case of ruptured ectopic pregnancy based on several key clinical findings. The patient's history of IUCD usage is significant as it increases the risk of ectopic pregnancy. The presence of amenorrhea for 8 weeks is particularly noteworthy, around which clinical manifestations of ectopic pregnancy appears.

The patient's presentation with vaginal bleeding, preceded by amenorrhea of more than 4 weeks, is highly suggestive of an ectopic gestation. This suspicion is further strengthened by a positive urine pregnancy test. Most critically, the patient's unstable vital signs point to internal blood loss, which is a classic presentation of a ruptured ectopic pregnancy. The combination of these findings creates a clinical picture that warrants immediate medical attention for suspected ruptured ectopic pregnancy.

In unstable patients with such findings, urgent surgical management with exploratory laparotomy is warranted. This approach helps control bleeding and manage hemodynamic instability. It also provides the surgeon with improved visibility of the operative field.

Risk factors of tubal ectopic pregnancy:

* Abnormal tube anatomy

* Surgeries done on the tubes earlier- previous ectopic, fertility restorative, sterilization.

* Sexually transmitted diseases causing distortion of tubal architecture

* Peritubal adhesions

* Salpingitis isthmica nodosa

* Congenital anomalies secondary to diethyl stilbesterol exposure

* Infertility, Artificial reproductive techniques

* Smoking

* Intrauterine contraceptive systems

Other differentials :

* In Abruptio placenta there is painful vaginal bleeding that is associated with contractions and uterine hypertonicity which have not been mentioned in the question, which is basically a shock scenario due to an underlying a condition.

*  In Placenta previa the classic presentation is painless, bright red vaginal bleeding that often stops spontaneously and then recurs with labor. The bleeding most likely occurs in 3rd trimester and does not lead to a shock-like condition.

* In an un-ruptured ectopic pregnancy, there is no history of shock-like symptoms.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 30-year-old female, married for the past 5 years, presents with complaints of inability to conceive despite regular intercourse. Physical examination is unremarkable. Semen analysis of the husband revealed no abnormalities. Hysterosalpingography reveals the following picture. The anomaly shown in the image below falls under which category of the american fertility society classification of mullerian duct anomalies?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Class II

The image shows a hysterosalpingogram of a unicornuate uterus, which falls under Class II of Mullerian duct anomalies

In the unicornuate uterus, the formation of the uterus and fallopian tube occurs entirely from one Mullerian duct due to developmental arrest of other Mullerian ducts. On Hysterosalpingography, the endometrial cavity usually appears fusiform shape tapering at the apex and draining into a single Fallopian tube. The uterus generally appears shifted off the midline.

The AFS (American Fertility Society) classification of Mullerian duct anomalies is as follows:

* Class I—Mullerian agenesis or hypoplasia.

* Class II—Unicornuate uterus, with absent or defective development of one Mullerian duct.

* Class III—Uterus didelphys

* Class IV—Bicornuate uterus

* Class V—Septate uterus

* Class VI—Arcuate uterus

Infertility is defined as lack of conception despite 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse in women aged < 35 years old and despite 6 months of regular unprotected intercourse in women aged > 35 years old.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 30-year-old woman presents with severe dysmenorrhoea,dyspareunia infertility and a diagnosis of endometriosis was made.The patient was posted for laparoscopy and at surgery dense pelvic adhesions were seen with bowel stuck to the fundus. Ovaries were cystic and stuck to each other. What is the next step of management in this patient?
options: Gestrinone to decrease the LH surge
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Cystectomy and adhesiolysis

The clinical scenario is suggestive of endometriosis and the next step in the management of this patient is cystectomy and adhesiolysis.

After the surgery the patient is advised to start infertility treatment too.

Medical management of endometriosis:

* Gestrinone is an anti-estrogenic, anti-progestational, and mildly anabolic drug that reduces sex-hormone-binding globulin to release free testosterone. It also decreases the LH surge. It causes regression of lesions and amenorrhea. It is a 19-nortestosterone derivative similar to danazol, but with fewer side effects.

* Combined oral contraceptives are used for symptom control and alleviate disease. These also cause menstrual cycle regulation and delay pregnancy.

* Oral progestogens exert an anti-estrogenic effect and cause decidualization and endometrial atrophy. This causes disease regression. It doesn't prevent ovulation, thus is suitable for women who are trying to conceive.

* Mirena IUCDs reduce dysmenorrhea and menorrhagia. It is a single-sitting treatment with minimal side effects.

* Aromatase inhibitors like letrozole are anti-estrogens given for disease regression.

* Anti-inflammatory drugs like mefenamic acid and naproxen relieve dysmenorrhea.

Therapeutic procedures:

* Aspiration of Peritoneal fluid from the cul-de-sac removes PGE2, relieves dysmenorrhea, pelvic pain, and improves fertility

* Destruction of endometriotic lesions <3cm with diathermy, Nd-YAG laser or CO2 vaporization can be attempted.

* Larger lesions and chocolate cysts can be excised.

* Cystectomy can be done for pelvic pain but can reduce fertility potential.

* Laparoscopic breaking of adhesions relieves dysmenorrhea and chronic pelvic pain. It also restores tubal patency and improves ovulation. Pre-sacral neurectomy can be done simultaneously..

* Laser uterosacral nerve ablation (LUNA) is done for pelvic pain.

Pearl PF1294: Endometriosis

Sites of Endometriosis:

* Pelvic endometriosis: Pelvic peritoneum, the pouch of Douglas, uterosacral ligament.

* Rectovaginal endometriosis.

* Ovarian endometriosis.

* Chocolate cyst of the ovary.

* Other sites—appendix, pelvic lymph nodes.

* Metastatic— lungs, umbilicus, scar endometriosis.

One pathology review revealed that endometriosis has been identified on all organs except the spleen.

Examination findings in endometriosis:

* Abdomen: Cystic swelling, fixed and tender.

* Pelvis: Cystic tender mass.

* Vaginal examination: Fixed, tender, retroverted uterus. Tenderness in the lateral fornices (indicative of endometriosis even if no mass).

* Speculum inspection of the Posterior fornix: Bluish/blackish puckered spots on speculum, tender to touch. The presence of puckered spots is pathognomonic of endometriosis.

* Posterior Fornix Palpation: Uterosacral ligaments & pouch of Douglas feel thickened and shotty with multiple small palpable nodules. This is called the cobblestone feel of uterosacral ligaments.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 34-year-old G2P1L1 presents with abdominal pain, bleeding per vaginum in labourand loss of fetal movements.She occasionally smokes but does not consume alcohol or recreational drugs. On examination, her pulse rate is 80 bpm and BP is 150/90 mm of Hg and a tense abdomen on palpation. What is the probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Abruptio placenta

The given clinical picture with abdominal pain, bleeding per vaginum, and loss of fetal movements in a hypertensive pregnant woman points to the diagnosis of placental abruption.

Premature separation of a normally implanted placenta is placental abruption.

Hypertension and smoking are important etiological factors in abruption. Hypertension leads to vasospasm of the placental blood vessels, which causes uteroplacental insufficiency.

The hemorrhage into decidua basalis causes separation and compression of the placenta. This leads to a compromise of circulation to fetus leading to fetal distress. The bleeding may escape through the cervix to cause external hemorrhage.

The common etiological factors for abruptio placentae include:

* Hypertension

* Preterm prematurely ruptured membranes

* Advanced maternal age

* Cigarette smoking

* Cocaine abuse

* Trauma

* Uterine fibroids

* Isolated single umbilical artery

* Short umbilical cord

* Prior abruption

* Subclinical hypothyroidism

Clinical classification of placental abruption:

Grade 1

Vaginal bleeding mild to moderate

Uterine tenderness is always present

Maternal pulse increased, BP maintained

Maternal shock absent

Other options:

* Placenta previa presents with painless vaginal bleeding. Hypertension is not a predisposing factor. High-risk factors include multiparty, previous cesarean, or myomectomy scar in the uterus.

* In preterm labor, fetal movements are not compromised.

* Hydramnios does not present with bleeding PV.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 45-year P3L3 woman presented with a lower abdominal mass and lower abdominal discomfort. On examination, the uterus appears uniformly enlarged and adnexa is free. MRI shows the presence of a myometrial cyst. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Adenomyosis

Multiparous women > 40yrs, presenting with abdominal mass with free adnexa and myometrial cysts on MRI, all point towards a diagnosis of adenomyosis.

Adenomyosis (Endometritis interna):

Adenomyosis is ingrowth of endometrium ( stromal and glandular components ) directly into the myometrium.

Etiology: Vigorous curettage, repeated childbirth or excess of estrogen

Clinical features:

* Multiparous females >40 years

* Most common symptom: Menorrhagia > Dysmenorrhea

* Pelvic discomfort, backache, dyspareunia

* Per-Vaginal: Symmetrical enlargement of the uterus ( corresponding to <12-14 weeks of pregnancy )

* Bimanual examination: Halbans sign: Tender, softened uterus

Diagnosis:

* It is mainly clinical

* Diagnostic hysteroscopy with curettage

Management of adenomyosis

* Total Hysterectomy ( Treatment of choice )

* Localized excision/ Levonorgestrel containing IUCD is tried in younger women.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 60-year-old woman comes with chronic vulval itching and pain. On examination, there is a vulval lesion suspicious of vulval cancer. Which of the following lymph node/s should be considered for sentinel node biopsy to look for the metastatic spread?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Superficial inguinal lymph nodes

The first lymph node/s the vulval malignancy spreads to is superficial inguinal lymph nodes.

The sentinel lymph node, which is the first node in a regional lymphatic basin that receives lymph flow from the primary tumour, is often used to assess the presence or absence of metastatic lesions in the lymph nodes.

The most common type of spread in vulval cancer: Lymphatic. A most important prognostic factor is Lymph node status.

First lymph node involved: Superficial inguinal lymph node > Deep inguinal lymph node > (Gland of Cloquet) Femoral group of lymph nodes to external iliac glands, obturator and common iliac nodes in the advanced stages. The sentinel lymph node biopsy is helpful for evaluating the spread of vulval cancer.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 62-year-old nulliparous female who is on hormone replacement therapy developed abdominal pain. On examination, a non-tender right adnexal mass was palpable. She underwent laparotomy and the resected ovaries are shown below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Ovarian carcinoma

The clinical scenario in a 62-year-old female with a larger, irregular and solid tumor growth with cystic spaces and necrosis is suggestive of ovarian carcinoma.

The risk factors of ovarian carcinoma are:

* Low parity

* Infertility

* Unopposed estrogen therapy

* Obesity

* Smoking

Note: Hormone replacement therapy does not provide protection against the development of a borderline ovarian tumor.

Complications of an ovarian tumor:

* Torsion

Other options:

Option A: There is no proper entity as Nodular carcinoma of the ovary

Option B: Chocolate cysts are seen in endometriosis involving the ovary. The cysts form secondary to endometriotic implants in the ovarian stroma that bleed periodically and undergo shedding.

Option C: Fibroids are benign growth of smooth muscles of the uterus and not the ovary.

Pearl PF0900: WHO Classification of Ovarian Tumors

questions.text: A G2P1L1 lady underwent LSCS in previous pregnancy for fetal distress.This time she had an uneventful vaginal birth after caesarean section (VBAC) but the placenta could not be removed completely.The cord snapped on traction but the placenta did not deliver.She also started to bleed more profusely now.What is the likely reason for this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Placenta percreta

The above clinical scenario with a h/o caesarean section with adherent placenta is placenta percreta.

Placenta accreta syndromes (PAS) include any placental implantation with abnormally firm adherence to myometrium because of the partial or total absence of the decidua basalis and imperfect development of the fibrinoid.

* The increased risk conveyed by previous uterine trauma(Ex, cesarean delivery) may be partially explained by increased vulnerability of the decidua to trophoblast invasion following incision into the decidua.

* Microscopically, placental villi are anchored to muscle fibers rather than to decidual cells. Decidual deficiency then prevents normal placental separation after delivery.

* In cases of first- and second-trimester accrete syndromes, there is usually hemorrhage that is the consequence of coexisting placenta previa.

* MR imaging can be used as an adjunct to sonography to define anatomy, degree of invasion, and possible ureteral or bladder involvement.

* Complications: Variable degree of hemorrhage

* Treatment: C-section followed by Hysterectomy

Variants of placenta accreta syndromes are classified by the depth of trophoblastic growth:

* Placenta accreta: Villi are attached to the myometrium.

* Placenta increta: Villi invade the myometrium.

* Placenta percreta: Villi penetrate through the myometrium and to or through the serosa.

The Nitabuch layer (also known as the fibrinoid layer) is a layer of fibrinoid degeneration where the invading trophoblasts meet the decidua basalis. The absence of the Nitabuch layer in the uterine decidua leads to the placenta accreta spectrum.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A mother of a 5 day old baby presents with the complaint that her baby is "unable to latch on " for breastfeeding. She also says there is some leakage of milk at times and on examination, there is bilateral tenderness and swelling. What is the most likely cause of this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Breast engorgement

The most likely cause for this is due to breast engorgement.

Breast Engorgement :

* Common in women who do not breastfeed often, leakage of milk and breast pain is seen.

* Presents 24 to 72 hours post-partum, peaks 3 to 5 days after delivery and resolves spontaneously

* Characterized by bilateral breast tenderness and swelling typically

* Treatment is by cold compresses and analgesics.

* Breasts can be supported with a sports bra or binder.

* Antibiotics are not indicated.

* Pharmacological or hormonal agents are in general not recommended to suppress lactation.

Other options:

Lactational mastitis:

* Pathogenesis: Bacteria enters ducts through nipple and multiplies in stagnant milk.

* A firm, red, tender, swollen quadrant of unilateral breast, +/- myalgias, chills, malaise

* Treatment:analgesia,frequent breast feeding or pumping,antibiotic of choice: Dicloxacillin or Cephalexin

Bacterial mastitis

* Localized inflammationdue to ascending infection or infection due to milk stasis

* Dull pain

* Tenderness, erythema

* Antibiotics, analgesics

Breast abscess

* Occurs as a complication of mastitis, pus formation

* Throbbing pain

* Point tenderness, erythema

* Induration of skin(if chronic), lymphadenopathy

* Fluctuation test +ve

* Aspiration of Pus, antibiotics, analgesics

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A patient is seen in the OPD after her delivery which was 5 days ago. She presents with smelly greenish vaginal discharge. What is the initial step in the management of this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Per vaginum examination

The most likely diagnosis in this patient is postpartum endometritis however, the next line of management in this patient is to undergo a per vaginal examination to rule out other differentials.

Puerperal infection:

* The most common site of puerperal infection is a placental site in vaginal delivery and uterine incision in cesarean section.

* The most common manifestation of puerperal infection is Endometritis.

* The most common cause of puerperal sepsis is Streptococcus.

* The most important risk factor for the development of puerperal sepsis is the route of delivery (Cesarean > Vaginal).

* The only proven way of decreasing uterine infection following cesarean section is by administrating a single dose of ampicillin or 1st generation cephalosporin at the time of cesarean delivery. None of the other steps with respect to surgical closure of the abdomen have proven beneficial in decreasing puerperal infection.

* Treatment is with antibiotics and symptomatic measures.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A woman 3 months postpartum who regularly breastfeeds presented with amenorrhea for 3 months and is concerned about this problem and is requesting surgery. Before considering surgery what can be done to manage this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Reassure

The best management of this patient is to reassure her as this is normal during postpartum and is due to lactactional amenorrhea.

Lactactional amenorrhea:

* Type of secondary amenorrhea due to the effect or prolactin secretion.

* During lactation, there are pulsatile bursts of prolactin secretion in response to suckling.

* Prolactin suppresses GnRH, LH and FSH causing lactational amenorrhea.

* Regular lactation with one feed at night delays ovulation and pregnancy for up to 6 months, provided she remains amenorrhoeic.

* After 6 months, lactation has no bearing on ovulation and pregnancy can occur, despite amenorrhoea and might need other forms of contraception.

Other options:

Oral combined pill in a lactating woman is contraindicated because:

* It reduces the quality and quantity of milk.

* The hormone in the milk may be harmful to the infant.

* Increased risk of thromboembolism.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: As a senior resident in the OBG department, You would consider uterine artery embolization as a treatment option in all of the following cases except ________
options: Prior to the removal of Placenta accreta in Multiparous woman
Patient diagnosed with calcified and pedunculated submucous fibroids
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Patient diagnosed with calcified and pedunculated submucous fibroids

Uterine artery embolization is indicated in all the above-given cases except in a patient with calcified and pedunculated submucous fibroids.

A calcified fibroid does not shrink with the procedure. The pedunculated fibroids can fall off after the procedure resulting in intrauterine or peritoneal infections.

Hence, the calcified, submucous, and subserous types of fibroids are contraindications for this procedure.

Other indications for Uterine artery embolization(UAE) include,

* Postpartum hemorrhage.

* Placenta accreta to reduce bleeding prior to placental removal, or caesarean delivery.

* This technique is most suited for menorrhagia in a multiparous woman

Technique:

* Under local sedation, bilateral UAE is approached through percutaneous femoral catheterization.

* It is done using polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), gel foam particles or metal coils.

Embolization reduces vascularity and the size of the fibroid in 3–4 months

Advantages of UAE:

* No major surgery.

* No intraoperative bleeding.

* Short hospital stay.

* Less abdominal adhesions.

Pearl PF1535: Contraindications to Uterine artery embolization

Absolute contraindications:

* GnRH agonist use

* Asymptomatic fibroids

* Pregnancy

* Pelvic inflammatory disease

* Uterine malignancy

* Calcified fibroid

Relative contraindications:

* A desire for future pregnancy: Poor uterine perfusion and pelvic adhesions following UAE would negatively impact fertility, and result in obstetric complications or adverse fetal effects.

* Postmenopausal status: The procedure is indicated primarily for premenopausal women since fibroids tend to decrease in size and symptoms improve or resolve after menopause. An enlarging uterus after menopause should raise the suspicion of malignancy and careful follow-up is warranted.

* Subserosal or submucosal fibroids: They are pedunculated and may detach either intraperitoneally or within the uterine cavity. Detachment may be associated with sterile peritonitis or intrauterine infection.

* Size or number of fibroids: The volume of necrosis after UAE in a large fibroid uterus can be substantial with a proportionate level of postprocedural pain and risk of infection.

* Contraindications to radiologic contrast agents.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: In a patient being treated for eclampsia, the next dose of MgSO4 should be skipped if:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Knee jerks are sluggish

The next dose of MgSO4 should be skipped if there are signs of magnesium toxicity.

Repeat injections of Mg So4 are given only if respiratory rate is more than 12/min, knee jerks are present, urine output exceeds 30 ml/hr.

Monitoring of magnesium toxicity:
- heart block, Chest pain,
- Decreased respiratory rate(<12 per minute)
- Urine output (<30ml/h)
- Loss of deep tendon reflexes (first sign)

Management of magnesium toxicity:
- Stop magnesium therapy
- Injection of calcium gluconate 10ml (10% solution) IV
- Estimation of creatinine levels and serum magnesium and

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Minimum number of antenatal visits according to WHO is ______
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 8

According to WHO, the minimum number of antenatal visits should be 8.

Ideal number of antenatal visits is 12-14.

The ideal number of antenatal visits should be:

* Monthly visits upto 28 weeks

* Two weekly visits between 28-36 weeks

* Weekly visits from 36 weeks onwards

This means a total of 12-15 visits.

In the Indian scenario, according to MCH the suggested schedule is as follows and requires minimum of 4 visits:

* 1st visit: within 12 weeks preferably as soon as pregnancy is suspected, for the registration of pregnancy and 1st antenatal check-up.

* 2nd visit: between 14-26 weeks

* 3rd visit: between 28-34 weeks

* 4th visit: between 36 weeks and term

A booked case is one that has at least 3 antenatal visits, with two visits in the third trimester.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The following chart shows the hormonal variations in the menstrual cycle. Identify the true statement : (LH: luteinizing hormone, FSH: follicle-stimulating hormone)
options: The blue line represents FSH hormone
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. The blue line represents FSH hormone

The blue line represents follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) in the menstrual cycle.

Other options :

* The pink line represents luteinizing hormone.

* The grey line represents estrogen.

* The purple line represents progesterone.

Phases of the menstrual cycle :

Follicular phase (days 0–14)

* A primordial follicle develops to the Graafian stage, with atresia of neighboring follicles.

* LH and FSH receptors are up-regulated in theca and granulosa cells.

* Estradiol levels increase and cause proliferation of the uterus.

* FSH and LH levels are suppressed by the negative feedback effect of estradiol on the anterior pituitary.

* Progesterone levels are low.

Ovulation (day 14)

* Occurs 14 days before menses, regardless of cycle length. Thus, in a 28-day cycle, ovulation occurs on day 14; in a 35-day cycle, ovulation occurs on day 22.

* A burst of estradiol synthesis at the end of the follicular phase has a positive feedback effect on the secretion of FSH and LH (LH surge).

* Ovulation occurs as a result of the estrogen-induced LH surge.

* Estrogen levels decrease just after ovulation (but rise again during the luteal phase).

* Cervical mucus increases in quantity; it becomes less viscous and more penetrable by sperm.

Luteal phase (days 14–28)

* Progesterone levels are high.

* The corpus luteum begins to develop, and it synthesizes estrogen and progesterone. Vascularity and secretory activity of the endometrium increase to prepare for receipt of a fertilized egg.

* Basal body temperature increases because of the effect of progesterone on the hypothalamic thermoregulatory center.

* If fertilization does not occur, the corpus luteum regresses at the end of the luteal phase. As a result, estradiol and progesterone levels decrease abruptly.

Menses (days 0–4)

* The endometrium is sloughed because of the abrupt withdrawal of estradiol and progesterone.

Pearl PF0568: Hormonal Regulation of Menstrual Cycle

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following indication is not true regarding medical termination of pregnancy?
options: Baby with serious mental or physical abnormality
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. When the family is large

All the options except, option B : family being large, is an indication for medical termination of pregnancy.

MTP act was passed on August 1971 in India and came into effect from April.

Indications :

* Therapeutic : When continuation of pregnancy endangers the life of the woman, or may injure her physical or mental health.

* Eugenic : The risk of child being born with serious mental or physical abnormality. This includes first trimester viral infections, maternal drug intake (thalidomide, cortisone, antimitotics), xray or radioisotope treatment of the mother, insanity of parents and viral hepatitis.

* Humanitarian : Pregnancy resulted from rape.

* Social : Pregnancy resulted from failure of contraceptives.

Pearl PF1107: Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act - MTP Act 1971

MTP Act 1971

Indications :

* Therapeutic : When continuation of pregnancy endangers the life of the woman, or may injure her physical or mental health.

* Eugenic : The risk of child being born with serious mental or physical abnormality. This includes first trimester viral infections, maternal drug intake (thalidomide, cortisone, antimitotics), xray or radioisotope treatment of the mother, insanity of parents and viral hepatitis.

* Humanitarian : Pregnancy resulted from rape.

* Social : Pregnancy resulted from failure of contraceptives.

Rules :

* Only a registered medical practitioner who is qualified (one who has assisted in performance of 25 cases of MTP in a recognized hospital) can terminate a pregnancy.

* MTP should be carried out in a government or government recognised hospital.

* Private hospitals may take up MTP if they obtain a license from the chief medical officer of the district.

* The consent of the woman is required for conducting an abortion. The written consent of the guardian is required if the woman is a minor or mentally ill. Consent of the husband is not necessary.

* If the woman is not willing, abortion can not be performed on the request of the husband alone.

* The woman need not produce proof of her age. The statement of the woman that she is over 18 years of age is accepted.

* It is enough for the woman to say that she was raped, and it is not necessary that a complaint was lodged with the police.

* Professional secrecy has to be maintained.

* If the period of pregnancy is below 20 weeks, it can be terminated on the opinion of a single doctor.

* If the period of pregnancy is between 20-24 weeks, two doctors must opine that there is an indication. Once there is an indication, the termination can be done by any one doctor.

* In an emergency, the termination can be done by a single doctor, even without the required training, even after 20 weeks, without consulting a second doctor, in a private hospital which is not recognised.

* The termination of pregnancy by a person, who is not a registered medical practitioner (the person concerned), or in an unrecognised hospital (administrative head) shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than 2 years, but which may extend to 7 years.

Confidentiality :

The head of the hospital must maintain a register for recording the details of MTP. This register is a secret document which should be kept under safe custody for five years, and each patient is given a reference number. The name of the patient should not be entered anywhere, any case sheet or operation theatre register or any other record.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is true regarding UTI in pregnancy?
options: It is lower in people with sickle cell trait
The preferred antibiotic in pregnancy is amoxicillin
If ASB is not treated 75 % of them will develop symptomatic infection
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. The preferred antibiotic in pregnancy is amoxicillin

The true statement regarding UTI in pregnancy is that the preferred antibiotic in pregnancy is amoxicillin.

Asymptomatic bacteriuria(ASB) is characterized by persistent and actively multiplying bacteria in the urinary tract without any symptoms. It is defined as the presence of ≥105 colony-forming units/mL in a urine culture. Its prevalence during pregnancy is around 2-7% and it is a precursor of infection.

It is more common in patients with sickle cell anaemia/trait and diabetes. There is a high risk of developing chronic renal lesions in later life. ASB in pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of premature labour and low birth weight.

If ASB is not treated approximately 25% of the affected women will develop symptomatic infection during pregnancy

The oral antibiotics that can be used to treat asymptomatic bacteriuria are amoxicillin, ampicillin, cephalosporin, nitrofurantoin, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Recurrent cases need to be treated until delivery with prophylactic doses.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following methods of cervical ripening is a type of hygroscopic dilator?
options: Foley catheter at internal os of cervix
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Intracervical laminaria tent

Among the given methods of cervical ripening, the one which is a type of hygroscopic dilator is an intracervical laminaria tent.

Hygroscopic osmotic dilators are devices that draw water from cervical tissues and expand to gradually dilate the cervix. They expand to an ultimate diameter 3-4 times that of its dry state.

Laminaria tent is derived from various species of Laminaria algae that are harvested from the ocean floor. Synthetic dilators include Dilapan and Lamicel.

The image below shows Dilapan on the left and Laminaria tent on the right:

Pharmacological methods of cervical ripening:

Misoprostol at a dose of 25 μg is placed in the posterior fornix. Although it has increased efficacy, it is associated with a higher incidence of meconium-stained amniotic fluid (MSAF) and uterine tachysystole, especially when used in higher doses.

Dinoprostone is the synthetic analog of PGE2, available in three forms, as a gel, as a time-release vaginal insert, and as a suppository. Of these, the first two forms are used in cervical ripening whereas suppository is used only in abortion

The gel form is available in a prefilled syringe for local application in the cervical canal. The dosage used per procedure is 0.5 mg. This procedure can be repeated for a maximum of 3 doses in 24 hours with a time interval of 6 hours between each administration. The vaginal insert has a dose of 10 mg of dinoprostone. 0.3 mg of the drug is released per hour. It is placed horizontally in the posterior fornix.

Monitoring uterine contraction and fetal heart rate is a must after each dose. Adverse effects of dinoprostone include uterine tachysystole (especially when the gel is used in labour that has started spontaneously).

Cervidil (Dinoprostone) vaginal insert:

Note: Dinoprostone, which is a synthetic analogue of PGE2, not to be confused with Dinoprost, is a natural PGF2-α preparation.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 16 year old girl presents to the OPD with a history of primary amenorrhoea and cyclical pain. Perineal examination reveals a bulge protruding from the vagina and is shown as below. Identify the cause of this presentation:
options: Transverse septum in the proximal vagina
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Imperforate hymen

A history of cyclical abdominal pain, primary amenorrhea and a bulging vaginal membrane suggest cryptomenorrhoea caused by an imperforate hymen.

In addition to this, retention of urine and a palpable abdominal mass may be present. An ultrasound scan of the pelvis confirms the diagnosis. The condition is treated by making a cruciate incision on the hymen. This would resume a normal reproductive function in her.

questions.text: A 20-year-old female presents with irregular periods. Her ultrasound scan revealed the finding shown in the image. This is most likely due to:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. PCOD

The given ultrasound shows multiple ovarian follicles arranged in a necklace pattern, which is a feature of polycystic ovarian disease (PCOD).

USG Criteria for PCOD-  Either one of the ovaries with:

* Increased ovarian stroma

* 12 follicles, each measuring 2 to 9 mm arranged in a necklace pattern

* Ovarian volume >10 ml

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 22 year old female presents within 8 hours of having sexual intercourse and asking for emergency contraception.She says she doesn't want multiple pills and wants just one pill. What will be your advice?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg

The patient asks for emergency contraception and the drug used is Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg.

Levonorgestrel (LNG):

Prostinar tablet contains 0.75 mg LNG. One tablet should be taken within 72 h of unprotected intercourse and another 12 h later. Alternately, two tablets can be taken as a single dose. The failure rate is 1.1%. The tablets can be offered up to 120 h but their efficacy decreases with the longer coital-drug interval. LNG prevents ovulation and causes desynchronization of endometrium through its receptors (luteal phase deficiency). The period may come earlier or be delayed.

Side effects are those of progestogens. The hormone is not teratogenic in case pregnancy does occur but the risk of ectopic pregnancy remains.

Advantages:

* It has no estrogen and its associated side effects

* It can be offered to hypertensive, cardiac, and diabetic women

* It can be offered to a lactating woman

* It can be given as late as 120 hours after the unprotected intercourse

* Single-dose therapy is an advantage

Contraindicated in liver disease, contains lactate, and with an allergy to galactose. The drug is also contraindicated in a woman with a history of thrombophlebitis and migraine.

Pearl PF1657: Hormonal contraceptives

Oral pills:

* Combined oral contraceptive pills (COC)

* Mala D - Levonorgestrel 0.15 mg + Ethinyl estradiol  0.03 mg + Ferrous fumarate

* Mala N - Levonorgestrel 0.15 mg + Ethinyl estradiol  0.03 mg + Ferrous fumarate (Govt. supply, free of cost)

* Progesterone only pills (POP) - suitable for lactating women

* Norethisterone 350 μg

* Norgestrel 75 μg

* Levonorgestrel (LNG) 30 μg

* Once a month or long-acting pills - highly disappointing results

* Quinestrol (long-acting estrogen) + short-acting progesterone

* Gossypol - male pill : Cottonseed derivative and causes azoospermia and severe oligospermia

* Post-coital pills or interceptive

* Levonorgestrel 0.75 mg, 2 doses, 12 hours apart

* Mifepristone 10-600 mg

* Ulipristal 30 mg, within 5 days of intercourse

* Centchroman 60 mg, 2 tablets, within 24 hrs of intercourse

* GnRH agonists

* CuT IUCD, inserted within 5 days

Injectable contraceptives

* Progesterone only injectables

* DMPA 150 mg IM every 3 months

* NET-EN 200 mg IM every 2 months

* Combined injectables

* Cyclofem - DMPA 25 mg + Estradiol cypionate 5 mg

* Mesigyna - NET-EN 50 mg  + Estradiol valerate 5 mg

Subdermal implants

* Norplant I - Levonorgestrel 35 mg

* Norplant II or Jadelle - 2 rods with levonorgestrel 70 mg in each and released at a rate of 50 μg/day

Others

* Hormonal IUCD - Mirena which contains LNG 52 mg with release rate of 20 μg/day

* Orthoevra patch - Norelgestomin + Ethinyl estradiol weekly for 3 weeks, then patch free for 1 week

* Vaginal ring or Nuvaring - Etonogestrel + ethinyl estradiol daily release, use for 3 weeks with withdrawal for 1 week

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 24 year old primigravida presents with painless vaginal bleeding in the first trimester. On examination the cervical os is closed and uterine size is normal. Gestational sac is visible on ultrasound. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Threatened abortion

The given clinical features are suggestive of a threatened abortion.

The patient presents with a bloody vaginal discharge or bleeding through a closed cervical os. On ultrasound, gestational sac can be visible. In about two thirds of the cases pregnancy continues beyond 28 weeks. If the pregnancy continues, there is an increased risk of preterm labor, placenta previa, intrauterine growth restriction and fetal anomalies.

Treatment:

* Bed rest

* Analgesics if there is pain

* Progesterone

Pearl PF1290: Clinical classification of Spontaneous Abortion
