questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 26-year-old woman, presenting with 12 weeks of amenorrhea, underwent a sonographic evaluation that revealed a twin gestation, as shown in the image below. What type of twins are depicted in this ultrasound?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Dichorionic diamniotic (DCDA)

The image shows the lambda sign or twin peak sign seen in Dichorionic Diamniotic(DCDA) twin pregnancy.

If the inner cell mass divides within 3 days, it leads to the formation of dichorionic diamniotic (DCDA) twins. The sonographic image of DCDA is given below.

Chorionicity of the placenta is best diagnosed by ultrasound at 10–13 weeks of gestation. In dichorionic twins, there is a thick septum between the two gestational sacs. A triangular projection is seen at the base of the membrane. This is known as lambda or twin peak sign. The presence of lambda or twin peak sign indicates a dichorionic placenta.

Twinning and time of division:

Time of division
Type of twin

<3 days
Dichorionic diamniotic (DCDA)

4-8 days
Monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA)

>8 days
Monochorionic monoamniotic (MCMA)

>13 days
Conjoint twins

Other options :

Option a : In monochorionic diamniotic gestation, the twins are separated only by the two amniotic membranes, with no intervening chorion. So, a thin 'T sign' is formed at the point at which the amnions meet the placenta. It is best seen in the latter part of the first trimester or at the beginning of the second trimester.

Option c : In monochorionic monoamniotic gestation, there is an absence of a dividing membrane.

Option d :  Incomplete separation of the monozygotic twins results in the birth of two infants that are joined or fused together at some part of the body. These twins are known as conjoined twins or Siamese twins.

Pearl PF1942: Radiological Signs in Obstetrics

Bagel Sign (USG)

It is seen in unruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy. It is also known as the tubal ring sign or the blob sign. It refers to the appearance of an anechoic gestational sac in the adnexa surrounded by a hyperechoic ring.

Twin Peak Sign/ Lambda Sign (USG)

Chorionicity of the placenta is best diagnosed by ultrasound at 10–13 weeks of gestation. In dichorionic twins, there is a thick triangular projection of placental tissue between the two gestational sacs. This is known as the lambda sign or twin peak sign.

T Sign (USG)

The T sign which is seen in monochorionic diamniotic gestation is thin and T-shaped because there is no extension of placental tissue or chorion in between the amniotic membranes.

Double Decidual Sac Sign (USG)

It is seen in early intrauterine pregnancy as two concentric echogenic rings surrounding the gestational sac.

Lemon Sign (USG)

At the level of the lateral ventricles, there is inward bowing or scalloping of frontal bones (indicated by the arrow in the image below) giving rise to the lemon sign. It is suggestive of spina bifida. It is also characteristically associated with Chiari II Malformation.

Banana Sign (USG)

Anterior curvature of the cerebellum with effacement of the cisterna magna in the posterior fossa is seen as banana sign.

Spalding sign (USG)

It usually appears 7 days after intrauterine death and is caused by liquefaction of the brain matter and softening of the ligamentous structures supporting the vault, leading to irregular overlapping of the cranial bones on one another.

Frog Eye Sign (USG)

It is seen in anencephaly. Due to the absence of calvaria, the orbits appear more prominent. This is known as the "frog-eye sign".

Omphalocele (USG)

It is a congenital midline abdominal wall defect at the base of the umbilical cord insertion, with herniation of the solid abdominal viscera and/or bowel out of the fetal abdomen  (indicated with an asterisk). The extruded abdominal contents are covered in a sac.

Double Bubble Sign (USG)

Dilatation of stomach and first part of duodenum due to duodenal atresia.

Bunch of grapes sign or Snowstorm appearance (USG)

The appearance of multiple cystic spaces or lesions in a complete mole.

Ball sign (X-ray)

It is due to the crumpled up spine of the fetus seen in case of intrauterine death.

Robert’s sign (X-ray)

The presence of gas in the fetal great vessels in case of intrauterine fetal demise is known as Robert's sign.

Stuck twin sign (USG)

Smaller twin is held in a fixed position along the uterine wall due to the severe oligohydramnios. It is seen in twin-twin transfusion syndrome.

Butterfly sign (USG)

Normal appearance of the choroid plexuses on axial imaging of the fetal brain. An absence of this sign suggests holoprosencephaly.

Cloverleaf skull (USG)

Seen in craniosynostosis

Empty amnion sign (USG)

Visualization of an amniotic sac without concomitant visualization of an embryo. It is an indicator of pregnancy failure.

Pearl PF1493: Twinning

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 29-year-old G2P1 comes to the physician at 32 weeks of gestation. She underwent OGTT(75 g of glucose) and her values were fasting 110 mg/dl and 2 hours of glucose at 180 mg/dl. Which among the following is the next step regarding the management of this patient?
options: Induce labour due to risk of fetal macrosomia
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Admit and start insulin

Since her values are more than the normal limits with a 75 g OGTT she is having gestational diabetes and the next step in the management is to admit her and start insulin.

The glucose tolerance test is considered the diagnostic test for gestational diabetes mellitus and insulin is the drug of choice for the treatment of gestational diabetes mellitus. It does not cross the placenta and tight glycemic control can typically be achieved.

Diagnosis of GDM with 75 g OGTT according to IADPSG is made if any one of the following are met:

* Fasting: ≥92 mg/dl

* 1 hour: ≥180 mg/dl

* 2 hours: ≥153 mg/dl

The initial management of GDM is maternal nutrition therapy with diet and exercise. Insulin therapy is started if :

* Fasting plasma glucose levels persistently ≥95 mg/dl or the 2-hour postprandial plasma glucose ≥120 mg/dL in women with gestational diabetes treated with maternal nutrition therapy.

* Glucose levels on OGTT are in the range for overt diabetes.

Since this question does not have the option of Maternal nutrition therapy, the best step would be to start her on insulin.

The starting dose is typically 0.7 to 1 unit/kg/d and is given in divided doses. A combination of intermediate-acting and short-acting insulin may be used.

50% of women with gestational diabetes develop overt diabetes within 20 years. Hence, they are recommended to undergo screening & revaluation between 4-12 weeks postpartum.

Earlier, a two-step approach was used to diagnose GDM. In this, the first step (screening) is a 50-gram one-hour glucose challenge test (GCT). The patients having a positive result for this test were then subject to the second step, a 100-gram, three-hour oral glucose tolerance test (GTT), which is the diagnostic test for gestational diabetes mellitus. This has now been replaced by the one-step approach that omits the screening test and simplifies diagnostic testing by performing only a 75-gram, two-hour oral GTT.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 30-year-old woman who underwent dilatation and curettage previously, now presents with amenorrhea. The urine pregnancy test is negative. HSG revealed a honeycomb appearance in the uterine cavity.What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Asherman syndrome

The given clinical features, history and hysteroscopy are suggestive of Asherman syndrome.

Asherman syndrome refers to the presence of adhesion within the endometrial cavity. It is also called uterine synechiae and can be asymptomatic tiny bands or can completely or almost completely obliterate the endometrial cavity. It can occur as a result of trauma to the endometrium following vigorous uterine curettage, tuberculous endometritis, pelvic radiation, or endometrial ablation.

It causes secondary amenorrhoea, oligomenorrhoea, dysmenorrhoea, habitual abortion and infertility depending upon the extent of uterine cavity obliteration.

Asherman syndrome (uterine synechiae) is classified as follows:

* Mild: <25% adhesion involves the uterine cavity, flimsy adhesions involving the fundus and tubal ostia.

* Moderate: 25–70% adhesion of the endometrial surfaces, but no agglutination of the uterine wall.

* Severe: 75% adhesions with agglutination and thick adhesions.

Hysterosalpingography (HSG) may show honeycomb or moth-eaten appearance. Definitive diagnosis requires hysteroscopy as polyps, leiomyomas, air bubbles and blood clots may masquerade as adhesions.

Treatment involves hysteroscopic lysis of the adhesions.

The image below shows a moth-eaten appearance on hysterosalpingography

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 35-year-old asymptomatic woman on USG shows a unilocular cyst in the ovary of 6 cm with negative serology. Treatment involves:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Follow-up after 1-2 cycles of OCPs

Follow up after 1-2 cycles of oral combined pills (conservative management) is the best treatment modality in the given scenario as it is most likely to be a functional cyst.

For conservative management of ovarian cysts, the following criteria should usually be met:

* Asymptomatic

* Unilocular

* Unilateral

* No solid areas

* Normal CA 125

* Less than 7cm

* Ultrasound re-examination after 3-6 months (no signs of increase in size or malignancy)

Features of a functional cyst:

* Related to temporary hormonal disorders

* Benign and rarely become complicated

* Usually 6-8cm in diameter

* Usually asymptomatic

* Unilocular

* Contains clear fluid, unless haemorrhage occurs

* Lining epithelium corresponds to the functional epithelium of the unit from which they arise

* Spontaneous regression occurs within 4-6 months

Treatment of functional cysts:

* Usually conservative; spontaneous regression occurs after 4-6months.

* Oral combined pills to hasten the regression of cyst.

* Laparotomy for tumours more than 7 cm to prevent complications or malignant transformation.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 45-year-old woman presents with post-coital bleeding. On per vaginal examination, the following lesion is seen which bleeds on touching. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Cervical polyp

The given image with the history of post-coital bleeding in a woman of childbearing age is suggestive of a cervical polyp.

Endocervical polyp:

* They arise from the mucous membrane of the cervical canal and form a swelling about the size of a pea.

* The mucous polypi are regarded as being produced by hyperplasia of the mucous membrane of the cervical canal which becomes thrown into folds and finally one of the folds, which projects into the cervical canal, assumes the characteristics of a polypus.

* The lesion is red and vascular which bleeds easily on the touch and is covered by smooth glistening epithelium with clear mucus.

* The polypus is pedunculated, the pedicle being attached to the mucous membrane of the cervical canal.

* Histologically, the surface epithelium is the high columnar type similar to that of the endocervical canal. Glands found in the stroma are lined by tall columnar epithelium. The stroma is extremely vascular, containing a large number of dilated capillaries with round-celled infiltration near the lower pole of the polypus.

* Occur in women during the childbearing period of life, but may occasionally develop in menopausal and postmenopausal women.
Treatment- avulsion or by torsion and specimen should always be sent for microscopic examination as malignant changes may be seen.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A middle-aged woman presented with dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, and infertility. On examination, you note fixed, tender, retroverted uterus and tender nodularity of the uterosacral ligaments. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Endometriosis

This patient presents with symptoms of dyspareunia and dysmenorrhea with a fixed retroverted uterus and tenderness in the pouch of Douglas most likely suffering from endometriosis.

For minimal disease, medical management with NSAIDs and oral contraceptive pills are given if associated menstrual complaints are present. OCPs inhibit gonadotropin release and decrease the menstrual flow. For moderate to severe diseases, oral progestogens, GnRH agonists or danazol that antagonize estrogenic effects on the endometrium causing endometrial atrophy are used.

Surgery is preferred in infertile women because hormonal treatment would delay pregnancy. Endometrial deposits are destroyed by electrocautery/laser and resection of endometrioma can be done. Laparoscopic uterosacral nerve ablation (LUNA) to control pain .Total hysterectomy with bilateral oophorectomy is a definitive and most effective therapy for women with endometriosis who do not wish to retain fertility.

Pearl PF1294: Endometriosis

Sites of Endometriosis:

* Pelvic endometriosis: Pelvic peritoneum, the pouch of Douglas, uterosacral ligament.

* Rectovaginal endometriosis.

* Ovarian endometriosis.

* Chocolate cyst of the ovary.

* Other sites—appendix, pelvic lymph nodes.

* Metastatic— lungs, umbilicus, scar endometriosis.

One pathology review revealed that endometriosis has been identified on all organs except the spleen.

Examination findings in endometriosis:

* Abdomen: Cystic swelling, fixed and tender.

* Pelvis: Cystic tender mass.

* Vaginal examination: Fixed, tender, retroverted uterus. Tenderness in the lateral fornices (indicative of endometriosis even if no mass).

* Speculum inspection of the Posterior fornix: Bluish/blackish puckered spots on speculum, tender to touch. The presence of puckered spots is pathognomonic of endometriosis.

* Posterior Fornix Palpation: Uterosacral ligaments & pouch of Douglas feel thickened and shotty with multiple small palpable nodules. This is called the cobblestone feel of uterosacral ligaments.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A patient was posted for dilatation and curettage and a Sim's sound was introduced into the uterus but there was no resistance felt. What is the next line of management in the given options?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Immediate laparascopy

As the Sim's sound goes into without any resistance it suggests that there is a perforation for which acute management is needed, that is immediate laparoscopy.

Sims uterine sound is used in dilatation and curettage. The instrument can cause uterine perforation and is hence introduced into the uterine cavity by keeping it in the midline and ensuring it is not forced. It is held like a pencil with the thumb and the first 2 fingers.

After introducing the instrument, a gentle resistance is felt when it meets the fundus and the distance from the fundus to the external os is measured by score marks along the length of the sound.

Note:

Operative hysteroscopy with Versapoint does not require cervical dilation, thus avoiding cervical incompetence, cervical lacerations, and uterine perforation.

Karman’s type suction cannulas made of plastic, reduce the risk of uterine perforation during suction evacuation procedures. (Suction Evacuation is a procedure by means of which products of conception are sucked out of the uterus with a cannula attached to a suction apparatus.)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A primigravida presents with labour pain and on per vaginal examination her cervix is 7 cm dilated and fully effaced.What stage of labour is she in?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Phase of maximum slope

This woman, with 7 cm dilation and fully effaced cervix, is in the active phase of labor specifically the phase of maximum slope, where cervical dilatation occurs most rapidly.

Based on Friedman’s curve, the first stage of labor is divided into two phases; the latent and the active phase, which were further subcategorized only for the purpose of partograph-based monitoring.

The latent phase of labour is defined as the period between the onset of true labour pain and the point when the cervical dilatation becomes 3–4 cm.

The active phase has got three components:

* Acceleration phase with cervical dilatation of 3–4 cm.

* The phase of maximum slope of 4–9 cm dilatation.

* The phase of deceleration of 9–10 cm dilatation.

Note: Newer guidelines have demonstrated that in active labor cervical dilatation typically progresses at 5–6 cm. As per WHO 2020, active labour begins at ≥5 cm and as per ACOG 2019 ≥6 cm.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Identify the finding seen in this hysterosalpingogram:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Bilateral hydrosalpinx

Bilateral hydrosalpinx is observed in the given image of hysterosalpingogram.

Hydrosalpinx is often bilateral and occurs following acute salpingitis. The tubes are retort shaped due to dilatation of the ampulla and filled with a clear fluid. The interstitial end of the tube is open whereas the fimbrial end is indrawn and closed. This permits the dye to enter but not exit the tube during hysterosalpingography.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Identify the genetic disorder.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Turner's syndrome

This patient's picture of short stature, webbed neck, low hairline at the back of the neck, widely spaced nipples, and lack of secondary sexual characteristics is seen in Turner's syndrome.

Turner's syndrome is a chromosomal abnormality with partial or complete monosomy of the X chromosome (45+XO). Gonadal dysgenesis causes primary ovarian failure which is hypogonadism.

Important features associated with Turner's syndrome: (mnemonic: See A Baby CLOWN Here)

* Short stature, Short fourth metacarpal, Sensorineural hearing loss, Shield chest

* Amenorrhea (primary), infertility

* Barr body absent

* Cardiac defects(bicuspid aortic valve >coarctation of aorta), Cubitus valgus, Congenital lymphedema

* L: Learning disabilities

* Ovaries underdeveloped (streak ovaries), Gonadoblastoma (increased risk if Y chromosome material is present)

* Webbed neck

* Nipples widely spaced

* Horseshoe kidneys

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Identify the obstetric grip performed in the picture.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Pelvic grip

The obstetric grip shown in the picture is a pelvic grip.

Leopold's manoeuvres help assess the fetal pole, lie, presenting part, engagement, and attitude of the fetal head. They are as follows:

* Fundal grip (first Leopold): Assesses the uterine fundus.

* Helps in the identification of fetal lie and determination of fetal pole at the fundus.

* The breech is felt as a large, irregular mass. The head feels hard and round and is more mobile.

* Lateral grip (second Leopold):  Assesses fetal orientation.

* The palms are placed on either side of the maternal abdomen, and gentle but deep pressure is exerted.

* The back is felt on one side as a hard, resistant structure. The fetal extremities are felt on the other side as numerous small, irregular, mobile parts.

* Pawlik's grip/ 1st pelvic grip (third Leopold): Assesses the presenting part.

* The thumb and fingers of one hand grasp the lower portion of the maternal abdomen just above the symphysis pubis.

* If the presenting part is not engaged, a movable mass will be felt, usually the head.

* Deep pelvic grip/ 2nd pelvic grip (fourth Leopold): Assesses the engagement and attitude of the fetal head.

* The examiner faces the mother's feet, and the fingertips of both hands are positioned on either side of the presenting part.

* They exert inward pressure and then slide along the axis of the pelvic outlet.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: In the anteroposterior diameters of the pelvic inlet, the true conjugate is___
options: the distance from midpoint of sacral promontory to the upper most margin of the symphysis pubis.
the shortest distance between the sacral promontory and the symphysis pubis.
the distance from the lowest margin of the symphysis to the sacral promontory.
the distance from the posterior margin of the sacral promontory to the symphysis pubis.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. the distance from midpoint of sacral promontory to the upper most margin of the symphysis pubis.

The true conjugate is the distance between the midpoint of the sacral promontory to the inner margin of the upper border of the symphysis pubis.

Anteroposterior diameters of the pelvic inlet:

* Diagonal conjugate:

* It is the distance between the lower border of the symphysis pubis to the midpoint on the sacral promontory.

* It measures 12 cm (4 ¾")

* Obstetric conjugate:

* It is the distance between the midpoint of the sacral promontory to prominent bony projection in the midline on the inner surface of the symphysis pubis.

* It measures 10 cm (4")

* Anatomical/true conjugate/conjugate vera:

* It is the distance between the midpoint of the sacral promontory to the inner margin of the upper border of the symphysis pubis.

* It measures 11 cm

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The USG given below is seen in
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Hydatidiform mole

The above image shows the characteristic snow storm appearance seen in hydatidiform mole.

Hydatidiform Mole is principally a disease of the chorion. Death of the ovum or failure of the embryo to grow is essential to develop complete (classic) hydatidiform mole. The secretion from the hyperplastic cells and transferred substances from the maternal blood accumulate in the stroma of the villi which results in distension of the villi to form small vesicles.

Classical clinical feature of a complete mole:

* Abnormal vaginal bleeding

* Lower abdominal pain

* Hyperemesis gravidarum

* Features of early onset preeclampsia < 20 weeks

* Uterus > dates (50%)

* Absent fetal parts and FHS

* Expulsion of vesicular tissues

* Theca lutein cyst of ovaries (25%) > 6 cm

* Hyperthyroidism (rare)

* Serum hCG > 100,000 mIU/mL

* USG: snowstorm appearance

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the mode of insertion of this contraceptive?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Hysteroscopic

The image shows an Essure coil which is inserted hysteroscopically to occlude both the fallopian tubes.

Essure(not yet licensed in India):

* It is a spring-like device introduced using a hysteroscope inserted through the vagina into the uterus and then into each fallopian tube.

* In 3 months' time, scar tissue grows into the device and plugs the fallopian tube; hence, sperms cannot pass through to fertilize an egg.

* Made of nickel and titanium alloy and is considered irreversible.

* Contraindicated in patients who are uncertain about ending fertility, can have only one insert placed (including contralateral proximal tubal occlusion or suspected unicornuate uterus), an abnormal uterine cavity that makes visualization of the tubal ostia impossible, and/or abnormal tubal anatomy or previous tubal ligation (including failed ligation), pregnant or suspect pregnancy, delivered or terminated a pregnancy less than 6 weeks, an active upper or lower genital tract infection, unexplained vaginal bleeding, a gynecological malignancy, known allergy to contrast media.

* Side effects-cramping, nausea/vomiting, back pain, abdominal pain, and dyspareunia.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is not an absolute contraindication of the device shown below?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. HIV infected women

The given image is of intrauterine contraception CuT 380 A which is not contraindicated in HIV-infected women

Intrauterine contraceptive devices (IUCDs) are placed in the uterine cavity with the objective of providing long-term contraception, mainly by preventing fertilisation.

Contraindications for IUCD:

* Suspected pregnancy

* Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)

* STIs — current or recurrent

* Distorted uterine cavity (fibroids, uterine anomalies)

* Severe dysmenorrhea

* Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding

* Wilson disease and copper allergy, for copper-containing IUCDs

* Breast cancer, for hormone-containing IUCDs

Complications of IUCD usage:

*

* Immediate

* Vasovagal attack

* Uterine cramps

* Early

* Expulsion of IUCD

* Perforation of uterus

* Spotting, menorrhagia

* Dysmenorrhoea

* Vaginal infection

* Actinomycosis

* Late

* PID

* Ectopic pregnancy

* Perforation of uterus

* Menorrhagia

* Dysmenorrhoea

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is the most dependent part of a female?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Rectouterine pouch

The rectouterine pouch, which is also called the pouch of Douglas is the most dependent part of a female.

Peritoneum of the female pelvis:

In females, the peritoneum covers the anterior and anterolateral surfaces of the rectum, uterus, and urinary bladder. Spaces found in the female pelvis are:

Pararectal fossae: Present on either side of the rectum. They are limited laterally by the peritoneum that covers the uterosacral ligaments.

Paravesical fossae: Present on either side of the bladder. It is limited laterally by the peritoneum which covers the round ligament of the uterus.

Rectouterine pouch: The peritoneum which covers the anterior surface of the rectum is reflected anteriorly to cover the posterior surface of the posterior fornix of the vagina and the uterus, forming a rectouterine pouch.  This is also known as the pouch of Douglas or posterior pelvic cul-de-sac. It forms the most dependent part when a woman is sitting or standing.

Vesicouterine pouch: The peritoneum covering the fundus and body of the uterus, is reflected anteriorly to cover the posterosuperior surface of the bladder forming a vesicouterine pouch.

Ovarian fossa: It is a shallow depression in the peritoneal lining of the lateral pelvic wall between the peritoneal ridges. It is formed by the obliterated umbilical arteries anteriorly, the ureter posteriorly, and the external iliac vessels above. It lies behind the lateral attachment of the broad ligament and contains the ovary in nulliparous females.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 14-year-old girl presented with cyclical abdominal pain and a midline hypogastric lump. She has not achieved menarche yet. The per vaginal examination is shown below and a bluish swelling is seen along with it. What is the likely cause of her condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Imperforate hymen

The given case scenario is suggestive of an imperforate hymen, which has led to cryptomenorrhoea. This is a condition where menstruation occurs but is not visible due to an obstruction of the outflow tract.

The menstrual fluid gets collected in the reproductive tract. When this collection occurs in the vagina, it is known as hematocolpos. If the collection extends to the uterus, it is known as hematometra. The collection of blood in the fallopian tubes is called hematosalpinx.

The most common causes of cryptomenorrhea are:

* Intact/imperforate hymen - a bluish convex bulge is seen.

* Transverse vaginal septum - a pinkish concave covering is seen

Ultrasound pelvis confirms the diagnosis.

Management:

Imperforate hymen - A simple cruciate incision of the hymen allows the free drainage of the collected menstrual blood, and leads to normal reproductive function.

Transverse vaginal septum - Extensive dissection and vaginoplasty is required.

Option A: Bartholin's cyst appears as a swelling on the inner side of the labia majora. Larger cysts can bulge across the introitus. Small cysts can remain asymptomatic.

Option D: Endometriomas are endometriotic lesions seen on the ovary. They present as adnexal masses. Endometriosis is a complication in cryptomenorrhea, due to retrograde menstruation.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 22-year-old primigravida at 10weeks gestation comes to the ER with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Nausea and vomiting began one day back and now the patient is unable to tolerate fluids. She complains of pain in the right upper quadrant which started a few hours back. On examination, her temperature is 100.2 F, the pulse is 118 bpm and her BP is 110/70 mm of Hg. She has swelling of her lower limbs up to the ankles bilaterally. Abdominal examination shows a gravid uterus corresponding to 10 weeks of gestation and tenderness in the right upper quadrant, with mild guarding and is diagnosed as acute appendicitis. What is the next step of management? Complete blood count * Hemoglobin: 11g/dL * Leukocytes: 13,000 cells/μL * Platelets: 150,000 cells/μL Liver function tests * Aspartate transaminase (AST): 40U/L * Alanine transaminase (ALT): 48U/L Urinalysis * Protein: negative * Pus cells: 1-2/HPF * Bacteria: none USG Abdomen: Reveals a 7mm diameter, aperistaltic, non-compressible, dilated, blind-ending structure arising from the base of the caecum
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Do appendicectomy

Based on the given clinical vignette, the next step of management is Laparoscopic appendicectomy at the earliest. Laparoscopic appendicectomy can be done before 28 weeks of gestation.

Acute appendicitis is the most common surgical non-gynecological cause of acute abdomen in pregnancy.

The diagnosis of acute appendicitis in pregnancy is difficult due to

* Nausea and vomiting may be considered normal, especially in the first trimester of pregnancy

* Leukocytosis is a physiological finding in pregnancy

* A gravid enlarging uterus can push the appendix upward and outward, causing the pain to localize in the right flank or right upper quadrant.

Acute appendicitis in pregnancy is associated with miscarriage, preterm delivery, increased risk of peritonitis, perinatal and maternal mortality.

USG abdomen is used to confirm. MRI abdomen can be done if USG is inconclusive.USG Abdomen would reveal a >6mm diameter, aperistaltic, non-compressible, dilated appendix seen as a blind-ending structure arising from the base of the caecum

Other options:

Option B,C,D are not appropriate because they do not treat the urgent cause of the pathology.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 27-year-old woman presents with malodorous vaginal discharge that began a week ago. On examination, the Whiff test is positive, and a Gram stain reveals the presence of clue cells. Which of the following is the most common treatment for this infection?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Metronidazole

Foul-smelling frothy vaginal discharge and a positive whiff test with clue cells in the gram staining suggest bacterial vaginosis and it is treated with metronidazole.

Bacterial vaginosis is caused due to the alteration in the normal vaginal flora. There is a decrease in the number of lactobacilli. These lactobacilli reduce the pH and release hydrogen peroxide which is antibacterial. Therefore, a decrease in the number of lactobacilli leads to an increase in the number of other organisms like Hemophilus vaginalis, Gardnerella, Mobiluncus, and Mycoplasma hominis.

According to Amsel's criteria, the discharge has the following characteristics:

* White milky non-viscous discharge, adherent to the vaginal wall.

* The pH of the discharge is >4.5.

* Fishy odor when mixed with 10% KOH. This is called the Whiff test.

* Presence of clue cells-the epithelial cells have a fuzzy border due to the adherence of bacteria.

* Decrease in the number of lactobacilli and increase in the number of Gardnerella and other bacteria.

It is treated with 500 mg of metronidazole twice daily for 7 days.

The below image shows the presence of clue cells.

Other options:

Option B: Nystatin pessary is used in the treatment of candidal vaginitis. They present with severe itching, dysuria, and passage of thick curdy discharge. On examination, the vagina is congested and thick curdy discharge can be seen at the vulval mucocutaneous junction and posterior fornix.

Options C and D: Tetracycline and azithromycin are used in the treatment of chlamydial infection. They usually present with vaginal discharge, dysuria, increased urinary frequency, and sometimes cervicitis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 56-year-old multiparous woman presented with grade II/III uterine prolapse with cystocele. She complains of passing urine on coughing and sneezing. What is the type of urinary incontinence seen in this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Stress incontinence

The type of urinary incontinence present in a patient with prolapse and cystocele experiencing urination on coughing and sneezing is stress incontinence.

Stress incontinence refers to the involuntary leakage of urine when there is increased intraabdominal pressure (eg, coughing, sneezing, laughing, Valsalva maneuver). There is an absence of detrusor muscle contraction, seen in urodynamic studies.

Causes:

* Age and menopause - due to estrogen deficiency

* Multiparity - due to loss of pelvic muscle tone

* Obesity

* Smoking

* Constipation, chronic cough

* Pelvic organ prolapse

* Pregnancy - due to the effect of progesterone and pressure of the gravid uterus on the bladder neck.

* Puerperium - due to descent of the bladder neck, loss of urethro-vesical angle, and reduced pelvic muscle tone

* Surgical repair of vesicovaginal fistula

Grading of genuine stress incontinence (GSI) :

* Grade I: Incontinence with only severe stress, such as coughing, sneezing, and jogging.

* Grade II: Incontinence with moderate stress, such as fast walking, and going up and down the stairs.

* Grade III: Incontinence with mild stress such as standing.

Investigations are only done prior to surgery to confirm the diagnosis. They include the stress test, cotton swab or Q tip test, Marshall and Bonney’s test, urethroscopy, and urodynamic studies. These are not required prior to conservative management.

Conservative management includes Kegel's pelvic exercises, electric nerve stimulation, devices like pessaries, vaginal cones, and artificial sphincters. Medical treatment with estrogen creams, anti-adrenergic, venlafaxine, and imipramine may be useful.

Other options:

Option A: Overflow incontinence is an old term that refers to the inability to empty the bladder, with involuntary, continuous urinary dribbling. Currently, it refers to another presentation of urge incontinence.

Option B: Urge incontinence is the involuntary escape of urine when there is an imminent need to urinate. It occurs due to detrusor muscle overactivity or detrusor instability. It is seen more commonly in old women with decreased bladder capacity, decreased sensation, and central nervous system (CNS) inhibition.

Option D: Neurogenic bladder occurs in patients with neurogenic dysfunction leading to detrusor hyperreflexia. Conditions such as multiple sclerosis, stroke, Parkinson's disease, and spinal injury give rise to this. They present with urgency or urge incontinence.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A patient presents to you with complaints of mass descending per vaginum for the past 6 months. On examination, you notice a grade 3 uterovaginal prolapse and a decubitus ulcer over the prolapse. Which of the following is a cause for this decubitus ulcer and treatment?
options: Venous congestion and reduction of the prolapsed part into the vagina and daily packing with glycerine and acriflavine
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Venous congestion and reduction of the prolapsed part into the vagina and daily packing with glycerine and acriflavine

The given case scenario is suggestive of pelvic organ prolapse with a decubitus ulcer. It is due to venous congestion and local circulatory changes.

Friction, congestion and circulatory changes in the dependent part of prolapse cause keratinization and pigmentation of the vaginal mucosa, as well as ulceration of the prolapsed tissue with a clean edge.

Treatment includes the reduction of the prolapsed part into the vagina and daily packing with glycerine and acriflavine. Acriflavine is an antiseptic agent while glycerine is a hygroscopic agent. This helps in the healing of the ulcer within a week or two.

Complications of prolapse:

* Kinking of the ureter with resulting renal damage can occur in procidentia and enterocele.

* Chronic Urinary tract infection due to retention of urine in a cystocele, and can lead to upper renal tract infection and renal damage.

* Decubitus ulcer due to venous congestion and local circulatory changes.

* Stress incontinence occurs when the internal urinary meatus and neck of the bladder descend below the level of pelvic floor muscles.

* Cancer of the vagina can rarely occur over the decubitus ulcer and if the ring pessary is left in over a long period.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A patient with carcinoma endometrium is treated with pelvic external beam irradiation to the whole pelvis. Which of the following organs is most radiosensitive in the pelvic region?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Ovary

Among the options most radiosensitive organ is ovary> rectum> bladder> vagina.

The radiation tolerance dose for the ovary is 2-3 Gy whereas the vagina 90 Gy.

The radiation dose necessary to induce ovarian failure is age-dependent. A single dose of 3-4 Gray can induce amenorrhea in almost all women >40 yrs of age. In young women, oogenesis is much less sensitive to radiation as compared to the elderly.

* Most radioresistant organ: Vagina

* Radiation most commonly affects the stratum basalis layer of the skin.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A woman with a history of infertility is on treatment with HMG. She presented with the following finding in the USG. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome

The given clinical scenario and the USG findings are suggestive of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome.

Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome is characterized by multiple ovarian follicular cysts accompanied by increased capillary permeability. It most often is a complication of ovulation induction therapy for infertility, although it may rarely develop in an otherwise normal pregnancy. It has also been reported with a partial molar pregnancy. Its etiopathogenesis is thought to involve the stimulation of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) expression in granulosa-lutein cells by hCG.

Human menopausal gonadotropin (HMG) is a medication that is composed of FSH and LH. It is used to stimulate the release of ova in women who do not ovulate spontaneously. It can lead to ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Cardiac output returns back to prepregnant levels by
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 10 days postpartum

Cardiac output usually remains elevated for 24 to 48 hours postpartum and declines to non-pregnant values by 10 days.

* Heart rate changes follow this pattern

* Systemic vascular resistance and blood pressure rise

* Systemic vascular resistance remains in the lower range characteristic of pregnancy for 2 days postpartum and then begins to steadily increase to normal nonpregnant values.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: During your internship, you notice the following instrument being used by the senior resident. The uses of this instrument include all of the following except______
options: To differentiate between chronic inversion and fibroid polyp
It is used to diagnose cervical stenosis
It is used in Fallopian Tube Recanalization
It is used to measure the uterine cavity and the cervical length
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. It is used in Fallopian Tube Recanalization

The instrument shown in the above image is Simpson’s uterine sound. It is not used in the Fallopian Tube Recanalization procedure.

The instrument is held like a pencil with the thumb and the first 2 fingers and introduced into the uterine cavity by keeping it in the midline and ensuring it is not forced.

Uses include:

* To measure uterine cavity and cervical length

* To diagnose cervical stenosis

* To sound a polyp, IUCD or uterine septum

* To break uterine adhesions in Asherman syndrome

* To differentiate between chronic inversion and fibroid polyp

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Marsupialization is an ideal treatment of choice for condition X involving the female reproductive tract, the lesion responsible for condition X is located at?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Bartholin gland

Marsupialization is an ideal treatment of choice for Bartholin cyst/abscess. The given clinical vignette is suggestive of leison of the Bartholin gland.

Bartholin glands:

Bartholin glands are the homologs of the male bulbourethral or Cowper glands. The ducts of these glands open in the groove between the hymen and the labia minora at approximately 5 and 7 o’clock positions. These glands are stimulated by sexual arousal. Bartholin glands are the homologs of the male bulbourethral or Cowper glands.

Clinical conditions :

* Bartholin cyst: Caused by obstruction of the Bartholin ducts by proteinaceous material or by inflammation from infection. Symptomatic or recurrent cysts may require marsupialization or gland excision.

* Bartholin abscess: An infected Bartholin cyst can lead to an abscess. It usually requires surgical drainage.

Pathology:

* These commonly involve the duct and are most commonly sexually transmitted. Infection is generally polymicrobial.

Clinical features:

* If the size is big, it might cause abdominal and vaginal discomfort with dyspareunia.

* A vulval cleft of 'S' shape is usually noted on inspection.

* It is fluctuant swelling and transillumination can be positive as the fluid collected is generally clear.

Treatment:

* Analgesics for pain

* Antibiotic for combating infections.

* Specific treatment include Marsupialization, Incision and drainage with word catheter placement and Bartholinectomy.

Notes:

In any woman above the age of forty with recurrent Bartholin cyst, a suspicion of Bartholin gland cancer should arise and the cyst wall should be sent for biopsy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Revised A woman presented in her 8th week of pregnancy seeking MTP. What is the appropriate dosage of Misoprostol administered by the mucosal route?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 800 mcg

The dosage of Misoprostol administered by mucosal route in this case, is 800 mcg.

Mucosal misoprostol administration has increased efficacy and minimizes gastrointestinal side effects and is now preferred over the prior oral administration. The mucosal route includes buccal, sublingual, and vaginal.

Medical management protocol for induced abortion for < 12 weeks of gestation (As per WHO 2018 guideline):

* Combined Regimen (Recommended): 200 mg of oral Mifepristone followed 1-2 days later by 800 mcg of buccal, vaginal or sublingual Misoprostol

* Misoprostol-only regimen (Alternative): 800 μg misoprostol administered vaginally, sublingually, or buccally.

Outpatient medical abortion is an acceptable option for pregnancies with a menstrual age < 63 days (9 weeks)

Various regimens for medical termination of pregnancy

First trimester

* Mifepristone/Misoprostol Combined Regimen (Recommended)

* Misoprostol-only regimen (Alternative)

Second Trimester

* Mifepristone/Misoprostol Combined Regimen (Recommended): 200 mg of oral Mifepristone followed 1-2 days later by 400 mcg of buccal, vaginal or sublingual Misoprostol every 3 hours

* Misoprostol Alone(Alternative): 400 mcg of buccal, vaginal or sublingual Misoprostol every 3 hours

* Dinoprostone- 20 mg vaginal suppository every 4 hr

* Concentrated Oxytocin- 50 units of oxytocin in 500 mL of normal saline infused in an incremental fashion through 150, 200, 250, and finally 300 units of oxytocin each in 500 mL of normal saline

Pearl PF1638: Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act - MTP Act 1971

MTP Act with 2021 amendments

Indications:

* Therapeutic - to save the life of the mother

* Eugenic - to prevent the risk of the child being born with serious mental or physical abnormality i.e. first-trimester viral infections, teratogenic drug intake, radiation exposure

* Humanitarian - pregnancy resulted from rape or incest

* Social - pregnancy resulted from failure of contraceptives

Rules:

* Only a registered medical practitioner who is qualified (one who has assisted in the performance of 25 cases of MTP in a recognized hospital) can terminate a pregnancy.

* MTP should be carried out in a government or government-recognized hospital. Private hospitals may take up MTP if they obtain a license from the chief medical officer of the district.

* The termination of pregnancy by a person, who is not a registered medical practitioner (the person concerned), or in an unrecognised hospital (administrative head) shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than 2 years, but which may extend to 7 years.

Consent:

The consent of the woman is required for conducting an abortion. The written consent of the guardian is required if the woman is minor or mentally ill. Consent of the husband or partner is not necessary.

If the woman is not willing, abortion cannot be performed at the request of the husband alone. The woman need not produce proof of her age. It is enough for the woman to say that she was raped, and it is not necessary that a complaint was lodged with the police.

Opinion of doctors:

* Till 20 weeks - 1 doctor's opinion

* 20 to 24 weeks - 2 doctors' opinion

* For substantial fetal anomalies - approval from the medical board consisting of obstetrician, paediatrician, radiologist and a person appointed by the state

Upper limit of MTP:

* Up to 24 weeks of gestation in victims of rape and incest, fetal anomalies, or congenital malformations

* Up to 20 weeks in case of contraception failure (any female with her partner)

* At any gestational age for substantial fetal anomalies decided by the medical board

Confidentiality:

A register for recording the details of MTP must be kept for at least 5 years. The patient's name must not be entered, only the reference number is used. Unlawful disclosure of patient's details is punishable with 1-year imprisonment ± fine.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Serial monitoring of serum beta hCG is required for which of the following conditions?
options: Pregnancy associated with Neural tube defects
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Molar Pregnancy

Serial monitoring of serum Beta hCG testing is done for a molar pregnancy.

Follow-up after the termination of molar pregnancy is done with serum β hCG levels. During the follow-up period, pregnancy must be avoided as it might interfere with the β hCG levels. The initial β-hCG level is obtained 48 hours after evacuation and used as a baseline. It is measured weekly till it becomes negative, and three consecutive normal values are obtained.

All patients should be followed-up for 2 years because choriocarcinoma if it occurs, develops within this period of the evacuation of the mole. Commonly, the circulating levels of βhCG decrease or becomes negative within 4 to 8 weeks post-evacuation. Once negative, the patient is usually followed up monthly for 6 months, then 3 monthly in the first year, and 6 monthly in the second year.

After beta HCG levels have become normal, subsequent conception must be avoided for one year(preferably 2 years). Pregnancy should also be avoided for 1 year after the stoppage of chemotherapy because of the teratogenic effect of drugs.

Other options:

Options A and B: Downs syndrome and Pregnancy associated with Neural tube defects require Maternal serum AFP testing.

Option D: Rh-negative pregnancy requires Coombs antibody testing.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The ultrasound finding of a 24-year-old primi with 3 months of amenorrhoea is shown below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Multiple Renal Cysts in the fetus
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Hydatidiform mole

The USG shows the characteristic snowstorm appearance which is seen in hydatidiform mole.

Hydatidiform mole is a benign abnormal condition of the placenta characterised by partial degenerative or partial proliferative changes of the chorionic villi. Though benign, it has some malignant potential and hence requires follow-up.

It is of 2 types

* Complete mole - grossly appears as a mass of clear vesicles.

* Partial mole - has fewer hydatidiform changes and contains some fetal tissue.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The usage of the given device in the picture is?
options: Measure the length of the uterus
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Menstrual regulation/aspiration

The instrument given in the image is Karman’s cannula which is used for menstrual regulation or aspiration.

Menstrual regulation or aspiration is the aspiration of the endometrial cavity 1-3 weeks after a missed period in a woman with a previous normal cycle and a positive urine pregnancy test. It is performed using Karman's cannula.

Procedure -

* Under aseptic precautions, the cervix may be gently dilated using 4-5 mm size dilators.

* Then 5-6mm Karman’s cannula is inserted and attached to a 50ml syringe for suction.

* The cannula is rotated, and pushed in and out with gentle strokes.

This procedure is contraindicated in advanced pregnancy and in the presence of local pelvic inflammation.

The drawback of the procedure - an implanted zygote , and an ectopic pregnancy can be missed.

Other options:

Option A:  Hysterosalpingography is done using a Rubins cannula.

Option B:  The length of the uterus is measured using Simpson's uterine sound.

Option C: Retraction is done using Doyen's retractor

Pearl PF1727: Instruments in OBG

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What dose of folic acid is recommended for a woman who wants to become pregnant but has a history of pregnancy complicated with a neural tube defect?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 4 mg/day

In a pregnancy complicated with a history of neural tube defect, 4 mg/day of folic acid is recommended.

Supplementation with folic acid is standard practice before and during pregnancy to reduce the incidence of neural tube defects and for as long as a woman is breastfeeding.

Option A: In a normal pregnancy, folic acid is given at a dose of 400-500 mcg/day.

Options B and C: In adults with conditions having a high cell turnover like hemolytic anemia, supplementation of folic acid at a dose of 1-2 mg/day is recommended.

In hyperhomocysteinemia, folic acid is given at a dose of 1 mg/day.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which filter is used in a colposcope?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Green

The filter used in a colposcope is green.

A colposcope is used to perform colposcopy where the cervix is visualized at a distance of around 20 cm with the patient in the lithotomy position.

This instrument provides binocular vision with a magnification of 6x-15x. A green filter is used to study vascular patterns as the vessels appear black. Abnormal areas can be identified by their peculiar vascular pattern such as mosaic, reticular, and punctate.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is not an indication for expectant management in unruptured ectopic gestation?
options: Initial serum beta hCG level < 200 mIU/mL
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Gestational sac size >4 cm

Gestational sac > 4cm is an indication for surgical management of ectopic pregnancy.

Management of ectopic pregnancy:

Expectant management is where only observation is done hoping for spontaneous resolution.

Indications:

* Asymptomatic

* No evidence of bleeding or rupture on TVS

* Initial serum hCG level <200 mIU/mL

* Gestational sac size less than 4 cm

* No fetal heartbeat on TVS

Medical management with intramuscular methotrexate injection, which can be done in single-dose or multidose protocols. The dose for single-dose therapy is 50 mg/m2.

Indications

* Low initial serum beta-hCG level

* Small gestational sac size- 4cm

* Absent fetal cardiac activity

* Hemodynamically stable

Surgical management of ectopic pregnancy includes laparoscopic salpingostomy/ salpingectomy and microsurgical laparotomy.

Indications

* Criteria for expectant and medical management are not met

* Significant pain and hemoperitoneum

* Gestational sac ≥4cm

* Fetal cardiac activity present

* Beta-hCG >5000 mIU/mL

* Failure of expectant or medical management

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding vasectomy?
options: The procedure is done under local anesthesia.
Sterility is achieved 3 weeks after the procedure.
A no-scalpel technique is being widely used now.
The vas deferens is the structure that is divided in the procedure.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Sterility is achieved 3 weeks after the procedure.

Option B is incorrect as sperms can remain in the reproductive tract for up to 3 months and thus sterility is not immediate. It can take up to 3 months after the procedure and during this time period, the couple must abstain from intercourse or use other methods of contraception.

Vasectomy:

Vasectomy is done under local anaesthesia. A small incision is made in the scrotum. The vas deferens are divided on both sides which disrupts the passage of sperms.

The no-scalpel technique has been now adopted. One single incision is made with special forceps and skin stitch is not required. Clips and plugs can be applied over the vas instead of cutting.

Approximately, 20 ejaculates clear the semen of all sperms. Two semen analysis reports must confirm the absence of sperms before the man can be declared sterile.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which serotype of HPV is responsible for Ca Cervix?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 16, 18, 31, 33

HPV – 16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 52, 56, 58, 59, 68 are associated with Ca Cervix.

Human Papilloma Virus (DNA Virus):

* The most common serotype of HPV responsible for Ca.Cervix: HPV 16

* The most malignant serotype of HPV for Ca.Cervix: HPV 18

* HPV serotype most specific for Ca. Cervix is HPV 18.

* The most common serotype of HPV associated with Squamous Cell Carcinoma is HPV 16

* The most common serotype of HPV associated with Adenocarcinoma is HPV 18

* Viral proteins required for malignant transformation are E6 and E7 oncoproteins.

* The E6 gene acts through the p53 gene, and E7 acts through the Retinoblastoma gene.

* Viral proteins required for replication are E1 and E2.

* Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) or southern blot or Hybrid capture technique is used for HPV DNA detection.

As per the December 2022 WHO Position on HPV vaccines, WHO recommends the following schedule:

* A one or two-dose schedule for girls aged 9-14

* A one or two-dose schedule for girls and women aged 15-20

* Two doses with a 6-month interval for women older than 21

A minimum of 2 doses and when feasible 3-doses remain necessary for those known to be immunocompromised and/or HIV-infected.

Note: Cervavac is India's first indigenously prepared quadrivalent HPV (qHPV) vaccine.

* Targeted strains: 6, 11, 16, and 18.

* Targeted group: 9-26 years of age

* Dose and route of administration: 0.5 ml, IM.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: While performing the USG assessment of a woman at 28 weeks of gestation, you note her amniotic fluid index to be 12.8. When does this parameter reach its maximum value in a normal pregnancy?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 34 weeks of gestation

The amniotic fluid index (AFI) is a measure of the amniotic volume which is maximum at 34 weeks of gestation.

The volume of amniotic fluid each week is variable. The volume gradually increases till 32-34 weeks of gestation. At 34 weeks, it is maximum and thereafter it starts declining till term.

Amniotic fluid volume is a passive reflector of the fetal condition. Its volume is determined by the following:

Pathway
Volume in ml

Fetal urination
+1000

Fetal swallowing
-750

Fetal lung fluid secretion
+350

Intramembranous flow across fetal vessels on the placental surface
-400

Early in pregnancy, amnionic fluid arises mainly from a transudate of plasma either from the fetal skin or across the uterine decidua and placenta. Fetal urine production becomes a major component in the second trimester.

Any alteration in fetal homeostasis, caused by fetal and maternal conditions, affects the amniotic fluid volume. Thus, AFI is measured as a part of the biophysical score.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A patient presents with an endometrial thickness of 14mm with an adnexal mass. She has a history of complex endometrial hyperplasia with the presence of atypical cells. Which of the following is likely the diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Metastasis endometrial cancer to ovary

This patient with endometrial hyperplasia and an adnexal mass likely has endometrial cancer with metastasis to the ovaries.

For those who undergo TVUS (transvaginal USG) and have an EEC (endometrial echo complex) >4 mm, localized thickening, or an indistinct or nonvisible EEC, endometrial sampling is a reasonable next step.

Investigations for endometrial carcinoma include:

* Endometrial aspiration biopsy is the first investigation for abnormal uterine bleeding, especially in females >35 years.

* Dilatation and fractional curettage was the best diagnosis method, but now it is not used.

* Hysteroscopy and biopsy: The investigation of choice for endometrial cancer.

* Transvaginal USG is used as an adjunct to endometrial biopsy.

* A Pap smear is not reliable to diagnose endometrial carcinoma. It is more useful as a screening tool rather than a diagnostic tool.

If symptoms of postmenopausal bleeding persist, imaging of the endometrial cavity should be performed with one or a combination of the following: TVUS, contrast sonography, or hysteroscopy.

Note: Surgical staging is the gold standard investigation for staging endometrial carcinoma.

Other options:

Option A: Struma ovarii is a type of highly specialized teratoma that contains only thyroid tissue. If it is functioning, it may lead to hyperthyroidism.

Option C: Polycystic ovarian disease is a disease characterized by menstrual abnormalities and hyperandrogenism in women of reproductive age. This condition has been linked to risk factors such as obesity and insulin resistance. Clinically these patients present with infertility and features of hyperandrogenism such as hirsutism and acne. On ultrasound, these patients have larger ovaries with an increased number of follicles. Multiple follicles that are peripherally located in the ovary can be seen on ultrasound. This is also called the string of pearls sign.

Option D: Immature teratomas such as solid teratomas of the ovary are solid and trabeculated. They also contain cartilage, bone, hair, and sebaceous material. There is no structural order. They are generally malignant. Grossly, they have a smooth external surface and are solid on sectioning. There may be areas of necrosis or hemorrhage.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A primigravida woman at 26 weeks gestation, presented with a BP of 150/90 mm Hg. Which test should be done next?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Urine dipstick

Urine dipstick should be the test that should be done next.

The patient is found to have BP> 140/90mm/hg after 20 weeks of gestation. It can be either gestational hypertension or Preeclampsia.

Gestational hypertension: BP≥ 140/90 mm of hg for the first time in pregnancy after 20 weeks of gestation in a previously normotensive woman without proteinuria.

Pre-eclampsia: Gestational hypertension along with proteinuria.

Proteinuria is the presence of total protein in 24 hours of urine of 0.3 g or more OR urine protein/creatinine (P/C) ratio >0.3 OR equal to 1 + (persistent 30 mg/dL) protein in at least two random clean-catch urine samples tested 4 hours apart in the absence of urinary tract infection is considered significant.

Hence the test done next is a urine dipstick.

Other investigations in pre-eclampsia:

* Ophthalmoscopic examination

* Blood values: They are usually non-specific. Serum uric acid level and S. creatinine is done. A liver function test is also done. A coagulation profile is not necessary when platelet count and liver enzymes are normal.

* Antenatal fetal monitoring

Chronic Hypertension in pregnancy

Rise in BP >140/90 mmHg after 20 weeks of pregnancy

Previously known hypertensive or BP  >140/90mmHg before 20 weeks of gestation

Proteinuria present(>300 mg in 24 hrs urine or >30 mg/dl in the random urine sample or urine dipstick 1+)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A woman presents with complaints of greenish-frothy vaginal discharge for 1 month. On examination vulvovaginal erythema is noticed. On saline microscopy, motile organisms are seen. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Trichomoniasis

The clinical vignette and microscopic findings are suggestive of trichomoniasis.

The clinical features include vaginal discharge which is profuse, thin, slightly green in color, and frothy. It may be associated with vaginal irritation, dysuria, and increased frequency. Cervical inflammation with punctate hemorrhagic spots known as the strawberry cervix is typically seen in trichomoniasis, caused by Trichomonas vaginalis. It is a sexually transmitted infection. Motile trichomonads are seen on wet mount examination.

The below image shows the strawberry cervix seen in trichomoniasis.

Other options:

Option B: Bacterial vaginosis is caused by an alteration in the normal vaginal flora and presents a malodorous grey-white discharge. It is diagnosed using Amsel's criteria, where at least three of the four following criteria should be present to confirm the diagnosis:

* Homogenous vaginal discharge

* Vaginal pH > 4.5

* Amine-like odor on adding KOH (Whiff test positive)

* Clue cells (>20% of cells)

Option C: Chlamydial cervicitis may present with severe abdominal pain with high fever, dyspareunia, prolonged menstrual cycles, and intermenstrual bleeding can be elicited. On examination, cervicitis with a yellow, cloudy, mucoid discharge can be seen from the os. The cervix tends to bleed easily when scraped.

Option D: Candidiasis is caused by infection with Candida albicans and presents with pruritus, burning, and dysuria with vulvar erythema, edema, and excoriations. A curdy white discharge will be present.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A young sexually active female patient presented to the outpatient department with complaints of lower abdominal pain, fever, vomiting, and foul-smelling vaginal discharge. On examination, the body temperature is 103 degrees Fahrenheit, pulse rate is 109 per minute and there is abdominal tenderness. Cervical motion tenderness is present on examination. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Pelvic inflammatory disease

The likely diagnosis in this patient is pelvic inflammatory disease(PID).

Pelvic inflammatory disease is characterized by inflammation of the upper genital tract including the fallopian tubes as well as the ovaries. This disease is commonly seen in sexually active young women and is usually preceded by a sexually transmitted disease. Gonococcal and chlamydial infections are commonly associated with PID.

Patients present with lower abdominal pain, fever, vomiting, dysuria, dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia and vaginal discharge. The symptoms also vary depending on the causative organism. On examination, there is a fever of around 103- 104°F, abdominal tenderness, tachycardia, and pelvic mass. Chronic PID is associated with sequelae such as chronic pelvic pain, menorrhagia, ectopic pregnancy, and infertility.

Acute PID is diagnosed if uterine tenderness, adnexal tenderness, or cervical motion tenderness is present and other etiologies are excluded or unlikely. One or more of the following can be used to diagnose PID on the clinical findings:

* Oral temperature >38.3°C (101.6°F),

* Mucopurulent cervical discharge or cervical friability,

* Abundant WBCs on saline microscopy of cervical secretions,

* Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) or C-reactive protein (CRP), and

* Presence of cervical N gonorrhea or C trachomatis

Depending on the extent of tissue involved, PID can be classified into five stages

Stage I
Acute salpingitis without peritonitis - No adhesions

Stage II
Acute salpingitis with peritonitis - purulent discharge

Stage III
Acute salpingitis with superimposed tubal occlusion or tubo ovarian complex

Stage IV
Ruptured tuba ovarian abscess

Stage V
Tubercular salpingitis

Other complications of chronic pelvic inflammatory disease:

* Hydrosalpinx

* Chronic pyosalpinx

* Chronic interstitial salpingitis

* Tubo ovarian cyst

Other options:

Option B: Endometriosis is a condition characterized by ectopic benign endometrial tissue that occurs outside the uterine cavity. Patients present with dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, menorrhagia, and infertility. There is no foul-smelling vaginal discharge or fever hence this option is incorrect.

Option C: Adenomyosis is seen in multiparous women >40 years. The most common symptom involves menorrhagia and dysmenorrhea. Per-Vaginal examination reveals symmetrical enlargement of the uterus corresponding to <12 weeks of pregnancy.

Option D: Migrating abdominal pain from the periumbilical area to the right iliac fossa is classic for appendicitis. The abdominal pain also causes nausea and vomiting. Other nonspecific signs of appendicitis include low-grade fever, abdominal tenderness, guarding, and rebound tenderness.

Aerobes: Staphylococci , Streptococci ,E. coli

Anaerobes: Bacteroides fragilis, Peptococcus, Clostridium, Actinomyces (IUD)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All of the following are true about audit in obstetrics except:
options: Change in hospital administration and practices
Should be done before analyzing outcomes
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Should be done before analyzing outcomes

A clinical audit is done to ascertain if healthcare is being provided in line with set standards and lets care providers and patients know where their service is doing well, and where there could be improvements. As it is done to analyze the current level of care against standard practices, it is usually studied after analyzing data and selecting a topic that requires quality improvement and not before analyzing outcomes.

In audits or quality improvement initiatives, collecting data related to patient care and outcomes (like fetal death) can help improve treatment practices by making changes to hospital administration and current practice.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: How long should a couple use contraception post-vasectomy?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 12-16 weeks

The couple need to take contraceptive measures for 12-16 weeks or 3 months after the male partner undergoes vasectomy.

Vasectomy is a permanent sterilization procedure done in males, where a segment of the vas deferens is resected and ligated bilaterally.

This procedure is done under local anesthesia. A small incision is made in the scrotum. The vas deferens are divided into both sides, disrupting the passage of sperms. The no-scalpel technique has been now adopted. One single incision is made with special forceps and a skin stitch is not required. Clips and plugs can be applied over the vas instead of cutting. The failure rate of vasectomy is 0.15%.

It is a relatively simple procedure with low rates of complications. A vasectomy does not instantly render a man sterile. The distal vas deferens may continue to hold semen for some time after the procedure. For this reason, it is estimated that at least 20 ejaculations or 3 months are required to empty the stored semen.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Identify the following instrument used by obstetricians:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Outlet forceps

The image shows Wrigley's forceps, which is an outlet forceps.

The instrument is light, about a third of the weight of ordinary long-curved forceps. The instrument is short which is due to a reduction in the length of the shanks and handles. It has a marked cephalic curve with a slight pelvic curve.

Pearl PF1918: Obstetrics forceps

Commonly used forceps:

1) Simpson forceps

* The most commonly used types of forceps in outlet delivery.

* Has elongated cephalic curve.

* These are used when there is substantial molding of the fetal head.

2) Elliot forceps

* Has an adjustable pin for regulating the lateral pressure on the handles.

* They are used most often when there is minimal molding.

* More suitable for outlet delivery.

3) Kielland forceps

* Has small pelvic curve and a sliding lock.

* Suitable for head with little molding.

* The most common forceps used for rotational delivery.

* Helps correct asynclitism.

4) Piper forceps

* Distinct perineal curve.

* Allows for application to the after-coming head in breech delivery.

5) Tucker-McLane forceps

* Suitable for fetal head with little molding.

* Used in rotational delivery.

6) Barton forceps and traction handle

* Used in rotational delivery.

* Most importantly used for delivery of occipitotransverse positions in a platypelloid pelvis.

* It is an obsolete procedure.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Identify the given image of the placenta previa.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Marginal

The picture shown is of the Marginal placenta previa.

Placenta previa is used to describe a placenta implanted in the lower uterine segment. Painless bleeding towards the end of the second trimester or later is characteristic of the condition. It usually occurs without warning and resolves spontaneously only to recur.

There are four types of placenta previa according to the degree of placental expansion to the lower uterine segment.

* Type-I: Low-lying- The lower margin of the placenta reaches the lower uterine segment but not the os. (Option B)

* Type-II: Marginal- The placenta does not cover the internal os but reaches its margin.

* Type-III: Incomplete or partial central- The placenta covers the closed internal os but does not do so when fully dilated. (Option C)

* Type-IV: Complete or central- The placenta covers the internal os even when fully dilated. (Option D)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: If the division in the zygote occurs between 9-12 days after fertilization, which of the following twin is expected?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Monochorionic monoamniotic

If the division in the zygote occurs between 9-12 days after fertilization, monochorionic monoamniotic twins are expected.

Time of division

The following radiological signs help in the determination of the chorionicity and the amnionicity of a twin gestation.

Lambda sign: In dichorionic gestation, the twins are separated by amniotic membranes and an intervening chorion. So, a thicker twin peak sign or lambda (λ) sign is formed at the point at which the amnions meet the placenta. It is best seen in the first trimester.

T sign: It is the sonographic image seen in a monochorionic twin pregnancy. It refers to the lack of chorion extending between the layers of the intertwin membrane.

* In monochorionic diamniotic gestation, the twins are separated only by the two amniotic membranes, with no intervening chorion. So, a thin T sign is formed at the point at which the amnions meet the placenta. It is best seen in the latter part of the first trimester or the beginning of the second trimester.

* In monochorionic monoamniotic gestation, there is an absence of a dividing membrane.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: In which of the following cases is the drug given below contraindicated?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Malpresentation of fetus

The drug given in the image is Oxytocin, and it is contraindicated in the malpresentation of the fetus.

The smooth muscle contraction seen with the use of oxytocin is physiological, i.e., it causes fundal contraction and cervical relaxation that helps in the delivery of the fetus, and makes oxytocin a good agent for the induction of labor.

Uses of oxytocin:

* To accelerate abortion and to stop bleeding following evacuation of the uterus

* Used as an adjunct to induction of abortion along with other abortifacient agents (PGE1 or PGE2)

* To induce labor by ripening the cervix before induction

* Augmentation of labor

* Following the expulsion of the placenta as an alternative to ergometrine.

* In active management of the third stage of labor

* To minimize blood loss and control postpartum hemorrhage.

* Oxytocin is involved in the regulation of preterm and term labor, but the exact mechanisms are not fully understood.

Contraindications of Oxytocin-

* Hypersensitivity to the hormone itself or any part of its synthetic version

* Vaginal deliveries that are in themselves contraindicated. These include:

* Active genital herpes infection in the mother,

* Vasa previa,

* Complete placenta previa,

* Invasive cervical cancer

* Abnormal position (most notably including a transverse lie)

Other options:

Option B- Recent studies have shown that induction of labor with a modified oxytocin infusion is a safe and effective alternative for selected gravidas with heart disease where elective delivery is warranted.

Option C- Oxytocin is used to induce or augment labor, including in some cases of premature labor when delivery is necessary. It's not contraindicated in this situation.

Option D- There's no specific contraindication for oxytocin use in hypothyroidism. Thyroid disorders don't typically interfere with oxytocin administration during labor.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: In which of the following situations is ventouse delivery contraindicated?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Preterm

Ventouse delivery is contraindicated in preterm babies as it increases the risk of scalp avulsion or sub-aponeurotic haemorrhage.

Contraindications of vacuum delivery:

* Any presentation other than vertex (such as face/breech)

* Preterm fetus (less than 34 weeks)

* Suspected fetal coagulation disorder

* Fetal macrosomia (more than 4 kg estimated weight)

A vacuum extractor is an instrument used in operative vaginal delivery by creating a vacuum between it and the fetal scalp.

The instrument consists of

* Suction cup

* Vacuum generator

* Traction tubing device.

The suction cup is placed on the fetal head at a point near the occiput called the flexion point, which is an imaginary point on the sagittal suture, located about 6 cm from the centre of the anterior fontanel or about 3 cm in front of the posterior fontanel. The flexion point is closer to the posterior fontanel as shown in the image below.

Pearl PF1954: Vacuum delivery- indications and contraindications

Indications of ventouse:

Therapeutic-

* Fetal distress in second stage

* Maternal distress in second stage

* Prolonged second stage

* Deep transverse arrest and persistent occipitoposterior

* High vacuum for second twin

Prophylactic-

* Preeclampsia

* VBAC

* Cardiac defects

* Anemia

Contraindications of ventouse:

* Preterm head

* Face presentation

* Fetal coagulopathy

* Fetal blood sampling

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Ovarian drilling is done in which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Polycystic ovarian syndrome

Laparoscopic Ovarian drilling is a surgical management procedure done for Polycystic ovarian syndrome(PCOS).

PCOS is an endocrinopathy seen in women of reproductive age, affecting multiple systems. The Rotterdam criteria is used to diagnose PCOS. The presence of any two of the three components of this criteria establishes the diagnosis of PCOS.

* Clinical/biochemical hyperandrogenism (hirsutism, acne)

* Menstrual abnormalities (Oligo/amenorrhoea), anovulation, infertility

* Polycystic ovaries on ultrasound.

Sonographic criteria for polycystic ovaries include ≥ 20 follicles and/or an increased ovarian volume (> 10 mL) or both.

The ultrasound image given below shows an enlarged ovary seen in PCOS with multiple follicles in the periphery.

Management of PCOS:

* Weight reduction and lifestyle changes (like smoking cessation).

* Oral contraceptive pills (OCP) are used to treat menstrual abnormalities. It also reduces acne and further hirsutism.

* Anti-androgens are useful in treating hirsutism. OCP with cyproterone acetate is prescribed for PCOS patients with hirsutism.

* Patients with PCOD are more prone to developing insulin resistance which can be controlled with metformin. Acarbose can be used if metformin is contraindicated

* Patients presenting with infertility are treated by inducing ovulation using clomiphene as a first-line drug, along with dexamethasone and letrozole.

Laparoscopic ovarian drilling or puncture of the ovarian capsule. This is done either by laser or by unipolar electrocautery. The procedure's end goal is to reduce the amount of androgen-producing tissue.

Disadvantages include the risks of pelvic adhesion formation and concerns regarding long-term effects on ovarian reserve.

It can be useful in patients:

* Fail to ovulate with clomiphene citrate,

* Who are at risk for ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome

* Who desire to minimize their risk for multifetal gestation.

Pearl PF1877: Endocrinological changes of PCOD

* Elevated Estrone/E1 levels.

* LH level is raised over 10 IU/mL. FSH level remains normal to low, but FSH/LH ratio falls.

* Testosterone and epi-androstenedione levels rise.

* Testosterone elevated but < 200 ng/dL (normal range 20 - 70 ng/dL)

* Testosterone > 200 ng/dL suggests androgen-secreting ovarian tumor

* DHEA-S values may be normal or slightly elevated

* DHEA >700 ng/mL suggests adrenal tumour

* Serum SHBG is reduced.

* Triglyceride level >150 mg/dL-hyperlipidaemia HDL <50 mg/dL.

* Fasting blood glucose/fasting insulin <4.5 suggests insulin resistance

* Prolactin is mildly raised in 15% cases

* Fasting insulin is more than 10 mIU/L in PCOS in 50–70%cases

* Thyroid function tests may be abnormal (hypothyroidism)

* 17-a-hydroxyprogesterone in the follicular phase >300 ng/dL suggests adrenal hyperplasia due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency.

* Urinary cortisol <50 μg/24 h.
