questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 25-year-old G2A1 at 18 weeks of gestation came with complaints of draining PV for the past 4 hours. On examination, membranes are ruptured and uterine contractions present. Transvaginal ultrasound shows a short cervix <25 mm and funneling of internal os >1 cm. What is the diagnosis____
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Cervical incompetence

Features of Short cervix <25 mm and funneling of internal os >1 cm is seen in cervical incompetence.

Transvaginal ultrasound is the ideal method to follow up and detect cervical incompetence.

The typical history of painless rupture of membranes followed by quick delivery of a live fetus in mid-trimester is very suggestive of cervical incompetence.

Diagnosis of Cervical incompetence in the non-pregnant state:

* The internal os allows the passage of a No.6 to 8 Hegar's cervical dilator or foleys catheter filled with 1 ml water without resistance.

* Premenstrual hysterosalpingography will show the typical funneling of the internal os.

Note:

In cervical incompetence, as the number of pregnancy losses increases, the period of gestation at which the loss occurs decreases.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 30-year-old primigravida at 18 weeks of gestation presents for her antenatal check-up. Her random plasma glucose level was 243 mg/dL and thus she was asked to undergo further tests. The fasting blood glucose levels were 146mg/dL and HbA1c was 7.6%. Which among the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?
options: Maturity onset Diabetes of the young
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Overt diabetes

A fasting blood sugar > 126 mg/dL , random blood sugar > 200mg/dL and HbA1c> 6.5% is suggestive of overt diabetes or pregestational diabetes.

The following are the lab results that would be suggestive of overt diabetes in a mother.

* Fasting blood sugar at least 126 mg/dL

* A random blood sugar of at least 200 mg/dL

* HbA1c of at least 6.5%

Cardiac anomalies are most commonly seen in the fetuses of overt-diabetic mothers. Musculoskeletal, urogenital, and CNS anomalies are also seen,

Congenital malformations occur at a higher rate, in overt diabetes than in gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). This is because GDM manifests in the second trimester and by then organogenesis would be complete.

Threshold values for gestational diabetes (75 g OGTT):

Plasma glucose
Glucose concentration threshold

Fasting
92 mg/dl

1 hr OGTT
180 mg/dl

2 hr OGTT
153 mg/dl

According to WHO and ADA guidelines, the one-step approach omits the screening test and simplifies diagnostic testing for gestational diabetes mellitus by performing only a 75-gram, two-hour oral GTT.

Diagnostic criteria or cut-off values with a 75 g OGTT are as follows:

* Fasting: 92 mg/dl

* 1 hour: 180 mg/dl

* 2 hours: 153 mg/dl

Two-step approach :

* The first step (screening) is a 50-gram one-hour glucose challenge test (GCT) at 24-28 weeks of gestation who are not previously diagnosed with diabetes.

* If the plasma glucose level measured 1 h after the load is ≥130, a 100-gram, three-hour oral glucose tolerance test (GTT) is done, which is the diagnostic test for gestational diabetes mellitus.

At least 2 of the following 4 values should be raised for a diagnosis to be made:

* Fasting: 95 mg/dL (5.3 mmol/L)

* 1 h: 180 mg/dL (10.0 mmol/L)

* 2 h: 155 mg/dL (8.6 mmol/L)

* 3 h: 140 mg/dL (7.8 mmol/L)

Other options:

Option A: MODY or maturity-onset diabetes of the young is a monogenic form of diabetes that occurs < 25 years. There is impaired insulin secretion, but no antibodies.

Option D: LADA  is a form of diabetes mellitus affecting lean and thin adults less than 50 years with a positive family history. It is insulin-dependent and associated with autoantibodies.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 34-year-old G3P2L2 woman with a past history of Caesarean section and a Dilatation and curettage , presents to the ER with hypotension, tachycardia, and severe abdominal pain. On examination, fetal parts are palpable in the abdomen and Fetal heart rate is weak. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Uterine rupture

The diagnosis of the given clinical scenario is uterine rupture.

Previous cesarean section and Dilatation and curettage are both potential risk factors for scar dehiscence and uterine rupture. Hypotension, tachycardia, dizziness, confusion, abdominal pain, scar site tenderness are all the signs of uterine rupture. Rarely, Hemoperitoneum can irritate the diaphragm and cause chest and shoulder tip pain.

CTG in uterine rupture will show non-reassuring variable fetal heart rate which might progress to late decelerations and bradycardia.

Differential diagnoses for uterine rupture:

* Pre-eclampsia

* Eclampsia

* Pulmonary embolism - amniotic fluid embolism / venous embolism

* Abruptio placenta

* Anaphylaxis to anesthesia

* Peripartum cardiomyopathy

Management of uterine rupture:

* confirm the fetal station and arrest of labor

* Stabilize the patient's vitals

* Immediate cesarean section should be performed, immediately/ as early as possible to avoid neurological or hypoxic sequelae in newborns.

* Depending on the extent of rupture and vitals on the table decision of uterine suturing or hysterectomy or sub-total hysterectomy may be taken.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 37-week primigravida has mild labor pains for 20 hours and the cervix is persistently 1 cm dilated but non-effaced. What would be the appropriate management?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Sedation and wait

The given clinical scenario is suggestive of either prolonged latent phase. The appropriate management is to sedate the patient and wait.

The first stage of labour consists of two phases :

* Latent phase: It is considered to begin at the time the woman first perceives regular uterine contractions and is characterized by gradual cervical change (up to 5 cm of cervical dilatation).

* Active phase: This follows the latent phase and is characterized by regular painful uterine contractions, cervical effacement, and rapid cervical dilatation from 5 cm to full dilatation.

A latent phase that exceeds 20 hours in primigravidae or 14 hours in multiparae is termed as a prolonged latent phase of labour. Bed rest is the preferred treatment unless there is any indication for expediting the delivery.

The presence of false labour pains for a long time may be confused with a prolonged latent phase. The differences between them include

Features
True labour pains
False labour pains

Cervical dilatation and effacement
Present

Pain
Lower abdomen and back, radiating to thighs
Lower abdomen only

Show
Present

Bag of water
Formed

Relief with enema
No
Yes

Augmentation with oxytocin is done only in those patients who even after therapeutic rest continue to be in a prolonged latent phase. There is no indication of the cesarean section unless cephalopelvic disproportion is present. Amniotomy is not useful and should be avoided in patients with prolonged latent phases due to the risk of infections.

CPD- Cephalopelvic disproportion

Pearl PF1871: Partograph

Partograph types:

WHO Modified Partograph (2000)

* No latent phase

* Vaginal examination: This should be done no less than every 4 hours to assess cervical dilatation, descent of the fetal head, and moulding of skull bones. More frequent examination is only undertaken if indicated.

* Charting starts at 4 cm of cervical dilation.

* Colour of liquor mentioned as C-clear, B-blood stained, M-meconium stained.

* Moulding mentioned:

* bones are separated and sutures can be easily felt - (0)

* bones touching (1+)

* bones overlapping but can be reduced(2+)

* bones severely overlapping and irreducible ( 3+).

* Alert line reflects the average rate of cervical dilation of the slowest quintile of term primigravidas, if dilation slows or ceases, the partograph plot will cross the alert line.

* Alert line: at 4 cm dilation and expected dilation of 1 cm/hour.

* Action line is 2–4 hours after the alert line, which prompts interventions to accelerate labor or perform cesarean delivery.

* Higher rates of perinatal mortality are associated with delays of 4 hours or more after the alert line.

* Contractions measured for a span of 10 min (duration noted) and measured every 30 min (1 square = half hour).

* Pulse: record every 30 minutes and mark with a dot (•).

* Blood pressure: record every 4 hours and mark with arrows, unless the patient has a hypertensive disorder or pre-eclampsia, in which case record every 30 minutes.

* Temperature: record every 4 hours.

WHO Composite Partograph: It is same as modified except for it has latent phase and charting done at 3 cm.

WHO Simplified Partograph: WHO further modified the partograph for use by skilled attendants in health centers. This simplified partograph is colour coded.

* The area to the left of the alert line in the cervicograph is coloured green, representing normal progress.

* The area to the right of the action line is coloured red, indicating dangerously slow progress in labour.

* The area in between the alert and action line is coloured amber, indicating the need for greater vigilance.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 40 year old P2L2 presents to your office with foul smelling bloody discharge per vaginum. She has been diagnosed with Carcinoma of the cervix Stage III B as per FIGO classification. What is the primary treatment option for this case?
options: Radical Hysterectomy + Pelvic lymph node dissection
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Chemoradiation

The treatment option for Stage III B Ca Cervix ,as per FIGO 2018 guidelines is Chemoradiation.

Chemoradiation can improve survival rates. It allows for remission in certain cases or reduction in morbidity.

Pelvic exenteration may be considered in cases where a fistula is present.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A couple presented in the outpatient department with infertility. The husband's semen analysis was normal. The wife reported menorrhagia and a hysterosalpingogram showed a tobacco pouch appearance with distal dilatation of the tubes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Tubal salpingitis

The clinical scenario along with a hysterosalpingogram showing a tobacco pouch appearance is diagnostic of tubal salpingitis, most likely tubercular salpingitis.

Hydrosalpinx occurs following acute salpingitis. The tubes are retort-shaped due to dilatation of the ampulla and filled with a clear fluid. The interstitial end of the tube is open whereas the fimbrial end is indrawn and closed. This permits the dye to enter but not exit the tube during hysterosalpingography.

Genital tuberculosis is almost always secondary to the primary focus. The fallopian tubes are the first to be involved and are bilaterally affected.

It is secondary to hematogenous spread from a primary focus. The ampullary part of the tube appears dilated with the fimbrial end open and pouting. This gives the characteristic tobacco-pouch appearance as seen in the image below.

HSG should not be performed in a suspected case of genital tuberculosis as it causes dissemination of the infection. This further increases the damage to the fallopian tubes.

If performed, HSG findings in tubercular salpingitis include:

* A rigid non-peristaltic pipe-like tube (lead pipe appearance)

* Beading and variation in the filling defect

* Calcification of the tube, Coiling of the tubes

* Cornual block

* Tobacco-pouch appearance of hydrosalpinx and pyosalpinx

* Tubal diverticula and/or fluffiness of tubal outline.

* Uterine cavity—irregular outline, honeycomb appearance, or presence of uterine synechia

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A hypertensive pregnant woman presented with abdominal pain, bleeding per vagina, and loss of fetal movements. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Abruptio placenta

The given clinical picture with abdominal pain, bleeding per vagina, and loss of fetal movements in a hypertensive pregnant woman points to the diagnosis of placental abruption.

Abruptio placenta is the partial/total separation of a normally implanted placenta before delivery.

The bleeding may be either

* Revealed - Blood dissects downwards between membranes and uterine wall to escape through the cervix. Or,

* Concealed -Blood accumulates between the detached placenta and uterus. Or,

* Mixed

Risk factors for abruption placenta include prior abruption history, preterm premature rupture of membranes, and pregnancy-associated hypertension. The haemorrhage into decidua basalis causes separation and compression of the placenta. This compromises fetal circulation leading to fetal distress.

Depending upon the degree of placental abruption and its clinical effects, the cases are graded as follows:

Grade 1
Grade 2
Grade 3

Vaginal bleeding is slight
Vaginal bleeding mild to moderate
Bleeding is moderate to severe or concealed.

Uterus irritable, minimal tenderness

Uterine tenderness is always present
Uterine tenderness is marked.

Maternal BP and fibrinogen unaffected
Maternal pulse increased, BP maintained
Shock is pronounced

FHS good
Fetal distress present
Fetal death is the rule

Maternal shock absent
Maternal shock absent
Associated coagulation defect or anuria may complicate

Placenta previa occurs when the placenta is implanted in the lower uterine segment over or very close to the cervical os. Vaginal bleeding is usually painless in this condition. Fetal condition is generally good until bleeding is severe which occurs in later stages. High-risk factors include multiparty, previous cesarean, or myomectomy scar in the uterus.

In preterm labour, fetal movements are not compromised. Hydramnios does not present with bleeding PV.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A mother brought her 16-year-old daughter to the hospital with the complaints of primary amenorrhea. On evaluation axillary and pubic hair were present and other secondary sexual characteristics normal.LH and FSH levels are normal and USG showed absence of uterus.What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. MRKH syndrome

The child does not have any uterus but has normal sex hormones and normal secondary sexual characteristics suggesting it is a case of MRKH( Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser).

Congenital absence of both the uterus and vagina is termed Mullerian agenesis or Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome. Females have a shallow vaginal pouch (1 to 2 inches deep). The uterus, cervix, and upper part of the vagina are absent. Typically, normal ovaries persist, as they originate from the genital ridge. Individual presents with primary amenorrhea, have a normal female appearance, secondary sexual characteristics, and 46 XX karyotype. Most patients with Mullerian agenesis have only small rudimentary Mullerian bulbs without endometrial activity.

With Mullerian agenesis, traditional conception is not possible, but pregnancy may be achieved using oocyte retrieval, fertilization, and gestational surrogacy.

Individuals with Mullerian agenesis or hypoplasia have associated congenital renal or skeletal anomalies. Common renal anomalies include ectopic, horseshoe or pelvic kidney and collecting system anomalies. Skeletal malformations include spina bifida, sacralization, sacral bone lumbarization, and cervical vertebral anomalies.

A similar presentation is seen in Androgen insensitivity but LH and FSH levels would be abnormal in that case.

Turner's syndrome is a chromosomal abnormality with partial or complete monosomy of the X chromosome (45+XO). In Turner's syndrome, gonadal dysgenesis causes primary ovarian failure that is hypogonadism. The clinical picture of amenorrhea, short stature, webbed neck, low hairline at the back of the neck, widely spaced nipples, and lack of secondary sexual characteristics is seen in Turner's syndrome.

Sweyer syndrome or pure gonadal dysgenesis occurs as a result of a mutation in the SRY gene. This leads to underdeveloped, dysgenetic gonads that fail to produce androgens or anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH). The following features are seen:

* Normal prepubertal female phenotype- Absent or poorly developed secondary sexual characteristics.

* Normal Müllerian system development due to the absence of AMH. (Uterus and cervix present)

* Female external genitalia

* Presence of dysgenetic testes that cannot produce AMH or sex hormones. They have a risk of malignant transformation.

As there is gonadal dysgenesis in a patient with 46 XY karyotype, they are actually determined to be males and are a type of male pseudohermaphrodite. They present with primary amenorrhoea, absence of secondary sex characters, and female external genitalia.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A post-menopausal woman presented with pain in her lower abdomen for the past 4 months. She was informed to have fibroids for a long time. The radiological investigation is shown below. What is the type of degeneration that occurred in this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Calcific degeneration

The X-ray shows calcified fibroids and is due to the calcific degeneration of fibroids.

Calcific or calcareous degeneration most often involves subserous fibroid with small pedicle or myomas in post menopausal women.

In calcareous degeneration, phosphates and carbonates of lime are deposited in the periphery along the course of the vessels. The best examples of calcareous myomas are those in old patients with long-standing myomas. They are like ‘womb-stones’ in graveyards.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman at 36 weeks of gestation with a prosthetic valve replacement for mitral stenosis is on warfarin therapy. Her INR is 3. What is the appropriate next step in management? LMWH- Low molecular weight heparin
options: Stop warfarin, start LMWH and asprin
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Stop warfarin and start LMWH

The next appropriate step in the management of a pregnant woman with a prosthetic valve on warfarin therapy at 36 weeks of gestation is to stop warfarin and start LMWH.

Warfarin is safe and effective in preventing thromboembolism in people with prosthetic valve. However, it is teratogenic and can lead to miscarriage, stillbirths, and fetal embryopathy if used in the first trimester. LMWH is safe for the fetus as it does not cross the placenta but is less effective than warfarin.

Period of gestation
Anticoagulant

Till 12 completed weeks

LMWH or UFH

13 to 36 weeks
Warfarin

36 weeks to 6 hours before delivery
LMWH or UFH

6 hours after vaginal and 24 hours after cesarian section
LMWH or UFH (ACOG recommendation)

(LMWH- Low molecular weight heparin, UFH- Unfractionated heparin)

It is recommended that all women on warfarin switch to LMWH or IV UFH at weeks 34–36. Since giving IV UFH until delivery is difficult, LMWH would be the better option till UFH is started. UFH should be started approximately 24 hours prior to labour induction or caesarean. IV UFH should be stopped once in labour or 6 hours prior to caesarean. UFH should be restarted 4 to 6 hours post-vaginal delivery or 6–12 hours post-caesarean section. Warfarin should be restarted on day 1 postpartum (uncomplicated vaginal delivery) or on day 2-3 if caesarian or bleeding complications occur.

Heparin should be discontinued just before delivery. If delivery occurs before discontinuation and there is extensive bleeding, then iv protamine sulfate can be given.(Easy reversal of anticoagulation). Warfarin, LMWH, and UFH do not accumulate in breast milk and do not have an anticoagulant effect in the newborn. They are compatible with breastfeeding.

Other options:

Option B: Unfractionated heparin can also be given instead of LMWH. However, in this case, the better answer is to give LMWH; because, in clinical practice, LMWHs have a long half-life, once-daily dosing, and fewer side effects. If LMWH is unavailable or cost-prohibitive, or if anti-Xa levels cannot be monitored, continuous infusion of UFH can be used as an alternative to LMWH.

Option D: Aspirin 75-100 mg can be given daily during pregnancy. It can be continued in women with mechanical heart valves if needed for other indications.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A woman who underwent dilatation and curettage for molar pregnancy 6 months ago presents with persistent symptoms of abdominal pain and distention. On further evaluation, the beta-hCG levels were persistently elevated and cannonball foci were found on the chest X-ray. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia

A woman with a history of dilatation & curettage for molar pregnancy complaining of abdominal pain, distention, cannonball foci, and persistently elevated beta HCG levels is likely having Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia.

Based on the mentioned features in the question stem, the diagnosis is low risk gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) of stage III.

Gestational trophoblastic diseases are histologically is divided into:

Hydatiform mole
Non-molar trophoblastic neoplasms

Villi present

Villi absent

Benign:

• Complete hydatidiform mole
• Partial hydatidiform mole

-

Malignant:

• Invasive mole

Malignant:

• Choriocarcinoma
• Placental site trophoblastic tumor
• Epithelioid trophoblastic
tumor

They typically develop along with or after a molar pregnancy. Rarely, it may develop after live birth, miscarriage, or medical termination of pregnancy.

Risk factors for malignant change are:

* Molar pregnancy -

* partial moles - 1-5% risk

* complete moles - 15-20% risk

* Patient's age ≥ 40 years or <20 years

* Parity ≥3

* Serum β hCG >1,00,000 IU/mL

* Uterine size >20 weeks

* Previous history of molar pregnancy

* Large theca lutein cysts >6 cm in diameter

Treatment of GTN:

* Low-risk GTN (FIGO Stages I-III: score <7): Single-agent chemotherapy with methotrexate (MTX) or Dactinomycin (less commonly used).

* 50 mg MTX is given IM on days 1, 3, 5, and 7 with folinic acid on alternate days.

* High-risk GTN (FIGO Stages II-III: score >7 and Stage IV): Multiple agent chemotherapies, with or without adjuvant surgery or radiotherapy. The preferred multiple agent chemotherapy regime is the EMACO regime:

* Etoposide

* Methotrexate

* Dactinomycin (actinomycin D)

* Cyclophosphamide

* Vincristine (Oncovin)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: During the normal delivery of a primigravida with polyhydramnios, the intern prematurely removes the placenta, leading to profuse bleeding. Examination reveals an intact placenta and that the uterus is partly outside the introitus. The patient is in hemorrhagic shock, so initial resuscitative measures are taken. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Uterine inversion

The given clinical picture is suggestive of uterine inversion and it is the most likely cause of shock immediately after delivery.

Uterine inversion:

* A rare cause of postpartum collapse, acute in onset, and occurs immediately after delivery.

*  Profuse bleeding after a premature attempt to remove the placenta and the development of shock immediately after delivery with the uterus partially outside the introitus is suggestive of uterine inversion.

Causes:

* Mismanagement of 3rd stage of labor - Delivering a yet to be separated placenta (Creede’s method): Most common

* Spontaneous

* Placenta accreta.

Features:

* Shock immediately after delivery, degree of shock out of proportion to the amount of bleeding,

* Shock is both neurogenic and hemorrhagic.

* Per abdomen examination: Fundus of the uterus is felt to be absent.

Management:

Vaginal operations

Oguch

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Identify the type of myoma labeled as '4' in the image given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Pedunculated submucosal myoma

The type of myoma labeled as '4' is pedunculated submucosal myoma.

Uterine myomas are broadly classified into 3 types.

They are:

* Intramural: remains within the myometrial wall.

* Submucous: present inside the uterine cavity and covered only by a thin endometrium.

* Subserous: present towards the peritoneal surface.

Treatment includes:

* Hormones to shrink the fibroid

* Uterine artery embolization.

* Myomectomy.

* Total / subtotal hysterectomy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Oligohydramnios is associated with which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Renal agenesis

Oligohydramnios is associated with renal agenesis.

Oligohydramnios is a condition where the liquor amnii is deficient in an amount to the extent of less than 200mL at term.

Sonographically, it is defined when the maximum vertical pocket of liquor is less than <2 cm or when amniotic fluid index (AFI) is less than 5 cm (less than 5 percentile).

Fetal urine production begins between 8-11 weeks but it does not become a major component of amniotic fluid until the 2nd trimester and is the major part of amniotic fluid after 20 weeks. In a case of renal agenesis, there is decreased or no urine output leading to oligohydramnios, which does not manifest till after 18 weeks.

Etiology of oligohydramnios:

* Placental condition:

* Amnion nodosum (failure of secretion by the cells of the amnion covering the placenta).

* Fetal conditions:

* Fetal chromosomal or structural anomalies

* Renal agenesis

* Obstructed uropathy

* Spontaneous rupture of membrane

* Intrauterine infection

* Drugs (PG inhibitors, ACE inhibitors)

* Post maturity

* IUGR

* Maternal conditions:

* Hypertensive disorders

* Uteroplacental insufficiency

* Dehydration

* Idiopathic

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the cause of lactational amenorrhea?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Increased prolactin secretion

The cause of lactational amenorrhea is increased prolactin secretion as a result of the baby sucking at the mother's breast.

Lactational amenorrhea:

* Type of secondary amenorrhea due to the effect of prolactin secretion.

* During lactation, there are pulsatile bursts of prolactin secretion in response to suckling.

* Prolactin suppresses GnRH, LH, and FSH causing lactational amenorrhea.

* Regular lactation with one feed at night delays ovulation and pregnancy for up to 6 months, provided she remains amenorrhoeic.

* After 6 months, lactation has no bearing on ovulation and pregnancy can occur, despite amenorrhoea and might need other forms of contraception.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the complication associated with IV bolus oxytocin?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Hypotension

An IV bolus of oxytocin can lead to hypotension. Thus, they are administered as dilute solutions at a controlled rate.

Oxytocin acts via G protein-coupled coupled receptors and the phosphoinositide-calcium second messenger system which contracts the uterine smooth muscle. It also acts via the release of prostaglandins and leukotrienes which augment the action of uterine contraction.

Oxytocin at smaller doses increases both the frequency and the force of contraction while at higher doses it produces sustained contractions. Other effects include contraction of myoepithelial cells leading to the ejection of milk and weak antidiuretic and pressor activity due to activation of vasopressin receptors.

Excess activation of vasopressin receptors can lead to water intoxication and hyponatremia. They also have a vasodilating property, particularly at high doses which can provoke hypotension.

Contraindications to oxytocin use include fetal distress, fetal malpresentation, placental abruption, and previous extensive uterine surgery.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the most common cause of consumptive coagulopathy in obstetrics?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Placental abruption

Placental abruption is the most common cause of severe consumptive coagulopathy in obstetrics.

Consumptive coagulopathy, also known as disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), is a pathologic disruption of hemostasis. It is characterized by systemic activation of blood coagulation, which results in thrombosis and fibrin deposition in the small blood vessels throughout the body.

Other causes of DIC in pregnancy:

* Amniotic fluid embolism

* Sepsis

* Preeclampsia and HELLP syndrome

* Acute fatty liver of pregnancy

* Postpartum haemorrhage.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following conditions shown below has a false positive Barr body?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Klinefelter's syndrome

A person with Klinefelter syndrome has an extra X chromosome and thus there is a false positive Barr body in this patient.

Barr body is the inactivated X chromosome in the cell which is peripherally situated as a darkly stained nodule, chromatin positive, and better seen in the epithelial cell nuclei. Male cells have only one X chromosome and are called chromatin negative as they do not have a Barr body. The total number of Barr bodies is given by the formula (X-1) as the inactivated X chromosome is seen as the Barr body.

Barr bodies are seen in 0-4% of genetic males (46XY) and 20-80% of genetic females (46XX and the most common sites for sampling for sex chromatin are Buccal mucosa, tooth pulp, and hair bulb.

In a normal male, there are no Barr bodies as the genotype is XY. Females are XX and thus have a Barr body in them.

Males with Klinefelter syndrome have XXY genotype and thus have a false positive Barr body while a female with Turner syndrome has XO and has no Barr body usually. Only in rare cases of mosaicism will Turner syndrome patients have a Barr body.

The image of a Barr body in a confocal microscope is shown below and is indicated by the arrow as the inactive X (Xi).

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following peaks marked in the image below is responsible for ovulation ?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 2

The label marked 2 represents the LH surge ,which is responsible for ovulation.

Phases of the menstrual cycle :

Follicular phase (days 0–14)

* A primordial follicle develops to the Graafian stage, with atresia of neighboring follicles.

* LH and FSH receptors are up-regulated in theca and granulosa cells.

* Estradiol levels increase and cause proliferation of the uterus.

* FSH and LH levels are suppressed by the negative feedback effect of estradiol on the anterior pituitary.

* Progesterone levels are low.

Ovulation (day 14)

* Occurs 14 days before menses, regardless of cycle length. Thus, in a 28-day cycle, ovulation occurs on day 14; in a 35-day cycle, ovulation occurs on day 22.

* A burst of estradiol synthesis at the end of the follicular phase has a positive feedback effect on the secretion of FSH and LH (LH surge).

* Ovulation occurs as a result of the estrogen-induced LH surge.

* Estrogen levels decrease just after ovulation (but rise again during the luteal phase).

* Cervical mucus increases in quantity; it becomes less viscous and more penetrable by sperm.

Luteal phase (days 14–28)

* Progesterone levels are high.

* The corpus luteum begins to develop, and it synthesizes estrogen and progesterone. Vascularity and secretory activity of the endometrium increase to prepare for receipt of a fertilized egg.

* Basal body temperature increases because of the effect of progesterone on the hypothalamic thermoregulatory center.

* If fertilization does not occur, the corpus luteum regresses at the end of the luteal phase. As a result, estradiol and progesterone levels decrease abruptly.

Menses (days 0–4)

* The endometrium is sloughed because of the abrupt withdrawal of estradiol and progesterone.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 14 year old girl presented with cyclical abdominal pain and a midline hypogastric lump. She has not achieved menarche yet. The per vaginal examination is shown below and a bluish swelling is seen along with it. What is the likely cause of her condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Imperforate hymen

The given case scenario is suggestive of an imperforate hymen, which has led to cryptomenorrhoea. This is a condition where menstruation occurs but is not visible due to an obstruction of the outflow tract.

The menstrual fluid gets collected in the reproductive tract. When this collection occurs in the vagina, it is known as hematocolpos. If the collection extends to the uterus, it is known as hematometra. The collection of blood in the fallopian tubes is called hematosalpinx.

The most common causes of cryptomenorrhea are:

* Intact/imperforate hymen - a bluish convex bulge is seen.

* Transverse vaginal septum - a pinkish concave covering is seen

Ultrasound pelvis confirms the diagnosis.

Management:

Imperforate hymen - A simple cruciate incision of the hymen allows the free drainage of the collected menstrual blood, and leads to normal reproductive function.

Option A: Bartholin's cyst appears as a swelling on the inner side of the labia majora. Larger cysts can bulge across the introitus. Small cysts can remain asymptomatic.

Option B - Transverse vaginal septum is a much rarer condition that occurs due to faulty fusion or canalization of the urogenital sinus and the Müllerian ducts. The majority of the cases involve the upper portion of the vagina. It can be differentiated from imperforate hymen by the presence of a short vagina and the absence of a bulging membrane. Extensive dissection and vaginoplasty are required.

Option D: Endometriomas are endometriotic lesions seen on the ovary. They present as adnexal masses. Endometriosis is a complication in cryptomenorrhea, due to retrograde menstruation.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 21 year old woman is brought in a drowsy state from a PHC with complaints of fever, severe lower abdominal pain, and purulent vaginal discharge. Her friend revealed that she had had an unsafe abortion a week ago. On examination, her abdomen was distended, BP was 80/60 mmHg, PR was 140 bpm and RR was 36 /min. Which of the following is not a causative agent of her present condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Escherichia coli

The given clinical scenario is suggestive of toxic shock syndrome (TSS) following septic abortion. Escherichia coli can be detected in septic abortion but it is not a causative agent for TSS.

Organisms causing toxic shock syndrome in septic abortion are:

* Streptococcus pyogenes

* Clostridium perfringens

* Clostridium sordellii

Clinical features of septic abortion include:

* Fever with chills and rigors

* Abdominal or chest pain

* Diarrhoea and vomiting

* Renal angle tenderness

* Offensive purulent vaginal discharge.

Clinical grading of septic abortion:

* Grade I - infection localized in the uterus

* Grade II - infection spreads to parametrium, tubes, ovaries, or pelvic peritoneum

* Grade III - generalized peritonitis, endotoxic shock, jaundice, or acute renal failure

Empirical antibiotic therapy in septic abortion is started for the broadest microbial coverage. Piperacillin-tazobactam or carbapenem and clindamycin are given intravenously. Antibiotics can be changed once culture sensitivity reports are available.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 24-year-old woman visits the infertility clinic with complaints of recurrent abortions. Upon investigations, she is found to have a septate uterus. Which of the following corrective procedures has the best obstetric outcome?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Transcervical resection of septum

Transcervical hysteroscopic resection of the septum has the best obstetric outcome.

The procedure involves the resection of septum under hysteroscopic guidance. Hence, it doesn't scar the uterus and avoids the necessity of cesarean sections for future pregnancies improving the outcomes.

Jones metroplasty, Strassmann metroplasty, Tompkins metroplasty involve approaching the uterus transabdominally which causes uterine scarring and are hence not preferred.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 27-year-old female presents to emergency following bleeding per vaginum, preceded by amenorrhea for 7 weeks. She's in hemodynamic shock with a positive serum beta hCG. On examination, a mass is palpable in the lower abdomen. What is the most likely diagnosis in this scenario?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Ruptured ectopic pregnancy

The given clinical scenario of amenorrhea for 7 weeks with bleeding per vaginum and palpable mass on examination is indicative of ruptured ectopic pregnancy, as suggested by:

* A positive urine/serum beta hCG test: suggestive of pregnancy.

* Bleed per vaginum: The patient experienced amenorrhea for more than four weeks before the onset of the current vaginal bleeding.

* 6 - 8 weeks post last regular menstrual cycle

* Unstable vitals: suggestive of internal blood loss.

Unstable patients with these findings should undergo urgent surgery. It involves surgical exploration(laparotomy). It reduces haemorrhage and also gives a better view of the operating field to the surgeon.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 28-year-old woman complaints of inability to conceive, dysmenorrhea, and pelvic pain. She has a history of frequent pelvic inflammatory disease. Hysterosalpingogram shows an absence of peritoneal spillage on the right side. Identify the given clinical scenario.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Tubal block

The given clinical scenario is indicative of a tubal block.

The presenting complaints of tubal block are:

* Dysmenorrhea

* Pelvic pain

* Inability to conceive

* Repeated episodes of PID

* History of ectopic pregnancy

Tubal block can be due to:

* Strictures - fibrotic block

* Inspissated amorphous material

* Tubal spasm - This can occur in apprehensive patients. It is prevented by premedication with atropine and analgesia

Hysterosalpingography (HSG) is a technique used for visualization of the uterine cavity and fallopian tubes by the injection of a radio-opaque dye, and visualization of the dye by fluoroscopy as it passes through the uterine cavity and fallopian tubes. It is best performed between the end of the menstrual period and ovulation (i.e 9th or 10th day of the cycle). 10-15ml of the dye is injected using a Leech-Wilkinson cannula, Rubin's cannula, or Foley's catheter. If the tubes are patent, the dye will spill out of the tubal Ostia and smear the adjacent bowel.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 30-year-old woman presents with severe dysmenorrhoea, dyspareunia and infertility. A diagnosis of endometriosis was made and she was posted for laparoscopy surgery. During the procedure, dense pelvic adhesions were seen with the bowel stuck to the fundus and cystic ovaries stuck to each other. What is the next step in managing this patient?
options: Gestrinone to decrease the LH surge
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Cystectomy and adhesiolysis

The clinical scenario is suggestive of endometriosis and the next step in the management of this patient is cystectomy and adhesiolysis.

After the surgery the patient is advised to start infertility treatment too.

Medical management of endometriosis:

* Gestrinone is an anti-estrogenic, anti-progestational, and mildly anabolic drug that reduces sex-hormone-binding globulin to release free testosterone. It also decreases the LH surge. It causes regression of lesions and amenorrhea. It is a 19-nortestosterone derivative similar to danazol, but with fewer side effects.

* Combined oral contraceptives are used for symptom control and alleviate disease. These also cause menstrual cycle regulation and delay pregnancy.

* Oral progestogens exert an anti-estrogenic effect and cause decidualization and endometrial atrophy. This causes disease regression. It doesn't prevent ovulation, thus is suitable for women who are trying to conceive.

* Mirena IUCDs reduce dysmenorrhea and menorrhagia. It is a single-sitting treatment with minimal side effects.

* Aromatase inhibitors like letrozole are anti-estrogens given for disease regression.

* Anti-inflammatory drugs like mefenamic acid and naproxen relieve dysmenorrhea.

Therapeutic procedures:

* Aspiration of Peritoneal fluid from the cul-de-sac removes PGE2, relieves dysmenorrhea, pelvic pain, and improves fertility

* Destruction of endometriotic lesions <3cm with diathermy, Nd-YAG laser or CO2 vaporization can be attempted.

* Larger lesions and chocolate cysts can be excised.

* Cystectomy can be done for pelvic pain but can reduce fertility potential.

* Laparoscopic breaking of adhesions relieves dysmenorrhea and chronic pelvic pain. It also restores tubal patency and improves ovulation. Pre-sacral neurectomy can be done simultaneously..

* Laser uterosacral nerve ablation (LUNA) is done for pelvic pain.

Pearl PF1294: Endometriosis

Sites of Endometriosis:

* Pelvic endometriosis: Pelvic peritoneum, the pouch of Douglas, uterosacral ligament.

* Rectovaginal endometriosis.

* Ovarian endometriosis.

* Chocolate cyst of the ovary.

* Other sites—appendix, pelvic lymph nodes.

* Metastatic— lungs, umbilicus, scar endometriosis.

One pathology review revealed that endometriosis has been identified on all organs except the spleen.

Examination findings in endometriosis:

* Abdomen: Cystic swelling, fixed and tender.

* Pelvis: Cystic tender mass.

* Vaginal examination: Fixed, tender, retroverted uterus. Tenderness in the lateral fornices (indicative of endometriosis even if no mass).

* Speculum inspection of the Posterior fornix: Bluish/blackish puckered spots on speculum, tender to touch. The presence of puckered spots is pathognomonic of endometriosis.

* Posterior Fornix Palpation: Uterosacral ligaments & pouch of Douglas feel thickened and shotty with multiple small palpable nodules. This is called the cobblestone feel of uterosacral ligaments.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 34-year-old G2P1L1 presents with abdominal pain, bleeding per vaginum in labour and loss of fetal movements. She occasionally smokes but does not consume alcohol or recreational drugs. On examination, her pulse rate is 80 bpm, BP 150/90 mm Hg and has a tense abdomen on palpation. What is the probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Abruptio placenta

The given clinical picture with abdominal pain, bleeding per vaginum, and loss of fetal movements in a hypertensive pregnant woman points to the diagnosis of placental abruption.

Premature separation of a normally implanted placenta is placental abruption.

Hypertension and smoking are important etiological factors in abruption. Hypertension leads to vasospasm of the placental blood vessels, which causes uteroplacental insufficiency.

The hemorrhage into decidua basalis causes separation and compression of the placenta. This leads to a compromise of circulation to fetus leading to fetal distress. The bleeding may escape through the cervix to cause external hemorrhage.

The common etiological factors for abruptio placentae include:

* Hypertension

* Preterm prematurely ruptured membranes

* Advanced maternal age

* Cigarette smoking

* Cocaine abuse

* Trauma

* Uterine fibroids

* Isolated single umbilical artery

* Short umbilical cord

* Prior abruption

* Subclinical hypothyroidism

questions.text: A 75 year old woman with complaints of mass per vaginum, as shown in the below image was posted for operative repair. During the pre-anaesthetic check-up, she was found to be unfit for major surgery. Which of the following procedures is recommended for her?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Le Fort’s repair

The given scenario and the image is suggestive of severe uterine prolapse in elderly women. Le Fort’s repair is recommended in this case.

This repair is done in patients who satisfy the following criteria:

* Very elderly menopausal patient with an advanced prolapse

* Do not wish to retain sexual function

* Medically unfit for major surgeries

This procedure can be performed under sedation and local anesthesia, or epidural anesthesia. The vaginal flaps from the anterior and posterior vaginal walls are excised, the raw areas are apposed in the midline with catgut sutures. This prevents the uterus from prolapsing.

This operation limits marital functions; hence, it should not be advised in women who wish to retain sexual function.

Other options

Abdominal sling operations are designed for women with type II or III degree prolapse and who are desirous of retaining childbearing function and menstrual function.

Sling operations are best suited to nulliparous prolapse. It includes,

* Shirodkar’s abdominal sling operation (Option B)

* Khanna’s abdominal sling operation (Option D)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman at 36 weeks of gestation with a prosthetic valve replacement for mitral stenosis is on warfarin therapy. Her INR is 3. What is the appropriate next step in management?
options: Stop warfarin, start LMWH and asprin
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Stop warfarin and start LMWH

The next appropriate step in the management of a pregnant woman with a prosthetic valve on warfarin therapy at 36 weeks of gestation is to stop warfarin and start LMWH.

Warfarin is safe and effective in preventing thromboembolism in the mother during the 2nd trimester. However, it is teratogenic and can lead to miscarriage, stillbirths, and fetal embryopathy if used in the first trimester. Heparin is safe for the fetus as it does not cross the placenta but is less effective than warfarin.

Period of gestation
Anticoagulant

Till 12 completed weeks

13 to 36 weeks
Warfarin

36 weeks to 6 hours before delivery
LMWH or UFH

6 hours after vaginal and 24 hours after cesarian section

LMWH- Low molecular weight heparin, UFH- Unfractionated heparin

Heparin should be discontinued just before delivery. If delivery occurs before discontinuation and there is extensive bleeding, then iv protamine sulfate can be given. Warfarin or heparin anticoagulation can be restarted after 6 hours of vaginal delivery, usually without any problem.

Warfarin, LMWH, and UFH do not accumulate in breast milk and do not have an anticoagulant effect in the newborn. They are compatible with breastfeeding.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A woman who underwent dilatation and curettage following a missed abortion now presents with amenorrhoea. Urine pregnancy test is negative. Hysterosalpingography shows the findings seen in the image below. What is your diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Asherman syndrome

The history along with the moth-eaten appearance on hysterosalpingography suggests a diagnosis of Asherman syndrome.

In Asherman syndrome, oligomenorrhoea, amenorrhoea, dysmenorrhoea, abortion and infertility are seen with uterine synechiae.

The synechiae are caused by the following factors:

* Vigorous curettage following postpartum haemorrhage or abortion

* Tubercular endometritis

* Uterine infections with or without intra-uterine device

Treatment involves hysteroscopic lysis of the adhesions

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: An 18 year old girl presents with a history of low-grade fever, weight loss, abdominal pain and amenorrhoea for six months. On examination, a pelvic mass is felt on the left side and signs of ascites are positive. What is the probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Genital tuberculosis

This female with a 6 months chronic history of symptoms along with the presence of a palpable abdominopelvic mass suggests genital tuberculosis.

Genital tuberculosis commonly affects women in the reproductive age group. It presents with menstrual irregularities such as amenorrhoea, menorrhagia, dysmenorrhoea, pelvic pain. Non specific symptoms like fever and weight loss are also present. It affects fallopian tube causing infertility, tubo-ovarian masses, hydrosalpinx, pyosalpinx. Pelvic and abdominal peritoneum is often involved with multiple tubercles, ascites and abdominal masses.

Other options:

Option A: Submucous fibroid presents with menorrhagia, dyspareunia, pelvic pain, infertility or recurrent pregnancy loss.

Option B: Ovarian malignancy can also present with symptoms like abdominal fullness, bloating, nausea, abdominal distention, early satiety, fatigue, change in bowel movements, urinary symptoms, back pain, dyspareunia, weight loss, palpable pelvic mass or ascites . But this patient's young age and a chronic course of 6 month is unlikely to be a malignancy.

Option C: Ectopic pregnancy presents as amenorrhoea followed by an acute symptoms of vaginal bleeding and pelvic pain in a reproductive age women. It does not have a long course of 6 months and other symptoms seen in this girl.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Identify the condition given in the image below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Placenta previa

The given image shows placenta previa.

The grades of placenta previa are:

* Type I (Low-lying): The major part of the placenta is attached to the upper segment and only the
lower margin encroaches onto the lower segment but not up to the os.

* Type II (Marginal): The placenta reaches the margin of the internal os but does not cover it.

* Type III (Incomplete or partial central): The placenta covers the internal os partially (covers the
internal os when closed but does not entirely do so when fully dilated).

* Type IV (Central or total): The placenta completely covers the internal os even after it is fully dilated.

It can remain effective for 24 h. It is used only once. It acts as a mechanical barrier and prevents entry of sperms into the cervical canal, absorbs semen and contains a spermicidal agent.

Pearl PF1929: Pearl index and couple protection rate:

Pearl Index is defined as the number of contraceptive failures per 100 woman-years of exposure (HWY).

* In this formula, the total accidental pregnancies that are used as the numerator must include every known conception, irrespective of its outcome.

* In the denominator, total months of exposure is obtained by deducting, 10 months for full-term deliveries and 4 months for abortion, from the total period under review.

Couple Protection Rate:

* It is an indicator of couple protection practice in the community.

* It is defined as the percentage of eligible couples effectively protected against childbirth by one or the other approved methods of family planning.

* Attaining a 60% CPR would mean restricting all third or higher-order births.

questions.text: Preconceptional use of ______ leads to reduced incidence of neural tube defects.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Folic Acid

Pre-conceptional use of folic acid reduces the incidence of neural tube defects and folic acid is the commonly used active form of vitamin B9.

Folic acid deficiency is implicated in neural tube defects like spina bifida, encephalocele, and anencephaly.

As per the Anemia Mukt Bharat Program, during the period of pre-conception up to the first trimester, women are advised to have 400 mcg of folic acid tablets daily to reduce the incidence of neural tube defects in the fetus.

Note that, non-pregnant, non-lactating Women of reproductive age (20–49 years) who are not actively planning a pregnancy in near term should receive 1 iron and folic acid tablet containing 60 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Revised A woman presented in her 8th week of pregnancy seeking MTP. The appropriate dosage of Misoprostol (administered by mucosal route) would be ______
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 800 mcg

The dosage of Misoprostol (administered by mucosal route) in this case is 800 mcg.
Mucosal misoprostol administration has increased efficacy and minimizes gastrointestinal side effects and is now preferred over the prior oral administration. The mucosal route includes buccal, sublingual, and vaginal Misoprostol administration.

Medical management protocol for induced abortion for < 12 weeks of gestation (As per WHO 2018 guideline):

* Combined Regimen (Recommended): 200 mg of oral Mifepristone followed 1-2 days later by 800 mcg of buccal, vaginal, or sublingual Misoprostol

* Misoprostol-only regimen (Alternative): 800 μg misoprostol administered vaginally, sublingually, or buccally.

Outpatient medical abortion is an acceptable option for pregnancies with a menstrual age < 63 days (9 weeks).

First trimester:

Mifepristone/misoprostol combined regimen (recommended): 200 mg of oral Mifepristone followed 1-2 days later by 800 mcg of buccal, vaginal, or sublingual Misoprostol

Misoprostol-only regimen (alternative): 800 μg misoprostol administered vaginally, sublingually, or buccally.

Methotrexate/misoprostol:

(d) Methotrexate, 50 mg/m2 body surface area intramuscularly or orally; followed in 3-7 days by:

(e) Misoprostol, 800 mcg vaginally. Repeat if needed 1 week after methotrexate initially given

Second trimester:

Mifepristone/misoprostol combined regimen (recommended): 200 mg of oral Mifepristone followed 1-2 days later by 400 mcg of buccal, vaginal, or sublingual Misoprostol every 3 hours

Misoprostol alone (alternative): 400 mcg of buccal, vaginal, or sublingual Misoprostol every 3 hours

Dinoprostone: 20 mg vaginal suppository every 4 hr

Concentrated oxytocin:

50 units oxytocin in 500 mL of normal saline infused during 3 hr; then 1-hr diuresis (no oxytocin); then escalate sequentially in a similar fashion through 150, 200, 250, and finally 300 units oxytocin each in 500 mL normal saline

Note: This recommendation has been updated from the WHO 2012 Safe abortion guidance. This updated recommendation applies to pregnancies up to 12 weeks of gestation, whereas, in the prior guidance, different regimens were recommended for pregnancies up to 7 weeks, 9 weeks, and 12 weeks.

Pearl PF1638: Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act - MTP Act 1971

MTP Act with 2021 amendments

Indications:

* Therapeutic - to save the life of the mother

* Eugenic - to prevent the risk of the child being born with serious mental or physical abnormality i.e. first-trimester viral infections, teratogenic drug intake, radiation exposure

* Humanitarian - pregnancy resulted from rape or incest

* Social - pregnancy resulted from failure of contraceptives

Rules:

* Only a registered medical practitioner who is qualified (one who has assisted in the performance of 25 cases of MTP in a recognized hospital) can terminate a pregnancy.

* MTP should be carried out in a government or government-recognized hospital. Private hospitals may take up MTP if they obtain a license from the chief medical officer of the district.

* The termination of pregnancy by a person, who is not a registered medical practitioner (the person concerned), or in an unrecognised hospital (administrative head) shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than 2 years, but which may extend to 7 years.

Consent:

The consent of the woman is required for conducting an abortion. The written consent of the guardian is required if the woman is minor or mentally ill. Consent of the husband or partner is not necessary.

If the woman is not willing, abortion cannot be performed at the request of the husband alone. The woman need not produce proof of her age. It is enough for the woman to say that she was raped, and it is not necessary that a complaint was lodged with the police.

Opinion of doctors:

* Till 20 weeks - 1 doctor's opinion

* 20 to 24 weeks - 2 doctors' opinion

* For substantial fetal anomalies - approval from the medical board consisting of obstetrician, paediatrician, radiologist and a person appointed by the state

Upper limit of MTP:

* Up to 24 weeks of gestation in victims of rape and incest, fetal anomalies, or congenital malformations

* Up to 20 weeks in case of contraception failure (any female with her partner)

* At any gestational age for substantial fetal anomalies decided by the medical board

Confidentiality:

A register for recording the details of MTP must be kept for at least 5 years. The patient's name must not be entered, only the reference number is used. Unlawful disclosure of patient's details is punishable with 1-year imprisonment ± fine.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Ritodrine, which prevents premature labour, causes all of the following maternal complications, except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Hypoglycaemia

Ritodrine when administered predisposes to fetal hypoglycaemia and maternal hyperglycaemia.

Preterm labour and delivery (labour starts before the 37th completed week, counting from the first day of the last menstrual period) can be delayed by drugs such as ritodrine, in order to improve the perinatal outcome. A short-term delay of 48 hours allows the use of corticosteroids that can reduce perinatal mortality and serious morbidity significantly.

Complications of ritodrine are as follows :

* Maternal:

* Headache

* Palpitation

* Tachycardia

* Pulmonary oedema

* Hypotension

* Cardiac failure

* Hyperglycaemia

* Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)

* Hyperinsulinemia

* Lactic acidemia

* Hypokalaemia

* Potential death

2. Fetal:

* Hypoglycaemia

* Intraventricular haemorrhage

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The most common cause of post-menopausal bleeding all over the world is
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Senile endometrial atrophy

The most frequent cause of post menopausal bleeding globally is senile endometrial atrophy.

Hypoestrogenism in a menopausal woman causes atrophy of the endometrium and vagina. In the uterus, the atrophic endometrial surfaces contain little or no fluid to prevent intracavitary friction. This results in microerosions of the surface epithelium and a subsequent chronic inflammatory reaction, which is prone to light bleeding or spotting.

Other Options :

* Cervical cancer : Cervical cancer is the most common cause of post menopausal bleeding in India, and not over the world.

* Endometrial cancer : Endometrial cancer is the most common cause of postmenopausal bleeding in developed countries, and not over the world.

* Hormone replacement therapy : Hormone replacement therapy is the second most common cause of post-menopausal bleeding all over the world.

Note: Endometrial cancer accounts for 10% of cases of post-menopausal bleeding. Unexpected post-menopausal bleeding should be assessed for endometrial carcinoma. Remember, no cancer is as prevalent as hypoestrogenism in a postmenopausal woman, and this is why senile endometrial atrophy is the most common cause of bleeding in them, and not any cancer.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The normal placenta is _____ 1. Discoid 2. Hemochorial 3. Deciduate
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1 ,2 and 3

The human placenta is of discoid, deciduate and hemochorial type.

* Placenta is discoid like in shape.

* It is deciduate as it is shed at the time of parturition.

* Hemochorial as majority of it is vessel derived.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the average duration of lochial discharge in a puerperal woman?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 24-36 days

The average duration of lochial discharge in a puerperal woman is about 24-36 days. The average amount of discharge for the first week is 250 mL.

During early puerperium, sloughing of the decidual tissue causes vaginal discharge which is known as lochia. Most women experience an increase in the amount of bleeding at 7-14 days secondary to the sloughing of the eschar on the placental site. But the average duration of lochial discharge ranges from 24 to 36 days.

The lochial discharge appears as follows:

Name

Lochia rubra

Blood, decidua, fetal membranes, vernix, lanugo, meconium

The persistence of red lochia beyond one week might be an indicator of uterine subinvolution. The presence of an offensive odour, large pieces of tissue or blood clots in lochia, excessive or absence of lochia might be a sign of infection.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the best-recommended management in a case of vault prolapse with cystocele and rectocele?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Anterior colporrhaphy + Posterior colpoperineorrhaphy

A combination of anterior colporrhaphy and posterior colpoperineorrhaphy is best recommended in managing a case with both cystocele and rectocele.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the investigation of choice in a 55-year-old woman who presents with post-menopausal bleed?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Endometrial biopsy

Endometrial biopsy is the investigation of choice in a case of post-menopausal bleed, as the chances of endometrial cancer are quite high.

For those who undergo TVUS (transvaginal USG) and have an EEC (endometrial echo complex) >4 mm, localized thickening, or an indistinct or nonvisible EEC, endometrial sampling is a reasonable next step.

Investigations for endometrial carcinoma include:

* Endometrial aspiration biopsy is the first investigation for abnormal uterine bleeding, especially in females >35 years.

* Dilatation and fractional curettage was the best method to diagnose but now it is not used.

* Hysteroscopy and biopsy: The investigation of choice for endometrial cancer.

* Transvaginal USG is used as an adjunct to endometrial biopsy.

* A Pap smear is not reliable to diagnose endometrial carcinoma. It is more useful as a screening tool rather than a diagnostic tool.

If symptoms of postmenopausal bleeding persist, imaging of the endometrial cavity should be performed with one or a combination of the following: TVUS, contrast sonography, or hysteroscopy.

Note: Surgical staging is the gold standard investigation for staging endometrial carcinoma.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the use of the instrument given below?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Hysterosalpingography

The given image is that of a Leech-Wilkinson cannula. It is used to inject dye in hysterosalpingography.

The following images show the cannula placed in the cervix for the procedure:

Other cannula used for the same purpose is the Rubin’s cannula which is shown below:

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: When does secondary post-partum haemorrhage develop?
options: Shortly after the delivery of placenta
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 24 hours - 12 weeks after delivery

Secondary postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) occurs between 24 hours and 12 weeks after delivery.

Types of PPH:

* Primary: haemorrhage occurring within 24 hours of childbirth

* Most common cause: atonic PPH

* Secondary: haemorrhage occurring after 24 hours and up to 12 weeks postpartum

* Most common cause: retained placenta

Causes of PPH (mnemonic: 4’T’):

* T - Tone: Atonic PPH

* T - Trauma: Traumatic PPH

* T - Thrombin: Coagulopathy (DIC and hypofibrinogenemia)

* T - Tissue: retained products of conception.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which among the following is an ideal treatment for a 55 year old with simple hyperplasia of endometrium with atypia?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Simple hysterectomy

Simple hysterectomy is the best treatment in the above case.

Best treatment of atypical hyperplasia in a post-menopausal woman is hysterectomy.

Management of Endometrial hyperplasia:

1) Non-atypical hyperplasia:

* Pre-menopausal women: Progesterone therapy

* Post menopausal women:

* Simple hyperplasia without atypia: Follow up without therapy

* Complex hyperplasia without atypia: Progesterone therapy

2) Atypical hyperplasia:

* Pre-menopausal women: High-dose progesterone therapy

* Post-menopausal women: Hysterectomy

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which is the most common benign tumour of the ovary in the reproductive age group?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Benign teratoma

A benign teratoma or dermoid cyst is the most common benign tumor of the ovary in the reproductive age group. It is also the:

* Most common benign tumor of ovary diagnosed in pregnancy

* Most common germ cell tumor (overall)

* Most typical tumor to undergo torsion.

* Bilateral in 10-15% cases.

It consists of a Rokitansky’s protuberance, which is a projection covered by skin, sebaceous glands, sweat glands along with teeth & bones can be seen. Sometimes thyroid tissue can be seen on histopathological study – known as Struma Ovarii. The most common tissue elements found are ectodermal derivatives.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following can reduce the risk of endometrial cancer in a post-menopausal woman on hormone replacement therapy (HRT)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Adding progesterone to oestrogen

Adding progesterone to estrogen in HRT can reduce the risk of potential endometrial cancer.

For women with a uterus, it is recommended to add micronized progesterone to prevent endometrial hyperplasia which can occur after 6 months of oestrogen therapy. For women without a uterus, just estrogen therapy is sufficient.

Hormone therapy is only indicated for the treatment of vasomotor symptoms,genitourinary syndrome of menopause like vaginal and vulvar atrophy and for the prevention of osteoporosis.

The daily estrogen content in most oral contraceptive pills is 35µg or less and levonorgestrel is 100-150 mg. But the HRT commonly used have a different concentration of estrogen and progesterone. Hence the regular combined oral contraceptive pills are not used.

Clonidine reduces hot flashes during menopause but does not have any action on endometrium. Vitamin E has no role in endometriual proliferation.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which part of the fallopian tube is most commonly involved in genital tuberculosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Ampulla

The ampullary part of the fallopian tube is most commonly involved in genital tuberculosis.

Fallopian tube in genital tuberculosis:

The fallopian tubes are almost always involved in genital tuberculosis. The lesions are generally bilateral. The mode of spread of disease is hematogenous, arising from a primary infective focus in the lung.

The ampulla is most commonly affected while the fimbriae and interstitium are spared.

Hysterosalpingography may reveal the following:

* Tobacco pouch appearance of hydrosalpinx and pyosalpinx

* Lead pipe appearance (rigid, nonperistaltic pipe)

* Beading and variation due to filling defects

* Calcification of the tube

* Cornual block

* Jagged fluffiness of tubal outline

Hysteroscopy will reveal the presence of synechiae, partial obliteration of the cavity, the golf-hole appearance of the tubal ostia, and presence of ulcers.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which phase of the menstrual cycle features vacuolation as a histological feature?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Secretory phase

Subnuclear vacuolation is a histological feature of the secretory phase of the menstrual cycle.

The histological features as per the respective phases are:

Proliferative/oestrogenic phase:

* The glands of the functional layer are simple tubules with regular epithelium

* The endometrium is thick, stoma compact, and short straight glands are present.

* Arteries become more coiled and spiralled

Secretory phase :

* The secretory phase of the endometrium begins on the 15th day and persists until the onset of menstruation.

* Subnuclear vacuolation (presumptive evidence of progesterone activity)

* Corkscrew-shaped glands

Menstrual Phase:

* Glands shrink with prominent vessels and haemorrhagic spots.

The image below shows secretory endometrium:

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 30-year-old gravida 2 with previous LSCS develops suprapubic pain during contractions with maternal tachycardia and fetal bradycardia at 8 cm dilation. What is the most appropriate next step?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Immediate cesarean section

These findings strongly suggest Uterine scar dehiscence (or uterine window), a life-threatening obstetric emergency. Uterine rupture occurs when the uterine wall tears partly, often at the previous cesarean scar.

This leads to:

• Massive hemorrhage
• Fetal hypoxia
• Maternal shock

Classic Clinical Signs

| Sign | Explanation

| ---- | -----------

| Severe abdominal/suprapubic pain | Scar tearing

| Maternal tachycardia | Blood loss

| Fetal bradycardia | Fetal hypoxia

| Loss of fetal station | Indicates complete rupture

Fetal bradycardia is the most common early sign of uterine dehiscence/ rupture.

Suspected uterine dehiscence

↓

Immediate resuscitation

↓

Emergency laparotomy

↓

Cesarean delivery

↓

Repair uterus or hysterectomy

The goal is rapid delivery to save the fetus and prevent maternal hemorrhage.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A G3P1A1 woman is admitted to the labor room at term with a cervix dilated to 4 cm, intact membranes, and the fetal head palpable at 3/5 per abdomen. After 4 hours, a repeat examination shows the cervix dilated to 5 cm with an unchanged station, and the cervicograph remains on the right side of the alert line. Which of the following statements about the progress of labor is correct?
options: The head was engaged at the time of presentation
The cervicograph status suggests that intervention is likely to be required
The cervicograph on repeat examination would touch the action line
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. The cervicograph status suggests that intervention is likely to be required

A partograph (cervicograph) is used to monitor the progress of labor by plotting cervical dilatation against time. Important lines on the partograph:

• Alert line → represents expected normal cervical dilatation
• Action line → placed 4 hours to the right of the alert line and indicates need for intervention if crossed

In this patient:

• Cervical dilatation progressed only from 4 cm to 5 cm in 4 hours
• Fetal station remained unchanged
• Cervicograph lies to the right of the alert line

This indicates abnormal or slow progress of labor and suggests that intervention may soon be required (eg, augmentation or operative delivery).

Additional concepts:

• “3/5 head palpable per abdomen” means the head is not fully engaged
• Engaged head usually corresponds to ≤2/5 palpable abdominally

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A woman presents to OPD at 36 weeks of gestation and presents with complaints of breathlessness and excessive abdominal distension. On examination, fetal movements are normal, fetal parts not easily felt and muffled fetal heartbeat is heard. Symphysis fundal height came out to be 41weeks. Per abdomen examination reveals tense abdomen but not tender. What can be the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Polyhydramnios

Polyhydramnios is diagnosed by ultrasound using:

| Parameter | Value

| --------- | -----

| Amniotic Fluid Index (AFI) | > 24 cm

| Deepest vertical pocket | > 8 cm

Causes of Polyhydramnios

Maternal causes

• Gestational Diabetes Mellitus

Fetal causes

• Anencephaly
• Esophageal Atresia

Idiopathic

• Most common (\~60%).

Complications

| Maternal | Fetal

| -------- | -----

| Breathlessness | Preterm birth

| Preterm labor | Cord prolapse

| Postpartum hemorrhage | Malpresentation

Excessive distension, SFH far ahead of dates, difficulty feeling fetal parts and muffled FHR are classic of polyhydramnios. Abdomen is tense but non-tender with no bleeding or pain suggestive of abruption. Hydrocephalus alone doesn’t explain this degree of maternal breathlessness and distension.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All of the following parameters have a Bishop’s Score of 3 except: (NEET PG 2015)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Soft consistency

The Bishop score is used to assess cervical favorability before induction of labor. Components of the Bishop score:

• Cervical dilatation
• Effacement
• Cervical consistency
• Cervical position
• Fetal station

Parameters scoring 3 points include:

• Cervical dilatation ≥5 cm
• Effacement >80%
• Fetal station +1 or +2

Cervical consistency scoring:

• Firm = 0
• Medium = 1
• Soft = 2

Thus, soft cervical consistency does not receive a score of 3.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Among the following options, which one is considered a presumptive sign of early pregnancy? (NEET PG 2015)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Amenorrhea

| Presumptive signs (Signs felt by patient herself) | Probable signs (Signs seen by doctor) | Positive signs (Definitive)

| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------

| Amenorrhoea | Goodell’s sign: Softening of cervix | Fetus seen on ultrasound

| Nausea/vomiting | Hegar’s sign: On bimanual palpation, vaginal and abdominal fingers touch each other. | Hearing fetal heart sounds

| Fatigue | Chadwick’s sign: Blue/violet discoloration of vagina and vulva (Jacquemier’s sign). | Palpation of fetal parts

| Increased urinary frequency (T1 & T3) | Osiander’s sign: Pulsations felt in lateral fornix of vagina. | Fetal skeleton seen on X-ray

| Breast changes | Palmer’s sign: • Rhythmic painless uterine contractions. •Not felt by patient. |

| Quickening | Piskacek’s sign: Unequal growth of uterus |

| | Positive pregnancy test |

| | Increased pigmentation |

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: An NST shows 1 acceleration in 20 minutes with no decelerations. What is the next best step?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Continue the NST till 40 minutes

Non Stress Test evaluates fetal well-being by monitoring fetal heart rate accelerations with fetal movements.

A reactive NST requires:

| Criterion | Requirement

| --------- | -----------

| Accelerations | ≥2 accelerations

| Time | Within 20 minutes

| Duration | ≥15 seconds

| Increase | ≥15 bpm above baseline

2 accelerations in 20 minutes = reactive NST.

Sometimes the fetus is sleeping, which may reduce accelerations.

Therefore:

NST started

↓

Only 1 acceleration in 20 min

↓

Extend test to 40 minutes

↓

Reassess accelerations

Thus the correct next step is continue NST up to 40 minutes.

BPP is performed when: NST remains non-reactive after 40 minutes.

| Parameter | Score

| --------- | -----

| NST | 2

| Fetal breathing | 2

| Fetal movement | 2

| Fetal tone | 2

| Amniotic fluid | 2

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: During fetal heart rate monitoring, variable decelerations are noted on the CTG trace. What is the most likely cause or mechanism of this finding?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Cord compression

Cardiotocography detects changes in fetal heart rate patterns during labor.

Variable decelerations are abrupt decreases in fetal heart rate caused by Umbilical Cord Compression.

Variable decelerations on CTG indicate umbilical cord compression and are commonly associated with oligohydramnios. Early decelerations indicate fetal head compression, while late decelerations indicate fetal hypoxia from uteroplacental insufficiency.

Mechanism of Variable Decelerations

Umbilical cord compression

↓

Reduced blood flow to fetus

↓

Baroreceptor stimulation

↓

Sudden drop in fetal heart rate

This produces the characteristic abrupt V-shaped deceleration on CTG.

| Type | Cause | Pattern

| ---- | ----- | -------

| Early deceleration | Head compression | Mirror of contraction

| Variable deceleration | Cord compression | Abrupt V-shaped

| Late deceleration | Uteroplacental insufficiency | Delayed after contraction

Conditions Causing Cord Compression

Common causes include:

• Oligohydramnios
• Cord prolapse
• Nuchal cord
• Cord around limbs

Management of Variable Decelerations

Initial steps include:

• Maternal position change
• Oxygen administration
• IV fluids
• Amnioinfusion if severe

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following conditions is least likely to be associated with fetal bradycardia?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Maternal fever

Normal fetal heart rate:

| Parameter | Range

| --------- | -----

| Normal baseline FHR | 110–160 bpm

| Bradycardia | <110 bpm

| Tachycardia | >160 bpm

Bradycardia generally indicates fetal hypoxia or cardiac abnormalities.

Causes of Fetal Bradycardia

1. Placental Abruption

In Placental Abruption:

• Placenta separates prematurely.
• Causes acute fetal hypoxia.

2. Fetal Head Compression

Head compression during labor causes:

• Vagal stimulation
• Resulting in early decelerations on CTG.

These appear as temporary fetal heart rate slowing.

3. Congenital Heart Disease

Congenital cardiac defects can affect the fetal conduction system, producing:

• Complete heart block
• Persistent fetal bradycardia

Example:

• Congenital AV block
• Seen in maternal lupus (anti-Ro antibodies).

Maternal fever, especially in chorioamnionitis, causes:

• Increased fetal metabolic rate
• Sympathetic stimulation

Result:➡ Fetal tachycardia (>160 bpm)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which one of the following statements regarding fetal well-being is not correct?
options: Daily fetal movement count is a simple reliable method of fetal well-being.
Modified biophysical profile includes non-stress test and fetal breathing.
Healthy fetus should have minimum of 10 movements in 12 hours period.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Modified biophysical profile includes non-stress test and fetal breathing.

• The Modified Biophysical Profile (Modified BPP) consists of Non-Stress Test (NST) + Amniotic Fluid Index (AFI) (or deepest vertical pocket)
• It does not include fetal breathing movements. Fetal breathing is assessed only in the Complete Biophysical Profile (BPP).

Why are the statements correct/incorrect?

• A. Daily fetal movement count is a simple reliable method of fetal well-being. Correct.
• B. Modified biophysical profile includes non-stress test and fetal breathing. Incorrect. It includes NST + AFI, not fetal breathing.
• C. Mothers perceive 88% of fetal movements. Correct.
• D. Healthy fetus should have a minimum of 10 movements in 12 hours. Correct (Cardiff “Count-to-10” method).

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 28-year-old woman presents with vaginal bleeding and lower abdominal pain. Serum β-hCG is markedly elevated. Endometrial biopsy shows nuclear enlargement with hyperchromasia, loss of nuclear polarity, and intraluminal papillary projections of glandular epithelium.
