No chorionic villi are identified in the curettage specimen. Which of the following statements about this finding is most accurate?
options: Presence of this reaction on curettage confirms intrauterine pregnancy
Absence of this reaction excludes ectopic pregnancy
This reaction can mimic clear cell carcinoma of the endometrium histologically
This reaction is driven by rising FSH levels in early pregnancy
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. This reaction can mimic clear cell carcinoma of the endometrium histologically

This patient demonstrates the Arias-Stella reaction, a benign hypersecretory change of the endometrium caused by exposure to high levels of β-hCG and progesterone during pregnancy, including ectopic pregnancy and gestational trophoblastic disease.

Histologic features include:

• Nuclear enlargement and hyperchromasia
• Loss of nuclear polarity
• Cytoplasmic vacuolization
• Papillary glandular projections

Because these atypical changes can appear markedly pleomorphic, the Arias-Stella reaction may mimic clear cell carcinoma histologically.

Important concepts:

• Presence of Arias-Stella reaction indicates exposure to pregnancy-related hormones but does not confirm intrauterine pregnancy
• It may occur in ectopic pregnancy
• Absence of chorionic villi in curettage raises concern for ectopic pregnancy or trophoblastic disease
• The reaction is hormonally driven primarily by β-hCG/progesterone effects, not FSH

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 30-year-old nulliparous woman with primary infertility is found to have a 5–6 cm ovarian endometrioma on pelvic ultrasonography. She desires future fertility. Which of the following is the most appropriate fertility-preserving treatment?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Laparoscopic cystectomy (cyst wall excision)

For women with ovarian endometrioma ≥4 cm who desire future fertility, the preferred fertility-preserving treatment is laparoscopic cystectomy (complete excision of the cyst wall).

Compared with drainage or ablation, laparoscopic cystectomy:

• Improves spontaneous pregnancy rates
• Reduces recurrence of endometrioma
• Provides tissue for histopathological examination
• Relieves pain more effectively

Why not the other options?

• A. Oophorectomy: Not appropriate in a young nulliparous woman as it reduces ovarian reserve and fertility.
• B. Cauterization (ablation) of the cyst wall: Higher recurrence rates and lower spontaneous pregnancy rates than cystectomy.
• C. Transvaginal cystectomy: Not the standard approach; laparoscopic surgery is preferred.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 34-year-old woman presents for routine cervical cancer screening, and her Pap smear shows atypical glandular cells. What is the next best step in management?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Endocervical + Endometrial biopsy

Atypical glandular cells (AGC) on Pap smear carry a significant risk of premalignant or malignant lesions involving the cervix or endometrium. Therefore, histopathological evaluation of both the endocervical canal and the endometrium is required, particularly in women ≥35 years or those with abnormal uterine bleeding or risk factors for endometrial cancer.

Why not the other options?

• A. Cervical biopsy: Evaluates only visible cervical lesions and may miss endocervical or endometrial pathology.
• B. Colposcopy: Recommended as part of the evaluation, but AGC also requires endocervical sampling and endometrial biopsy because glandular lesions can arise beyond the visible transformation zone.
• D. Hysterectomy: Not indicated without a confirmed diagnosis of malignancy or a high-grade premalignant lesion.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 35-year-old woman presents with intermenstrual bleeding. Atypical glandular cells are seen on a pap smear. What is the mast appropriate next step in management?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Colposcopy and endometrial sampling

Atypical glandular cells (AGC) are abnormal cells arising from:

• Endocervical glands
• Endometrial glands

These abnormalities are clinically significant because they may indicate:

• Cervical adenocarcinoma
• Endometrial carcinoma
• Adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS)

Therefore, immediate evaluation is required.

Atypical glandular cells (AGC) carry a high risk of premalignant and malignant lesions in both the cervix and endometrium, especially in women ≥35 or those with abnormal bleeding. Hence the correct next step is colposcopy with cervical evaluation plus mandatory endometrial sampling.

Management of AGC requires evaluation of both cervical and endometrial sources.

Recommended evaluation includes:

1. Colposcopy
2. Endocervical sampling
3. Endometrial biopsy (especially if >35 years or abnormal bleeding)

| Cytology finding | Next step

| ---------------- | ---------

| ASC-US | Repeat cytology or HPV testing

| LSIL | Colposcopy

| HSIL | Colposcopy ± excisional procedure

| AGC | Colposcopy + endometrial sampling

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 36-year-old asymptomatic woman visits the gynecology OPD for routine cervical cancer screening. She has no history of abnormal Pap smears, is immunocompetent, and has undergone regular screening in the past. Which of the following is the preferred screening strategy for her?
options: Co-testing (Pap smear + high-risk HPV DNA test) every 5 years
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Co-testing (Pap smear + high-risk HPV DNA test) every 5 years

For women 30–65 years of age, the preferred cervical cancer screening strategy is co-testing with cytology (Pap/LBC) plus high-risk HPV DNA testing every 5 years. Persistent HPV infection is more clinically significant after age 30, making HPV testing highly sensitive and specific for detecting high-grade cervical lesions.

Why not the other options?

• A. LBC every 5 years – Incorrect. Cytology alone is recommended every 3 years, not every 5 years.
• C. VIA – Used mainly in low-resource settings (including India's national screening program) where laboratory-based testing is unavailable. It is feasible but less accurate than HPV-based screening.
• D. Colposcopy – A diagnostic procedure performed after an abnormal screening test, not a primary screening method.

High-Yield Screening Schedule

• 21–29 years: Pap smear (cytology) every 3 years
• 30–65 years: Co-testing every 5 years (preferred), or primary HPV testing every 5 years, or cytology alone every 3 years
• >65 years: Screening may be discontinued if prior screening has been adequate and consistently negative.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 39-year-old nulliparous female has presented to Gynaecology OPD with complaint of post coital bleeding for past six months. The first investigation to be offered to this female will be:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Pap smear

A woman with postcoital bleeding should first undergo cervical evaluation, and the initial screening investigation is a Pap smear (cervical cytology) to detect premalignant or malignant cervical lesions.

Why not the other options?

• A. Colposcopy: Performed after an abnormal Pap smear or when the cervix appears suspicious on examination.
• B. Dilatation and Curettage (D&C): Used for evaluation of endometrial pathology, not as the first test for postcoital bleeding.
• D. Cone biopsy of cervix: Reserved for confirmed high-grade CIN or suspected microinvasive carcinoma, not as the initial investigation.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 45-year-old lady complains of post-coital bleeding. She has a positive pap smear. What is the next line of management? (NEET PG 2018)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Colposcopy directed biopsy

Postcoital bleeding is an important warning symptom of cervical pathology, including cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and cervical cancer.

If a Pap smear is abnormal, the next step is Colposcopic evaluation with directed biopsy of suspicious areas

Purpose of colposcopy:

• Magnified visualization of the cervix
• Identification of acetowhite areas, abnormal vessels, and lesions
• Targeted biopsy for histopathologic diagnosis

Why other options are incorrect:

• Cone biopsy is reserved for high-grade lesions or when invasive disease cannot be excluded
• Repeat Pap smear delays diagnosis in symptomatic women with abnormal cytology
• Hysterectomy is not performed without histologic confirmation

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 45-year-old woman with a history of cervical erosion and spotting since 2 months. What is the next best step?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. LBC + HPV + cervical biopsy

Liquid Based Cytology

Advantages:

• Better sample preservation
• Reduced false negatives
• Allows HPV testing from same sample

Human Papillomavirus

High-risk types:

• HPV 16
• HPV 18

These cause \~70% of cervical cancers.

Cervical Biopsy

This confirms the definitive diagnosis.

Suspicious cervix

↓

Screening test (LBC)

↓

HPV testing

↓

Biopsy for confirmation

In a 45-year-old with persistent spotting and cervical erosion, cervical cancer must be ruled out. Liquid-Based-Cytology + HPV testing is the recommended screening combination. Biopsy is mandatory when symptoms persist or lesion appears suspicious.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 52-year-old woman came to the OPD with a diagnosis of advanced cervical cancer. She has a 14-year-old daughter. What advice would you give for her daughter?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Advise HPV vaccine

Most cases of cervical cancer are caused by Human Papillomavirus infection.

High-risk oncogenic types include:

• HPV 16
• HPV 18

These account for \~70% of cervical cancers.

| Age group | Schedule

| --------- | --------

| 9–14 years | 2 doses (0 and 6 months)

| ≥15 years | 3 doses

Best time for HPV vaccination is before sexual debut.

Since the daughter is 14 years old, she falls into the ideal vaccination age group.

At 14 years, the best preventive strategy is HPV vaccination (primary prevention). Screening with Pap/HPV testing starts later (usually ≥25 years). BRCA/PTEN mutations are linked to other cancers, not typical cervical carcinoma.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 52-year-old woman diagnosed with carcinoma cervix stage 2B was advised radiotherapy. Which of the following statements regarding radiotherapy is false? (NEET PG 2020)
options: Point B is 3 cm lateral to point A
Point A is 2 cm above the external os and 5 cm lateral to the internal uterine canal
Point A receives a dose of 7000 cGy
Point B receives a dose of 6000 cGy
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Point A is 2 cm above the external os and 5 cm lateral to the internal uterine canal

Point A

• A point 2 cm lateral and 2 cm superior to the external cervical os.
• Represents the anatomical location of the ureter.
• The total dose to point A should not exceed 8000 cGy.

Point B

• A point 3 cm lateral to point A.
• Represents a dose to the pelvic wall.
• The dose to point B is about 25 – 30% of the dose to point A (4500 – 6500 cGy)

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 52-year-old woman presents with foul-smelling bloody discharge per vagina mixed with mucous discharge. On examination, a necrotizing growth is seen in the cervix with lateral parametrium involvement. What will be the management for this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Chemoradiation

Lateral parametrium involvement = FIGO Stage IIB carcinoma cervix. Standard of care from Stage IIB onwards is concurrent chemoradiation (external beam + brachytherapy). Surgery is reserved for earlier stages (up to 2A1). For Stage IIB cervical cancer, the treatment of choice is: Concurrent chemoradiation

This involves:

| Treatment | Purpose

| --------- | -------

| External beam radiotherapy | Destroy tumor

| Cisplatin | Enhances radiation effect

| Brachytherapy | Internal radiation

Once parametrium is involved, surgical removal becomes difficult because:

Tumor extends into parametrium

↓

Cannot obtain clear surgical margins

↓

Higher recurrence risk

Thus chemoradiation is preferred.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 54-year-old woman with cervical cancer shows parametrial involvement and bilateral hydroureteronephrosis. What is the FIGO stage?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Stage IIIB

Cervical Cancer is one of the most common gynecological cancers worldwide.

The staging is done using the FIGO Staging for Cervical Cancer.

Stage III means tumor extends to pelvic wall or causes kidney obstruction.

| Stage | Description

| ----- | -----------

| IA
IA1
IA2 | Invasive carcinoma that can be diagnosed only by microscopy
Measured stromal Invasion <3mm in depth
Measured stromal Invasion ≥3mm and <5mm in depth

| IB1
IB2
IB3 | Invasive carcinoma  < 2cm
Invasive carcinoma  ≥2cm and < 4cm
Invasive carcinoma ≥4cm

| IIA
IIA1
IIA2
IIB | Involvement limited to the upper two-thirds of the vagina
Invasive carcinoma < 4cm
Invasive carcinoma ≥4cm
With parametrial involvement but not to the pelvic wall

| IIIA
IIIB
IIIC1
IIIC2 | The carcinoma involves the lower third of the vagina
Extension to the pelvic wall and/or hydronephrosis or nonfunctioning kidney
Pelvic lymph node metastasis only
Para-aortic lymph node metastasis

| IVA
IVB | Spread to adjacent pelvic organs
Spread to distant organs

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 65-year-old postmenopausal lady presents in Gynaecology OPD with abdominal distension and weight loss. On investigation, she was diagnosed to have an ovarian tumour. The most common type of ovarian tumour in this woman would be:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Epithelial tumour

Epithelial ovarian tumors are the most common ovarian tumors in postmenopausal women and account for \~90% of malignant ovarian neoplasms. They commonly present with:

• Abdominal distension
• Weight loss
• Early satiety
• Ascites
• Pelvic/abdominal mass

Why not the other options?

• A. Germ cell tumour: Common in children and young women (<30 years).
• B. Sex cord tumour: Less common; often presents with hormonal manifestations (e.g., estrogen secretion by granulosa cell tumor).
• D. Trophoblastic tumour: Arises from gestational trophoblastic tissue, not the ovary.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 65-year-old postmenopausal woman presents with abdominal distension and discomfort. Imaging reveals an ovarian mass with solid components, ascites, and omental caking. Her serum CA-125 level is markedly elevated at 990 U/mL. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Serous cystadenocarcinoma

Serous Cystadenocarcinoma of the Ovary

Ovarian Serous Cystadenocarcinoma is the most common malignant ovarian tumor.

Key characteristics

• Usually occurs in postmenopausal women
• Often bilateral
• Forms complex cystic-solid masses
• Characterized by papillary projections

Histological hallmark- Psammoma bodies (concentric calcifications)

The question provides several classic exam clues-

| Finding | Significance

| ------- | ------------

| Postmenopausal age | Typical for epithelial ovarian cancer

| Ascites | Advanced disease

| Omental caking | Peritoneal metastasis

| Solid components in mass | Malignant tumor

| Very high CA-125 | Serous epithelial tumor

CA-125 is the most important tumor marker for epithelial ovarian carcinoma, especially serous type.

Omental Caking

Omental caking refers to diffuse infiltration and thickening of the omentum by tumor cells.

It indicates:

• Peritoneal carcinomatosis
• Advanced ovarian cancer

Ovarian cancer commonly spreads by transcoelomic spread within the peritoneal cavity.

| Marker | Associated tumor

| ------ | ----------------

| CA-125 | Epithelial ovarian carcinoma

| AFP | Yolk sac tumor

| β-hCG | Choriocarcinoma

| Inhibin | Granulosa cell tumor

| LDH | Dysgerminoma

| Tumor | Tumor Marker | Key Feature

| ----- | ------------ | -----------

| Serous cystadenocarcinoma | CA-125 | Psammoma bodies

| Mucinous tumor | CEA | Large multiloculated cyst

| Granulosa cell tumor | Inhibin | Estrogen production

| Dysgerminoma | LDH | Young women

| Yolk sac tumor | AFP | Schiller-Duval bodies

A) Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma

Features:

• Large multiloculated cysts
• Usually unilateral
• Less commonly associated with ascites and omental caking

Tumor marker: CEA, not CA-125.

C) Endometrioid tumor

Associated with:

• Endometriosis
• Endometrial carcinoma

Less commonly presents with massive ascites and omental spread.

D) Granulosa cell tumor

A sex cord stromal tumor.

Features:

• Produces estrogen
• Causes postmenopausal bleeding

Tumor marker: Inhibin, not CA-125.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 65-year-old postmenopausal woman presents with blood-stained vaginal discharge. On examination, her BP is 160/100 mmHg. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. TVS

This presentation should immediately raise suspicion for Endometrial Cancer or other causes of postmenopausal bleeding (PMB).

The first step in evaluation is: Pelvic examination + Pap smear + Transvaginal ultrasound (TVS)

PMB is defined as any bleeding occurring ≥12 months after menopause. Postmenopausal bleeding should be considered endometrial cancer until proven otherwise.

The recommended initial evaluation includes:

| Step | Purpose

| ---- | -------

| Pelvic examination | Look for cervical or vaginal lesions

| Pap smear | Detect cervical pathology

| TVS | Measure endometrial thickness

TVS measures the endometrial stripe.

| Endometrial thickness | Interpretation

| --------------------- | --------------

| ≤4 mm | Low risk of endometrial cancer

| >4 mm | Requires endometrial biopsy

Causes of Postmenopausal Bleeding-

| Cause | Frequency

| ----- | ---------

| Endometrial atrophy | Most common

| Endometrial hyperplasia | Premalignant

| Endometrial carcinoma | Must rule out

| Cervical cancer | Possible

| Hormone therapy | Drug related

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A woman who underwent dilatation and curettage for molar pregnancy 6 months ago presents with persistent symptoms of abdominal pain and distention. On further evaluation, the beta- hCG levels were persistently elevated and cannonball foci were found on the chest X-ray. What is the appropriate management in this case? (NEET PG 2021)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Methotrexate with folinic acid

• Persistent elevation of β-hCG after evacuation of a molar pregnancy with metastatic “cannonball” lesions in the lungs indicates gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN), most likely choriocarcinoma or invasive mole. This patient is most consistent with Low-risk metastatic GTN
• First-line treatment for low-risk GTN: Methotrexate with folinic acid rescue

Why folinic acid is added:

• Reduces methotrexate toxicity to normal cells
• Allows safer repeated chemotherapy cycles

Features suggesting GTN:

• Persistently elevated β-hCG after molar evacuation
• Metastatic lung lesions
• Abdominal pain/distention

EMACO regimen is reserved for:

• High-risk metastatic GTN
• Poor prognostic score disease

GTN is highly chemosensitive and has an excellent cure rate with appropriate chemotherapy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: All of the following are features of granulosa cell tumor of the ovary except:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Increased CA 125 levels

Granulosa cell tumors characteristically show Call-Exner bodies and “coffee-bean” nuclei due to nuclear grooves. They secrete estrogen and express inhibin B (as well as A, even though B is measured routinely), which serves as a useful tumor marker. These tumors are sex-cord stromal in origin, not epithelial.

Call–Exner bodies marked with black circles micrograph of a granulosa cell tumor of sex cord stromal tumour.

Think of a granulosa tumor as a tiny ovary trying to act like a full endocrine gland

→ making estrogen

→ forming mini follicles (Call-Exner bodies)

Inhibin-B is a typical marker

CA-125 is typically elevated in epithelial ovarian cancers, not granulosa cell tumors.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Dr. Savita is training her interns who are being posted for rural posting. Which is appropriate for cervical cancer screening?
options: Pap smear + HPV DNA every 5 yearly
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Pap smear alone every 3 yearly

Cervical Cancer Screening- The most widely used screening test is the Pap smear (cervical cytology). The Pap smear detects precancerous lesions (CIN) before they progress to invasive cancer. It samples cells from the transformation zone of the cervix, where most cervical cancers originate.

For low-resource settings (such as rural areas), the recommended approach is:

| Age Group | Screening Method | Interval

| --------- | ---------------- | --------

| 21–29 years | Pap smear alone | Every 3 years

| 30–65 years | Pap smear every 3 years OR HPV testing | Depending on resources

Because HPV testing may not be widely available in rural setups, Pap smear every 3 years is considered practical and effective.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasm does not include? (NEET PG 2019)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Partial mole

Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia (GTN), on the other hand, includes only the malignant forms of trophoblastic disease:

1. Invasive Mole
2. Choriocarcinoma
3. Placental Site Trophoblastic Tumor
4. Epithelioid Trophoblastic Tumor

A partial mole is a type of hydatidiform mole and is considered benign. It is not included under GTN as it does not have malignant potential unless it transforms into an invasive mole, which is rare.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Glands of Cloquet are:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Lymphatic drainage of vulva

The Gland (Node) of Cloquet, also known as the Rosenmüller node, is the highest deep inguinal lymph node, located in the femoral canal beneath the inguinal ligament. It serves as a link between the deep inguinal lymph nodes and the external iliac lymph nodes and is an important sentinel node in the lymphatic drainage of the vulva.

• The vulva drains primarily to the superficial inguinal lymph nodes, then to the deep inguinal nodes, including the Node of Cloquet, before reaching the external iliac nodes.
• It is clinically important in carcinoma of the vulva, as involvement of the Node of Cloquet suggests more advanced nodal spread.

Why not the other options?

• B. Lymphatic drainage of cervix: The cervix drains mainly to the parametrial, obturator, internal iliac, external iliac, and sacral lymph nodes.
• C. Lymphatic drainage of uterus: The uterus drains to the external iliac, internal iliac, para-aortic (lumbar), and superficial inguinal nodes (via the round ligament from the fundus).
• D. Lubricating glands of vagina: Vaginal lubrication is provided mainly by Bartholin’s glands (greater vestibular glands) and cervical secretions. There are no glands within the vaginal mucosa.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Identify the correct statements regarding HPV vaccination: 1. Primary target group = girls 9– 14 years 2. It is recommended to give single dose by both WHO and national guidelines in targeted age group 3. Target coverage is 90% of eligible girls 4. Provides complete protection
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 2 and 3 only

1. Primary target group = girls 9– 14 years: Correct.

• WHO target: Girls aged 9– 14 years

2. It is recommended to give single dose by both WHO and national guidelines in targeted age group: Correct.

• Current WHO recommendations and GOI guidelines support: single-dose HPV vaccination in males and females upto 21 years, and 2 doses following that.

3. Target coverage is 90% of eligible girls: Correct.

• WHO cervical cancer elimination target: 90% - 70% - 90%
•

Pillar 1: 90% HPV Vaccination

• 90% of girls fully vaccinated with HPV vaccine by age 15

•

WHO's updated single-dose recommendation (2022):

• WHO SAGE (Strategic Advisory Group of Experts) reviewed evidence and concluded that one dose provides comparable efficacy to 2– 3 doses in girls aged 9– 14
• This simplifies logistics and reduces cost, critical for low-middle income countries (LMICs)

•

Pillar 2: 70% Screening

• 70% of women screened with a high-performance test by age 35, and again by age 45

Screening Intervals

| Strategy | Interval

| -------- | --------

| HPV testing | Every 5 years

| Cytology (Pap) | Every 3 years

| Co-testing | Every 5 years

• Pillar 3: 90% Treatment

• 90% of women with pre-cancer treated; 90% of women with invasive cancer managed appropriately

4. Provides complete protection: False.

• \~97-100% efficacy against HPV 16/18 related CIN2+ (precancerous lesions) in HPV-naive women
• Does not treat existing HPV infection — purely prophylactic

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: In a Pap smear, which fixative agent is commonly used to fix the slides immediately after sample collection?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 95% ethanol

Pap Smear is used to detect precancerous and cancerous changes in cervical cells. After collecting the sample, immediate fixation is essential to preserve cellular morphology.

The smear must be fixed immediately after spreading the cells on the slide.

Standard fixative: 95% ethanol

Purpose:

| Function | Explanation

| -------- | -----------

| Prevent drying artifact | Maintains cell morphology

| Preserve nuclear details | Important for detecting dysplasia

| Improve staining quality | Essential for Pap stain

Delayed fixation causes:

• Nuclear distortion
• Poor staining
• Diagnostic errors.

The smear is stained using the Papanicolaou Stain.

It helps identify:

• Dysplasia
• Carcinoma in situ
• Cervical cancer.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: In a patient diagnosed with dysgerminoma of the ovary, which tumor marker is most likely to be elevated? (NEET PG 2015)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Serum Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH)

Dysgerminoma is the most common malignant germ cell tumor of the ovary and is the ovarian counterpart of seminoma in males. The tumor marker most commonly elevated in dysgerminoma is Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH)

Important tumor marker associations:

• Dysgerminoma → LDH (sometimes β-hCG mildly elevated)
• Yolk sac tumor → AFP
• Choriocarcinoma → β-hCG
• Epithelial ovarian tumors → CA-125

Clinical features of dysgerminoma:

• Occurs in adolescents and young women
• Rapidly enlarging pelvic mass
• Highly radiosensitive and chemosensitive
• Excellent prognosis with treatment

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: In the context of cervical cancer screening protocols, co-testing refers to performing which of the following diagnostic tests together?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. HPV testing + Pap smear

Cervical Cancer is strongly associated with persistent infection by high-risk HPV types.

The most common oncogenic types:

• HPV 16
• HPV 18

Co-testing means performing: HPV DNA Test + Pap Smear

• Together in the same screening visit.
• Purpose:

| Test | Detects

| ---- | -------

| Pap smear | Abnormal cervical cells

| HPV DNA test | High-risk HPV infection

Screening Recommendations

| Age group | Recommended test

| --------- | ----------------

| 21–29 years | Pap smear every 3 years

| 30–65 years | Co-testing (HPV + Pap) every 5 years

| Alternative | Pap smear every 3 years

Persistent infection with high-risk HPV causes:

HPV infection

↓

Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN)

↓

Carcinoma in situ

↓

Cervical cancer

Thus detecting HPV early improves screening accuracy.

B) VIA + Pap smear

Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid

Used in low-resource settings, not standard co-testing.

C) Antibody testing + Pap smear

Antibody testing does not detect cervical precancer.

D) HPV testing + VIA

Not a standard screening combination.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Point A in radiotherapy in carcinoma cervix marks the site for which of the following structures?
options: Crossing of ureter by uterine artery
Crossing of ureter by descending cervical artery
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Crossing of ureter by uterine artery

Point A in intracavitary brachytherapy for carcinoma cervix is located approximately 2 cm lateral and 2 cm superior to the external cervical os, and corresponds anatomically to the region where the uterine artery crosses the ureter.

• A. Obturator nodes: Not represented by Point A.
• B. Inguinal nodes: Not represented by Point A.
• C. Crossing of ureter by uterine artery — Correct
• D. Crossing of ureter by descending cervical artery: Not the standard anatomical correlate of Point A.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Reinke crystals are seen in which of the following gonadal tumours:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Leydig cell tumor

Reinke crystals are rod-shaped, eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions characteristic of Leydig cell tumors. They are composed of crystallized proteins related to steroidogenesis.

Leydig cell tumors arise from testicular interstitial cells and often produce androgens.

Seminoma, yolk sac tumor, and Sertoli cell tumor do not show Reinke crystals.

Because Leydig cells produce androgens, hormonal effects occur.

| Age group | Presentation

| --------- | ------------

| Children | Precocious puberty

| Adults | Gynecomastia or infertility

Gynecomastia occurs due to peripheral conversion of testosterone to estrogen.

| Tumor | Characteristic Feature

| ----- | ----------------------

| Leydig cell tumor | Reinke crystals

| Yolk sac tumor | Schiller–Duval bodies

| Granulosa cell tumor | Call–Exner bodies

| Dysgerminoma | Fried egg cells

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The commonest ovarian tumour seen during pregnancy is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Benign cystic teratoma

Benign cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst) is the most common ovarian tumor encountered during pregnancy. It is a benign germ cell tumor that often remains asymptomatic and is detected incidentally during routine antenatal ultrasonography. The major complication during pregnancy is ovarian torsion, particularly in the first trimester and early puerperium. It accounts for a significant proportion of persistent adnexal masses detected during pregnancy.

Why not the other options?

• B. Mucinous cystadenoma: A common benign epithelial ovarian tumor but less common than dermoid cyst during pregnancy.
• C. Endometrioma: Usually regresses during pregnancy because of decidualization and is less frequently encountered.
• D. Adenocarcinoma ovary: Malignant ovarian tumors are rare in pregnancy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The most common site for vulvar carcinoma is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Labia majora

The labia majora is the most common site of vulvar carcinoma, particularly squamous cell carcinoma.

• A. Labia minora: Less commonly involved.
• B. Labia majora — Correct: Most common site.
• C. Clitoris: Can be involved but is less common.
• D. Mons pubis: An uncommon primary site.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What are the characteristics of dermoid cyst? I. Germ cell ovarian tumour II. Bilateral in 15–20% cases III. Torsion is common IV. Rupture is common Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. I, II and III

A dermoid cyst (mature cystic teratoma) is the most common benign ovarian germ cell tumor, occurring predominantly in women of reproductive age (20–40 years). It arises from totipotent germ cells and contains tissues derived from all three germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm). The following statements are correct:

• I. Germ cell ovarian tumour: Dermoid cyst is a benign germ cell tumor and is the most common ovarian germ cell neoplasm.
• II. Bilateral in 15–20% cases: Approximately 10–20% of dermoid cysts are bilateral.
• III. Torsion is common: Ovarian torsion is the most common complication because the cyst is usually mobile and has a long pedicle.

Why is IV incorrect?

• IV. Rupture is common: Rupture is uncommon. When it occurs, it may cause chemical peritonitis due to spillage of sebaceous material, but it is much less common than torsion.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the antigen present in the recombinant HPV vaccine?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. L1

Recombinant HPV vaccines contain L1 capsid protein, which self-assembles into virus-like particles, generating strong immunity. HPV contains:

| Gene Type | Function

| --------- | --------

| Early genes (E1–E7) | Viral replication & oncogenesis
-  p53 inhibition
-  RB inhibition

| Late genes (L1, L2) | Structural capsid proteins

• L1 → Major capsid protein
•

L2 → Minor capsid protein

Human Papillomavirus Vaccine is made using recombinant DNA technology.

The vaccine contains: L1 protein virus-like particles (VLPs)

These VLPs:

•

Mimic the outer shell of the virus

• Do not contain viral DNA
• Cannot cause infection

They stimulate strong neutralizing antibody production.

| Vaccine | HPV Types Covered

| ------- | -----------------

| Bivalent (Cervarix) | 16, 18

| Quadrivalent (Gardasil) | 6, 11, 16, 18

| Nonavalent (Gardasil 9) | 6, 11, 16, 18, 31, 33, 45, 52, 58

High-risk HPV types 16 and 18 are responsible for most cases of Cervical Cancer.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following are favourable factors in prognosis of ovarian malignancy? 1. Older age group 2. Well-differentiated tumour 3. Smaller tumour volume 4. Absence of ascites Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 2, 3 and 4

The prognosis of ovarian malignancy depends on several factors, including stage at diagnosis, tumor grade, residual tumor after surgery, presence of ascites, histological subtype, and patient age. Patients diagnosed at an early stage, with well-differentiated tumors, small tumor burden, and no ascites have the best outcomes.

• 1. Older age group ✗

• Younger age is associated with a better prognosis because of better performance status, fewer comorbidities, and a higher likelihood of early-stage disease.

• 2. Well-differentiated tumour ✓

• Low-grade (well-differentiated) tumors are less aggressive, grow more slowly, and have a better survival rate.

• 3. Smaller tumour volume ✓

• Smaller tumor burden and minimal residual disease (<1 cm) after cytoreductive surgery are among the strongest predictors of improved survival.

• 4. Absence of ascites ✓

• Ascites is associated with advanced disease and peritoneal dissemination. Its absence indicates a more favorable prognosis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following are poor prognostic factors in endometrial adenocarcinoma? I. Estrogen and progesterone receptor positivity II. HER-2/neu gene expression III. Histologic types papillary serous or clear cell carcinoma IV. Aneuploid tumours Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. II, III and IV

Endometrial adenocarcinoma is the most common gynecological malignancy in developed countries. Prognosis depends on several clinicopathological factors, including stage, grade, histological subtype, depth of myometrial invasion, lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI), receptor status, and molecular markers. Poor prognostic factors are associated with aggressive tumor behavior, increased recurrence, and reduced survival. The following are poor prognostic factors:

• II. HER-2/neu gene expression: Overexpression of HER-2/neu is associated with high-grade tumors, aggressive disease, and poor prognosis, particularly in uterine serous carcinoma.
• III. Histologic types papillary serous or clear cell carcinoma: These are Type II endometrial carcinomas, which are high-grade, aggressive tumors with early extrauterine spread and poor prognosis.
• IV. Aneuploid tumors: DNA aneuploidy is associated with higher tumor grade, increased recurrence, and worse survival.

Why is I incorrect?

• I. Estrogen and progesterone receptor positivity: ER and PR positivity are favorable prognostic factors because they indicate:

• Better differentiation
• Better response to hormonal therapy
• Improved survival

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following are the characteristic features of Meigs’ syndrome in a female? 1. Right sided hydrothorax 2. Ascites 3. Genital warts 4. Fibroma ovary Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 2 and 4

Meigs’ syndrome is the triad of:

• Benign ovarian fibroma
• Ascites
• Pleural effusion (usually right-sided hydrothorax)

The ascites and pleural effusion resolve after surgical removal of the ovarian tumor.

Why are the statements correct/incorrect?

• 1. Right-sided hydrothorax: Correct. Pleural effusion is typically right-sided.
• 2. Ascites: Correct.
• 3. Genital warts: Incorrect. Unrelated to Meigs’ syndrome.
• 4. Fibroma ovary: Correct. The ovarian tumor is classically a fibroma (may also rarely be thecoma or Brenner tumor).

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is a risk factor for progression to borderline ovarian tumor?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Nulliparity

Borderline Ovarian Tumor are epithelial tumors that show cellular proliferation and atypia but no stromal invasion. They are also called tumors of low malignant potential (LMP).

Several reproductive factors increase the risk of epithelial ovarian tumors and borderline tumors.

| Risk factor | Reason

| ----------- | ------

| Nulliparity | More ovulatory cycles

| Early menarche | Increased ovulation

| Late menopause | Prolonged estrogen exposure

| Infertility | Hormonal imbalance

| Protective factor | Mechanism

| ----------------- | ---------

| OCP use | Suppresses ovulation

| Pregnancy | Anovulation

| Breastfeeding | Reduced ovulatory cycles

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is a virilizing ovarian tumor?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Arrhenoblastoma

Arrhenoblastoma is another name for a Sertoli-Leydig Cell Tumor, which produces androgens, leading to virilization. This tumor arises from sex cord–stromal cells of the ovary.

Hormone produced- Testosterone (androgens)

Effects

| Clinical feature | Reason

| ---------------- | ------

| Hirsutism | Increased androgens

| Deepening of voice | Virilization

| Clitoromegaly | Androgen effect

| Amenorrhea | Suppression of estrogen

Other Ovarian Tumors and Hormones

| Tumor | Hormone produced | Effect

| ----- | ---------------- | ------

| Granulosa cell tumor | Estrogen | Feminization

| Theca cell tumor | Estrogen | Postmenopausal bleeding

| Arrhenoblastoma | Androgens | Virilization

A) Brenner tumor

Brenner Tumor

• Usually benign epithelial tumor
• May produce estrogen
• Does not cause virilization.

C) Carcinoid tumor of ovary

Ovarian Carcinoid Tumor

• Produces serotonin
• Causes carcinoid syndrome, not virilization.

D) Theca cell tumor

Thecoma

• Produces estrogen
• Leads to postmenopausal bleeding.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is not classified as a germ cell tumor of the ovary?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Granulosa cell tumor

Classification of Ovarian Tumors

Ovarian tumors are broadly classified into three main categories.

| Tumor Type | Origin | Examples

| ---------- | ------ | --------

| Epithelial tumors | Surface epithelium | Serous, mucinous

| Germ cell tumors | Primordial germ cells | Dysgerminoma, yolk sac tumor

| Sex cord–stromal tumors | Ovarian stroma | Granulosa cell tumor

Image- yolk sac tumor

Germ cell tumors arise from primitive germ cells of the ovary and usually occur in young women.

Common germ cell tumors

| Tumor | Tumor Marker | Key Feature

| ----- | ------------ | -----------

| Dysgerminoma | LDH | Most common malignant GCT

| Yolk sac tumor | AFP | Schiller–Duval bodies

| Choriocarcinoma | β-hCG | Trophoblastic tumor

| Teratoma | None / AFP | Mature tissues

Image- granulosa cell tumor

Granulosa Cell Tumor is a sex cord–stromal tumor.

Key features

| Feature | Description

| ------- | -----------

| Tumor marker | Inhibin

| Hormone produced | Estrogen

| Histology | Call–Exner bodies

| Nuclei | Coffee-bean appearance

These tumors often cause hormonal manifestations, such as:

• Precocious puberty (children)
• Menstrual irregularities
• Postmenopausal bleeding

Ovarian Tumor Markers

| Tumor | Marker

| ----- | ------

| Dysgerminoma | LDH

| Yolk sac tumor | AFP

| Choriocarcinoma | β-hCG

| Granulosa cell tumor | Inhibin

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of steps for performing a Pap smear? 1. Lithotomy position 2. Per speculum examination 3. Per vaginal examination 4. Take sample with Ayre's spatula
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 2, 4

Steps:

1. Lithotomy position

· Patient lies with hips flexed and abducted.

· Allows proper visualization of the cervix.

1. Per speculum examination

· A Cusco’s speculum is inserted.

· Cervix and transformation zone are visualized.

1.

Take sample with Ayre's spatula

2.

Use Ayre’s spatula or cytobrush.

3. Rotate 360° around the squamocolumnar junction.

The sample is then:

• Spread on a glass slide or placed in liquid-based cytology medium
• Fixed with alcohol and sent for cytological examination.

Per vaginal examination is not done before collecting the Pap smear sample, because it may contaminate or remove cervical cells, reducing diagnostic accuracy.

Pap smear specifically targets the transformation zone, where:

• Squamous epithelium meets columnar epithelium
• Most HPV infections and cervical cancers originate

Squamocolumnar junction = most common site for cervical carcinoma.

Per Vaginal Examination is Not Done Before Pap Smear

If per vaginal (PV) examination is performed first:

• Cervical cells may be dislodged
• Cytology sample becomes inadequate
• Results may be false negative

Therefore PV examination is done after Pap smear if needed.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which one of the following states the diagnostic criteria for postmolar gestational trophoblastic neoplasia?
options: A rise of hCG levels of more than 10% for >3 values over 2 weeks’ time
A rise of hCG levels of more than 5% for >4 values over 2 weeks’ time
A rise of hCG levels of more than 15% for >3 values over 2 weeks’ time
A rise of hCG levels of more than 10% for >3 values over 4 weeks’ time
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. A rise of hCG levels of more than 10% for >3 values over 2 weeks’ time

Postmolar gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) is diagnosed when serial β-hCG measurements demonstrate a rising plateau/persistent pattern after evacuation of a molar pregnancy.

FIGO criterion for a rise in hCG (as clarified in the 2026 FIGO GTN staging update):

• An increase in β-hCG of >10% across three consecutive weekly measurements, over a period of at least 2 weeks (i.e., days 1, 7, 14).

The companion criterion (plateau) was also restated in 2026:

• A plateau in hCG, defined as a change of less than 10% (rise or fall) across four measurements over a period of at least 3 weeks (i.e. days 1, 7, 14, 21) — this also satisfies the definition of GTN.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which strain of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is most commonly linked to the development of cervical cancer?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 16, 18

Persistent infection with high-risk HPV types leads to cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) and eventually cervical carcinoma.

The two most important oncogenic strains are:

• HPV 16
• HPV 18

Together they cause \~70% of cervical cancers worldwide.

High-risk HPV strains produce two key oncogenic proteins:

| Viral Protein | Target | Effect

| ------------- | ------ | ------

| E6 | p53 tumor suppressor | Inhibits apoptosis

| E7 | Rb tumor suppressor | Uncontrolled cell cycle

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 17-year-old girl was brought by her mother to the outpatient department with primary amenorrhea. She had normal breast development and pubic hair. On examination, the vagina was blind-ending and the uterus was not palpable. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Mullerian agenesis

The given clinical scenario of a girl with primary amenorrhea, normal breasts, and pubic hair, with a blind-ending vagina and uterus not palpable, is suggestive of Mullerian agenesis.

Absent uterus and vagina in a person with female genotype and phenotype are features of Mullerian agenesis, also known as Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser syndrome.

Ovaries are normal and secondary sexual characters are well developed with normal external genitalia. This condition is associated with anomalies of the spine/skeleton and the kidneys along with the urinary tract.

Diagnosis is made with the help of pelvic sonography, MRI, and laparoscopy. Patients may have rudimentary Mullerian bulbs without an endometrial cavity. These should be surgically excised if they are symptomatic.

Other options:

Option B: Gonadal dysgenesis patients present with primary amenorrhoea, absence of secondary sex characters (poorly developed breasts), and female external genitalia.

Option C: In Turner syndrome, short stature with poor development of secondary sexual characters and short stature will be seen. It has a karyotype of 45 XO. Barr body will be absent. Female genital organs (vagina, uterus, fallopian tubes, ovaries) are present. The ovaries, though present, are atrophic.

Option D: Testicular feminization syndrome also known as androgen insensitivity syndrome has a karyotype of 46XY. Secondary sexual characters like the development of axillary hair and pubic hair are absent in these females. However, breast development is adequate due to the conversion of androgen into estrogen during puberty.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 24-year-old female presents with complaints of foul-smelling vaginal discharge. Wet smear of the discharge is shown below. Drug of choice to treat this condition is_____
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Metronidazole

A female patient presenting with foul-smelling vaginal discharge and a wet smear showing clue cells points to a diagnosis of bacterial vaginosis, and the drug of choice is metronidazole.

Bacterial vaginosis is a polymicrobial infection caused by Mobiluncus curtisii, Gardnerella vaginalis, Mycoplasma hominis, and Haemophilus vaginalis. It has a foul-smelling (fishy smell) vaginal discharge with minimal vulval irritation.

Amsel's criteria is helpful in diagnosing bacterial vaginosis when 3 of the following 4 are present:

• Thin, white homogenous vaginal discharge
• A pH of vaginal fluid >4.5
• Fishy odor of discharge accentuated by adding 10% KOH-Whiff test
• Presence of clue cells on microscopy: Clue cells are epithelial cells with a fuzzy border or granular cytoplasm caused by small gram-negative bacilli adhering to their surface

Treatment is oral metronidazole 500 mg BD for 7 days.

The image below shows clue cells:

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 26-year-old woman who has had 2 children through normal delivery presents with a dull aching pain over the abdomen, with irregular menses. Per vaginal examination revealed a mass felt through the posterior fornix. A USG showed a clear ovarian cyst of size 5 x 5 cm. What is the next best step?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Follow up after 6 weeks

A clear ovarian cyst with size less than 7 cm in a woman of reproductive age group is most likely to be a functional ovarian cyst. The next best step in the management of this case is to follow up after 6–12 weeks and perform a repeat USG.

A simple unilocular cyst under 7 cm is often a functional cyst and should be observed. Most functional cysts resolve spontaneously within 4-6 months. A follow-up ultrasound will detect any persistent cyst, which may necessitate laparoscopic evaluation. To expedite resolution or to treat symptoms like pain and irregular menses, oral combined pills may be prescribed for 3-4 months in women of reproductive age.

Features of a functional cyst:

• Related to temporary hormonal variation
• Benign and rarely become complicated
• Usually 6–8 cm in diameter
• Usually asymptomatic
• Unilocular
• Contains clear fluid, unless hemorrhage occurs
• Lining epithelium corresponds to the functional epithelium of the unit from which they arise

Management of functional cysts in women of child-bearing age group is summarized in the flowchart attached below.

Other options:

Option A: Tumour markers such as CA-125 and CEA are particulary useful in postmenopausal women suspected of having a malignant epithelial cell tumor.

Option C: If the cyst does not resolve spontaneoulsy it can be removed laparoscopically or by laparotomy.

Option D: Imaging modalities such as CT scan and MRI help to detect ovarian neoplasms and assist in staging of ovarian cancers.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 62-year-old patient with a history of diabetes and hypertension came with post-menopausal bleeding. Which of the following you will do to evaluate the cause?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Endometrial sampling

Endometrial sampling is done to evaluate a patient presenting with postmenopausal bleeding.

Postmenopausal bleeding is defined as any bleeding from the genital tract after 12 months of menopause in a woman not on hormone replacement. Any vaginal bleeding occurring after 6 months of amenorrhea in a menopausal woman should also be considered as postmenopausal bleeding and investigated. All postmenopausal women with unexpected uterine bleeding should be evaluated for endometrial malignancy since age is a significant risk factor for this.

Transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) is a better first-line investigation. Since TVS is not included in the options, endometrial sampling is the next best answer.

Endometrial sampling is indicated if:

• The endometrial thickness is >4 mm
• The endometrium shows diffuse or focal increased echogenicity (heterogeneity)
• The endometrium is not adequately visualized on transvaginal sonography
• The woman has persistent bleeding, as it can be a sign of endometrial cancer even when the endometrial thickness is less than 4mm.

The image below gives a summary of the evaluation of postmenopausal bleeding, as per the FOGSI guidelines.

Other options:

Option A: Pap smear should be offered to all women above the age of 21 years who are sexually active for at least 3 years. Colposcopic examination and selective biopsy are considered in patients with abnormal Pap smears.

Option B: Visual inspection with iodine is done where the facilities for Pap screening do not exist. This involves painting the cervix with Lugol's iodine. It is used to detect any abnormal cytology in the cervix and vagina, such as in cases of carcinoma cervix.

The normal vaginal and cervical epithelium contains glycogen, therefore stains mahogany brown on being painted with Lugol's iodine. The abnormal cells remain unstained. These areas need to be biopsied and sent for histopathological examination.

Option C: The colposcopic study is challenging in postmenopausal women because of narrow vaginas, senile vaginitis, indrawn and poorly visible squamocolumnar junction, and atrophic cervix.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text:
A couple presents to the infertility clinic with a normal hysterosalpingogram and a semen analysis report with azoospermia. Which of the following is the next best test to differentiate between an obstructive and a testicular cause of azoospermia?

FSH- Follicle-stimulating hormone, LH- Luteinizing hormone
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Serum FSH levels

Serum FSH level is the next best test to differentiate between an obstructive and a testicular cause of azoospermia. FSH is the main hormone stimulating the production of sperm in the testis and has the highest specificity and sensitivity among hormonal assays while differentiating between obstructive and non-obstructive azoospermia.

The absence of sperm in semen is known as azoospermia. It can be due to:

• Pre-testicular azoospermia due to a hypothalamic or pituitary abnormality (hypogonadotropic-hypogonadism)
• Testicular failure or non-obstructive azoospermia
• Post-testicular obstruction implies normal spermatogenesis but failure to deliver the sperm into the ejaculate because of ductal obstruction.

The algorithm for differentiating the causes of normal semen volume azoospermia is as follows:

• A low FSH level indicates pituitary or hypothalamic failure
• A high FSH level denotes primary gonadal failure or testicular cause
• A normal FSH level could be due to either non-obstructive or obstructive azoospermia. A testicular biopsy is usually required in such people to provide a definitive diagnosis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A doctor tells a 31-year-old woman, who is 20 weeks pregnant, that her baby has a developmental defect. She has come to you for a second opinion. The following USG finding is seen. Identify the defect.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Anencephaly

The given ultrasound image shows an open defect in the calvaria and skin leading to the exposure of the cranial neural tube. This is consistent with the diagnosis of anencephaly.

Anencephaly results from incomplete closure of the neural tube. It is one of the earliest detectable congenital defects that can be detected as early as 10 to 11 weeks of gestation.  Screening can also be done by serum estimation of maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein (MSAFP). The following are the radiological signs seen in anencephaly.

• Frog eye sign - Absence of cranial calvaria, prominent orbits thereby resembling the face of a frog.
• Shower cap sign - The absence of the cranium could lead to the protrusion of a disorganized mass of brain tissue. This resembles a shower cap giving rise to a characteristic triangular facial appearance.

Many neural-tube defects can be prevented with preconceptional supplementation of folic acid. A dose of 4 mg daily is recommended in subsequent pregnancies.

Other options:

Option B: Omphalocele is a midline anterior abdominal wall defect through which the solid abdominal viscera and/or bowel may herniate. The extruded abdominal contents are covered in a sac. These are due to the persistence of physiological herniation of the gut or as a part of the OEIS complex (omphalocele, exstrophy, imperforate anus, and spinal abnormality) and cloacal exstrophy. The ‘elephant’s trunk’ sign on ultrasound, due to the prolapsed terminal ileum is said to be pathognomonic for cloacal exstrophy of the OEIS complex.

The first image below shows a patient with cloacal exstrophy showing the elephant trunk sign representing the intussuscepted ileum. The second image shows omphalocele while the third image shows gastroschisis (a close differential diagnosis for omphalocele). The fourth image demonstrates an ultrasound image of the fetus suggestive of an omphalocele (asterix)

Option C: Cystic hygroma is a congenital multiloculated lymphatic lesion that is classically found in the left posterior triangle of the neck. It occurs as a result of sequestration or obstruction of developing lymph vessels. It must be carefully differentiated from nuchal translucency (NT) as both may appear similar. This defect can be picked up in a first-trimester ultrasound.

The image below shows a newborn with cystic Hygroma on the right side of the neck and cystic hygroma of the neck in the fetus.

Option D: Encephalocele is caused due to defects in the skull through which the meninges and/or neural tissue herniate. The squamous part of the occipital bone is the most frequently affected bone. In meningoencephalocele or occult spina bifida with Chiari malformations, the scalloping of the frontal bones is observed in the ultrasound as the lemon sign while anterior curvature of the cerebellum with effacement of the cisterna magna in the posterior fossa forms the banana sign.

The image shows a newborn with encephalocele. The second and third images below show the banana and the lemon sign respectively.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A female patient having frothy vaginal discharge was found to have a strawberry cervix. Which of the following is the drug of choice?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Metronidazole

The given clinical scenario of frothy vaginal discharge and strawberry cervix is suggestive of trichomoniasis and metronidazole is the drug of choice for the treatment.

Trichomonas vaginalis is one of the most common causes of vaginal discharge. It is transmitted by sexual intercourse, with an incubation period of 4–21 days. The clinical features include vaginal discharge which is profuse, thin, slightly green in colour, and frothy.  It may be associated with vaginal irritation, pruritus, dysuria, and increased frequency. Cervical inflammation with punctate hemorrhagic spots known as the strawberry cervix is typically seen. Motile trichomonads are seen on wet mount examination.

The below image shows the strawberry cervix seen in trichomoniasis.

Administration of metronidazole 2 g orally in a single dose or 500 mg 2 times/day for 7 days is the standard treatment. It should be taken at night and after meals to avoid vomiting. If this too causes vomiting, or in resistant cases an alternate regimen is to be considered. Both the partners need to be treated simultaneously to avoid recurrence.

The alternative regimen includes tinidazole 500 mg orally twice a day for 7 days or secnidazole in a single dose of 1000 mg daily for 2 days. The use of tinidazole is not recommended during pregnancy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text:
A pregnant woman at 36 weeks gestation is found to have high blood pressure recording and a urine protein of 3+. Concomitant presence of which of the following symptoms would make you suspect imminent eclampsia?

1. Headache
2. Blurred vision
3. Persistent pedal oedema
4. Epigastric pain
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 2, 3, 4

The clinical case of a pregnant women at 36 weeks of gestation with hypertension and proteinuria points to a diagnosis of pre-eclampsia. Certain symptoms if present might suggest impending eclampsia. These include 1, 2, 3, 4.

Pre-eclampsia is defined as hypertension with blood pressure ≥140/90 mm Hg along with proteinuria that develops after 20 weeks of gestation in a previously normotensive and non-proteinuric woman. Preeclampsia when complicated with generalized tonicclonic convulsions and/or coma is called eclampsia.

Ominous symptoms of impending eclampsia:

• Headaches - usually over the occipital or frontal region
• Visual disturbances - These could include scotomas. These are due to spasm of retinal vessels following retinal infarction, occipital lobe damage secondary to vasogenic edema, or retinal detachment.
• Epigastric or right upper quadrant pain. This is due to hepatocellular necrosis, ischemia, and edema that stretches the Glisson capsule. This is usually seen along with elevated serum hepatic transaminase levels.
• Sudden and generalized or persistent edema may indicate imminent eclampsia. Visible edema over the ankles despite rest, especially on rising from the bed in the morning hours is pathological.
• Disturbed sleep
• Diminished urinary output - less than 400 mL in 24 hours is considered a poor sign ominous

Other symptoms include:

• Renal or cardiac involvement
• Obvious fetal-growth restriction
• Thrombocytopenia - usually due to microangiopathic hemolysis.

It is essential that the patient should be warned and educated against these symptoms. The presence of these symptoms may warn the obstetrician and possibly avert the progression into eclampsia.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A primigravida in her 10th week of gestation presents with spotting. On examination, the uterus corresponds to 12 weeks. Transvaginal ultrasound was done and it is given below. What is your diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Hydatidiform mole

The given clinical scenario of a primigravida with spotting and an ultrasound showing a characteristic snowstorm appearance (anechoic cystic spaces) is suggestive of a hydatidiform mole (complete mole). It refers to an echogenic uterine mass that has numerous anechoic cystic spaces.

Hydatiform mole belongs to the benign group of gestational trophoblastic diseases (GTD). It is an abnormality in chorionic villi making them partly proliferative and degenerative, thereby resulting in the formation of multiple small cysts. Based on the portion of the chorionic villi involved, they could be complete (diffused) or partial (focal)

The classical clinical features of a complete mole are:

• Abnormal vaginal bleeding -Most common (90%)
• Lower abdominal pain
• Hyperemesis gravidarum due to increased β-hCG
• Features of early-onset preeclampsia
• Uterus appears large for date
• Absent fetal parts and FHS
• Expulsion of vesicular tissues (grape-like vesicles)
• Theca lutein cyst of ovaries of more than 6 cm
• Hyperthyroidism (rare)
• Serum hCG > 100,000 mIU/ml
• USG - snowstorm appearance

The definitive management after diagnosis is suction and evacuation, after making the cervix favorable. Follow-up of the patients with serial hCG values is crucial.

Prophylactic chemotherapy can be started on high-risk women (WHO prognostic score > 7) with methotrexate 1mg/kg/day intramuscular/intravenous on days 1, 3, 5, and 7. Patients are also advised to not get pregnant for at least a year.

Other options:

Option A: Blighted ovum (silent miscarriage) occurs when a fertilized egg implants in the uterus but doesn't develop into an embryo. It is a sonographic diagnosis where there is an absence of a fetal pole in a gestational sac with a diameter of 3 cm or more.

Option B: Missed abortion is when the fetus is dead and retained inside the uterus for a variable period. USG shows an empty sac early in the pregnancy or the absence of fetal cardiac activity and fetal movements.

Option C: Ectopic pregnancy is one in which the fertilized ovum is implanted and develops outside the normal endometrial cavity. The majority of ectopic pregnancies occur in the fallopian tube, the ampulla being the most common site.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A primigravida is in labour. Her per-vaginal examination revealed a posterior cervix with 5 cm cervical length, 1 cm dilatation, soft consistency, and head at -1 station. Calculate the modified Bishop score.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 5

The Modified Bishop score of the given patient is calculated to be 5.

From the data given in the question:

• The position of the cervix is posterior, hence score = 0
• Cervical length is 5 cm, hence score = 0
• Cervical dilatation is 1 cm, hence score = 1
• Consistency of cervix is soft, hence score = 2
• The station of the head is –1, hence score = 2

Hence, the Modified Bishop score is 0+0+1+2+2 = 5.

The Bishop score is a scoring system used to assess labor induction outcomes. It is based on the station of the head, dilation, effacement (or length), position, and consistency of the cervix noted by doing a vaginal examination.

According to the NICE guidelines, a score of >/=6 is considered favorable.

According to Williams Obstetrics 26th edition, a score >/=9 is considered favorable.

Note: In the modified Bishop score (1991) the effacement is replaced by the cervical length in cm.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text:
A teenage girl presented with irregular cycles and increased facial hair. Her ovaries showed increased volume. Which of the following are used in the first line treatment?

1. Laparoscopic ovarian drilling
2. Anti-androgens
3. Lifestyle modifications
4. Combined oral contraceptive pills
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 2,3,4

This patient's irregular menstrual cycles, increased facial hair (signifying clinical hyperandrogenism), and increased ovarian volume are suggestive of polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS). Anti-androgens, lifestyle modifications, and combined oral contraceptives (2, 3, and 4) constitue first-line treatment modalities for this condition. Laparoscopic drilling is a surgical procedure done when medical therapy fails.

PCOS is an endocrinopathy seen in women of reproductive age, affecting multiple systems. Rotterdam criteria is used to diagnose PCOD. The presence of two of the three components of this criteria establishes the diagnosis:

• Oligo/amenorrhoea, anovulation, infertility
• Hirsutism/acne
• Ultrasound findings:

• Enlarged ovaries with ovarian volume will be more than 10 mm3
• 12 or more small follicles each of 2-9 mm in size placed peripherally

Ultrasound image given below shows an enlarged ovary seen in PCOS with multiple follicles in the periphery.

Treatment of PCOD:

• Weight reduction alone is beneficial in mild hirsutism.
• Lifestyle changes, such as smoking cessation, are recommended.
• Fourth-generation oral contraceptive pills (OCP) containing ethinyl estradiol and drospirenone are used for treating menstrual abnormalities, reducing acne, and hirsutism.
• OCP with cyproterone acetate is prescribed for PCOS patients with hirsutism.
• Patients with PCOD are prone to developing insulin resistance, which can be controlled with metformin. Acarbosecan be used as an alternative if metformin is contraindicated.
• Infertility in PCOD patients is treated with clomiphene as the first-line drug for inducing ovulation. Dexamethasone is used in combination to improve fertility rates. Letrozole is used off-label in clomiphene-resistant cases.

Surgical options include laparoscopic ovarian drilling or puncture of not more than four cysts in each ovary. This is done either by laser or by unipolar electrocautery. It restores endocrine levels and improves fertility. Surgery is indicated only if:

• Medical therapy fails
• Hyperstimulation occurs
• Infertile women
• Previous pregnancy losses

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text:
According to IADPSG, what is the cut-off value of fasting blood glucose for the diagnosis of gestational diabetes mellitus?

IADPSG- International Association of Diabetes and Pregnancy Study Group
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. >92 mg/dL

According to IADPSG, the cut-off value of fasting blood glucose for the diagnosis of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is >92 mg/dL.

Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) refers to any degree of glucose intolerance having its onset or first recognition during pregnancy.

For IADPSG criteria, an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) is done in the fasting state using 75 g of glucose, and GDM is diagnosed if any one of the following cut-offs is met i.e.

• Fasting: >92 mg/dL
• 1hour: >180 mg/dL
• 2 hr: >153 mg/dL

Earlier, a two-step approach was being used to diagnose GDM. In this, the first step (screening) is a 50-gram one-hour glucose challenge test (GCT). The patients having a positive result of >140mg/dl, are candidates for the OGTT. A 100-gram, three-hour OGTT is the diagnostic test for GDM. GDM is diagnosed if two or more values are positive, as follows.

Time
Carpenter and Coustan
NDDG

Fasting
95 mg/dL
105 mg/dL

1 hour
180 mg/dL
190 mg/dL

2 hour
155 mg/dL
165 mg/dL

3 hour
140 mg/dL
145 mg/dL

This has now been replaced by the one-step approach that omits the screening test and simplifies diagnostic testing by performing only a 75-gram, two-hour oral GTT.

Some complications of GDM:

• Maternal

• Hypertension, preeclampsia
• Hydramnios
• Increased operative interventions
• Future development of diabetes mellitus

• Fetal and neonatal

• Fetal macrosomia
• Congenital anomalies
• Metabolic abnormalities such as hypocalcemia, hypomagnesemia, hyperbilirubinemia, and neonatal hypoglycemia.
• Respiratory distress syndrome
• Subsequent childhood and adolescent obesity

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: An 18-year-old girl presented with amenorrhoea. On examination, she had normal genitalia & normal breast development. Her tests reveal a 5 alpha-reductase deficiency. What could be the probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Male pseudohermaphroditism

A girl presenting with amenorrhea, normal female external genitalia and breasts with 5 alpha-reductase deficiency is suggestive of male pseudohermaphroditism.

In pseudohermaphroditism, the sex glands are of a certain sex while the external genitalia is of the opposite sex.

Male pseudohermaphroditism or male intersex is an association of male gonads (XY genotype) with female external genitalia. The production of testosterone from the testes requires 5 alpha-reductase. This enzyme converts testosterone into DHT (dihydrotestosterone), which is capable of acting on peripheral target tissues to produce the male phenotype. The absence of this enzyme results in failure of the testis to descend to the scrotum and ill development of the penis, thereby resulting in the female phenotype. Many individuals develop their attitudes and psyche according to their sex of rearing (as a female). Rehabilitation to their gender roles is the best line of management.

Other options:

Option A: Concealed sex refers to the deliberate concealment of sex usually done by criminals by changing clothes or by other methods to avoid detection. This can be detected by physical examination.

Option B: In true hermaphroditism the glands of both the sexes are present in the same individual. Such cases are very rare. In most cases, the accessory sex gland is atrophic and lacks functional activity.

Option C: Female pseudohermaphrodites are genetic females (XX genotype) with male/ambiguous external genitalia due to the deficiency of 21 alpha-hydroxylase enzymes resulting in an excess of androgens. This causes clitoromegaly resembling the penis,and the fused labioscrotal folds resemble a rudimentary scrotum. Management includes administration of steroids to control excess ACTH, estrogen to confer the secondary sexual characteristics, and surgical restoration of the external genitalia to a feminine pattern.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text:
Arrange the following in sequential order with regards to the steps of collection of samples for pap smear testing:

1. Use posterior vaginal wall retractor
2. Take the sample
3. Make smear on a slide
4. Fix the smear
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 2, 3, 4

The correct sequence of the procedure involved in the collection of a sample for a pap smear is 1, 2, 3, 4.

The Pap/Papanicolaou smear is used for screening cervical neoplasia.

Procedure:

• The patient is put in a dorsal position & the labia are separated.
• Cusco’s self-retaining speculum is introduced/posterior vaginal wall retractor is used
• The squamocolumnar junction is identified and scraped with Ayre’s spatula.
• Endocervix is scraped with a cytobrush.
• Samples are spread separately on 2 different glass slides.
• The slide is immediately fixed using 95% ethyl alcohol.
• Stained with Pap stain or Short stain.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Asherman syndrome is most commonly associated with
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Hypomenorrhea

Among the given options, Asherman syndrome is most commonly associated with hypomenorrhea.

Asherman syndrome is the presence of uterine synechiae, due to the destruction of the endometrium. It can occur as a result of trauma to the endometrium following vigorous curettages such as incomplete abortion, postpartum hemorrhage, and elective abortion. Damage may also result from other uterine surgery such as metroplasty, myomectomy.

They usually present with menstrual abnormalities, infertility, recurrent pregnancy loss due to inadequate placentation. Menstrual abnormalities, including hypomenorrhea and amenorrhea, remain the most common clinical features associated with Asherman syndrome. Dysmenorrhea is occasionally present.

The diagnosis is confirmed with hysterosalpingography.

Management includes hysteroscopy, which enables adhesiolysis. Recurrence of adhesions is prevented by insertion of IUCD for 3 months and giving estrogen cyclically (21 days) for 3 months to develop endometrium.

Note:

Amenorrhea indicates the complete absence of menstruation.

Oligomenorrhoea is the term used to describe infrequent and irregular menses. In this condition, the cycle length is prolonged without affecting the duration and amount of flow.

Hypomenorrhoea refers to the condition in which the cycle length remains unaltered, however the duration of bleeding or the amount of blood loss, or both are substantially reduced.

Menorrhagia denotes excessive blood loss (increase in the duration and /or amount of bleeding) without any change in the cycle length.

Dysmenorrhoea is defined as cramping pain accompanying menstruation.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Identify the instrument given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Cusco’s speculum

The instrument shown in the image is Cusco’s speculum.

Cusco’s speculum is a self-retaining bivalve speculum used for visualisation of the cervix, vaginal fornices and for performing pap smear.

Other options:

Option B: Sims' speculum is used for the assessment of rectocele and cystocele. The speculum is applied against the vaginal wall and slowly retracted out until a bulge appears, indicating cystocele or rectocele.  It can also be used for visualization of the vaginal walls.

Option C: A surgeon uses a lubricated proctoscope to visualize lesions in the anus, anorectal junction, and lower rectum. It is done as an OPD procedure to detect hemorrhoids, polyps, or ulcers.

Option D: Doyen's retractor is used to retract the abdominal wall as well as the bladder to facilitate better exposure of the lower uterine segment during cesarian operation. It is also used to pull back the soft tissues to widen the surgical field during laparotomy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text:
Match the following :

Section A
Section B

1. Yolk sac tumor
A. LDH

2. Dysgerminoma
B. Beta-hCG

3. Choriocarcinoma
C. AFP

4. Epithelial cell tumor
D. CA-125

LDH - Lactate dehydrogenase

HCG - Human chorionic gonadotropin

AFP - Alpha fetoprotein
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1-C, 2-A, 3-B, 4-D

Option B represents the correct answer. 1-C, 2-A, 3-B, 4-D

Ovarian tumors
Tumor marker

1. Yolk sac tumor
C. AFP

2. Dysgerminoma
A. LDH

3. Choriocarcinoma
B. Beta-HCG

4. Epithelial cell tumor
D. Ca-125

Endodermal sinus tumor/yolk sac tumor is a type of ovarian germ cell tumor that is seen in premenarchal girls. Schiller-Duval bodies are pathognomonic on histopathology. Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is commonly produced by this tumor and is used as a tumor marker.

Dysgerminona is a type of germ cell tumor and it corresponds to the seminoma of the testis. It does not secrete either male or female sex hormones. It secretes placental alkaline phosphatase (ALP), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), and β-hCG. Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) is usually used in monitoring individuals or disease recurrence.

Choriocarcinoma is a type of mixed germ cell tumor. It is highly vascular. Histologically, the tumor shows syncytiotrophoblasts and cytotrophoblasts. It secretes large quantities of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) hormone, which is used as a tumor marker in the diagnosis and management of the tumor.

Malignant epithelial cell tumors of the ovary secrete CA-125. It is a glycoprotein and surface cell antigen which is secreted by malignant epithelial tumors of the ovary. A level of more than 35 U/mL suggests a malignant and residual tumor and indicates the need for chemotherapy. CA-125 is also raised in abdominal tuberculosis and endometriosis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text:
Match the following disorders causing secondary amenorrhoea with their respective lab findings.

Condition
Lab markers

1. Sheehan's syndrome
A. Normal FSH, Normal LH, Normal estradiol

2. Premature Ovarian failure
B. High LH, Low FSH, Low estradiol

3. PCOS
C. Low LH, Low FSH, Low estradiol

4. Asherman's syndrome
D. High LH, High FSH, Low estradiol
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1-C, 2-D, 3-B, 4-A

The correct answer is 1-C, 2-D, 3-B, 4-A.

Condition
Lab markers

1. Sheehan's syndrome
C. Low LH, Low FSH, Low estradiol

2. Premature Ovarian failure
D. High LH, High FSH, Low estradiol

3. PCOS
B. High LH, Low FSH, Low estradiol

4. Asherman's syndrome
A. Normal FSH, Normal LH, Normal estradiol

Secondary amenorrhoea is the absence of menses for more than three months in girls or women who previously had regular menstrual cycles or six months in girls or women who had irregular menses.

Premature Ovarian failure or premature menopause is the development of menopause before the age of 40 years. It is diagnosed when at least 2 serum FSH levels are elevated (>40 mIU/l) when measured at least 1 month apart in a woman <40 years. The other findings consistent with POF include low estradiol and an elevated FSH/LH ratio.

Asherman's syndrome is the presence of uterine synechiae, due to the destruction of large areas of the endometrium, most commonly as a result of trauma to the endometrium following pregnancy-related curettages. Oligomenorrhoea, amenorrhoea, dysmenorrhoea, abortion, and infertility are seen with uterine synechiae. The laboratory investigations and hormonal assays are generally normal in isolated cases of uterine synechiae. Diagnosis is generally established using hysteroscopy. Moth-eaten appearance on hysterosalpingography suggests a diagnosis of Asherman syndrome. Treatment is by hysteroscopic adhesiolysis.

PCOS is a multisystem, metabolic, endocrine dysfunction that commonly occurs among women in the reproductive age group. The endocrinological changes reflecting in the assays are summarized in the pearl attached below.

Sheehan's syndrome/ pituitary apoplexy is hemorrhagic infarction of large pituitary adenomas or pituitary infarction due to traumatic major blood loss. If this blood loss occurs during delivery, it's called Sheehan's syndrome. Affected women may present with panhypopituitarism and may have persistent hypotension, tachycardia, hypoglycemia, and lactation failure. The most prominent among symptoms are lactation failure (due to deficiency of prolactin) and postpartum amenorrhea (due to deficiency of gonadotropins).

Note: Estradiol level in PCOS is low in comparison to Estrone (E1).
