• Sacrocotyloid diameter → smallest diameter of the true pelvis

| Diameter | Measurement

| -------- | -----------

| Interspinous (bispinous) | 10.5 cm

| Diagonal conjugate | 12.5 cm

| True (obstetric) conjugate | 10 cm

| Obstetric conjugate | 10 cm

| Sacrocotyloid diameter | 9–9.5 cm ← smallest

Sacrocotyloid diameter = distance from sacral promontory → iliopectineal eminence (cotyloid notch) bilaterally

• Represents the posterior sagittal diameter of the pelvic brim
• At 9–9.5 cm, it is the smallest diameter of the true pelvis
• Clinically significant in flat/platypelloid pelvis — head engagement affected

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following vertex positions is the least common during childbirth? (NEET PG 2015)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Left Occipitoposterior (LOP)

The most common fetal vertex position during labor is occipitoanterior, especially Left Occipitoanterior (LOA), because the left oblique diameter of the maternal pelvis is slightly larger and better accommodates fetal descent.

Frequency of vertex positions:

• LOA → most common
• ROA → common
• Occipitoposterior positions → less common
• Left Occipitoposterior (LOP) → least common

Occipitoposterior positions are associated with:

• Prolonged labor
• Increased back pain (“back labor”)
• Higher risk of instrumental delivery or cesarean section

Thus, LOP is considered the least common vertex position during childbirth.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 30-year-old female patient, on treatment for infertility, came with 6 weeks of amenorrhea, abdominal pain, and mild vaginal bleeding. Her beta hCG level was 2800 mlU/mL. On ultrasound, a 3cm mass was seen in the left adnexa. It contained a gestational sac with no fetal cardiac activity. What is the most appropriate management for this patient? (NEET PG 2021)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Single dose methotrexate

This patient has an unruptured ectopic pregnancy, suggested by:

• Amenorrhea
• Abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding
• Elevated β-hCG
• Adnexal mass containing a gestational sac without cardiac activity

She is an ideal candidate for medical management with single-dose methotrexate because:

• Hemodynamically stable
• Ectopic mass <3.5–4 cm
• No fetal cardiac activity
• β-hCG relatively low (<5000 mIU/mL)

Methotrexate:

• Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase
•

Stops rapidly dividing trophoblastic tissue

•

Avoids surgery

• Preserves fallopian tube and fertility

Why other options are incorrect:

• A. Expectant management is reserved for falling β-hCG levels and very small ectopic pregnancies
• C. Salpingectomy is used for rupture, instability, or failed medical therapy
• D. Tubal milking has high risk of persistent trophoblastic tissue

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 39-year-old G6P2L1A3 presents with a history of previous 2 LSCS with PAS. What will you NOT counsel her about?
options: Risk of bladder injury in case of PAS
Risk of bowel injury in case of PAS
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Risk of bowel injury in case of PAS

Placenta accreta spectrum is mainly associated with massive hemorrhage, bladder invasion, and need for peripartum hysterectomy. Bowel injury is not a typical or expected complication.

Placenta accreta spectrum includes abnormal adherence of placenta to the uterine wall due to defective decidua basalis. Types of PAS

| Type | Depth of invasion

| ---- | -----------------

| Placenta accreta | Attached to myometrium

| Placenta increta | Invades myometrium

| Placenta percreta | Penetrates through uterus

In severe cases, placenta may invade adjacent organs, most commonly the bladder.

| Complication | Reason

| ------------ | ------

| Massive hemorrhage | Placenta cannot separate

| Blood transfusion requirement | Severe bleeding

| Bladder injury | Placental invasion into bladder

| Peripartum hysterectomy | Life-saving procedure

Thus A, B, and D are valid counseling points.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A G2P1 woman with a previous lower segment cesarean section presents with bleeding per vaginum and is diagnosed with placenta previa. During cesarean delivery, the placenta is noted to be invading into the bladder wall. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Placenta percreta

Placenta Accreta Spectrum occurs when the placenta attaches abnormally deep into the uterus due to absence of decidua basalis.

| Type | Depth of invasion

| ---- | -----------------

| Placenta accreta | Placenta attaches to myometrium

| Placenta increta | Invades into myometrium

| Placenta percreta | Penetrates through myometrium to serosa or adjacent organs

Previous cesarean scar

↓

Defective decidua basalis

↓

Placenta attaches deeply

↓

Placenta invades uterine wall

In placenta percreta, invasion may extend into:

• Bladder (most common)
• Broad ligament
• Bowel (rare)

Clinical Features

• Antepartum hemorrhage
• Difficult placental separation
• Massive postpartum hemorrhage

Management

Definitive management: Cesarean hysterectomy with placenta left in situ

Reason:

• Attempting placental removal causes catastrophic hemorrhage.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman at 30 weeks presents with painful bleeding PV, reduced fetal movement, increased uterine tone, and absent FHR. BP is 166/98 mmHg, and the cervix is 6 cm dilated, 70% effaced with intact membranes. What is the next best step?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Start Antihypertensives and ARM

These findings are typical of Placental Abruption with intrauterine fetal demise (IUFD). Placental abruption occurs when the placenta separates prematurely from the uterine wall, causing bleeding behind the placenta.

Classic features

| Feature | Explanation

| ------- | -----------

| Painful bleeding PV | Placental separation

| Hypertonic uterus | Blood irritates myometrium

| Fetal distress or death | Reduced placental perfusion

| Hypertension | Major risk factor

The fetus in this case has already died (absent FHR).

Therefore the goal is rapid vaginal delivery to protect the mother. Artificial rupture of membranes (ARM) helps by:

• Reducing uterine pressure
• Accelerating labour
• Controlling bleeding

A) Emergency LSCS

Cesarean section is indicated only if fetus is alive.

B) Antihypertensives + LSCS

Again unnecessary because IUFD already occurred.

D) Tocolysis

Tocolytics suppress labour and are contraindicated in placental abruption.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A primigravida at 22 weeks of gestation presents to you with profuse vaginal bleeding. Her blood pressure and glucose levels are within normal limits. Placental implantation at which of the following sites can cause this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Internal os

Placenta previa occurs when the placenta implants in the lower uterine segment, partially or completely covering the internal cervical os.

| Type | Description

| ---- | -----------

| Type I | Placenta in lower segment but not reaching os

| Type II | Placenta reaches os

| Type III | Placenta partially covers os

| Type IV | Placenta completely covers os

As pregnancy progresses:

• Lower uterine segment stretches
• Placental attachment disrupts
• Leads to painless vaginal bleeding

Painless bleeding in 2nd or 3rd trimester = placenta previa.

| Feature | Placenta previa | Abruptio placentae

| ------- | --------------- | ------------------

| Pain | Painless bleeding | Painful bleeding

| Uterus | Soft | Tender

| Cause | Placenta over os | Placental separation

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Consider the following statements regarding oligohydramnios: 1. It is defined on USG when maximum vertical pocket of liquor is less than 5 cm. 2. It is defined on USG when AFI is less than 5 cm. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 2 only

Oligohydramnios refers to decreased amniotic fluid volume and is associated with increased maternal and fetal morbidity. It is diagnosed by ultrasonography using either the Amniotic Fluid Index (AFI) or the Single Deepest Vertical Pocket (SDVP/Maximum Vertical Pocket, MVP).

Why is B correct?

• 1. It is defined on USG when maximum vertical pocket of liquor is less than 5 cm. ✗

• Oligohydramnios is defined when the Single Deepest Vertical Pocket (SDVP/MVP) is <2 cm, not <5 cm.

• 2. It is defined on USG when AFI is less than 5 cm. ✓

• AFI <5 cm is the standard ultrasound definition of oligohydramnios.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following are correct regarding pathological findings of placenta accreta? 1. Absence of decidua basalis 2. Absence of Nitabuch’s fibrinoid layer 3. Loss of normal hypoechoic retroplacental myometrial zone in ultrasonography Select the answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1, 2 and 3

Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) is characterized by abnormal adherence of the placenta to the uterine wall due to defective decidualization. It occurs because of absence or deficiency of the decidua basalis and Nitabuch’s fibrinoid layer, allowing chorionic villi to attach directly to or invade the myometrium. Ultrasound is the primary modality for antenatal diagnosis.

• 1. Absence of decidua basalis ✓

• The fundamental pathological defect in placenta accreta is the absence or deficiency of the decidua basalis, permitting abnormal placental attachment.

• 2. Absence of Nitabuch’s fibrinoid layer ✓

• Nitabuch’s layer normally separates the placenta from the myometrium. Its absence facilitates abnormal trophoblastic invasion.

• 3. Loss of normal hypoechoic retroplacental myometrial zone on ultrasonography ✓

• One of the characteristic ultrasound findings is loss of the retroplacental clear (hypoechoic) zone, suggesting placental invasion into the myometrium.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is not a cause of secondary PPH? (NEET PG 2018)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Placenta previa

Secondary postpartum hemorrhage (secondary PPH) is excessive vaginal bleeding occurring:

• After 24 hours postpartum
• Up to 6 weeks after delivery

Common causes include:

• Retained placental tissue or retained cotyledon
• Endometritis
• Placental polyp
• Subinvolution of the placental site

Placenta previa is a cause of antepartum hemorrhage, not secondary postpartum hemorrhage.

Important concepts:

• Retained products prevent proper uterine contraction and involution
• Infection causes uterine inflammation and delayed healing
• Placental polyp refers to retained placental tissue forming a vascular mass

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which one of the following parameters precisely defines grade 3 abruptio placentae?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Intrauterine fetal death

The Sher classification of abruptio placentae is based mainly on the clinical severity and fetal status:

• Grade 1 (mild): Minimal vaginal bleeding, no maternal or fetal distress.
• Grade 2 (moderate): More significant bleeding, maternal tachycardia, uterine tenderness, and fetal distress.
• Grade 3 (severe): Intrauterine fetal death (IUFD), often associated with significant concealed hemorrhage and maternal complications such as coagulopathy/DIC.

Therefore, IUFD precisely defines Grade 3 abruptio placentae.

Why not the other options?

• A. Moderate vaginal bleeding: More consistent with Grade 2.
• B. Maternal tachycardia: Usually indicates Grade 2 disease.
• C. Low fibrinogen: May occur in severe abruption due to DIC, but it is not the defining criterion for Grade 3.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 22-year-old primigravida with a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy at 22 weeks undergoes ultrasonography. One twin has severe polyhydramnios with signs of hydrops fetalis, while the co-twin has oligohydramnios. Which Quintero stage best describes this condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Stage IV

Hydrops fetalis in either twin is the defining feature of Quintero Stage IV TTTS. TTTS occurs due to unbalanced placental vascular anastomoses in monochorionic twins, resulting in a hypovolemic donor twin and a hypervolemic recipient twin. The recipient may develop cardiac failure leading to hydrops.

Quintero Staging (High-Yield)

| Stage | Finding

| ----- | -------

| I | Oligohydramnios–polyhydramnios sequence; donor bladder visible

| II | Donor bladder not visualized

| III | Abnormal Doppler studies (AEDF/REDF in UA, reversed a-wave in DV, or pulsatile UV)

| IV | Hydrops fetalis in either twin

| V | Demise of one or both twins

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 26-year-old Rh-negative woman had one full-term pregnancy 3 years ago. Her husband is Rh-positive. She is unsure whether she received anti-D immunoglobulin after delivery. The child was later found to be Rh-negative. She is now planning another pregnancy. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Administer anti-D immunoglobulin immediately before conception
Perform an Indirect Coombs Test (Indirect Antiglobulin Test) to assess maternal sensitization
Administer anti-D immunoglobulin only after the next delivery regardless of the baby’s Rh status
No further evaluation or prophylaxis is required
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Perform an Indirect Coombs Test (Indirect Antiglobulin Test) to assess maternal sensitization

A previously pregnant Rh-negative woman with an uncertain history of anti-D prophylaxis should undergo an Indirect Coombs Test (ICT) before or early in the next pregnancy to determine whether she has already become alloimmunized (sensitized).

In this case, the previous baby was Rh-negative, so anti-D prophylaxis was actually not indicated after that delivery because there was no Rh incompatibility. However, since the maternal sensitization status is unknown, the appropriate next step is to screen for anti-D antibodies using ICT.

High-Yield Points

• Indirect Coombs Test (ICT): Detects maternal anti-D antibodies (screening for Rh sensitization).
• Direct Coombs Test (DCT): Detects antibodies attached to fetal/neonatal RBCs.
• Anti-D immunoglobulin is prophylactic, not therapeutic—it is not given before conception.
• Anti-D is administered only if the mother is unsensitized and after a sensitizing event or delivery of an Rh-positive infant.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 28-year-old married woman who is anxious to conceive presents with copious vaginal discharge, without any itching. Her last menstrual period was 13 days ago. What is the cause of her vaginal discharge? (NEET PG 2021)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Physiological

Physiological vaginal discharge (physiological leukorrhea) is common during the ovulatory phase of the menstrual cycle due to rising estrogen levels.

This patient likely has ovulatory discharge because:

• Last menstrual period was 13 days ago (peri-ovulatory period)
• Discharge is copious and non-irritating
• No itching or foul smell is present

Characteristics of physiological discharge:

• Clear or white
• Thin and mucoid
• Non-offensive
• Not associated with itching, burning, or pain

Why other options are unlikely:

• A. Candidiasis → intense itching with curdy white discharge
• B. Bacterial vaginosis → fishy odor with thin gray discharge
• C. Trichomoniasis → frothy yellow-green discharge with itching

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 28-year-old primigravida presents at 36 weeks with painful vulval ulcers. She does not give history of similar lesions ever in the past. On examination, there are multiple painful vesicular lesions. Which is the best treatment option? (NEET PG 2021)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Acyclovir and elective Cesarean section

This patient has a primary genital herpes infection in late pregnancy, suggested by:

• Painful vesicular vulval lesions
• No prior history of similar lesions
• Presentation at 36 weeks gestation

Primary HSV infection near term carries a high risk of neonatal herpes transmission during vaginal delivery because maternal protective antibodies are absent.

Management:

• Acyclovir therapy to reduce viral shedding and lesion duration
•

Elective cesarean section to prevent neonatal exposure during birth vaginal delivery is avoided because Neonatal herpes can cause severe disseminated disease, encephalitis, and high mortality

•

Recurrent HSV infection has a lower transmission risk because maternal antibodies are present

• Active genital lesions or prodromal symptoms at labor are indications for cesarean delivery

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 28-year-old primigravida with a dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy undergoes vaginal delivery. The first twin is delivered cephalically without complications. Ultrasound immediately after delivery confirms that the second twin is in breech presentation, fetal heart rate is reassuring, membranes are intact, and the cervix is fully dilated. What is the preferred method of delivery for the second twin?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Assisted breech delivery

When the first twin is delivered cephalically, vaginal delivery is appropriate regardless of the presentation of the second twin, provided there are no contraindications. If the second twin is breech, assisted breech delivery is the preferred technique. The breech is allowed to descend spontaneously until the umbilicus is visible ("hands off the breech"), after which maneuvers such as Lovset (for the arms) and Burns–Marshall or Mauriceau–Smellie–Veit (for the after-coming head) are used.

Why not the other options?

• A. Lower segment cesarean section (LSCS ) – Not routinely required. Combined vaginal–cesarean delivery has higher maternal morbidity and is reserved for failed vaginal delivery or fetal compromise.
• B. Internal podalic version (IPV) – Indicated for a transverse or oblique lie of the second twin, not for a fetus already presenting by the breech.
• C. Breech extraction – Involves immediate traction on the fetal feet from the outset and is reserved for selected situations such as fetal distress or after internal podalic version, not for a spontaneously descending breech.

High-Yield Pearl:

Second twin breech with full cervical dilatation:

• Assisted breech delivery = Wait, then assist.
• Breech extraction = Pull from the start.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 35-year-old primigravida who conceived after in-vitro fertilization therapy came for an antenatal checkup at 38 weeks of gestation. Her obstetric history revealed that she was pregnant with DCDA twins. On examination, the first twin was found to be in a breech position and the maternal blood pressure was found to be greater than 140/90 mm Hg on two occasions with grade 1+ proteinuria. What should be done next? (NEET PG 2020)
options: Monitor BP and terminate pregnancy if BP rises
Terminate pregnancy at 40 weeks of gestation
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Immediate Caesarean section

In twin pregnancy, the presentation of the first twin determines the mode of delivery.

Key Principles:

•

First twin breech → Cesarean section indicated

•

Twin pregnancy at term (≥37 weeks) with complications (e.g., preeclampsia) → prompt delivery recommended

•

Vaginal delivery is considered only when first twin is cephalic

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A patient with O negative and husband B positive delivered a baby. Has received anti-D prophylaxis at 28 weeks. In which of the following conditions will you give anti-D post-delivery?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Baby +ve, DCT -ve

Rh Isoimmunization occurs when:

• Rh-negative mother
• Rh-positive fetus

Fetal red blood cells entering maternal circulation stimulate production of anti-D antibodies, which can attack fetal RBCs in future pregnancies.

Rh-positive fetal RBCs enter maternal circulation

↓

Mother forms anti-D antibodies

↓

Antibodies cross placenta in next pregnancy

↓

Fetal hemolysis

↓

Hemolytic disease of the newborn

Anti‑D Immunoglobulin prevents maternal sensitization by destroying fetal Rh-positive cells before the immune system reacts.

Anti-D is given within 72 hours after delivery if:

• Mother is Rh-negative
• Baby is Rh-positive
• Mother is not already sensitized

Thus:

| Baby Rh status | DCT | Anti-D required

| -------------- | --- | ---------------

| Rh negative | Any | ❌ Not required

| Rh positive | DCT negative | ✅ Give Anti-D

| Rh positive | DCT positive | Usually sensitization already present

DCT detects antibodies bound to fetal RBCs.

| DCT result | Meaning

| ---------- | -------

| Negative | No antibodies attached

| Positive | Hemolysis due to antibodies

Doses of Anti-D-

| Situation | Dose

| --------- | ----

| Routine antenatal prophylaxis | 300 µg at 28 weeks

| Post-delivery prophylaxis | 300 µg within 72 hours

| Early pregnancy events | 50–100 µg

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: At 28 weeks gestation, amniocentesis reveals AOD450 in Liley's Zone 3. What is the best line of management? (NEET PG 2016)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Intrauterine transfusion

Liley chart interpretation is used to assess the severity of fetal hemolysis in Rh isoimmunization by measuring amniotic fluid bilirubin (ΔOD450).

Liley zones:

• Zone 1 → mild or absent hemolysis
• Zone 2 → moderate disease, close monitoring required
• Zone 3 → severe fetal hemolytic disease with high risk of hydrops fetalis and fetal death

At 28 weeks gestation:

• The fetus is preterm and unlikely to tolerate delivery well
• Therefore, severe anemia should be treated with intrauterine transfusion

Intrauterine transfusion:

• Corrects fetal anemia
• Reduces risk of hydrops and fetal demise
• Usually performed via intravascular transfusion into the umbilical vein

Important principle:

• Immediate delivery is preferred only when fetal maturity is sufficient
• Before fetal maturity, intrauterine transfusion is the treatment of choice for severe Rh isoimmunization

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Doppler assessment of which fetal vessel is most useful in detecting fetal anemia?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Middle Cerebral Artery

Middle Cerebral Artery Doppler is the most sensitive non-invasive method to detect fetal anemia, especially in Rh Isoimmunization.

Middle Cerebral Artery (MCA) peak systolic velocity >1.5 multiples of median indicates fetal anemia. This non-invasive Doppler technique is the gold standard for monitoring fetal anemia, particularly in Rh isoimmunization cases.

anagement if MCA PSV >1.5 MoM

Next step: Cordocentesis (PUBS) to confirm anemia.

Treatment: Intrauterine fetal blood transfusion.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: If division occurs on the 7th day during twin gestation, the result would be: (NEET PG 2016)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Diamnionic, monochorionic

The timing of division of a monozygotic twin pregnancy determines chorionicity and amnionicity.

Timing of division:

• 0–3 days → Diamniotic, dichorionic
• 4–8 days → Diamniotic, monochorionic
• 8–13 days → Monoamniotic, monochorionic
• 13 days → Conjoined twins

Division on the 7th day occurs after formation of the chorion but before formation of the amnion, resulting in:

• One chorion
• Two amniotic sacs

Thus, the twins are diamniotic and monochorionic.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The best time to identify the type of twin pregnancy on ultrasound is? (NEET PG 2018)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 11-14 weeks

The best time to determine chorionicity and amnionicity in twin pregnancy is during the first trimester, especially between 11–14 weeks of gestation.

Why this period is ideal:

• Membranes and placental relationships are clearly visible
• Lambda (twin peak) sign and T-sign can be identified accurately
• Early diagnosis guides antenatal surveillance and management

Ultrasound findings:

• Lambda (twin peak) sign → dichorionic twins
• T-sign → monochorionic twins

Importance of determining chorionicity:

• Monochorionic twins have higher risks of:

• Twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS)
• Selective fetal growth restriction
• Twin anemia-polycythemia sequence
• Increased perinatal morbidity and mortality

Accuracy of chorionicity assessment decreases later in pregnancy as membranes become thinner and placentas may fuse.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The next step to follow for a mother with Rh-negative pregnancy and antibody titre above critical level (husband Rh-positive) is:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. MCA PSV

In an Rh-negative pregnancy with a positive antibody screen and antibody titre above the critical level, the fetus is at risk of hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN).

The next step is to assess for fetal anemia non-invasively using the middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity (MCA-PSV) by Doppler.

• A. Umbilical artery Doppler: Mainly assesses placental resistance and fetal growth restriction, not fetal anemia.
• B. Cordocentesis: Invasive and used when fetal anemia is suspected/confirmed, particularly for diagnostic assessment and possible intrauterine transfusion.
• C. MCA PSV — Correct: MCA-PSV >1.5 MoM is suggestive of moderate-to-severe fetal anemia.
• D. Amniocentesis: Historically used for bilirubin assessment, but has largely been replaced by MCA Doppler for fetal anemia surveillance.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Twin pregnancy should have ultrasound at 10–13 weeks to confirm which of the following? I. Number of foetus II. Viability of foetus III. Chorionicity of twins IV. Malformation in either foetus Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. I, II, III and IV

A first-trimester ultrasound (10–13+6 weeks) is the most important scan in twin pregnancy. It establishes the diagnosis of multiple gestation, accurately determines chorionicity and amnionicity, confirms fetal viability, dates the pregnancy, and screens for major fetal anomalies. Early determination of chorionicity is essential because it is the single most important predictor of pregnancy outcome in twin gestations.

All the listed objectives are achieved by ultrasound at 10–13 weeks:

• I. Number of fetus: Confirms whether the pregnancy is singleton, twin, or higher-order multiple gestation. ⭐
• II. Viability of fetus: Demonstrates cardiac activity in each fetus and confirms viability. ⭐
• III. Chorionicity of twins: The most important purpose of the first-trimester scan is to determine chorionicity and amnionicity. This is best assessed between 11 and 13+6 weeks using:

• Lambda (Twin Peak) sign → Dichorionic twins
• T-sign → Monochorionic twins

• IV. Malformation in either fetus: A first-trimester scan includes screening for major structural anomalies and nuchal translucency assessment.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Twin pregnancy where 1 twin is older by 1 month than the other on ultrasound. What is this known as?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Superfetation

Superfetation = twins conceived in different cycles, giving different gestational ages. Superfecundation happens in the same cycle. MCMA twins are identical and same age.

| Feature | Superfetation | Superfecundation

| ------- | ------------- | ----------------

| Timing | Two different ovulation cycles | Same ovulation cycle

| Gestational age | Different ages | Same age

| Fathers | May be same | May be different

A) Superfecundation

• Occurs in same menstrual cycle, so fetuses have same gestational age.

C) Illegitimate

• Not a medical term.

D) Monochorionic monoamniotic

• Twins are same age, not different gestational ages.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the term used to describe the demise of a twin in the second trimester, accompanied by maceration? (NEET PG 2017)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Fetus Papyraceus

Fetus papyraceus refers to the compressed, mummified remains of a dead fetus retained in a multiple pregnancy after demise in the second trimester.

Pathogenesis:

• One twin dies in utero
• Dead fetus undergoes dehydration and compression between the uterine wall and surviving twin
• Produces a flattened, parchment-like fetus

Important distinction:

• Vanishing twin → early first-trimester fetal loss with resorption
• Fetus papyraceus → later fetal demise with retained macerated fetus

Complications:

• Preterm labor
• Coagulopathy (rare)
• Neurologic injury in surviving monochorionic twin due to shared circulation

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the treatment of choice for a woman with atrophic vaginitis with complaints of itching? (NEET PG 2019)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Topical estrogen

Topical Estrogen in the Treatment of Atrophic Vaginitis

Atrophic vaginitis (vaginal atrophy) is a condition predominantly seen in postmenopausal women, arising from declining estrogen levels. It manifests as vaginal dryness, itching, and discomfort.

For the management of postmenopausal vaginal atrophy, local estrogen preparations are preferred over systemic hormone replacement therapy (HRT), as they act directly at the site of involvement while minimizing systemic exposure and associated side effects.

A standard regimen of conjugated estrogen cream 1 g applied intravaginally daily for 1–2 weeks is generally effective in providing symptomatic relief.

Why Other Options Are Incorrect

• Option A — Steroids: Steroids are not appropriate for atrophic vaginitis. While they may possess anti-inflammatory properties, they fail to address the root cause — estrogen deficiency.
• Option C — Antihistamines alone: Antihistamines may offer transient relief from pruritus but do not correct the underlying hormonal deficiency responsible for the condition.
• Option D — None of the above: This is incorrect, as topical estrogen is well-established as the treatment of choice.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which infection is typically associated with a creamy, fishy odor? (NEET PG 2015)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Gardnerella

Bacterial Vaginosis (BV) caused by Gardnerella vaginalis produces a characteristic fishy odor vaginal discharge. This distinctive odor is one of the key diagnostic criteria for BV. The discharge is typically thin, homogeneous, gray-white that coats the vaginal walls. The fishy smell becomes more pronounced during the "Whiff test" when 10% potassium hydroxide (KOH) is added to the discharge, releasing volatile amines.

Other Options:

Option A. Trichomonas: Trichomonas infection causes a greenish-yellowish discharge that is often frothy. It's associated with dysuria, dyspareunia, and the characteristic "strawberry cervix" appearance, but lacks the fishy odor.

Option C. Candida: Candida infection presents with thick curdy white discharge resembling cottage cheese or flakes adherent to the vaginal wall. It causes intense pruritus but has no fishy odor. The vaginal pH remains acidic (<4.5).

Option D. Chlamydia: Chlamydia typically causes mucopurulent cervical discharge but is not associated with fishy odor. It's often asymptomatic and is a common cause of cervicitis and PID when it ascends to the upper genital tract.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following are correct regarding pathology of stress urinary incontinence? 1. Hypermobility of urethra 2. Ascend of bladder neck and proximal urethra above pelvic diaphragm 3. Lowered urethral pressure 4. Increased detrusor activity Select the answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1 and 3

Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) is the involuntary leakage of urine during activities that increase intra-abdominal pressure (e.g., coughing, sneezing, laughing, exercise).

• 1. Hypermobility of urethra ✓

• The most common mechanism of SUI is urethral hypermobility due to weakness of the pelvic floor and endopelvic fascia, resulting in loss of urethral support.

• 2. Ascend of bladder neck and proximal urethra above pelvic diaphragm ✗

• In SUI, the bladder neck and proximal urethra descend below the pelvic floor, not ascend.

• 3. Lowered urethral pressure ✓

• Intrinsic sphincter deficiency causes reduced urethral closing pressure, contributing to stress incontinence.

• 4. Increased detrusor activity ✗

• Detrusor overactivity is the hallmark of urge urinary incontinence, not stress urinary incontinence.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the vaginal preterm delivery of twins is accurate? (NEET PG 2016)
options: The first twin has a higher risk of birth asphyxia
The second twin has a higher risk of Hyaline Membrane Disease
The first twin has a higher risk of mortality
The second twin has a higher risk of intracranial hemorrhage
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. The second twin has a higher risk of intracranial hemorrhage

During vaginal delivery of twins, the second twin has a higher risk of complications, especially in preterm births. The second twin is more prone to intracranial hemorrhage due to:

• Delayed delivery after birth of the first twin
• Cord prolapse or cord compression
• Placental separation
• Greater risk of hypoxia and birth trauma
• Hemodynamic instability in premature infants with fragile germinal matrix vessels

Additional risks for the second twin:

• Birth asphyxia
• Malpresentation
• Operative delivery
• Increased perinatal morbidity and mortality

Why other options are incorrect:

• Hyaline membrane disease mainly depends on prematurity, not birth order
• The first twin generally has lower risk compared with the second twin

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which one of the following statements regarding Rh isoimmunization are correct? 1. Liley’s chart identifies anemia better than middle cerebral artery Doppler. 2. Indirect Coombs’ test is positive in mother. 3. Baby is at risk of developing anemia. 4. Direct Coombs’ test is positive in baby. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 2, 3 and 4

Rh isoimmunization occurs when an Rh-negative mother develops anti-D antibodies against fetal Rh-positive red blood cells. These maternal IgG antibodies cross the placenta and cause hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN).

Why are the statements correct/incorrect?

• 1. Liley’s chart identifies anemia better than middle cerebral artery (MCA) Doppler: Incorrect. MCA peak systolic velocity (MCA-PSV) Doppler is now the preferred and more accurate non-invasive method for detecting fetal anemia. Liley’s chart (based on amniotic fluid bilirubin, ΔOD450) has largely been replaced.
• 2. Indirect Coombs’ test is positive in the mother: Correct. It detects circulating maternal anti-D antibodies.
• 3. Baby is at risk of developing anemia: Correct. Maternal IgG antibodies destroy fetal RBCs, causing hemolytic anemia.
• 4. Direct Coombs’ test is positive in the baby: Correct. It detects antibodies bound to the neonatal RBCs.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which will you not see in twin pregnancy?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. MADC (Monoamniotic Dichorionic)

Twin pregnancies are classified based on:

• Chorionicity → number of placentas
• Amnionicity → number of amniotic sacs

| Type | Chorion | Amnion | Frequency

| ---- | ------- | ------ | ---------

| Dichorionic diamniotic (DCDA) | 2 | 2 | Most common

| Monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA) | 1 | 2 | Common in identical twins

| Monochorionic monoamniotic (MCMA) | 1 | 1 | Rare

MADC = Monoamniotic Dichorionic

This means:

• Two placentas (dichorionic)
• Only one amniotic sac (monoamniotic)

This is embryologically impossible because:

• Each chorion normally develops its own amniotic sac.
• If two chorions exist, there must be two amniotic sacs.

Thus monoamniotic dichorionic twins cannot exist.
